findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-103-002: Love is the programme's most constitutionally comprehensive characteristic — it occupies all five constitutional levels simultaneously: spirit-sourced (implied via Spirit-as-agent, Rom 5:5, Gal 5:22),…
findings.finding_value: Love is the programme's most constitutionally comprehensive characteristic — it occupies all five constitutional levels simultaneously: spirit-sourced (implied via Spirit-as-agent, Rom 5:5, Gal 5:22), soul-located (Song 5:6 — soul failing at beloved's absence; Mat 22:37 — love with all your soul; Joh 15:13 — laying down the soul), heart-inscribed (Pro 3:3; Rom 5:5 infused into hearts), mind-engaged (Mat 22:37 — love with all your mind; Joh 15:15 — love as knowledge-sharing), and body-expressed (kiss, embrace, tears, womb-movement across multiple groups). The constitutional movement pattern is consistently downward: Spirit origin → heart reception → soul experience → body expression. Love's heart-inscription (Pro 3:3) is the closest evidence to a constitutional deposit — the metaphorical writing of chesed into the heart's deepest register produces a lasting dispositional quality (the chasid person-type). The primary finding: love is not confined to any single constitutional level but operates across all levels in an integrated movement from deepest to most outward. This comprehensive constitutional architecture is consistent with love's function as the programme's organising characteristic.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-103-007: Love's constitutional architecture and its faculty engagement are structurally aligned. The heart's engagement with love (Q&A-044, Q&A-045) corresponds to the heart's known integrating function across…
findings.finding_value: Love's constitutional architecture and its faculty engagement are structurally aligned. The heart's engagement with love (Q&A-044, Q&A-045) corresponds to the heart's known integrating function across the programme: the heart is the location of knowing (Joh 15:15 — knowledge-disclosure as love's act), willing (Mat 22:37 — love commanded), feeling (Song 5:2 — heart awake in love-awareness), and moral awareness (Pro 3:3 — chesed inscribed). Each of the heart's functions corresponds to a faculty: knowing → reason and memory; willing → will; feeling → emotion; moral awareness → moral sensitivity. The soul-level constitutional location (Song 5:6 — soul failing at beloved's absence) corresponds to the identity and relational capacity faculties: the soul whose vitality is partly constituted by the love-object is the soul whose identity (T3.10) and relational capacity (T3.11) are most deeply invested in love. The Spirit-sourced origin of love (implied) corresponds to the deep pre-reflective faculty level (L-005 — love below conscious attention): the Spirit's infusion produces love at a depth below ordinary faculty-awareness. Constitutional depth and faculty depth are directly correlated.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-103-008: The constitutional location data and the relational interface data converge on the same structural claim: love's inner depth is its relational reach. The deeper love is constitutionally (heart-inscrib…
findings.finding_value: The constitutional location data and the relational interface data converge on the same structural claim: love's inner depth is its relational reach. The deeper love is constitutionally (heart-inscribed, soul-constitutive, Spirit-sourced), the further its relational reach — from neighbour-love (soul-level reciprocal) to enemy-love (will-level against grain) to divine love (Spirit-level transcendent). The constitutional movement pattern (Spirit → heart → soul → body — Q&A-056) maps onto the relational directional pattern: divine love enters at the deepest constitutional level (Spirit, heart) and produces relational acts at the outermost level (community legibility, bodily expression). The GOD→HUMAN axis operates at the constitutional depth where love is received (heart-infusion — Rom 5:5); the HUMAN→GOD axis requires total constitutional mobilisation (Mat 22:37 — all heart, soul, mind); the HUMAN→HUMAN axis is the outward bodily expression of the internal constitutional reality. Constitutional and relational are thus not two separate dimensions of love but the inside and outside of the same movement.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-103-011: The evidential foundation supports and grounds the constitutional location claims. Each constitutional level identified in T2 has specific vocabulary evidence in T7: Spirit-level origin — Gal 5:22 (fr…
findings.finding_value: The evidential foundation supports and grounds the constitutional location claims. Each constitutional level identified in T2 has specific vocabulary evidence in T7: Spirit-level origin — Gal 5:22 (fruit of the Spirit), Rom 5:5 (poured into hearts through the Spirit); soul-level — Song 5:6 (soul failing), Mat 22:37 (all your soul), Joh 15:13 (lay down the soul); heart-level — Pro 3:3 (heart inscription), Rom 5:5 (into our hearts); mind-level — Mat 22:37 (all your mind), Joh 15:15 (knowledge disclosure); body-level — kiss/embrace/tears/inner-organ-movement vocabulary across multiple groups. The lexical range of the primary terms (Q&A-122 — chesed, racham, agapē, dod, phileō) corresponds precisely to the five constitutional levels: each term carries a different constitutional register as its primary habitat. The evidential foundation thus not only confirms the constitutional claims but shows them to be lexically grounded in the vocabulary's own structure.

The mercy-mechanism (atonement) operates specifically on the soul level — it addresses the guilt-state of the *nephesh*. Soul/R182 shares the Lev 23:27 anchor. OBS-111-037, OBS-111-045.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-111-002: T2 reveals mercy as a whole-person constitutional reality. No single level contains it: mercy originates at the spirit-soul interface, operates on the soul (addressing the nephesh-guilt), engages the …
findings.finding_value: T2 reveals mercy as a whole-person constitutional reality. No single level contains it: mercy originates at the spirit-soul interface, operates on the soul (addressing the nephesh-guilt), engages the heart through the visceral compassion vocabulary (splanchna), engages the mind through the memory-erasure mechanism (Heb 8:12), and operates through the body as both the medium of mercy-seeking (embodied posture) and the mechanism of mercy's effect (blood-atonement). The triadic constitutional movement (Q&A-065): inner disposition → soul-transformation → embodied expression. The key finding reading T2 as a whole is the receiving-before-generating origin structure (Q&A-062): mercy cannot be generated from within the person but must be received from outside and then expressed through the constitutional architecture. Body deposit: none. T5.7: formally closed.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-111-008: T1 defines mercy as a four-element structure (disposition, mechanism, petition-response, spatial locus) and T2 maps mercy's constitutional architecture across all levels. Reading T1 and T2 together: t…
findings.finding_value: T1 defines mercy as a four-element structure (disposition, mechanism, petition-response, spatial locus) and T2 maps mercy's constitutional architecture across all levels. Reading T1 and T2 together: the constitutional location of mercy precisely maps the four definitional elements. The felt disposition (T1) corresponds to the spirit-soul interface location (T2). The institutional mechanism (T1) corresponds to the soul-level atoning operation (T2). The petition-response (T1) corresponds to the embodied seeking and heart-level engagement (T2). The spatial locus (T1) corresponds to the mercy seat as constitutional-institutional anchor (T2). T1's definitional complexity is explained by T2's constitutional complexity — mercy's definition is complex because its constitutional location is complex.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-111-014: T2 maps mercy's constitutional locations (soul, mind, heart, body, spirit-soul interface) and T3 maps its faculty engagements. Reading together: the constitutional locations and the faculty engagement…
findings.finding_value: T2 maps mercy's constitutional locations (soul, mind, heart, body, spirit-soul interface) and T3 maps its faculty engagements. Reading together: the constitutional locations and the faculty engagements are co-extensive. Soul-level location (T2) corresponds to conscience and moral evaluation faculty engagement (T3) — the soul is where guilt resides and where conscience/moral evaluation operate. Mind-level location (T2, memory-erasure) corresponds to memory faculty engagement (T3, asymmetric memory structure). Heart/splanchna location (T2) corresponds to affect faculty (T3). The receiving-before-generating origin (T2) corresponds to relational capacity as foundational enabler (T3.11). T2 and T3 together: constitutional location and faculty engagement are two descriptions of the same inner-being reality — where mercy operates constitutionally (T2) is where it activates faculties (T3).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-111-015: T2 establishes the receiving-before-generating constitutional principle (Q&A-062) and T4 establishes the asymmetric relational chain (God→received human→extended human mercy). These are the constituti…
findings.finding_value: T2 establishes the receiving-before-generating constitutional principle (Q&A-062) and T4 establishes the asymmetric relational chain (God→received human→extended human mercy). These are the constitutional and relational descriptions of the same structural requirement: mercy cannot be generated from within the person (T2) and mercy cannot be extended without prior receipt (T4). T2 explains why T4's relational chain is necessary: the constitutional principle of receiving-before-generating is what creates the structural necessity of the T4 relational chain. The body-soul interface through which mercy's mechanism operates (T2 — blood atonement on nephesh) is the constitutionally specific expression of the God→human directional mercy (T4.1).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-111-016: T2's constitutional architecture (spirit-soul interface origin, soul-level operation, embodied expression) maps directly onto T5's formative sequences (the four inner-state sequences in Q&A-128 all sh…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional architecture (spirit-soul interface origin, soul-level operation, embodied expression) maps directly onto T5's formative sequences (the four inner-state sequences in Q&A-128 all show external mercy entering through the soul level and producing inner-state transformation). Reading T2 and T5 together: the constitutional route mercy travels (T2's triadic movement — OBS-111-065) is the same route the formative sequence takes (T5's external-to-internal pattern — Q&A-129). Mercy enters the constitutional architecture from outside (received) and then traverses spirit-soul-body in its transformative work. The receiving-before-generating origin (T2) means the formative developmental arc (T5) always begins with external mercy received, not internal mercy generated.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-111-017: T2's soul-level atoning operation (the nephesh addressed by kipper) maps to T6's sequential positioning of mercy (mercy as bridge from negative condition to positive outcome). The constitutionally spe…
findings.finding_value: T2's soul-level atoning operation (the nephesh addressed by kipper) maps to T6's sequential positioning of mercy (mercy as bridge from negative condition to positive outcome). The constitutionally specific operation on the nephesh (T2) is what makes mercy the bridge across the most fundamental negative condition (guilt as soul-condition addressed by atonement). T6's co-occurrence with guilt (R073 at 75) and its cross-registry sequential bridging function are the relational expression of T2's constitutional operation at the soul level. Mercy bridges guilt to forgiveness (T6) because it operates constitutionally on the soul-level guilt-condition (T2).

findings.finding_value: T2 establishes that contrition operates at the deepest constitutional level (spirit as primary locus) with secondary engagement at heart, soul, and body. The constitutional portrait is comprehensive: spirit broken at the innermost level, heart broken at the moral-evaluative level, nephesh crushed at the whole-self level, and bones as the somatic expression of the inner breaking. What T2 reveals as a whole is the embodied depth of contrition — it is not a disembodied inner experience but a constitutional event that traverses all levels of the person. The bidirectional constitutional movement (downward through divine confrontation, upward through reviving) is the structural frame within which contrition functions: it reaches the bottom and creates the conditions for movement back upward. The T2.8 finding (no body deposit) means contrition does not leave a permanent somatic trace — it is a passing constitutional event, not a permanent constitutional mark.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-062-002: T2 reveals fellowship's constitutional location is distributed across levels according to its mode: existential mode (soul/nephesh level — Ecc 9:4), companionship mode (heart level — Psa 119:63, Jer 1…
findings.finding_value: T2 reveals fellowship's constitutional location is distributed across levels according to its mode: existential mode (soul/nephesh level — Ecc 9:4), companionship mode (heart level — Psa 119:63, Jer 13:23), desire-driven mode (desire-faculty — 2Pe 1:4), suffering mode (somatic — Pro 20:30, Isa 53:5). The deepest mode (ontological — 2Pe 1:4) implies spirit-level but this is inferential rather than explicit. T2's most significant finding is the desire-faculty as the constitutional engine directing fellowship: desire determines the fellowship object, and the fellowship object determines the constitutional formation. The body-deposit question (T2.8) remains open — the wound-mark as a persisting joining-trace is the nearest evidence, but its programme-relevance is uncertain.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-062-008: T1's five-mode structure maps precisely onto T2's constitutional levels: existential mode (soul/nephesh), companionship mode (heart), desire-driven mode (desire-faculty), suffering mode (somatic), ont…
findings.finding_value: T1's five-mode structure maps precisely onto T2's constitutional levels: existential mode (soul/nephesh), companionship mode (heart), desire-driven mode (desire-faculty), suffering mode (somatic), ontological mode (spirit — inferential). Definition and constitutional location are co-determining: the mode of fellowship determines the constitutional level at which it operates. The T1 definition (object determines character) is confirmed by T2's constitutional evidence — the desire-faculty as the constitutional engine of fellowship direction means desire determines the object, and the object determines which constitutional level is most engaged.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-062-014: T2's constitutional locations map directly onto T3's faculty engagements. The desire-faculty location (T2.5) corresponds to T3.6 volition and T3.7 agency — desire and will are structurally adjacent in…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional locations map directly onto T3's faculty engagements. The desire-faculty location (T2.5) corresponds to T3.6 volition and T3.7 agency — desire and will are structurally adjacent in directing fellowship. The heart location (T2.3) corresponds to T3.8 moral evaluation, T3.9 conscience, T3.10 conscientiousness — the heart-level constitutional engagement with fellowship produces the moral-faculty effects. The soul-level (T2.2 — Ecc 9:4) corresponds to T3.4 affect — the existential fellowship produces hope as an affective state at the soul level. Constitutional location determines which faculties are primarily engaged.

findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional levels (soul, heart, desire-faculty, somatic) are each evidenced by specific lexical items that T7 analyses. Soul-level (Ecc 9:4 — H2266 Qal); heart-level (Psa 119:63, Jer 13:23 — H2270, H2266 Hithpael); somatic (H2250 — Pro 20:30, Isa 53:5). The grammatical range (T7.1.2) is the lexical expression of the constitutional range (T2): the Hithpael (volitional self-joining) is the heart-level agentive act; the Pual (being-joined — passive settled state) is the constitutional fixing endpoint; the adjectival terms (H2270/H2278 — companion/consort) are the heart-level dispositional forms. T7 provides the vocabulary basis for T2's constitutional account.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-064-002: T2 reveals that forgiveness engages multiple constitutional levels but with a distinctive constitutional pattern. The heart is the one explicitly named locus — Mat 18:35 ("from your heart") names the …
findings.finding_value: T2 reveals that forgiveness engages multiple constitutional levels but with a distinctive constitutional pattern. The heart is the one explicitly named locus — Mat 18:35 ("from your heart") names the heart as the required depth of genuine forgiveness-giving. The cognition-faculty (Jer 31:34 — "remember no more"; "they shall know me") is the most clearly evidenced constitutional engagement alongside the heart. The somatic compassion faculty (splagchnizomai — Mat 18:27) is the named somatic-affective origin-point of the forgiving act. Spirit and soul levels are inferred from the guilt-forgiveness structural relationship and the Spirit's mediating role (Mar 3:29, Joh 20:23) rather than explicitly named. The body-deposit question is data-silent (T2.8); T5.7 closes formally. The constitutional movement is explicit (Luk 7:47 — guilt-bearing → forgiveness received → love generated; Jer 31:34 — forgiveness → direct knowledge of God). T2's key finding: the constitutional structure of forgiveness is act-centred, not state-centred — it is a constitutional event (the moment of release) that produces constitutional consequences (love, reverence, direct access).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-002: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level …
findings.finding_value: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level (chesed as covenantal-soul character), heart-level (Hos 11:8 — "my heart recoils"), and somatic-level (re.chem, splanchnon) are all richly evidenced. The constitutional architecture is bottom-up: the womb and entrails are the originating ground; the soul and heart are the engagement points; the act is the constitutional expression. Four body-part functions are identified: constitutive (womb — the generative image of compassion), expressive (gut — the felt movement), indicative (Synoptic pattern — splanchnizō signals the compassion-event), and mediating (heart in Hos 11:8 — the deliberative locus where compassion and judgment contend). The four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) is uniquely evidenced in this registry — consistently inside-out and bottom-up. T2.8 established no body deposit; T5.7 is formally closed. The constitutional portrait confirms the sb_classification (soul-body interface) and extends it: compassion is the most somatically grounded characteristic in the programme, with its originating logic residing in the body's deepest interior.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-008: T1's four-kind structure (character quality, inner event, condition of object, externalised act) maps precisely onto T2's constitutional levels. The character-quality kind (ra.chum — dispositional com…
findings.finding_value: T1's four-kind structure (character quality, inner event, condition of object, externalised act) maps precisely onto T2's constitutional levels. The character-quality kind (ra.chum — dispositional compassionate character) operates at the soul level (T2.2 — chesed as soul-character). The inner-event kind (splanchnizō — the moment of being-moved) operates at the somatic level (T2.6 — the gut as the site of the stirring). The condition-of-object kind (eleeinos — the pitiable state) is the constitutional trigger that activates the somatic-constitutional movement. The externalised-act kind is the constitutional endpoint of T2.10's four-stage movement sequence. T1's definition and T2's constitutional account are co-determining: the characteristic cannot be adequately defined without specifying the constitutional levels at which its four kinds operate.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-014: T2's four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) maps directly onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The somatic-arousal s…
findings.finding_value: T2's four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) maps directly onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The somatic-arousal stage (T2.6 — gut stirring, splanchnizō) corresponds to T3.1's perceptive-trigger stage (sight activates the somatic response) and T3.4's affect stage (the stirring is the affective movement). The soul-engagement stage (T2.2 — chesed as soul-character) corresponds to T3.8 moral evaluation (the soul assesses the need) and T3.9 conscience (the conscience activates the response). The volitional-engagement stage (T2.3 — heart-locus as deliberative site) corresponds to T3.6 volition (the will directs the action). The outward-action stage corresponds to T3.7 agency. T2 and T3 describe the same movement sequence from two perspectives: T2 maps the constitutional levels; T3 maps the faculties active at each level.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-002: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary…
findings.finding_value: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary point of reception (Zec 12:10 — spirit of grace poured out), not the point of generation (grace originates with God — T2.9). The soul level is the site of standing (Rom 5:2 — "this grace in which we stand") and identity (1Cor 15:10 — "by the grace of God I am what I am"). The constitutional movement follows the SD021 four-faces model: divine disposition received at spirit level → relational standing established at soul level → specific capacity gifted → character expressed outward. Heart-location is partially evidenced via eusplanchnos (Eph 4:32 — the tenderheartedness that grace produces, reaching the affective-somatic interface). T2.7 produces a new finding: grace operates bidirectionally through the body-soul interface — soul-to-body (inner posture enacted somatically in prostration, fasting, sackcloth) and body-to-soul (somatic enactment deepening and confirming the inner posture). T2.8 remains open (body deposit question unresolved); T5.7 is left open accordingly. The constitutional origin analysis (T2.9) is the most analytically significant T2 finding: grace does not originate in the human constitutional system at any level — it arrives from outside. This is confirmed at T6 as the structural uniqueness of grace: the only characteristic that is not produced by any other inner-being characteristic.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-008: T1's four-kind structure (disposition, standing, capacity, character quality) maps onto T2's constitutional levels. The divine-disposition kind operates at the level of grace's origin (T2.9 — God's ow…
findings.finding_value: T1's four-kind structure (disposition, standing, capacity, character quality) maps onto T2's constitutional levels. The divine-disposition kind operates at the level of grace's origin (T2.9 — God's own disposition; not a human constitutional level). The standing kind operates at the soul level (T2.2 — Rom 5:2 "this grace in which we stand"). The capacity kind operates at the spirit-soul interface — the specific enabling for specific tasks (2Cor 12:9) is received at the deepest level and expressed through specific faculties. The character-quality kind operates at the soul-to-body level (T2.7 — gracious conduct and speech expressing the received inner character outward). T1's constitutional movement finding (SD021 four-faces sequence) is the longitudinal form of T2's spatial map: T2 identifies the constitutional levels; T1 identifies the movement between them.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-014: T2's constitutional movement (spirit reception → soul standing → capacity → character expression) maps onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The spirit-reception stage (T2.1) corresponds to T3.1 (per…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional movement (spirit reception → soul standing → capacity → character expression) maps onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The spirit-reception stage (T2.1) corresponds to T3.1 (perception — grace enabling the inner sight and hearing that receives it). The soul-standing stage (T2.2) corresponds to T3.9 (conscience — grace as the condition within which conscience can operate without destruction) and T3.8 (moral evaluation — the standing produces the clarity of moral self-assessment). The capacity-gifting stage (T2.1 — spirit level) corresponds to T3.7 (agency — capacity given constitutes agency for the task). The character-expression stage (T2.7 — outward through body-soul) corresponds to T3.10 (conscientiousness — the integrated moral-action expression of received grace-character). T2 maps the constitutional space; T3 maps the faculties active at each spatial level; the two tiers describe the same movement from orthogonal perspectives.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-018: T2's constitutional levels are carried by specific grammatical forms in T7. The spirit-reception level (T2.1) is carried by the perfect passive form of charitoō (kecharitōmenē — the completed act of b…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional levels are carried by specific grammatical forms in T7. The spirit-reception level (T2.1) is carried by the perfect passive form of charitoō (kecharitōmenē — the completed act of being-made-the-object-of-grace, with continuing state) — the most precise grammatical encoding of a constitutional arrival that has permanently changed the person's standing. The soul-standing level (T2.2) is carried by charis as noun (the inhabited state of favour) and chen as the relational standing-in-favour term. The character-expression level is carried by chen in its conduct/speech register (889-003) and charizō in its human-forgiving mode. T7's NT coinage finding (charitoō invented to carry the standing-in-favour concept) is the lexical evidence that T2's spirit-level reception was conceptually unprecedented — no prior vocabulary could name what happened constitutionally when grace-as-standing arrived.

findings.finding_value: T2 reveals that covenant operates constitutionally in the heart, mind, soul, mouth, and body. T4 reveals that covenant operates relationally through God-to-human, human-to-God, and horizontal interfaces. The T2 × T4 synthesis: the constitutional locations and the relational interfaces are not separate registers — they are the same inner reality viewed from different angles. The soul's engagement in covenant (T2 — "with all his heart and all his soul") is precisely the inner posture required for genuine human-to-God movement (T4.2 — Q&A-106). The mouth as constitutional location (T2 — Isa 59:21) is the organ through which the human-to-God relational direction is enacted (oath as speech act — Q&A-024, T1.4). The blood as somatic covenant-medium (T2 — Q&A-053) is the mediating substance through which the God-to-human interface is constituted (the blood of the covenant — Q&A-101). Constitutional location and relational interface are two views of the same inner-being dynamic.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-117-001: T1 names peace's essence as integrative wholeness; T2 confirms this is constitutionally comprehensive — the soul (T2.2), heart (T2.3), mind (T2.4), hidden person (T2.5), and body (T2.6) are all in sco…

The essence and the constitutional address are co-extensive: the integrative wholeness of shalom is not located in one faculty but distributed across all constitutional levels simultaneously. The soul is the most explicitly named OT location (Lam 3:17); the heart is the most comprehensive (engaging all four heart functions); the mind is the most causally explicit (Isa 26:3 — direction of mind → perfect peace). Together: peace is not a faculty-specific characteristic but a whole-person condition whose essence (integrative wholeness) matches its constitutional scope (spirit-soul-heart-mind-body).

The constitutional and faculty maps are not independent but interlocking descriptions of the same whole-person reality.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-060-002: T2 as a whole reveals that this characteristic has no single constitutional home — it operates across the full spirit-soul-body register through different modes. Spirit is the location in two modes: a…
findings.finding_value: T2 as a whole reveals that this characteristic has no single constitutional home — it operates across the full spirit-soul-body register through different modes. Spirit is the location in two modes: as the object of endowing giving (Neh 9:20) and as the faculty transformed eschatologically (Isa 61:3). Soul (nephesh/nafshi) appears in divine self-reference in the giving-over context (Jer 12:7). Heart (leb) is the faculty where the giving decision is made (Hos 11:8). Hidden inner parts (tukhoth) are the target of wisdom-giving (Job 38:36). Rahamim (visceral compassion) is the inner-being quality that determines giving direction. Body appears as the expressive medium of self-giving (Isa 50:6) and as constituted by breath-giving (Isa 42:5). No constitutional body deposit is confirmed. Three movement patterns — constitutive (spirit→mind), expressive (inner→body), transformative (outside-in→inside renewed→inside-out) — show the characteristic is constitutionally dynamic. What T2 reveals as a whole: this characteristic operates at every constitutional level not because it is superficially distributed but because giving as an inner-being act can reach the spirit (endowing), the heart (deciding), the soul (attaching), the hidden inner parts (forming), and the body (expressing and constituting). It is constitutionally pervasive.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-008: The constitutional locations where the characteristic operates (T2 — heart, soul/nephesh, spirit, body) and the relational interfaces through which it operates (T4 — God-to-human, human-to-God) reveal…
findings.finding_value: The constitutional locations where the characteristic operates (T2 — heart, soul/nephesh, spirit, body) and the relational interfaces through which it operates (T4 — God-to-human, human-to-God) reveal a mirroring structure. God's giving proceeds from his leb (heart, Hos 11:8) and his nafshi (soul, Jer 12:7) — the deepest divine inner-being locations are engaged in the God-to-human direction. The human's giving toward God is expressed through the body (back, cheeks, face — Isa 50:6) and from the deepest inner orientation (Job 1:21 — recognition of divine sovereignty). The constitutional depths engaged in both directions are commensurate: God gives from his heart and soul; the human gives from the whole self, expressed bodily. What this pair reveals: the divine-human relational correspondence (DHC dimension, group 872-006) has a constitutional depth structure — the correspondence is not merely behavioural but engages the deepest constitutional levels of both parties. The giving that constitutes the correspondence is heart-to-body deep.

findings.finding_value: M01-A reverential fear is not explicitly located at the soul level. The nearest instance is Luk 1:50 ("fear of God here is the enduring inner orientation that receives divine mercy across generations — it is a reverent posture **of the soul** directed toward God") — but this is the translated Greek psychē context, and the meaning focuses on the posture being sustained, not on constitutional location at the soul level.

M01-D-VCG-01 has an explicit soul-level instance. Psa 6:3 (anchor): "**the psalmist's soul itself** is greatly dismayed — the inner being, not just the body, is the seat of this profound turmoil, and it drives the anguished cry to God asking how long." The dismay is explicitly in the soul (nefesh/Hebrew) as the seat of the profound turmoil.

M01-BOUNDARY and M01-B: Mat 26:37 (BOUNDARY term ademoneo): "Jesus begins to be sorrowful and troubled in Gethsemane; the distress is a deeply agitated inner state engaging **his soul** as he faces the approaching suffering." Soul-level location evidenced for ademoneo (BOUNDARY term).

Explicit soul-level location of fear within M01 is sparse: Psa 6:3 (dismay in the soul, M01-D-VCG-01 anchor) is the clearest instance. The Mat 10:28 material (M01-B-VCG-03: "fear of those who can only kill the body is contrasted with fear of God who can destroy **soul and body** in hell") locates the soul as the deeper seat of the person affected by ultimate fear — this is not a location statement but a comparative statement about depth. The cluster as a whole does not routinely locate fear at the soul level explicitly.

Job 6:4 (M02-B-VCG-06) describes God's arrows as carrying "poison his spirit drinks" — the rage is experienced as internal spiritual poisoning. While 'soul' specifically is not always the named faculty, several verses locate the experience in the inner person as a whole: Jam 1:20 (M02-A-VCG-04) speaks of "human wrath" as an inner drive. The characteristic operates throughout the soul in its broader sense as the inner personal life.

Ecc 7:9 (M02-D-VCG-02) states "anger settles as a resident in the heart of fools" — the heart is the soul's integrating centre, and the verse evidences anger taking up residence there as a condition of the inner person as a whole.

Most explicitly in M03-C-VCG-03: Jesus describes his soul as "very sorrowful, even to death" — perilupos (Mat 26:38; Mar 14:34). The soul is named directly as the constitutional seat of the sorrow. This is the most unambiguous soul-level location in the corpus.

The de.a.von term (Deu 28:65 — M03-C-VCG-01 anchor) explicitly locates sorrow in the soul: "sorrow in the soul as a languishing." The tu.gah corpus (Psa 119:28) names grief so deep the soul melts away.

Distress is located in the soul. Psa 31:7 (M03-D-VCG-01): "God has known my distress in my soul." Gen 42:21 (M03-D-VCG-02): the brothers recall Joseph's soul in distress. Soul-location of distress is repeatedly evidenced in the tsa.rah/tsar corpus.

The prophetic weeping of Jer 13:17 (M03-A-VCG-04 anchor) names the soul as the origin of the visible grief: "the soul's hidden grief" flows outward through the eyes. Soul-origin of weeping is confirmed here.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes, explicitly. Psa 35:9 — "my soul will rejoice in the Lord, exulting in his salvation" — names the soul (nephesh) as the active agent of exultation. Isa 61:10 — "my soul shall exult in my God" — confirms the soul as the constitutional locus. Psa 63:5 — "my soul will be satisfied as with fat and rich food, and my mouth will praise you with joyful lips" — shows exultation arising from the soul's deep satisfaction. These three explicit soul-level namings make exultation a confirmed soul-level characteristic.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes. Psa 86:4 — "Gladden the soul of your servant, for to you, O Lord, do I lift up my soul" (soul explicitly named as the seat of gladness to be produced by God). Psa 106:5 — "that I may rejoice in the gladness of your nation" (the aspirational soul-oriented joy of belonging to God's people). Eze 25:6 — "rejoiced with all the malice within your soul" (the soul as the corrupted source of malign joy). The soul appears as a locus of joy in specific passages, but less consistently than the heart.

**[CHAR-7]** S — No verse in the primary agalliao or ba.lag corpus explicitly names the soul (nephesh/psyche) as the constitutional seat of Suffering-Joy. Soul-level location is not directly evidenced in the M04-E-VCG-02 or M04-F corpus.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Partially. Lam 3:25 — "the Lord is good to those who wait for him, to the soul who seeks him" — the soul (nephesh) is named as the seeking agent whose waiting posture enables the experience of God's goodness. Lam 3:26 — "it is good that one should wait quietly" — the benefit is for the person as a whole, with soul implied as the seat of the waiting posture. Ecc 6:3 — "his soul is not satisfied with life's good things" — the soul is the seat of satisfaction/dissatisfaction with the good. These confirm soul-level location in the wellbeing-register of M04-O.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes, directly: (1) **Mat 12:18** — "my soul (psychē) is well pleased" — divine Delight located in the soul, establishing soul-level as the constitutional seat; (2) **Isa 66:3** — "their soul (nephesh) delights in their abominations" — soul named as the seat of misdirected corrupt Delight; (3) **Isa 53:10** — "when his soul makes an offering for guilt, he shall see his offspring" — the servant's soul is the constitutional seat of the self-offering that accomplishes God's purpose/delight; (4) **Heb 10:38** — "my soul has no pleasure in him" — soul (psychē) as the seat of divine withheld Delight; (5) **Psa 73:25** — "nothing on earth that I desire besides you" — the soul's exclusive directing of desire; (6) **Psa 94:19** — "your consolations cheer my soul" — the soul receiving delight-as-consolation. Soul-level is the most consistently named constitutional location across both divine and human registers of Delight.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Yes, explicitly: (1) **Pro 2:10** — "knowledge will be pleasant to your soul (nephesh)" — the soul is named as the seat receiving Pleasure in wisdom/knowledge; (2) **Pro 16:24** — "gracious words are like a honeycomb, sweetness to the soul and health to the body" — soul named first as the primary recipient; (3) **Psa 16:11** — "pleasures forevermore" at God's right hand — the pleasures are experienced by the whole person, with the soul as the experiential centre (the Psalm is addressed by the soul to God); (4) **Psa 36:8** — "river of your delights" from which worshippers drink — soul-level receptive drinking image.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Partially and indirectly: (1) **Psa 119:129** — "your testimonies are wonderful; therefore my soul keeps them" — the soul is named as the faculty that responds to Wonder by keeping the testimonies; Wonder in God's word moves the soul to obedience; (2) **Psa 139:14** — "I praise you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made; wonderful are your works; my soul knows it very well" — the soul explicitly knows the wonderful works; (3) The overall Psalmic proclamatory corpus (VCG-01) is addressed by the whole self, with the soul as the implicit experiential centre. Soul-level location is evidenced through the soul's response to wonder (keeping testimonies; knowing wonders well) rather than as a named seat.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Soul-level location is evidenced in six of the seven characteristics: (1) **Exultation (Char 1)**: Psa 35:9 ("my soul will rejoice"), Isa 61:10 ("my soul shall exult"), Psa 63:5 (soul satisfied → joyful lips); (2) **Joy (Char 2)**: Psa 86:4 (soul to be gladdened), Eze 25:6 ("malice within your soul" as corrupt joy's seat); (3) **Gladness (Char 3)**: Lam 3:25 ("the Lord is good to those who wait for him, to the soul who seeks him"), Ecc 6:3 (soul unsatisfied with life's good things); (4) **Delight (Char 4)**: Mat 12:18 ("my soul is well pleased"), Isa 66:3 ("their soul delights in their abominations"), Heb 10:38 ("my soul has no pleasure"); (5) **Pleasure (Char 5)**: Pro 2:10 ("pleasant to your soul"), Pro 16:24 ("sweetness to the soul"); (6) **Wonder (Char 6)**: Psa 119:129 ("my soul keeps them" — in response to wonder), Psa 139:14 ("my soul knows it very well"); (7) **Suffering-Joy (Char 7)**: not directly evidenced at the soul level — the primary constitutional location is spirit-level. This makes Suffering-Joy the one characteristic where the soul-level is not the primary locus.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes, by location and language. The soul (nefesh) is the locus of the felt inner life, and shame's experience — the felt collapse of dignity — is consistently located in the inner person without explicit anatomical precision but with the language of inner state that is characteristic of soul-level phenomena. Job 10:15 (vc=37502) — "I am *filled* with disgrace" — the language of inner saturation that aligns with soul-level experience. 1Jo 2:28 (vc=34832) uses aischunō in the context of "shrinking" (literally: "shrink back from him in shame") — the recoiling of the inner self before Christ's appearing, which is a soul-level response.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Soul-level location is evidenced by the felt inner collapse accompanying CHAR-2 (the dismay, confusion, and inner devastation of defeated nations; Zion's cry of utter shame, Jer 9:19, vc=65554). The inner experienced dimension of enforced humiliation operates at soul level, though secondary to the social-bodily primary.

---

**[CHAR-3]** E — Soul-level location is implied in the inner attitude of the dishonorer (the Luk 18:2/4 judge whose lack of regard is "a recognised inner character trait"; Luk 18:9's those who "trust in themselves that they were righteous" — a soul-level self-assessment producing contemptuous treatment of others). The inner disposition of worth-misassignment operates at soul level.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — CHAR-4 operates at soul level through the conscience — the faculty that registers the moral quality of conduct and desires against a standard. 2Cor 4:2's "commend ourselves to everyone's conscience in the sight of God" positions CHAR-4's evaluative operation in the conscience as a soul-level faculty. Phili 3:19's "minds set on earthly things" shows the evaluative faculty (mind/phronēma) as the location of the inversion in VCG-03.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — The soul-level dimension of CHAR-5 is evidenced in the wound to the person's sense of worth. Bartimaeus's beggar-identity (Mar 10:50) is a soul-level condition — his inner self-understanding has been shaped by the accumulated contempt of his social context.

---

**[CHAR-6]** E — CHAR-6 is a soul-level characteristic: the moral conscience and the will are both soul-level faculties, and it is their condition (clean, blameless, free from deliberate wrongdoing) that constitutes CHAR-6. The "integrity of my heart" (Gen 20:5) names the soul-level location explicitly: the heart as the integrating moral centre is the primary location of CHAR-6.

---

**[CLUSTER]** E — All six characteristics locate at the soul level, confirming that M07's domain is the soul in its moral-relational dimensions. The specific soul-level faculty varies: Char 1 operates primarily in the affective soul (felt inner collapse); Char 2 in the social-bodily soul (standing in community); Char 3 in the moral-volitional soul (the dishonorer's inner disposition); Char 4 in the conscience as soul-subset; Char 5 in the worth-sensing faculty; Char 6 in the moral-will and conscience. Soul-level location is unanimous but distributed across different soul-subsets — reflecting M07's multi-dimensional character. Char 1's "I am filled with disgrace" (Job 10:15 — language of inner saturation) and Char 6's "integrity of my heart" (Gen 20:5 — heart as the soul's integrating centre) mark the phenomenological depth at which M07 operates.

---

**[CHAR-1]** S — The verse evidence does not locate CHAR-1 constitutionally in the soul (nephesh). The four §3 occurrences of soul-language are all in the perspective of CHAR-1's victims: Jer 13:17 (vc=34091, M08-A3-VCG-03) — the prophet's soul weeps over the people's pride; Psa 13:2 (vc=34241, M08-A4-VCG-03) — the psalmist takes counsel in his soul and has sorrow in his heart as the experience of being dominated by an enemy's exaltation; Psa 123:4 (vc=33953, M08-A4-VCG-03) — the soul overwhelmed by the contempt of the proud. In each case, soul-language describes the inner experience of those crushed by CHAR-1, not the constitutional location of CHAR-1 in its possessor. The proud person's soul is not named as the seat of their pride. This is noted as a silence.
**[CHAR-2]** S — The verse evidence does not explicitly locate CHAR-2 in the soul (nephesh). No verse in §3.A names the soul as the constitutional seat of presumptuous defiance.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Partially. Psa 10:3 (vc=33354, M08-C-VCG-01): "the wicked person boasts of what his own soul [nephesh] desires" — the soul's desires are named as the object and generative ground of the boast. The soul (nephesh) here is the seat of the desires that CHAR-3 then publicly asserts. This is not CHAR-3 located in the soul as its constitutional seat, but the soul's desires as the content that CHAR-3 voices.

**[CHAR-4]** S — The verse evidence does not explicitly locate CHAR-4 in the soul (nephesh/psychē). The psychological vocabulary in §3.C (nous, froneō) specifically addresses the mind/cognitive faculty rather than the soul as a distinct location.
**[CHAR-5]** S — The verse evidence does not explicitly locate CHAR-5 in the soul (nephesh) within §3.D. The primary named location is the heart (lev).

**[CHAR-3]** E — The heart (lev/lebab in Hebrew) is explicitly named: Psa34:18 — "brokenhearted" (nishbar-lev). In Hebrew anthropology, lev (heart) encompasses what the programme framework would treat as soul-level functions (knowing, willing, feeling, moral awareness). The heart as constitutional location confirms soul-level operation alongside the spirit-level. Isa57:15 — "revive the heart of the contrite" — the heart's reviving as the outcome of God's dwelling with the contrite evidences the soul-level engagement.

**[CHAR-4]** S — The two-verse corpus does not explicitly name the soul level as the constitutional location of meekness or gentleness. The terms name capacities and qualities of engagement without specifying the soul as their location.

**[CHAR-5]** S — The three-verse corpus does not explicitly name the soul level as the constitutional location of semnotēs. The characteristic is named as an inner quality shaping the person's manner of existence without specifying the soul as its site.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The heart (lev) is explicitly named as a constitutional location: Exo35:5 — "generous/willing heart"; Exo35:22 — "willing heart"; 2Ch29:31 — "willing heart." The connexion is indirect: humility produces rest; that rest is received at the soul level. Within the Phili2:8 context, Christ's self-humbling produces the obedience that is the act of the will, and the M09-B register (experienced lowliness) names states that affect the person holistically, including at the soul level.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Three characteristics are explicitly soul-located. CHAR-2 Submission: 1Pe1:22 — "having purified your souls by your obedience to the truth" — the soul is the constitutional level that submission purifies. CHAR-3 Contrition: Psa34:18 — "brokenhearted" (nishbar-lev — heart/soul centre broken); Isa57:15 — "revive the heart of the contrite." CHAR-6 Willing-heartedness: heart (lev) explicitly in three of five verses (Exo35:5/22; 2Ch29:31). CHAR-1 Humility: Mat11:29 — "rest for your souls" — the soul as the beneficiary of the characteristic's fruit. CHAR-4 and CHAR-5: not explicitly soul-located in their corpora. **[CHAR-11]** E — Yes. Rom 3:23 — "all have sinned" — the "all" applies to every soul-level moral subject without exception: the universal scope names every person as a moral subject under the condition. Rom 6:17 — "you who were once slaves of sin have become obedient from the heart" — the heart-obedience that conversion involves confirms that the prior sin-condition was at the soul level (heart-slavery). The condition is thus a soul-level structural reality: every person as a moral-subject-before-God stands in this condition from birth (Joh 9:34).

**[CHAR-12]** E — Yes. Joh 8:34 — "everyone who practices sin is a slave to sin" — "everyone" names every moral subject (soul-level) without exception who practices sin; the slavery is a soul-level condition affecting the whole person as a moral subject. 1Jo 3:8 — "whoever makes a practice of sinning is of the devil" — the "of the devil" is a soul-level identity-marker: the whole person's deepest belonging is what is at stake. **[CHAR-21]** E — Yes. 2Pe 2:19 — "For whatever overcomes a person, to that he is enslaved" — the person (*anthrōpos* — the whole human being) is the entity enslaved by corruption; Jude 10 — "destroyed by all that they, like unreasoning animals, understand instinctively" — the person's whole being is destroyed by instinct-driven corruption. Luk 16:10 — "one who is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much" — the dishonesty is a character-property of the person (*anthrōpos*) at the whole-person level; 1Pe 3:18 — "the righteous for the unrighteous" — the *adikos* is named as the whole-person moral category; 2Pe 2:9 — "the unrighteous under punishment" — the whole person is held under divine custody for their injustice.

Within the CHAR-3 corpus proper, Mic 7:9 — "I will bear the indignation of the Lord because I have sinned against him" — names the confessor bearing divine indignation at the soul level: the person accepts the weight of God's displeasure upon themselves as the consequence of the sin they confess. **[CHAR-4]** E — Yes. Isa 66:3 (vc=1633 — VCG-04) is the primary soul-level evidence: "their soul delights in their abominations." The soul (nephesh) is the explicit locus of the characteristic's affective-attachment dimension — the soul's delight-faculty is attached to abominations rather than to God. This is the most direct soul-level location statement in the corpus and is analytically significant: the nephesh as the seat of deepest desire and delight is the constitutional location of the inverted affective attachment that characterises idolatrous abomination.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Yes. Isa 66:3 (vc=38204 — VCG-04): "their soul delights in their abominations" — the soul (nephesh) is the affective-desire faculty that is attached to and delights in the abominable iniquitous ways. The soul-level location reveals iniquity as reaching the deepest desire-centre of the person: the nephesh that should find delight in God instead finds delight in its own chosen abominable ways, of which iniquity is a key component.

**[CHAR-6]** S — The 17-verse corpus does not use explicit soul (psychē) vocabulary to locate this characteristic. The inner-being content is primarily accessed through volitional and cognitive language rather than soul-level designation. This silence is noted.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Soul-level evidence appears in four of six characteristics, with varying directness. Char 4 has the most direct soul-level evidence: Isa 66:3 (vc=1633 — VCG-04): "their soul delights in their abominations" — the nephesh as the explicit locus of the characteristic's inverted affective-desire. Direct nephesh language is not found in the 133-verse corpus for this characteristic in this register.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes. The soul-level faculties are the primary terrain of Characteristic 2. The evidence engages: will (Rom 6:19 — "slaves to impurity" — the will bound; Eph 4:19 — will surrendering to sensuality), desire (Rom 1:24 — "lusts of their hearts"), conscience (1Cor 8:7 — "conscience is defiled"), and heart (Rom 1:24 — "hearts"; Eph 5:5 — heart allegiance disorder as idolatry). The soul-level is the primary operational domain of the characteristic, engaging all its major sub-faculties.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes, at the level of the corporate will and heart. Eze 20:43 (VCG-02): "there you shall remember your ways and all your deeds with which you have defiled yourselves, and you shall loathe yourselves for all the evils that you have committed" — the loathing and remembering are soul-level responses to recognising the defilement. Eze 14:11 (VCG-02): "the house of Israel may no more go astray from me, nor defile themselves anymore with all their transgressions" — the corporate straying is a soul-level act of will (going astray from God). The will, desire, and corporate heart are the primary soul-level faculties through which the characteristic operates.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes, through soul-level faculty suppression. Mar 9:25 (VCG-01): the spirit is "mute and deaf" — it suppresses speech and hearing, which are soul-level communicative capacities. The will is overridden (Luk 8:29 — "driven by the demon") — the will is a primary soul-level faculty. The characteristic thus operates at the soul level by suppressing the soul's faculties through the external spirit's spirit-level domination.

**[CLUSTER]** E — All four characteristics evidence soul-level engagement, but as primary or secondary location differs. Characteristic 1: the soul-level faculties (conscience, affect, will) are engaged as secondary consequences of a primarily bodily-mechanism condition — the defilement arrives through the body and imposes itself on the soul's faculties. Characteristic 2: the soul level is the primary operational domain — conscience (1Cor 8:7), will (Rom 6:19), desire (Rom 1:24), and heart (Eph 5:5) are the characteristic's primary terrain. Characteristic 3: the corporate soul — the collective will, desire, and heart allegiance of the covenant community — is the primary generating force of the characteristic (Eze 23:7 — "all the idols of everyone after whom she lusted"; Eze 14:11 — the corporate will repeatedly straying). Characteristic 4: the soul level is engaged secondarily, as the domain of the faculties (will, speech/hearing) that the spirit suppresses — but the characteristic originates at the spirit level, above the soul. The soul-level gradient thus runs: secondary/body-to-soul (Char 1) → primary/soul-generated (Chars 2, 3) → secondary/spirit-level-suppressing-soul (Char 4).

findings.session_b_note:
Soul-level location reveals that forgiveness is not merely a social transaction or a cognitive decision but an **exercise of the whole inner person**:

- The heart-locus (Mat 18:35) names the seat of the will, the moral awareness, and the affective orientation simultaneously. Forgiving "from the heart" engages all of these — it is not a purely cognitive act (deciding not to hold the claim intellectually) but a whole-person inner release.
- The distinction between verbal/legal forgiveness and heart-level forgiveness (F-002; OBS-064-031) confirms that forgiveness can exist at the outer level without reaching the soul level. The soul-level location is the standard of genuine forgiveness — it must reach the innermost personal experience to be real.
- Q037 notes: "The soul mediates the received forgiveness into extended forgiveness." The soul is the translation layer — divine forgiveness received at the spirit level is processed through the soul-level volitional life and expressed as horizontal forgiveness toward others.

findings.session_b_note:
Soul-level location reveals that compassion is not merely an emotional response to circumstances — it is a constitutive inner orientation that defines the person's relationship to others at the deepest personal level. Three implications emerge from the data:

**Compassion as the soul's outward face.** The soul-level character qualities associated with compassion (ra.chum, sumpathēs, channum) are all constitutively other-oriented. This distinguishes compassion from inner-being characteristics that orient the person primarily toward God (worship, fear, trust) or primarily toward the self (integrity, purity). Compassion is the soul's fundamental orientation toward the suffering other — its outward relational face.

**Compassion as identity-constituting quality.** The adjectival forms (ra.chum, ra.cha.ma.ni, sumpathēs) name what kind of person one is, not merely what one does. Lam 4:10 — "compassionate women" who violate their compassion — shows that this soul-level quality is understood as identity-constituting: the tragedy is precisely that persons whose identity is defined by compassion were forced to act against it.

**Chesed as the deepest covenantal form of compassion.** The chesed vocabulary at the soul level names compassion in its most constitutive and enduring form — the loyal love that holds through covenant violation, exile, and judgment. This is compassion at the level of settled inner character, not responsive feeling. Its soul-level location is confirmed by its persistence: "his mercies never come to an end" (Lam 3:22).

findings.session_b_note:
Soul-level location in Psa 143:3 reveals that the crushing can reach the level of *nefesh* — the seat of personal vitality, desire, and the integrating inner life. When the crushing is sufficiently severe (produced here by enemy pursuit and threat of death), it does not remain at the spirit level but extends to the soul — the person's experience of their own life-force and inner existence. This indicates that contrition-vocabulary crushing, in its most severe experiential form, can affect the full constitutional depth of the person: spirit, heart, and soul.

The practical implication: the experiential-anguish mode of contrition is not a surface emotional disturbance but can penetrate to the existential level — the feeling of one's very life being pressed to the ground.

findings.finding_value: Love is the programme's most constitutionally comprehensive characteristic — it occupies all five constitutional levels simultaneously: spirit-sourced (implied via Spirit-as-agent, Rom 5:5, Gal 5:22), soul-located (Song 5:6 — soul failing at beloved's absence; Mat 22:37 — love with all your soul; Joh 15:13 — laying down the soul), heart-inscribed (Pro 3:3; Rom 5:5 infused into hearts), mind-engaged (Mat 22:37 — love with all your mind; Joh 15:15 — love as knowledge-sharing), and body-expressed (kiss, embrace, tears, womb-movement across multiple groups). This comprehensive constitutional architecture is consistent with love's function as the programme's organising characteristic.

findings.finding_value: T2 reveals mercy as a whole-person constitutional reality. No single level contains it: mercy originates at the spirit-soul interface, operates on the soul (addressing the nephesh-guilt), engages the heart through the visceral compassion vocabulary (splanchna), engages the mind through the memory-erasure mechanism (Heb 8:12), and operates through the body as both the medium of mercy-seeking (embodied posture) and the mechanism of mercy's effect (blood-atonement). The triadic constitutional movement (Q&A-065): inner disposition → soul-transformation → embodied expression. The key finding reading T2 as a whole is the receiving-before-generating origin structure (Q&A-062): mercy cannot be generated from within the person but must be received from outside and then expressed through the constitutional architecture. Body deposit: none. T5.7: formally closed.

T1's definitional complexity is explained by T2's constitutional complexity — mercy's definition is complex because its constitutional location is complex.

findings.finding_value: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level (chesed as covenantal-soul character), heart-level (Hos 11:8 — "my heart recoils"), and somatic-level (re.chem, splanchnon) are all richly evidenced. The constitutional architecture is bottom-up: the womb and entrails are the originating ground; the soul and heart are the engagement points; the act is the constitutional expression. Four body-part functions are identified: constitutive (womb — the generative image of compassion), expressive (gut — the felt movement), indicative (Synoptic pattern — splanchnizō signals the compassion-event), and mediating (heart in Hos 11:8 — the deliberative locus where compassion and judgment contend). The four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) is uniquely evidenced in this registry — consistently inside-out and bottom-up. T2.8 established no body deposit; T5.7 is formally closed. The constitutional portrait confirms the sb_classification (soul-body interface) and extends it: compassion is the most somatically grounded characteristic in the programme, with its originating logic residing in the body's deepest interior.

The inner-event kind (splanchnizō — the moment of being-moved) operates at the somatic level (T2.6 — the gut as the site of the stirring). The condition-of-object kind (eleeinos — the pitiable state) is the constitutional trigger that activates the somatic-constitutional movement. The externalised-act kind is the constitutional endpoint of T2.10's four-stage movement sequence. T1's definition and T2's constitutional account are co-determining: the characteristic cannot be adequately defined without specifying the constitutional levels at which its four kinds operate.

findings.finding_value: T2's four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) maps directly onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The somatic-arousal stage (T2.6 — gut stirring, splanchnizō) corresponds to T3.1's perceptive-trigger stage (sight activates the somatic response) and T3.4's affect stage (the stirring is the affective movement). The soul-engagement stage (T2.2 — chesed as soul-character) corresponds to T3.8 moral evaluation (the soul assesses the need) and T3.9 conscience (the conscience activates the response). T2 and T3 describe the same movement sequence from two perspectives: T2 maps the constitutional levels; T3 maps the faculties active at each level.

findings.finding_value: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary point of reception (Zec 12:10 — spirit of grace poured out), not the point of generation (grace originates with God — T2.9). The soul level is the site of standing (Rom 5:2 — "this grace in which we stand") and identity (1Cor 15:10 — "by the grace of God I am what I am"). The constitutional movement follows the SD021 four-faces model: divine disposition received at spirit level → relational standing established at soul level → specific capacity gifted → character expressed outward. Heart-location is partially evidenced via eusplanchnos (Eph 4:32 — the tenderheartedness that grace produces, reaching the affective-somatic interface). T2.7 produces a new finding: grace operates bidirectionally through the body-soul interface — soul-to-body (inner posture enacted somatically in prostration, fasting, sackcloth) and body-to-soul (somatic enactment deepening and confirming the inner posture). T2.8 remains open (body deposit question unresolved); T5.7 is left open accordingly. The constitutional origin analysis (T2.9) is the most analytically significant T2 finding: grace does not originate in the human constitutional system at any level — it arrives from outside. This is confirmed at T6 as the structural uniqueness of grace: the only characteristic that is not produced by any other inner-being characteristic.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-018: T2's constitutional levels are carried by specific grammatical forms in T7. The spirit-reception level (T2.1) is carried by the perfect passive form of charitoō (kecharitōmenē — the completed act of b…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional levels are carried by specific grammatical forms in T7. The spirit-reception level (T2.1) is carried by the perfect passive form of charitoō (kecharitōmenē — the completed act of being-made-the-object-of-grace, with continuing state) — the most precise grammatical encoding of a constitutional arrival that has permanently changed the person's standing. The soul-standing level (T2.2) is carried by charis as noun (the inhabited state of favour) and chen as the relational standing-in-favour term. The character-expression level is carried by chen in its conduct/speech register (889-003) and charizō in its human-forgiving mode. T7's NT coinage finding (charitoō invented to carry the standing-in-favour concept) is the lexical evidence that T2's spirit-level reception was conceptually unprecedented — no prior vocabulary could name what happened constitutionally when grace-as-standing arrived.

findings.session_b_note: Soul-level engagement means that covenant commitment calls upon the person's innermost seat of life and personal identity — the nephesh as the living person in their totality. findings.session_b_note: Soul-level location establishes peace as a fundamental condition of the whole inner person's experience — not a cognitive state (mind-level) or a moral quality (character-level) but the experiential condition of the nephesh as living, feeling, wanting creature. The nephesh is the person as they are most fully themselves — most vulnerable, most alive, most in need. Locating shalom in the nephesh means: (1) When peace is present, the whole person flourishes (Psa 55:18 — soul in safety); (2) When peace is absent, the whole person is destitute (Lam 3:17 — soul bereft, happiness forgotten); (3) Peace can be commanded to the soul (Psa 62:5, 131:2) — the soul can be directed toward peace by addressing it as a subject. This last point is analytically significant: the soul is not passive in relation to peace but can be called to orientation. The soul-level location means peace is the deepest personal experiential reality — the condition in which the self-as-person rests or is bereft.

findings.session_b_note: The soul-level evidence (Jer 12:7 — divine nephesh in connection with giving-over) reveals that inner-being giving at its deepest level is connected to the innermost personal experience of attachment and love. God's giving-over proceeds from — and is described in terms of — the beloved relationship at the soul level. "Beloved of my soul" is the language of deepest personal attachment; the giving-over is not cold judicial execution but an act that costs God at the soul level. This reveals that faithfulness-as-giving is not merely a moral or relational act — it touches the innermost identity of the giver. For the human person, the relinquishing giving of Job 1:21 similarly engages the innermost self: the person who blesses God under devastating loss is acting from the deepest constitutional level, not from surface composure. Soul-level location confirms that this characteristic is not merely behavioural — it is constitutionally deep.

findings.finding_value: The constitutional locations where the characteristic operates (T2 — heart, soul/nephesh, spirit, body) and the relational interfaces through which it operates (T4 — God-to-human, human-to-God) reveal a mirroring structure. God's giving proceeds from his leb (heart, Hos 11:8) and his nafshi (soul, Jer 12:7) — the deepest divine inner-being locations are engaged in the God-to-human direction. The human's giving toward God is expressed through the body (back, cheeks, face — Isa 50:6) and from the deepest inner orientation (Job 1:21 — recognition of divine sovereignty). The constitutional depths engaged in both directions are commensurate: God gives from his heart and soul; the human gives from the whole self, expressed bodily. What this pair reveals: the divine-human relational correspondence (DHC dimension, group 872-006) has a constitutional depth structure — the correspondence is not merely behavioural but engages the deepest constitutional levels of both parties. The giving that constitutes the correspondence is heart-to-body deep.

The soul (nephesh) in these verses is the seat of the person's deepest personal experience — it is where the person's most fundamental orientations are located. When David's soul hates (2Sa 5:8), the hatred is not merely a social attitude but an inner-personal reality. Soul-level location makes hatred a characteristic of the person's deepest self — which is why hatred in the heart (Lev 19:17) is treated as a sin even when it never produces an act.
