findings.finding_value: Psa 6:3's soul-level location of dismay reveals that the inner collapse of M01-D reaches to the person's deepest experienced self. It is not merely an emotional event at the surface of the inner life but a shattering of the person at their innermost experiential level. The soul (nefesh as the seat of hunger, desire, and personal life in Hebrew anthropology) being "greatly dismayed" means the characteristic has penetrated to the core of personal existence.

Where soul-level location is evidenced (Psa 6:3 for dismay), it reveals that fear at its most devastating reaches the person's innermost experienced life. The soul-level location confirms the depth of the characteristic's impact — it is not peripheral but central to who the person is.

Est 3:5 (M02-B-VCG-03) shows rage filling the inner being completely — "it takes possession of him." This total-possession description reveals that anger at its most intense is not a localized emotional flare but an experience that engages the entire inner personal life. The soul as the seat of personal experience is saturated and overridden by the anger.

Soul-level location reveals that grief reaches the innermost personal experience — the constitutional level at which the person is most fully themselves. When sorrow is located in the soul (perilupos, ya.gon, de.a.von), it is not a surface emotion but a constitutional state that engages the totality of the person at their core. Jesus's soul-sorrow "even to death" (Mat 26:38 — M03-C-VCG-03) shows that grief at the soul level can threaten life itself — the depth of soul-sorrow is the depth of personal existence. This level of grief is therefore the most personally definitive: what the soul grieves names what the person most deeply loves and has lost.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Soul-level location places exultation at the centre of the person's deepest and most individual inner experience. Nephesh (soul) in the OT consistently names the person in their deepest, most essential individuality — the seat of life, appetite, and longing. Exultation arising from the soul means it is not a superficial or peripheral emotional response but a movement of the person's innermost life toward God. Psa 63:5's "soul satisfied as with richest food" reinforces this: the soul's exultation is its deepest satiation, meeting a need as fundamental as hunger.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Soul-level location confirms that Joy reaches into the deepest personal identity of the individual — the soul (nephesh) is the person in their essential individuality and life-force. When the soul is the seat of gladness (Psa 86:4), this means Joy is not a peripheral emotional surface-event but an inner reality engaging the very core of personhood. Eze 25:6's "malice within your soul" as the source of corrupt joy shows that misdirected joy reaches just as deep — the distortion of Joy affects the soul's fundamental orientation.
**[CHAR-7]** S — Not evidenced; soul-level constitutional location cannot be commented on from this corpus.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Soul-level location in the Gladness corpus confirms that the soul's orientation (seeking, waiting, being satisfied or dissatisfied) determines whether Gladness is genuinely experienced. Lam 3:25's "the soul who seeks him" as the recipient of God's goodness shows Gladness is not available to any inner posture but specifically to the seeking soul. Ecc 6:3's unsatisfied soul is the inverse: the soul that is not oriented toward genuine goodness cannot receive it.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Soul-level location reveals Delight as the characteristic most deeply rooted in the person's core self — not a surface emotional response but the orientation of the essential person toward a treasured object. Mat 12:18's "my soul is well pleased" places divine Delight at the deepest level of God's inner being; Isa 66:3's "their soul delights in their abominations" shows the depth of corruption when Delight is misdirected — the soul itself has been formed around the wrong object. Soul-level location explains why Delight is so formatively powerful: what the soul orients itself toward becomes the organizing centre of the person's inner life.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Soul-level location confirms that Pleasure is genuinely an inner-being characteristic, not merely a surface sensory reaction. Pro 2:10's "pleasant to your soul" positions the inner person's deepest experiential self as the seat of Pleasure in wisdom — when genuine wisdom enters the heart, the soul experiences a qualitative pleasantness. Pro 16:24's "sweetness to the soul" shows that even speech-Pleasure penetrates to the soul level. The soul receives Pleasure from what is genuinely agreeable — this is the characteristic's primary constitutional function.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Psa 119:129's "my soul keeps them" in response to the testimonies being wonderful reveals that Wonder in God's word produces a soul-level obedience response — the wonderfulness of the testimonies motivates the soul to hold to them. This is analytically distinctive: Wonder is the cognitive-perceptive response, and the soul's keeping is the volitional consequence. Psa 139:14's "my soul knows it very well" places the knowing of Wonder at the soul level — an intimate, deeply personal knowing of God's wondrous works.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Soul-level location across six of the seven characteristics confirms that the cluster's positive inner-being states are not peripheral emotional events but engagements of the person's core self. The most analytically significant soul-location is Delight (Char 4): Mat 12:18's "my soul is well pleased" locates divine Delight in the soul; Isa 66:3's "their soul delights in their abominations" locates corrupt delight in the soul — confirming that Delight is the characteristic most deeply rooted in the soul's core orientation. The cluster as a whole reveals that the soul's native positive orientation is multi-faceted: it can exult (Char 1), rejoice (Char 2), be glad (Char 3), delight (Char 4), receive pleasantness (Char 5), and register wonder (Char 6) — these are all genuinely distinct soul-level states, not synonyms.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Soul-level location confirms that CHAR-1 is an experience of the whole inner person, not merely a cognitive judgment or physical reaction. Shame penetrates to the sense of personal identity and worth — it is not a belief about oneself but a felt state of being. The M07-A language of shame as "rottenness in the bones" (Pro 12:4, vc=65525) — an inward destructive force — and the ke.lim.mah language of shame as "carried" (Eze 34:29; 36:6; 39:26) confirm the weight and penetration of shame as a soul-level burden. The person who bears shame bears it as themselves, not merely as a label attached to them.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Soul-level location is evidenced by the felt inner collapse accompanying CHAR-2 (the dismay, confusion, and inner devastation of defeated nations; Zion's cry of utter shame, Jer 9:19, vc=65554). The inner experienced dimension of enforced humiliation operates at soul level, though secondary to the social-bodily primary.

---

**[CHAR-3]** E — Soul-level location is implied in the inner attitude of the dishonorer (the Luk 18:2/4 judge whose lack of regard is "a recognised inner character trait"; Luk 18:9's those who "trust in themselves that they were righteous" — a soul-level self-assessment producing contemptuous treatment of others). The inner disposition of worth-misassignment operates at soul level.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — CHAR-4 operates at soul level through the conscience — the faculty that registers the moral quality of conduct and desires against a standard. 2Cor 4:2's "commend ourselves to everyone's conscience in the sight of God" positions CHAR-4's evaluative operation in the conscience as a soul-level faculty. Phili 3:19's "minds set on earthly things" shows the evaluative faculty (mind/phronēma) as the location of the inversion in VCG-03.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — The soul-level dimension of CHAR-5 is evidenced in the wound to the person's sense of worth. Bartimaeus's beggar-identity (Mar 10:50) is a soul-level condition — his inner self-understanding has been shaped by the accumulated contempt of his social context.

---

**[CHAR-6]** E — CHAR-6 is a soul-level characteristic: the moral conscience and the will are both soul-level faculties, and it is their condition (clean, blameless, free from deliberate wrongdoing) that constitutes CHAR-6. The "integrity of my heart" (Gen 20:5) names the soul-level location explicitly: the heart as the integrating moral centre is the primary location of CHAR-6.

---

**[CLUSTER]** E — All six characteristics locate at the soul level, confirming that M07's domain is the soul in its moral-relational dimensions. The specific soul-level faculty varies: Char 1 operates primarily in the affective soul (felt inner collapse); Char 2 in the social-bodily soul (standing in community); Char 3 in the moral-volitional soul (the dishonorer's inner disposition); Char 4 in the conscience as soul-subset; Char 5 in the worth-sensing faculty; Char 6 in the moral-will and conscience. Soul-level location is unanimous but distributed across different soul-subsets — reflecting M07's multi-dimensional character. Char 1's "I am filled with disgrace" (Job 10:15 — language of inner saturation) and Char 6's "integrity of my heart" (Gen 20:5 — heart as the soul's integrating centre) mark the phenomenological depth at which M07 operates.

---

**[CHAR-1]** S — Since the verse evidence is silent on CHAR-1 being constitutionally located in the soul of its possessor, this prompt cannot be answered from evidence. The significance of the silence remains uncertain within the programme's constitutional framework — the evidence may simply not happen to use nephesh in describing the proud person's inner constitution, without that absence being analytically determinative about CHAR-1's depth of penetration into the soul. What can be noted is that the evidence consistently uses lev (heart) and ruach (spirit) rather than nephesh when naming CHAR-1's constitutional seat.

**[CHAR-2]** S — The evidence is silent on soul-level location. The significance of this absence is uncertain — CHAR-2 may penetrate to soul depth through the will's volitional acts without being explicitly named at that level in this corpus.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Psa 10:3 (vc=33354, M08-C-VCG-01): "boasts of what his own soul desires" — the connection between soul-level desires and the boasting act reveals that CHAR-3 is the public assertion of what the soul privately craves. The soul's desires become the boasting-content; CHAR-3 is the soul's cravings seeking social validation and public acknowledgment. This reveals CHAR-3 as a bridge between inner-soul desire and outer-speech assertion.
**[CHAR-4]** S — The evidence is silent on soul-level location. See T2.2.1.
**[CHAR-5]** S — Silent. See T2.2.1.

**[CLUSTER]** E — CHAR-3's soul-desire connection reveals that the boasting-act is the public assertion of what the soul privately craves — CHAR-3 is the bridge between inner soul-level desire and outer-speech assertion. This insight — that boasting externalises and seeks social validation for the soul's inner cravings — is unique in M08 to CHAR-3 and is not replicated in the other four characteristics' soul-level evidence.

**[CHAR-2]** E — 1Pe1:22 reveals that submission, as obedience to truth, is not merely an outer behavioural disposition but one that reaches and transforms the innermost personal level. The soul's purification suggests the characteristic operates as a sanctifying force within the person's deepest self — not only orienting behaviour but reshaping the person at the level of their most foundational inner experience. The fruit produced (sincere brotherly love from a pure heart) is not a merely rational conclusion but an affective-characterological product of this deep inner transformation, confirming that the soul-level operation is genuine and not merely metaphorical.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Psa34:18's "brokenhearted" reveals that contrition operates at the soul's integrating centre — the heart as the seat of knowing, willing, feeling, and moral awareness is broken. This depth of soul-level operation confirms that contrition is not a surface emotional state but a condition that reaches the inner person's integrating faculty. Isa57:15's "revive the heart of the contrite" confirms that the soul-level operation requires divine reviving — the characteristic at soul-level depth cannot restore itself but requires God's reviving action.

**[CHAR-4]** S — Soul-level location is not explicitly evidenced in §3.C. The characteristic's operation at the inner-person level is implied by its nature as an inner quality, but the soul is not named.
**[CHAR-5]** S — Soul-level location is not explicitly evidenced in §3.D.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The heart-location (Exo35:5/22; 2Ch29:31) reveals that willing-heartedness operates at the soul's integrating centre — not in a single faculty (will alone, or affect alone) but in the heart that integrates knowing, willing, and feeling together. The willing heart is one whose integrating centre is freely-moved toward God — the whole person's inner integration is oriented toward free giving rather than reluctant compliance. The soul-level location confirms that the characteristic is a whole-person orientation rather than a single-faculty operation.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The soul-level connexion via Mat11:29 reveals that humility, while constitutionally located primarily in the heart and will, produces its fruit at the level of the deepest personal experience — the soul finding rest. This suggests the characteristic has a reach that extends beyond its constitutional origin: it is generated in the will/heart, but its effect penetrates to the level of the person's most foundational experience of themselves before God. The rest the soul finds is not merely circumstantial calm but the settlement that comes from no longer needing to assert, protect, or elevate the self — the soul ceases striving when the will has genuinely released the claim to standing.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The four characteristics with explicit soul-level location reveal three distinct patterns of how the soul is engaged. Submission (CHAR-2) evidences the most constitutionally penetrating soul-operation: 1Pe1:22 names the soul as the site of purification through obedience — the characteristic does not merely orient conduct but reshapes the person at their most foundational inner level, producing sincere love from a pure heart as the downstream fruit. Contrition (CHAR-3) engages the soul at its integrating centre — the heart broken (Psa34:18 — nishbar-lev) means the faculty that integrates knowing, willing, and feeling is disrupted; Isa57:15's "revive the heart" confirms that restoration must reach the same depth. Willing-heartedness (CHAR-6) engages the heart as the integrating centre in its positive, freely-moving form — the whole person's inner integration oriented toward free giving. Humility (CHAR-1) reaches the soul as the recipient of the characteristic's fruit (Mat11:29 — rest for your souls), revealing a reach that extends beyond the will and heart in which it originates. Meekness and Gentleness (CHAR-4) and Dignity (CHAR-5) are silent at the soul-location level. Cluster-level pattern: soul-level location confirms that M09 characteristics with Godward or crisis-constitutive orientations (CHAR-2, CHAR-3, CHAR-6) are the deepest-constitutionally reaching; social-ordering characteristics (CHAR-4, CHAR-5) operate without named soul-level location.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — Soul-level location in Eze 18:4/20 (nephesh) reveals that wilful sinning is constitutionally deep — it is not merely a surface behaviour but an act that engages the person's innermost self as the responsible agent. The soul here is the irreducible personal subject: "the soul who sins alone shall die" — the personal self cannot delegate the sinning to social forces, ancestry, or circumstance. This locates wilful sinning within the person's inalienable moral selfhood. The consequence (death) follows the soul-as-agent, not a transferred entity.

**[CHAR-10]** E — Soul-level location (Jam 1:14 — "each person"; Gal 2:13 — Barnabas as individual moral subject) reveals that these mechanisms, despite their composite and mechanism-focused nature, engage real individual moral subjects who bear accountability for their response. The mechanisms are not impersonal forces but pathways through which individual persons are morally engaged and potentially captured. Jam 1:14's "his own desire" — the possessive — confirms: the enticement mechanism is person-specific; the desire that is the hook belongs to the individual person.

**[CHAR-11]** E — Soul-level location (Rom 3:23 — universal moral subjects; Rom 6:17 — heart-enslaved) reveals that sin as universal condition is not a peripheral social or behavioural phenomenon but a structural reality at the level of the person as a moral subject. Every moral subject's self-determination, identity, and accountability before God is shaped by this condition. The condition does not merely constrain behaviour but constitutes the person's standing: Eph 2:1 — "dead" — the soul-level life that the person requires for relation with God is absent due to the condition.

**[CHAR-12]** E — Soul-level location (Joh 8:34 — everyone; 1Jo 3:8 — whoever) reveals that sin's enslaving power does not target only one faculty (e.g. the will) but constitutes the whole person as a slave. The slave-identity is a total-person condition; every faculty operates within the slave-status. The soul-level enslaving means that liberation requires a total-person transformation (new birth — 1Jo 3:9) rather than faculty-specific correction.

**[CHAR-13]** E — Soul-level location (Mic 6:7 — "sin of my soul") reveals that the divine record is not merely a legal external notation but is carried at the level of the person's innermost selfhood. The soul is the level at which the record produces its most personal burden: Psa 51:3 — "my sin is ever before me" — the persistent inner presence of the record is a soul-level experience of the divine accounting. Every moral subject as a soul carries a sin-record; this is what makes the characteristic universal at the soul level.

**[CHAR-14]** E — Soul-level location (Luk 7:47 — her sins; Lev 23:27 — self-affliction; Act 2:38 — every one of you) reveals that forgiveness sought and received is irreducibly personal: every moral subject must make the seeking-movement individually and receive the forgiveness individually. Col 2:13 — "having forgiven us all our trespasses" — the corporate "us" does not eliminate the individual dimension; the characteristic operates at the soul level of each person as a moral subject, not merely as a collective event.

**[CHAR-15]** E — Soul-level location (1Ki 8:47 — heart-turning; Jer 8:14 — "we have sinned") reveals that generational sin, though corporate in origin, engages the individual soul-level moral subject: each person who confesses "we have sinned" participates personally in the corporate condition's acknowledgment. The characteristic is not merely an external legal-status imputed from outside but is genuinely carried at the soul level of each community member who stands within the lineage.

**[CHAR-16]** E — Soul-level location (Luk 5:8 — "sinful man"; Psa 26:9 — soul swept away; Jam 5:20 — soul saved from death) reveals that the sinner-identity is not merely a social label or external imputation but penetrates to the innermost personal identity: the soul is endangered by the identity (Jam 5:20 — heading toward death), is at risk of contagion from others who bear it (Psa 26:9), and spontaneously recognises itself through it (Luk 5:8). The characteristic thus operates at the soul's constitutive level.

**[CHAR-17]** E — Soul-level location (Gen 4:13 — unbearable; 1Sa 25:31 — conscience-stagger; Psa 65:3 — iniquities prevailing) reveals that guilt-as-inner-state engages the whole person as soul-level moral subject. The guilt is not merely cognitive recognition or legal status but a felt condition of the whole inner person — Cain's "I cannot bear it" names the soul's total engagement with the punitive weight of guilt. The soul is the locus where the objective guilt-record (CHAR-13) is experienced subjectively as unbearable weight (CHAR-17).

**[CHAR-18]** E — Soul-level location (Eze 18:20 — "the soul who sins shall die"; Psa 40:12 — "my heart fails me") reveals that iniquity-as-accumulated-crime is not merely a legal abstraction but attaches to the whole person at their deepest level. Eze 18:20's "the soul who sins" uses *nepeš* as the total-person subject of iniquity: the iniquity belongs to the whole person (soul) not merely a faculty. The death-consequence falls on the soul-level entity; the iniquity is the soul's personal crime.

**[CHAR-19]** E — Soul-level location (Mic 6:7 — "sin of my soul"; Psa 51:3 — "ever before me") reveals that transgression-as-deliberate-boundary-crossing is not merely a legal category but a soul-level moral reality that the person inhabits. The "ever before me" (Psa 51:3) names the sustained soul-level experiential weight of the acknowledged transgression. Mic 6:7's "sin of my soul" names the soul (*nepeš*) as the total-person subject of the transgression — the crossing implicates the whole person at their innermost level, not merely a faculty or action.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Soul-level location (Num 15:27 — nefesh as subject) reveals that unintentional sinning is attributed to the whole person as a moral unit — the soul is accountable for what the person did even without deliberate intent. The soul-location confirms that moral accountability is not conditioned on intentionality: the nefesh that sinned unintentionally bears the same kind of moral liability as the nefesh that sinned wilfully, though the prescribed remedy differs in scale. This reveals that in the Levitical framework, moral liability is constitutional — it attaches to the person (nefesh) regardless of the inner quality of the will at the moment of action.

**[CHAR-20]** E — Soul-level location (Eze 18:24 — death for treachery; Pro 11:6 — soul-level lust-captivity) reveals that faithlessness is not merely a legal status or behavioural pattern but attaches to the whole person at their innermost level. Eze 18:24's death-verdict for treachery names the soul as the entity bearing the full weight of the faithlessness-consequence. The lust-captivity of Pro 11:6 names the soul's desiring faculty as captured by the very desire that drove the faithlessness.

**[CHAR-21]** E — Soul-level location (2Pe 2:19 — whole-person enslavement; Jude 10 — whole-person destruction) reveals that perversion-as-inner-inversion is not compartmentalised to one faculty but encompasses the whole inner person. The slavery of 2Pe 2:19 is total: whatever overcomes the person (*anthrōpos*) enslaves the person — the entire person is subject to the corruption's mastery. Jude 10's destruction by instinct similarly encompasses the whole person.

**[CHAR-22]** E — Soul-level location (Luk 16:10 — whole-person character; 1Pe 3:18 — person-category; 2Pe 2:9 — whole-person divine custody) reveals that injustice is not compartmentalised to specific acts but constitutes the person's moral character at the whole-person level. Luk 16:10's scaling from small to large confirms: the inner character of injustice pervades the whole-person across all behavioural contexts, making CHAR-22 a soul-level character trait rather than merely a collection of specific unjust acts.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Mic 7:9's bearing of divine indignation post-confession reveals that genuine confession involves a soul-level acceptance of moral consequence: not just the verbal naming but the accepting of the weight that follows — "I will bear the indignation of the Lord because I have sinned against him." This is the whole personal self engaged with the consequences of the named sin. It distinguishes genuine confession (which includes this acceptance) from hollow confession (VCG-03 — Deu 1:41 — where the words are spoken but the self does not accept the weight of what they imply, immediately proceeding autonomously).

**[CHAR-4]** E — Soul-level location reveals that conscience suppression is not a peripheral cognitive failure but a failure of the whole personal self to receive its own moral reality. The *nefesh* that denies "I have not sinned" (Jer 2:35) is the whole personal subject claiming a false moral standing before God — a total-person moral position, not merely an intellectual error. This is what makes it so serious: the entire inner person has aligned itself against the truth of its own moral condition.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Soul-level location (Eze 18:24; 33:12) reveals that refusal to repent is not a peripheral moral failure but a soul-level condition that determines the person's fundamental standing before God. The life/death language — "for them he shall die" (Eze 18:24) — places refusal to repent at the deepest level of creaturely existence. The soul that persistently sins without turning back is the soul under mortal judgment. This deepens the gravity of the Kings pattern: each king who "did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam" was carrying a soul-level moral condition that, according to Ezekiel's framework, was life-threatening.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Soul-level location (through universality — 1Ki 8:46; Ecc 7:20 — and person-type — Pro 11:31/13:22; Ecc 9:2) reveals that habitual defection is not a peripheral or temporary condition but a characterisation of the person as a moral subject. The sinner-type terms describe a whole-person moral orientation: "the sinner" is what the person *is* at the soul level — their settled moral identity — not merely what they do occasionally. 1Jo 3:6's "no one who keeps on sinning has either seen him or known him" places the habitual sinning at the level of fundamental spiritual knowing — a soul-level epistemic-relational condition.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Soul-level accountability (1Ki 21:22; 2Ki 21:17) reveals that contagious sin does not dissolve the leader's personal moral responsibility into the community — the leader remains fully accountable as a moral subject for what they transmitted. The community's sinning does not reduce the leader's guilt; God explicitly holds the leader accountable for the community's sinning as the leader's own act. This is the reverse of the expectation: if anything, the transmitted sinning amplifies the leader's moral accountability (their sinning affected not just themselves but the whole community).

**[CHAR-8]** E — Soul-level location (via the moral-accountability dimension of pa.sha and the personal forsaking in 2Ch 21:10) reveals that political revolt is not merely a political-social event but a moral act for which the persons involved bear personal accountability. The pa.sha root's moral weight confirms this: revolt is not merely a political-strategic decision but a transgressive act that carries moral consequence before God's covenantal order.

**[CHAR-9]** E — Soul-level location (Mat 12:31; 1Ti 1:13) reveals that sinful speech is not merely a social failing but a soul-level moral act: the person who blasphemes or slanders bears the moral weight of what they have said at the deepest level of their personal accountability before God. Mat 12:31's unforgivable blasphemy makes this most explicit: the soul-level consequence is total and permanent — the person's moral standing before God is permanently altered by this specific form of sinful speech.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Soul-level location (Pro 21:10 — nephesh) reveals that wickedness-as-settled-person-identity reaches the innermost faculty of personal desire and appetite. The soul's desire being directed toward evil (rather than toward God, nourishment, or blessing) means the characteristic has penetrated to the person's deepest seat of longing. This explains why the characteristic is "settled" — it is not a surface preference but a desire-level orientation. The soul's craving in the wicked person is for evil (Pro 21:10) and its craving remains structurally unsatisfied (Pro 13:25 — "the belly of the wicked suffers want") — wickedness as a soul-level disposition generates an insatiable appetite that works against the person's own wellbeing.

**[CHAR-2]** E — While explicit soul-level location is limited (T2.2.1), Jam 1:21 (vc=14368 — VCG-05) reveals that the constitutional inner evil is the primary obstacle to soul-salvation — its removal is the precondition for the word to take root and save the soul. This implies the characteristic operates at the level that determines the soul's ultimate trajectory. The stakes of the characteristic being present or absent are soul-level stakes. The characteristic therefore has soul-level significance even without being explicitly located in the soul faculty — it determines whether the soul is reachable by the saving word.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Pro 13:19 (vc=1687 — VCG-05) reveals that in the most deeply corrupted state, the characteristic has reached the soul's desire faculty and inverted it. The soul that should desire good and find the fulfillment of righteous desire sweet (the first half of the verse) now finds the moral opposite abominable. This soul-level inversion is analytically significant: abomination has not merely occupied the heart and thoughts but has penetrated to the soul's desire-orientation, corrupting the faculty that governs what the person fundamentally wants. Soul-level location reveals the characteristic at its deepest penetration into the inner person.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Isa 66:3 (vc=1633 — VCG-04) reveals that idolatrous abomination has penetrated to the soul's delight faculty — not merely the surface behaviour or the will's momentary choice but the deepest affective centre. The soul that should delight in God (the designed delight-orientation of the nephesh) now delights in abominations. This soul-level penetration explains why the characteristic is so resistant to surface reform: it has reached the level where the person's fundamental affective orientation is attached to the idol. Soul-level location reveals the characteristic as an inner-being corruption that has reached the person's deepest motivational spring.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Isa 66:3 (vc=38204 — VCG-04) reveals that sustained iniquity penetrates to the soul's delight-faculty — the nephesh's capacity for deep affective attachment is redirected toward the iniquitous self-chosen ways. This soul-level penetration shows the characteristic at its deepest development: not merely cognition scheming or will choosing, but the soul itself finding pleasure in what is iniquitous. Soul-level location reveals the characteristic as having corrupted the motivational spring of the person when fully established.

**[CHAR-6]** S — Soul-level location is not evidenced in this corpus (T2.2.1). The inner-being depth the evidence reaches is the will's settled refusal to repent (Rev 16:9/11/21 — VCG-01) and the authority-rejection that precedes blasphemous expression (Jude 8 — VCG-01) — both of which engage the person's deepest motivational centre without using psychē vocabulary.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's soul-level evidence reveals that inner evil penetrates to the deepest motivational spring when fully established. Char 4's soul-level finding (Isa 66:3 — soul delights in abominations) and Char 3's secondary soul-level finding (Pro 13:19 — fool's soul finds departure from evil abominable) both show the characteristic reaching the soul's desire-faculty and attaching to or inverting it. Char 1's soul-level evidence (Pro 21:10 — "the soul of the wicked desires evil") confirms that settled wickedness penetrates to the desire-orientation level. At cluster scope: soul-level penetration in M10b characteristics is the marker of the characteristic's deepest establishment — when evil reaches the soul's delight and desire faculties, it has achieved constitutional depth that makes surface-level address insufficient.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The evidence suggests the ritual defilement-state is not primarily a soul-origin phenomenon but it impinges on soul-level experience through its consequences — exclusion, guilt-awakening, grief. The soul-level impact is secondary to the body-mechanism of acquisition: the condition arrives through the body and is felt by the soul. This reveals the characteristic's place as a bridge condition — it is constitutionally bodily in origin but cannot remain only bodily; it activates conscience, will, and affect, drawing the whole inner person into its management and resolution.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Soul-level location reveals the characteristic as operating in the domain of the person's most active inner life — their willing, desiring, evaluating, and feeling. The soul is where the person engages with their world and with God; the presence of the defilement-state at the soul level means that the primary instruments of engagement (will, desire, conscience, heart) are compromised. This makes the characteristic a condition that distorts the inner-person's most active and engaged dimensions — not a passive background condition but one that actively misdirects the person's inner dynamics.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The soul-level location reveals the characteristic as rooted in the community's deepest volitional and desiderative life — the corporate "heart" that has turned away from God (Eze 23:7 — "all the idols of everyone after whom she lusted"; Eze 20:31 — "you defile yourselves with all your idols to this day") generates the contamination that extends to the sacred environment. The soul-level generating force is communal — not only individual will but the collective will of the house of Israel, the city, the leadership — revealing the characteristic as operating at the level of shared inner orientation.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The soul-level location reveals that the characteristic's domination extends from the spirit level downward through the soul-level faculties to the body. The spirit inhabits and controls at the spirit level; the soul's faculties are suppressed (will overridden, speech and hearing suppressed); the body is subject to violent external control (convulsions — Mar 1:26, Luk 9:42; breaking chains — Luk 8:29). This downward cascade reveals the constitutional comprehensiveness of the characteristic: it reaches and dominates every layer of the human person.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The four soul-level findings together reveal the cluster's inner topology. Characteristic 1 shows the soul's faculties as the site where the bodily condition registers and is managed — the soul receives from the body. Characteristic 2 shows the soul's faculties as the originating site where defilement is generated (desire, will) and then deepens inward (toward spirit) and outward (toward body). Characteristic 3 shows the corporate soul as the generating force whose defilement extends outward to the sacred environment — the community's shared inner orientation determines the condition of land, sanctuary, and name. Characteristic 4 shows the soul's faculties as the domain where the spirit-level invasion manifests its control — the will is overridden (Luk 8:29), speech and hearing suppressed (Mar 9:25). The cluster's soul-level map confirms that defilement always engages the soul, but the direction of engagement reverses: bodily-to-soul (Char 1), soul-to-spirit (Char 2), soul-to-environment (Char 3), and spirit-to-soul (Char 4).

findings.finding_value: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level (chesed as covenantal-soul character), heart-level (Hos 11:8 — "my heart recoils"), and somatic-level (re.chem, splanchnon) are all richly evidenced. The constitutional architecture is bottom-up: the womb and entrails are the originating ground; the soul and heart are the engagement points; the act is the constitutional expression. Four body-part functions are identified: constitutive (womb — the generative image of compassion), expressive (gut — the felt movement), indicative (Synoptic pattern — splanchnizō signals the compassion-event), and mediating (heart in Hos 11:8 — the deliberative locus where compassion and judgment contend). The four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) is uniquely evidenced in this registry — consistently inside-out and bottom-up. T2.8 established no body deposit; T5.7 is formally closed. The constitutional portrait confirms the sb_classification (soul-body interface) and extends it: compassion is the most somatically grounded characteristic in the programme, with its originating logic residing in the body's deepest interior.

findings.finding_value: T1's four-kind structure (character quality, inner event, condition of object, externalised act) maps precisely onto T2's constitutional levels. The character-quality kind (ra.chum — dispositional compassionate character) operates at the soul level (T2.2 — chesed as soul-character). The inner-event kind (splanchnizō — the moment of being-moved) operates at the somatic level (T2.6 — the gut as the site of the stirring). The condition-of-object kind (eleeinos — the pitiable state) is the constitutional trigger that activates the somatic-constitutional movement. The externalised-act kind is the constitutional endpoint of T2.10's four-stage movement sequence. T1's definition and T2's constitutional account are co-determining: the characteristic cannot be adequately defined without specifying the constitutional levels at which its four kinds operate.

findings.finding_value: T2's four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) maps directly onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The somatic-arousal stage (T2.6 — gut stirring, splanchnizō) corresponds to T3.1's perceptive-trigger stage (sight activates the somatic response) and T3.4's affect stage (the stirring is the affective movement). The soul-engagement stage (T2.2 — chesed as soul-character) corresponds to T3.8 moral evaluation (the soul assesses the need) and T3.9 conscience (the conscience activates the response). The volitional-engagement stage (T2.3 — heart-locus as deliberative site) corresponds to T3.6 volition (the will directs the action). The outward-action stage corresponds to T3.7 agency. T2 and T3 describe the same movement sequence from two perspectives: T2 maps the constitutional levels; T3 maps the faculties active at each level.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-002: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary…
findings.finding_value: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary point of reception (Zec 12:10 — spirit of grace poured out), not the point of generation (grace originates with God — T2.9). The soul level is the site of standing (Rom 5:2 — "this grace in which we stand") and identity (1Cor 15:10 — "by the grace of God I am what I am"). The constitutional movement follows the SD021 four-faces model: divine disposition received at spirit level → relational standing established at soul level → specific capacity gifted → character expressed outward. Heart-location is partially evidenced via eusplanchnos (Eph 4:32 — the tenderheartedness that grace produces, reaching the affective-somatic interface). T2.7 produces a new finding: grace operates bidirectionally through the body-soul interface — soul-to-body (inner posture enacted somatically in prostration, fasting, sackcloth) and body-to-soul (somatic enactment deepening and confirming the inner posture). T2.8 remains open (body deposit question unresolved); T5.7 is left open accordingly. The constitutional origin analysis (T2.9) is the most analytically significant T2 finding: grace does not originate in the human constitutional system at any level — it arrives from outside. This is confirmed at T6 as the structural uniqueness of grace: the only characteristic that is not produced by any other inner-being characteristic.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-008: T1's four-kind structure (disposition, standing, capacity, character quality) maps onto T2's constitutional levels. The divine-disposition kind operates at the level of grace's origin (T2.9 — God's ow…
findings.finding_value: T1's four-kind structure (disposition, standing, capacity, character quality) maps onto T2's constitutional levels. The divine-disposition kind operates at the level of grace's origin (T2.9 — God's own disposition; not a human constitutional level). The standing kind operates at the soul level (T2.2 — Rom 5:2 "this grace in which we stand"). The capacity kind operates at the spirit-soul interface — the specific enabling for specific tasks (2Cor 12:9) is received at the deepest level and expressed through specific faculties. The character-quality kind operates at the soul-to-body level (T2.7 — gracious conduct and speech expressing the received inner character outward). T1's constitutional movement finding (SD021 four-faces sequence) is the longitudinal form of T2's spatial map: T2 identifies the constitutional levels; T1 identifies the movement between them.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-014: T2's constitutional movement (spirit reception → soul standing → capacity → character expression) maps onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The spirit-reception stage (T2.1) corresponds to T3.1 (per…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional movement (spirit reception → soul standing → capacity → character expression) maps onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The spirit-reception stage (T2.1) corresponds to T3.1 (perception — grace enabling the inner sight and hearing that receives it). The soul-standing stage (T2.2) corresponds to T3.9 (conscience — grace as the condition within which conscience can operate without destruction) and T3.8 (moral evaluation — the standing produces the clarity of moral self-assessment). The capacity-gifting stage (T2.1 — spirit level) corresponds to T3.7 (agency — capacity given constitutes agency for the task). The character-expression stage (T2.7 — outward through body-soul) corresponds to T3.10 (conscientiousness — the integrated moral-action expression of received grace-character). T2 maps the constitutional space; T3 maps the faculties active at each spatial level; the two tiers describe the same movement from orthogonal perspectives.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-018: T2's constitutional levels are carried by specific grammatical forms in T7. The spirit-reception level (T2.1) is carried by the perfect passive form of charitoō (kecharitōmenē — the completed act of b…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional levels are carried by specific grammatical forms in T7. The spirit-reception level (T2.1) is carried by the perfect passive form of charitoō (kecharitōmenē — the completed act of being-made-the-object-of-grace, with continuing state) — the most precise grammatical encoding of a constitutional arrival that has permanently changed the person's standing. The soul-standing level (T2.2) is carried by charis as noun (the inhabited state of favour) and chen as the relational standing-in-favour term. The character-expression level is carried by chen in its conduct/speech register (889-003) and charizō in its human-forgiving mode. T7's NT coinage finding (charitoō invented to carry the standing-in-favour concept) is the lexical evidence that T2's spirit-level reception was conceptually unprecedented — no prior vocabulary could name what happened constitutionally when grace-as-standing arrived.

findings.session_b_note:

findings.session_b_note:
Yes — the most theologically and emotionally dense verse in the data explicitly locates compassion in the heart. Hos 11:8: "My heart recoils within me; my compassion grows warm and tender." The Hebrew lev (heart) is the anatomical and constitutional reference. The heart recoiling is the precursor to the ni.chum (compassionate warmth) that follows — the heart's movement is what produces the compassion-stirring.

Joel 2:13 deploys the heart in a connected context: "rend your hearts and not your garments. Return to the LORD your God, for he is gracious and merciful (rachum ve-channum)." The divine compassion-character is the ground for a call to heart-rending (SD-029). Compassion here is both a divine heart-quality and the basis for a demand upon the human heart.

The heart location is implied by moral-evaluative and conscience-engaging operations, but not stated explicitly in the vocabulary.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-067-002: T2 as a whole reveals that goodness has a comprehensive multi-level constitutional presence — from Spirit-level origin through soul-orientation, heart-engagement, and mind-evaluative functions to outw…
findings.finding_value: T2 as a whole reveals that goodness has a comprehensive multi-level constitutional presence — from Spirit-level origin through soul-orientation, heart-engagement, and mind-evaluative functions to outward expression — but with a marked asymmetry in evidence quality. Spirit-level (Q&A-037-039), soul-level (Q&A-040-041), and heart-level (Q&A-043-044) are all substantively evidenced. Mind-level is partially evidenced through cognitive dimensions. Body-level is thin — the gladness-of-heart compound (tov-lev) and the taste-and-see perceptual metaphor are the somatic markers, but no constitutional body deposit is evidenced (T2.8 silent). The most structurally significant T2 finding is the six-step constitutional movement (Q&A-064): Spirit-level origin → soul reorientation → heart engagement → volitional alignment → agentive resolve → outward expression. This movement is top-down and outward, with no evidenced reversal from body to inner being. Goodness is constitutionally deep but does not leave a somatic deposit.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-067-014: T2 identified the constitutional movement of goodness from Spirit-level through soul and heart to outward expression (six-step sequence, Q&A-064). T3 names the faculty operations at each level: Spirit…
findings.finding_value: T2 identified the constitutional movement of goodness from Spirit-level through soul and heart to outward expression (six-step sequence, Q&A-064). T3 names the faculty operations at each level: Spirit-level corresponds to Spirit-production (T2.1) → T3.6 volitional reconstitution (the Spirit enables the resolve for good); soul-level seeking (T2.2) → T3.1 perceptual encounter (tasting and seeing); heart-level knowing and gladness (T2.3) → T3.3 memory and T3.4 affect; evaluative-cognitive function (T2.4) → T3.2 cognition and T3.8 moral evaluation; outward expression (T2.10) → T3.7 agency and T3.11 relational capacity. The two tiers together reveal that the constitutional movement is not an abstract structural description but a faculty-by-faculty account of how goodness moves through the person. Each constitutional level corresponds to specific faculty engagements. The T3 faculty map gives content to the T2 constitutional architecture.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-103-002: Love is the programme's most constitutionally comprehensive characteristic — it occupies all five constitutional levels simultaneously: spirit-sourced (implied via Spirit-as-agent, Rom 5:5, Gal 5:22),…
findings.finding_value: Love is the programme's most constitutionally comprehensive characteristic — it occupies all five constitutional levels simultaneously: spirit-sourced (implied via Spirit-as-agent, Rom 5:5, Gal 5:22), soul-located (Song 5:6 — soul failing at beloved's absence; Mat 22:37 — love with all your soul; Joh 15:13 — laying down the soul), heart-inscribed (Pro 3:3; Rom 5:5 infused into hearts), mind-engaged (Mat 22:37 — love with all your mind; Joh 15:15 — love as knowledge-sharing), and body-expressed (kiss, embrace, tears, womb-movement across multiple groups). The constitutional movement pattern is consistently downward: Spirit origin → heart reception → soul experience → body expression. Love's heart-inscription (Pro 3:3) is the closest evidence to a constitutional deposit — the metaphorical writing of chesed into the heart's deepest register produces a lasting dispositional quality (the chasid person-type). The primary finding: love is not confined to any single constitutional level but operates across all levels in an integrated movement from deepest to most outward. This comprehensive constitutional architecture is consistent with love's function as the programme's organising characteristic.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-103-001: Love's definition and its constitutional location are mutually illuminating. The definition identifies love as disposition + act + condition operating through directed attachment toward an object. The…
findings.finding_value: Love's definition and its constitutional location are mutually illuminating. The definition identifies love as disposition + act + condition operating through directed attachment toward an object. The constitutional mapping shows where this triple operation is located: the disposition is heart-inscribed (Pro 3:3) and spirit-sourced (implied via Rom 5:5), stable across constitutional levels; the act is will-engaged (Mat 22:37 — commanded) and soul-mobilised (Joh 15:13 — soul laid down); the condition of being-loved is received at the heart level (Rom 5:5 — poured in) and experienced at the soul level (Zep 3:17 — quieting). The constitutional movement pattern (Spirit → heart → soul → body) maps directly onto the definition's three registers: the deepest dispositional origin (spirit/heart) grounds the stable orientation; the soul-level is where love is experienced as feeling; the body-level is where act and condition become visible. Together: the constitutional location analysis confirms that love's definition is not a surface account but a constitutional claim — love operates at every depth of the inner person, which is precisely what the 'whole heart, soul, and mind' commandment (Mat 22:37) requires.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-103-007: Love's constitutional architecture and its faculty engagement are structurally aligned. The heart's engagement with love (Q&A-044, Q&A-045) corresponds to the heart's known integrating function across…
findings.finding_value: Love's constitutional architecture and its faculty engagement are structurally aligned. The heart's engagement with love (Q&A-044, Q&A-045) corresponds to the heart's known integrating function across the programme: the heart is the location of knowing (Joh 15:15 — knowledge-disclosure as love's act), willing (Mat 22:37 — love commanded), feeling (Song 5:2 — heart awake in love-awareness), and moral awareness (Pro 3:3 — chesed inscribed). Each of the heart's functions corresponds to a faculty: knowing → reason and memory; willing → will; feeling → emotion; moral awareness → moral sensitivity. The soul-level constitutional location (Song 5:6 — soul failing at beloved's absence) corresponds to the identity and relational capacity faculties: the soul whose vitality is partly constituted by the love-object is the soul whose identity (T3.10) and relational capacity (T3.11) are most deeply invested in love. The Spirit-sourced origin of love (implied) corresponds to the deep pre-reflective faculty level (L-005 — love below conscious attention): the Spirit's infusion produces love at a depth below ordinary faculty-awareness. Constitutional depth and faculty depth are directly correlated.

findings.finding_value: The formation process in T5 works precisely through the constitutional locations identified in T2. Spirit infusion (Rom 5:5) enters at the deepest level (Spirit → heart), establishing love's constitutional ground. Obedience-pathway purifies the soul (1Pe 1:22) — the soul-level constitutional location is the target of formation's clearing work. Training in the community (Tit 2:4) operates at the body-habit level — forming love through repeated communal acts that imprint the body's relational patterns. The heart-inscription of chesed (Pro 3:3) is the formation's goal-state: love sufficiently formed that it is constitutionally inscribed, no longer needing to be generated afresh for each act. The eschatological trajectory (perfect love, direct knowledge, pleasures forevermore) describes the perfection of the constitutional architecture: all levels operating without obstruction, permanently, toward the proper object. Constitutional location is thus not a static description but a dynamic formation target: each level can be more or less formed in love, and the formation process addresses each level in sequence.

findings.finding_value: The evidential foundation supports and grounds the constitutional location claims. Each constitutional level identified in T2 has specific vocabulary evidence in T7: Spirit-level origin — Gal 5:22 (fruit of the Spirit), Rom 5:5 (poured into hearts through the Spirit); soul-level — Song 5:6 (soul failing), Mat 22:37 (all your soul), Joh 15:13 (lay down the soul); heart-level — Pro 3:3 (heart inscription), Rom 5:5 (into our hearts); mind-level — Mat 22:37 (all your mind), Joh 15:15 (knowledge disclosure); body-level — kiss/embrace/tears/inner-organ-movement vocabulary across multiple groups. The lexical range of the primary terms (Q&A-122 — chesed, racham, agapē, dod, phileō) corresponds precisely to the five constitutional levels: each term carries a different constitutional register as its primary habitat. The evidential foundation thus not only confirms the constitutional claims but shows them to be lexically grounded in the vocabulary's own structure.

findings.session_b_note: The heart vocabulary appears in heart/R183's shared anchor at Col 3:12 ("compassionate hearts" — *splanchna oiktirmou*, literally "bowels of compassion") and Luk 1:78 ("tender mercy... from the heart of our God" — *dia splanchna eleous*). The *splanchna* (bowels/heart) vocabulary links mercy to the inner affective centre. Heart/R183 shares Col 3:12 as an anchor. However, the data does not have a direct verse saying "mercy is in the heart" — the link is through the splanchna-vocabulary which bridges bowel and heart imagery. OBS-111-069, OBS-111-025.

findings.finding_value: T2 reveals mercy as a whole-person constitutional reality. No single level contains it: mercy originates at the spirit-soul interface, operates on the soul (addressing the nephesh-guilt), engages the heart through the visceral compassion vocabulary (splanchna), engages the mind through the memory-erasure mechanism (Heb 8:12), and operates through the body as both the medium of mercy-seeking (embodied posture) and the mechanism of mercy's effect (blood-atonement). The triadic constitutional movement (Q&A-065): inner disposition → soul-transformation → embodied expression. The key finding reading T2 as a whole is the receiving-before-generating origin structure (Q&A-062): mercy cannot be generated from within the person but must be received from outside and then expressed through the constitutional architecture. Body deposit: none. T5.7: formally closed.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-030-002: T2 establishes that contrition operates at the deepest constitutional level (spirit as primary locus) with secondary engagement at heart, soul, and body. The constitutional portrait is comprehensive: …
findings.finding_value: T2 establishes that contrition operates at the deepest constitutional level (spirit as primary locus) with secondary engagement at heart, soul, and body. The constitutional portrait is comprehensive: spirit broken at the innermost level, heart broken at the moral-evaluative level, nephesh crushed at the whole-self level, and bones as the somatic expression of the inner breaking. What T2 reveals as a whole is the embodied depth of contrition — it is not a disembodied inner experience but a constitutional event that traverses all levels of the person. The bidirectional constitutional movement (downward through divine confrontation, upward through reviving) is the structural frame within which contrition functions: it reaches the bottom and creates the conditions for movement back upward. The T2.8 finding (no body deposit) means contrition does not leave a permanent somatic trace — it is a passing constitutional event, not a permanent constitutional mark.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-030-014: The constitutional tier (T2) establishes that contrition's primary loci are spirit and heart; the faculty tier (T3) shows that the faculties most engaged by contrition are precisely those associated w…
findings.finding_value: The constitutional tier (T2) establishes that contrition's primary loci are spirit and heart; the faculty tier (T3) shows that the faculties most engaged by contrition are precisely those associated with these loci. The spirit-level location (T2) corresponds to the deepest faculty engagements: conscience (at the spirit-heart interface), moral evaluation (heart-based), and perception of divine address (spirit-receptive). The heart-level location (T2) corresponds to the affective and volitional faculty engagements. Together T2 and T3 reveal that contrition's constitutional depth (reaching spirit and heart as primary loci) determines the depth of its faculty engagement: because it reaches the innermost constitutional levels, it engages the innermost faculties most profoundly.

The constitutional co-location (contrition and heart-characteristics both operating at the heart/spirit level) directly produces the co-occurrence signal (T6.1). The structural connection between contrition and R183 heart is not merely topical (the same word appears in the same verses) but constitutional — they both operate in the same inner-being space. T2's constitutional map and T6's co-occurrence data are mutually confirming.

findings.finding_value: The constitutional tier (T2) establishes spirit and heart as primary loci, bones as somatic expression; the evidential tier (T7) shows that these same loci are explicitly named in the primary anchor verses. The spirit/heart pairing in the verse evidence (Psa 34:18, Psa 51:17, Isa 57:15) and the bone imagery in Psa 51:8 are the exegetical ground for T2's constitutional account. T7 provides the textual evidence base from which T2 draws its constitutional conclusions. The two tiers are evidence-to-interpretation: T7 is the verse evidence; T2 is the constitutional interpretation of that evidence. Isa 57:15 as the primary anchor verse (T7) is also the verse that most completely names the constitutional event (T2): "contrite and lowly spirit... revive the spirit... revive the heart."

findings.finding_value: T2 reveals fellowship's constitutional location is distributed across levels according to its mode: existential mode (soul/nephesh level — Ecc 9:4), companionship mode (heart level — Psa 119:63, Jer 13:23), desire-driven mode (desire-faculty — 2Pe 1:4), suffering mode (somatic — Pro 20:30, Isa 53:5). The body-deposit question (T2.8) remains open — the wound-mark as a persisting joining-trace is the nearest evidence, but its programme-relevance is uncertain.

The heart is the one explicitly named locus — Mat 18:35 ("from your heart") names the heart as the required depth of genuine forgiveness-giving. The cognition-faculty (Jer 31:34 — "remember no more"; "they shall know me") is the most clearly evidenced constitutional engagement alongside the heart. The somatic compassion faculty (splagchnizomai — Mat 18:27) is the named somatic-affective origin-point of the forgiving act. Spirit and soul levels are inferred from the guilt-forgiveness structural relationship and the Spirit's mediating role (Mar 3:29, Joh 20:23) rather than explicitly named. The body-deposit question is data-silent (T2.8); T5.7 closes formally. The constitutional movement is explicit (Luk 7:47 — guilt-bearing → forgiveness received → love generated; Jer 31:34 — forgiveness → direct knowledge of God). T2's key finding: the constitutional structure of forgiveness is act-centred, not state-centred — it is a constitutional event (the moment of release) that produces constitutional consequences (love, reverence, direct access).

The somatic compassion origin-point (T2.5 — splagchnizomai) is the constitutional expression of the volitional-release act (T1.4.1 — the act must be chosen). Definition and constitutional location are co-determining: the mode of forgiveness determines which constitutional level is engaged.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-002: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level …
findings.finding_value: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level (chesed as covenantal-soul character), heart-level (Hos 11:8 — "my heart recoils"), and somatic-level (re.chem, splanchnon) are all richly evidenced. The constitutional architecture is bottom-up: the womb and entrails are the originating ground; the soul and heart are the engagement points; the act is the constitutional expression. Four body-part functions are identified: constitutive (womb — the generative image of compassion), expressive (gut — the felt movement), indicative (Synoptic pattern — splanchnizō signals the compassion-event), and mediating (heart in Hos 11:8 — the deliberative locus where compassion and judgment contend). The four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) is uniquely evidenced in this registry — consistently inside-out and bottom-up. T2.8 established no body deposit; T5.7 is formally closed. The constitutional portrait confirms the sb_classification (soul-body interface) and extends it: compassion is the most somatically grounded characteristic in the programme, with its originating logic residing in the body's deepest interior.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-014: T2's four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) maps directly onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The somatic-arousal s…
findings.finding_value: T2's four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) maps directly onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The somatic-arousal stage (T2.6 — gut stirring, splanchnizō) corresponds to T3.1's perceptive-trigger stage (sight activates the somatic response) and T3.4's affect stage (the stirring is the affective movement). The soul-engagement stage (T2.2 — chesed as soul-character) corresponds to T3.8 moral evaluation (the soul assesses the need) and T3.9 conscience (the conscience activates the response). The volitional-engagement stage (T2.3 — heart-locus as deliberative site) corresponds to T3.6 volition (the will directs the action). The outward-action stage corresponds to T3.7 agency. T2 and T3 describe the same movement sequence from two perspectives: T2 maps the constitutional levels; T3 maps the faculties active at each level.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-002: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary…
findings.finding_value: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary point of reception (Zec 12:10 — spirit of grace poured out), not the point of generation (grace originates with God — T2.9). The soul level is the site of standing (Rom 5:2 — "this grace in which we stand") and identity (1Cor 15:10 — "by the grace of God I am what I am"). The constitutional movement follows the SD021 four-faces model: divine disposition received at spirit level → relational standing established at soul level → specific capacity gifted → character expressed outward. Heart-location is partially evidenced via eusplanchnos (Eph 4:32 — the tenderheartedness that grace produces, reaching the affective-somatic interface). T2.7 produces a new finding: grace operates bidirectionally through the body-soul interface — soul-to-body (inner posture enacted somatically in prostration, fasting, sackcloth) and body-to-soul (somatic enactment deepening and confirming the inner posture). T2.8 remains open (body deposit question unresolved); T5.7 is left open accordingly. The constitutional origin analysis (T2.9) is the most analytically significant T2 finding: grace does not originate in the human constitutional system at any level — it arrives from outside. This is confirmed at T6 as the structural uniqueness of grace: the only characteristic that is not produced by any other inner-being characteristic.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-034-002: T2 as a whole reveals that covenant operates across the full constitutional range of the inner person with no single exclusive location. The heart is the primary site (Q&A-044), the mind is co-located…
findings.finding_value: T2 as a whole reveals that covenant operates across the full constitutional range of the inner person with no single exclusive location. The heart is the primary site (Q&A-044), the mind is co-located (Q&A-047), the soul gives totality of engagement (Q&A-041), the mouth is the expressive-constitutive organ (Q&A-050), and the body participates through blood and circumcision (Q&A-053). The single most structurally significant T2 finding is the constitutional movement shift from OT to NT covenantal mode: OT covenant moves outer→inner→outer; new covenant moves inner→inner→outer (Q&A-066). This movement-shift is the constitutional-level expression of the Sinai-to-new-covenant transformation — it places the origin of covenant faithfulness at the level of God's own interior action within the person rather than the person's compliance with external demand. T2 confirms that covenant is constitutively somatic as well as inner — it cannot be reduced to a purely invisible spiritual reality because it is enacted, sealed, and transmitted through bodily acts and substances.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-034-008: T1 defines covenant as constitutively composite — operating in four modes (disposition, act, quality, condition). T2 reveals that each mode has a distinct constitutional location: the disposition-mode…
findings.finding_value: T1 defines covenant as constitutively composite — operating in four modes (disposition, act, quality, condition). T2 reveals that each mode has a distinct constitutional location: the disposition-mode (God's relational commitment) operates at the deepest constitutional level (spirit/relational), the act-mode (human entry) is enacted through somatic performance (oath = mouth, cutting = body, blood), the quality-mode (moral faithfulness) resides in heart and character, and the condition-mode (new covenant transformation) is inscribed on heart and mind by divine action. The T1 × T2 synthesis: covenant's four modes correspond to four distinct constitutional locations and operations, and the new covenant's primary contribution is shifting the constitutional origin from external to internal — the condition-mode is not entered by human act but produced by God's inner writing. The composite mode structure (T1) is constitutionally grounded across the full inner person (T2).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-034-014: T2 locates covenant in the constitutional organs (heart, mind, soul, mouth, body). T3 reveals which inner faculties operate within and through those locations. The T2 × T3 synthesis: the constitutiona…
findings.finding_value: T2 locates covenant in the constitutional organs (heart, mind, soul, mouth, body). T3 reveals which inner faculties operate within and through those locations. The T2 × T3 synthesis: the constitutional location (T2) and the faculty operation (T3) are not separate realities but different analytical views of the same inner-being reality. The heart (T2) is where the integrating functions of willing, knowing, moral evaluation, and affect operate (T3.6 volition, T3.2 cognition, T3.8 moral evaluation, T3.4 affect). The mind (T2) is where cognition (T3.2) and memory (T3.3) operate. The soul-totality (T2) corresponds to the conscientiousness and relational capacity (T3.10, T3.11) that engage the whole person. The constitutional location and the faculty operation are two descriptions of the same inner reality: location is where the faculty is housed; faculty is what the location does. The new covenant writes on the heart/mind (T2) and thereby transforms cognition toward knowing God (T3.2) — the constitutional location is the mechanism for the faculty transformation.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-034-017: T2 establishes that the heart is the primary constitutional location of covenant, with body (blood, circumcision) as the somatic deposit. T6 reveals that covenant's deepest structural relationship is …
findings.finding_value: T2 establishes that the heart is the primary constitutional location of covenant, with body (blood, circumcision) as the somatic deposit. T6 reveals that covenant's deepest structural relationship is with faithfulness (lexically co-generated through the emunah-amanah root — Q&A-157). The T2 × T6 synthesis: the constitutional deposit of covenant (bodily circumcision, generational word-transmission — Q&A-059) is the constitutional mechanism through which covenant's structural relationships are transmitted to new participants. Covenant's bond with faithfulness (T6) is transmitted across generations through the bodily sign (circumcision) and the spoken word (Isa 59:21) — the somatic deposit (T2) is the mechanism of structural relationship preservation (T6). The body carries the covenant's relational structure forward through time.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-099-002: T2 reveals a clear and important constitutional asymmetry for kindness: the heart is its named constitutional site (Pro 3:3 — explicitly inscribed there), while the soul, mind, and body are not named …
findings.finding_value: T2 reveals a clear and important constitutional asymmetry for kindness: the heart is its named constitutional site (Pro 3:3 — explicitly inscribed there), while the soul, mind, and body are not named locations — the soul appears as beneficiary, the mind as instrument, the body as the direction of outward expression. This asymmetry is not a gap in the evidence but a structural feature: kindness is a heart-level characteristic. Its constitutional movement is a coherent downward-outward trajectory — Spirit-formation produces the heart-level disposition, which in turn generates deliberate relational acts. The origin of kindness is triple: divinely initiated (in God's own character), Spirit-mediated (Gal 5:22), and humanly formed (the chasid's character accumulated through covenantal faithfulness). These three are not competing explanations but sequential layers of the same formation process. T2's most significant intra-tier finding: the body-deposit question (T2.8) closes formally — no deposit evidence exists — which confirms that kindness does not transmit generationally through biological means but through covenantal-formative means (Exo 20:6 — "to a thousand generations" = covenantal, not biological).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-008: What kindness is (T1) and where it resides constitutionally (T2) are tightly integrated. T1's working definition — stable inner disposition of loyal goodwill, constituted by faithfulness/compassion/fo…
findings.finding_value: What kindness is (T1) and where it resides constitutionally (T2) are tightly integrated. T1's working definition — stable inner disposition of loyal goodwill, constituted by faithfulness/compassion/forgiveness — is realised at the heart level (T2). The heart is not merely the storage location of kindness but the site where its constituent elements are inscribed as character (Pro 3:3 — "write them on the tablet of your heart"). The T2 constitutional movement pattern (Spirit-formation → heart-inscription → relational disposition → deliberate acts) maps directly onto T1's three modes (Spirit formation / deliberate act / dispositional orientation) — the movement pattern is the mechanism by which the T1 disposition comes into being. The T1 finding that kindness is composite (faithfulness + justice + compassion + forgiveness) is structurally consistent with T2's finding that it is a heart-level characteristic: the heart in Scripture is precisely the site where complex moral orientation is integrated — not a single emotion but the whole-person covenantal direction.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-014: T2's finding that kindness is located in the heart and moves outward through a constitutional trajectory (Spirit → heart → disposition → acts) connects structurally with T3's finding that kindness eng…
findings.finding_value: T2's finding that kindness is located in the heart and moves outward through a constitutional trajectory (Spirit → heart → disposition → acts) connects structurally with T3's finding that kindness engages the heart's integrating faculties — volition, agency, conscientiousness, moral evaluation, relational capacity, and conscience. The heart in T2 is not merely a location label but the integrating site where all these faculties converge (T2.3.2 — Q&A-045). The constitutional movement pattern in T2 (downward-outward from Spirit to acts) is powered by the multi-faculty engagement that T3 documents: the Spirit-formation produces the heart-level disposition, but the heart exercises volition (choosing to be kind), agency (enacting kindness), and conscientiousness (sustaining kindness reliably over time) to move the disposition into action. The T3 finding that kindness engages taste as the primary perceptive faculty (1Pet 2:3 — "tasted that the Lord is good") is the perceptive entry point for the T2 constitutional movement: the person first tastes divine kindness, then the Spirit forms it in the heart, then the heart's faculties exercise it outward. The two tiers together describe a complete inner-to-outer movement with both location (T2) and mechanism (T3) identified.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-017: T2's heart-location finding and T6's structural relationship findings together reveal something about kindness that neither tier alone states: the heart is not only the constitutional site of kindness…
findings.finding_value: T2's heart-location finding and T6's structural relationship findings together reveal something about kindness that neither tier alone states: the heart is not only the constitutional site of kindness but the site where kindness's constituent adjacent characteristics (faithfulness, justice, compassion, forgiveness) are also inscribed. Pro 3:3 — "write them on the tablet of your heart" — names the heart as the inscription site for chesed and emet (faithfulness/truth) together, suggesting that the T6 co-occurrence pattern (kindness + faithfulness as the most persistent pair) has a constitutional basis: they are co-inscribed. This means T6's network of adjacent characteristics is not merely relational or contextual co-occurrence but a constitutional clustering: they share the same constitutional site. The T2 constitutional movement outward (heart → acts) and T6's causal network (kindness → reproduced kindness → sustained covenant relationships) trace the same movement from two angles — T2 names the direction, T6 names the mechanism of propagation.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-018: T2's constitutional location findings (heart as primary site; no body deposit; Spirit as origin) are grounded in and confirmed by T7's lexical evidence. The explicit heart-inscription language of Pro …
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional location findings (heart as primary site; no body deposit; Spirit as origin) are grounded in and confirmed by T7's lexical evidence. The explicit heart-inscription language of Pro 3:3 — the most important T2 finding — is a direct chesed text: the term being inscribed is chesed itself. T7's finding about chesed's semantic range (goodness/kindness/faithfulness as a unified concept) reinforces T2's origin finding: the triple origin structure (divine → Spirit → formed) is exactly what the chesed vocabulary expects — it names God's own inner attribute (Exo 34:6 — abounding in steadfast love), which the Spirit reproduces in the believer, which is then formed through practice and encounter. The T7 LXX finding (chesed → eleos/mercy) has a constitutional implication: the LXX translation emphasises the compassion/affective dimension of chesed over its faithfulness/constitutional dimension — which may explain why the NT Greek kindness vocabulary (chrēstos/chrēstotēs) emphasises quality of character rather than covenant obligation. The two tiers together: lexical depth (T7) explains why constitutional location (T2) lands at the heart — chesed is precisely a heart-level characteristic because it names the covenantal faithfulness that is inscribed in the inner person.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-117-001: T1 names peace's essence as integrative wholeness; T2 confirms this is constitutionally comprehensive — the soul (T2.2), heart (T2.3), mind (T2.4), hidden person (T2.5), and body (T2.6) are all in sco…
findings.finding_value: T1 names peace's essence as integrative wholeness; T2 confirms this is constitutionally comprehensive — the soul (T2.2), heart (T2.3), mind (T2.4), hidden person (T2.5), and body (T2.6) are all in scope. The essence and the constitutional address are co-extensive: the integrative wholeness of shalom is not located in one faculty but distributed across all constitutional levels simultaneously. The soul is the most explicitly named OT location (Lam 3:17); the heart is the most comprehensive (engaging all four heart functions); the mind is the most causally explicit (Isa 26:3 — direction of mind → perfect peace). Together: peace is not a faculty-specific characteristic but a whole-person condition whose essence (integrative wholeness) matches its constitutional scope (spirit-soul-heart-mind-body).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-117-007: T2 maps the constitutional territory; T3 maps the faculties engaged. The synthesis: every constitutional level (T2) corresponds to faculty engagement (T3) in the peace data. Soul-level (T2.2) ↔ Affect…
