Soul-level (T2.2) ↔ Affect (T3.4) — the soul's peace is primarily affective (Lam 3:17, Psa 62:5); Heart-level (T2.3) ↔ Moral evaluation + Volition + Conscience (T3.8/6/9) — the heart engages the moral-volitional-conscience cluster; Mind-level (T2.4) ↔ Cognition (T3.2) — the mind's directed orientation; Body-level (T2.6) ↔ Agency (T3.7) — the body's actions express inner peace; Hidden-person (T2.5) ↔ Conscientiousness (T3.10) — the hidden person of the heart is the site of the most integrated response. The constitutional and faculty maps are not independent but interlocking descriptions of the same whole-person reality.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-117-008: T2 establishes the constitutional location of peace; T4 establishes the relational directions through which peace moves into and out of those locations. The synthesis: God gives peace (T4.1 → T2) by a…
findings.finding_value: T2 establishes the constitutional location of peace; T4 establishes the relational directions through which peace moves into and out of those locations. The synthesis: God gives peace (T4.1 → T2) by addressing the constitutional locations directly — the Aaronic blessing (Num 6:26) addresses the whole person; Joh 14:27 ("let not your hearts be troubled") addresses the heart specifically; Phili 4:7 ("peace will guard your hearts and minds") names both heart and mind as the guarded locations. The human receives peace (T4.4) through the same constitutional locations — the receptive soul (Psa 131:2, T2.2) and the directed mind (Isa 26:3, T2.4) are the reception points. The relational and constitutional analyses converge: peace moves through relational channels (T4) into constitutional locations (T2).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-117-010: T2's body evidence (Psa 38:3 — no sha.lom in bones because of sin) connects directly to T6's finding that reconciliation constitutes relational peace (Col 1:20, Eph 2:14) — the same sha.lom that is ab…
findings.finding_value: T2's body evidence (Psa 38:3 — no sha.lom in bones because of sin) connects directly to T6's finding that reconciliation constitutes relational peace (Col 1:20, Eph 2:14) — the same sha.lom that is absent from bones when sin is present is the sha.lom that reconciliation restores. The SHA.L root (T6.4.2) names completeness — and Psa 38:3's use of sha.lom for somatic soundness is directly rooted in this: sha.lom IS somatic completeness, sha.lom IS relational completeness, sha.lom IS covenantal completeness — one root, all dimensions. The constitutional and structural analyses confirm the same root-level truth from different angles.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-060-002: T2 as a whole reveals that this characteristic has no single constitutional home — it operates across the full spirit-soul-body register through different modes. Spirit is the location in two modes: a…
findings.finding_value: T2 as a whole reveals that this characteristic has no single constitutional home — it operates across the full spirit-soul-body register through different modes. Spirit is the location in two modes: as the object of endowing giving (Neh 9:20) and as the faculty transformed eschatologically (Isa 61:3). Soul (nephesh/nafshi) appears in divine self-reference in the giving-over context (Jer 12:7). Heart (leb) is the faculty where the giving decision is made (Hos 11:8). Hidden inner parts (tukhoth) are the target of wisdom-giving (Job 38:36). Rahamim (visceral compassion) is the inner-being quality that determines giving direction. Body appears as the expressive medium of self-giving (Isa 50:6) and as constituted by breath-giving (Isa 42:5). No constitutional body deposit is confirmed. Three movement patterns — constitutive (spirit→mind), expressive (inner→body), transformative (outside-in→inside renewed→inside-out) — show the characteristic is constitutionally dynamic. What T2 reveals as a whole: this characteristic operates at every constitutional level not because it is superficially distributed but because giving as an inner-being act can reach the spirit (endowing), the heart (deciding), the soul (attaching), the hidden inner parts (forming), and the body (expressing and constituting). It is constitutionally pervasive.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-001: The definition of faithfulness-as-giving (T1 — disposition-in-action, triadic architecture) aligns precisely with the constitutional movement patterns (T2 — constitutive, expressive, transformative). …
findings.finding_value: The definition of faithfulness-as-giving (T1 — disposition-in-action, triadic architecture) aligns precisely with the constitutional movement patterns (T2 — constitutive, expressive, transformative). The disposition-in-action structure is not abstractly defined: it is enacted through specific constitutional pathways. The constitutive mode (Spirit→mind) corresponds to the endowing operational mode (T1.4). The expressive mode (inner→body) corresponds to the self-giving mode (T1.4). The transformative mode (outside-in→inside renewed→inside-out) corresponds to the eschatological operational mode (T1.4). What neither T1 nor T2 states alone: the definition of this characteristic is constitutionally embedded — each definitional mode maps onto a distinct constitutional movement pattern. The characteristic is not defined independently of its constitutional location; it is what it is through how it moves across the spirit-soul-body structure.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-007: The constitutional locations (T2 — spirit, heart, soul, hidden inner parts, body) and the inner faculties (T3 — perception, cognition, memory, affect, volition, agency, moral evaluation, relational ca…
findings.finding_value: The constitutional locations (T2 — spirit, heart, soul, hidden inner parts, body) and the inner faculties (T3 — perception, cognition, memory, affect, volition, agency, moral evaluation, relational capacity) are not independent — they occupy the same inner-being territory from two different analytical perspectives. T2 asks where; T3 asks which faculty. Reading them together reveals: the heart (leb, T2.3) is the location of affect-volition integration (T3.4, T3.6) — where compassion (affect) determines giving (volitional act). The hidden inner parts (tukhoth, T2.5) are the constitutional home of the cognitive-formative faculty (T3.2 — the wisdom that is given there). The body (T2.6-7) is the somatic site of agentive expression (T3.7 — agency expresses through the body). The spirit (ruach, T2.1) is both the object of constitutive giving and the faculty whose depletion the eschatological giving addresses — connecting to the agency and relational capacity faculties that cannot operate from a faint spirit. What this pair reveals: constitutional location and faculty engagement are two descriptions of the same inner-being event. The characteristic is located constitutionally precisely where the relevant faculties operate.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-008: The constitutional locations where the characteristic operates (T2 — heart, soul/nephesh, spirit, body) and the relational interfaces through which it operates (T4 — God-to-human, human-to-God) reveal…
findings.finding_value: The constitutional locations where the characteristic operates (T2 — heart, soul/nephesh, spirit, body) and the relational interfaces through which it operates (T4 — God-to-human, human-to-God) reveal a mirroring structure. God's giving proceeds from his leb (heart, Hos 11:8) and his nafshi (soul, Jer 12:7) — the deepest divine inner-being locations are engaged in the God-to-human direction. The human's giving toward God is expressed through the body (back, cheeks, face — Isa 50:6) and from the deepest inner orientation (Job 1:21 — recognition of divine sovereignty). The constitutional depths engaged in both directions are commensurate: God gives from his heart and soul; the human gives from the whole self, expressed bodily. What this pair reveals: the divine-human relational correspondence (DHC dimension, group 872-006) has a constitutional depth structure — the correspondence is not merely behavioural but engages the deepest constitutional levels of both parties. The giving that constitutes the correspondence is heart-to-body deep.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-010: The constitutional pervasiveness of the characteristic (T2 — it reaches every constitutional level through distinct modes) and the hub position it occupies in the structural landscape (T6 — connecting…
findings.finding_value: The constitutional pervasiveness of the characteristic (T2 — it reaches every constitutional level through distinct modes) and the hub position it occupies in the structural landscape (T6 — connecting multiple adjacent characteristics across all five dimensions) are causally related. The characteristic can occupy the hub position precisely because it is constitutionally pervasive: it is not anchored to a single constitutional level that would limit its relational scope. A purely spirit-level characteristic would only relate structurally to other spirit-level characteristics; a purely somatic characteristic would only relate somatically. This characteristic, moving across all levels, can relate structurally to characteristics at every level. What this pair reveals: constitutional breadth enables structural breadth. The connecting-hub position is a structural consequence of the constitutional polymorphism of giving as an inner-being act.

**[A1 — God Righteousness]** Indirectly — kardiognōstēs (heart-knower, Act 1:24; 15:8, in VSG M26-A1-002) names God as the one whose righteousness penetrates to the heart. God's righteous judgment reaches the heart — "God's righteous judgment" (Rom 2:5) confronts the "hard and impenitent heart" (same verse, VSG 3207-001). The heart is the location God's righteousness addresses in the human, not the location it inhabits in God.

**[A2 — Human Righteousness]** Yes — explicitly. VSG M26-A2-005 is "law written on the heart" — the internalisation of God's righteous standard within the heart of the person. "I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts" (Jer 31:33) and the new covenant parallel (Heb 8:10; 10:16). The heart is the constitutional location where righteousness as an inner principle is inscribed. Additionally, the hunger for righteousness (Mat 5:6, VSG M26-A2-006) is an appetite of the whole inner person, centered in the heart as the integrating organ of the inner life.

**[B — Moral Uprightness]** Yes — VSG 1211-001 contains the uprightness-of-heart language: yo.sher is used in contexts that describe an upright heart as distinct from upright conduct. The inner orientation of straightness has the heart as its constitutional seat. "The upright in heart" is a recognisable category in the Psalms and wisdom literature.

**[C — Justification]** Justification as an act is not explicitly located in the heart in the verse evidence. The result of justification (new standing before God) is not described as a heart-state. Silence.

**[D — Avenging Justice]** Indirectly — Rom 2:5 (VSG 3207-001) names the "hard and impenitent heart" as the heart condition that "stores up wrath" — the heart's condition is what makes divine avenging justice necessary. The inner determination to entrust vengeance to God (6841-002: "leave it to the wrath of God") is a heart-level resolution of will.

**[E — Condemnation]** Yes — "not to condemn you, for I said before that you are in our hearts, to die together and to live together" (2Cor 7:3, VSG 738-001). The condemnation-discourse reaches the heart — the heart as the location of the deep bond that Paul distinguishes from condemnation. Self-condemnation (autokatakritos) operates through the conscience — which is heart-adjacent in biblical anthropology. 1Jo 3:20–21 (not in this cluster's verses directly, but known): "whenever our heart condemns us, God is greater than our heart" — the heart as the location of self-condemnation. This reference is from known context, not from named verse in this cluster — recording as marginal rather than primary evidence.

**[F — Moral Reckoning]** Yes — "you thought that I was one like yourself. But now I rebuke you and lay the charge before you" (Psa 50:21, in the a.rakh group) — the reckoning act is associated with what is laid before God. More directly: "God tests the minds and hearts" (Psa 7:9, echoed in VSG M26-A2-013) — the heart is one of the organs that the reckoning faculty of God penetrates in its judicial assessment. The human reckoning (logizomai) operates in the mind, but the object of assessment is the heart-state.

**[G — Structural Opposites]** Yes — explicitly. "Hard and impenitent heart" (Rom 2:5, VSG 3207-001) — wickedness in G is constitutionally located in the heart as the governing organ of the inner person's orientation. The hard heart is the internal locus of sustained wickedness.

**[CLUSTER — T2.3]** E. The heart is the primary constitutional location of righteousness in M26. The pattern across sub-groups is: righteousness as written law (A2-005, heart as the location of inscribed righteous standard), as inner orientation of straightness (B, heart as the seat of uprightness disposition), and as the site of moral hardness when righteousness is absent (G, heart as the locus of wickedness). The heart is where righteousness is received (A2), oriented (B), and resisted (G). God's righteousness addresses the heart in its judgment (A1-002, F). The cluster's primary constitutional home is the heart.

---

**Cross-cluster finding 2 — Heart as primary constitutional location across all sub-groups**
Every sub-group that has a constitutional location in the cluster locates it primarily in the heart: the inscribed law (A2-005), the inner orientation of uprightness (B, 1211-001), the hard and impenitent heart of wickedness (G, Rom 2:5), the heart that God's righteous judgment confronts (A1/F). The heart is the primary constitutional site of M26 in all its modes.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Implicitly rather than explicitly. The heart (lev/lebab) is not named by that term in the 83-verse corpus, but the heart's allegiance-forming function is what drives the characteristic. Eze 23:7 (VCG-02): "she defiled herself with all the idols of everyone after whom she lusted" — lust/longing as the heart-level allegiance-direction toward idols. Eze 22:3 (VCG-02): "a city that makes idols to defile herself" — the corporate will's purposeful idolatrous devotion is a heart-allegiance reality. The Ezekiel oracle corpus throughout VCG-02 characterises the community as having turned their heart-allegiance toward idols — the defilement is the consequence of this allegiance disorder.

**[CHAR-4]** S — The 21-verse corpus does not explicitly name the heart (kardia) as the site of the characteristic. The characteristic's external-agency mechanism bypasses the heart's allegiance and desire functions — it is not generated from the heart's interior but from an external spiritual invasion.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's heart-location pattern is 1 explicit E : 1 implicit E : 2 S — Characteristic 2 explicitly names the heart (Rom 1:24: "lusts of their hearts"; Mat 23:27: "within full of... uncleanness"); Characteristic 3 names it implicitly through allegiance-language (Eze 23:7: lust toward idols; Eze 20:7/18/30/31: corporate heart directed toward idols); Characteristics 1 and 4 are silent on heart-location. The pattern reveals that the heart's allegiance-forming function is specifically engaged when the defilement's mechanism is desire-and-allegiance oriented (Chars 2, 3) and not engaged when the mechanism is bodily-external (Char 1) or externally-spiritual-invasive (Char 4). The heart is the defilement cluster's allegiance-diagnostic: its presence reveals that the defilement is fundamentally about where the person's or community's ultimate loyalty is directed. Its absence (Chars 1, 4) confirms that those characteristics do not arise from a disorder of ultimate loyalty.

findings.session_b_note:
The heart-location of forgiveness engages **all four aspects of the heart's integrating function**, not one exclusively:

- **Willing:** The primary engagement. Forgiveness is "from the heart" as a volitional act — the will releases the claim. The command structure (Mat 18:35; Luk 17:3-4) confirms that the will is the primary faculty addressed.
- **Moral awareness:** The heart must first register the wrong done (moral awareness of the legitimate claim) before it can genuinely release it. Forgiveness presupposes moral seriousness — the registry description states: "the release of a legitimate claim" — the legitimacy must be known before it can be waived.
- **Feeling:** The affective dimension is present in the background — the withheld grievance is an emotional state; the release of it is an inner-being movement that has affective texture. The "poisoning" of the inner life of the withholder (OBS-064-001) names an affective consequence.
- **Knowing:** More indirect. The cognitive component appears most clearly in the new covenant's "remember no more" (Jer 31:34) — the heart's knowing-and-remembering function is what forgiveness addresses at the cognitive level.

The primary integration point is **volitional-moral**: the heart knows the claim is legitimate (moral awareness) and chooses to release it (will). The affective and cognitive dimensions participate but do not lead.

findings.session_b_note:
Hos 11:8 engages all four aspects of the heart's integrating function simultaneously, which is what makes it the most complex single verse in the compassion data:

**Knowing:** The heart "recoils" — this is a form of inner-being recognition. God knows what Ephraim is and what will happen to him; the heart's recoiling is the response to that knowledge. Compassion at the heart level involves knowing the condition of the other and being moved by what one knows.

**Willing:** The verse narrates a divine inner deliberation: the heart's recoiling precedes and overrides the judgment that would have been executed. Compassion engages the heart's willing function — it contends with competing volitional orientations (judgment, withdrawal) and wins. The ni.chum is not the suppression of judgment but the outcome of an inner-heart contest (Pass 2 FRAMEWORK SIGNAL on ni.chum).

**Feeling:** The warmth of ni.chum — "my compassion grows warm and tender" — is the felt quality of the heart's compassion. Temperature language (warm) names the affective quality at the heart level.

**Moral awareness:** The deliberation in Hos 11:8 turns on a moral question — whether to execute judgment or withhold it. Compassion at the heart level is morally engaged: it is not pre-moral sentimentality but the moral determination that mercy is more constitutive of who God is than judgment.

findings.session_b_note:
The heart in Hebrew anthropology integrates knowing, willing, and feeling — it is the seat of the whole person's interior life. Contrition at the heart level engages all three aspects, but the verse evidence emphasises different aspects in different groups:

- **Knowing**: Psa 51:17 — the heart that is broken and contrite *knows* its condition. Psa 51 as a whole is the psalmist's articulate self-knowledge ("I know my transgressions"). The contrite heart is the heart that has arrived at honest self-understanding.
- **Willing**: Psa 38:8 — "the tumult of my heart" suggests inner volitional agitation — the heart is not at rest, it is in inner conflict. The contrite heart is not indifferent; it is engaged by what it knows. The voluntary offering of the broken heart (Psa 51:17 — "the sacrifices of God") suggests the will is involved in bringing the broken state before God.
- **Feeling**: The anguish mode (Psa 38:8 — groaning from the tumult of the heart) engages the heart's affective function. The broken heart is not merely a cognitive condition but an experienced one.

*New finding: contrition engages the heart's knowing, willing, and feeling functions — it is a fully integrating inner-being condition, not narrowly cognitive or narrowly affective. The knowing dimension (self-recognition of moral condition) is the initiating function; the willing dimension (bringing the broken heart as offering) is the directional function; the feeling dimension (anguish, groaning) is the experiential expression.*

findings.session_b_note:
Where fellowship operates at the heart level, it engages primarily:

**Moral evaluation and discernment:** The decision about whom to be in fellowship with is a heart-level discernment — distinguishing righteousness from lawlessness (2Cor 6:14), choosing fear-of-God companions (Psa 119:63), recognising moral complicity (Mat 23:30).

**Innermost moral purification:** Pro 20:30 explicitly names the innermost parts as the site of fellowship-through-wounding's purifying work. This is the heart's deepest moral sanctuary — the characteristic reaches to the core.

**Volitional commitment:** The covenantal companionship of Mal 2:14 is a heart-level commitment — faithfulness to the companion-wife is the expression of a deep inner volitional loyalty.

findings.session_b_note: Heart-location reveals that goodness engages multiple integrating functions of the heart simultaneously. (1) Knowing — Jos 23:14: the heart's cognitive function receives and holds the knowledge of God's good covenantal word. (2) Feeling — Est 5:9: the heart is the site of the affective gladness-state (tov-lev). (3) Moral awareness — Eze 36:31: the heart's moral self-assessment capacity is activated when not-goodness is recognised; memory and loathing are heart-operations. The heart as the integrating centre of the inner being engages goodness at all three levels — knowing, feeling, and moral awareness — which reflects the breadth of the tov vocabulary itself. (OBS-067-OBS-034, OBS-067-OBS-035, OBS-067-OBS-041)

findings.session_b_note: Heart-location reveals love's engagement with all four of the heart's functions: (a) **knowing** — the heart that loves also knows (Joh 15:15 — friendship constituted by knowledge-disclosure, OBS-103-052; Hos 6:6 — God desires knowledge of God alongside chesed, OBS-103-091); (b) **willing** — the heart is the seat of intention, and love is commanded at the heart level (Mat 22:37; 1Ki 8:18 — 'it was in your heart to build'); (c) **feeling** — Song 5:2 ('my heart was awake') — the heart's affective persistence in love; (d) **moral awareness** — Pro 3:3 (chesed and faithfulness written on the heart as moral character). findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-103-002: Love is the programme's most constitutionally comprehensive characteristic — it occupies all five constitutional levels simultaneously: spirit-sourced (implied via Spirit-as-agent, Rom 5:5, Gal 5:22),…
findings.finding_value: Love is the programme's most constitutionally comprehensive characteristic — it occupies all five constitutional levels simultaneously: spirit-sourced (implied via Spirit-as-agent, Rom 5:5, Gal 5:22), soul-located (Song 5:6 — soul failing at beloved's absence; Mat 22:37 — love with all your soul; Joh 15:13 — laying down the soul), heart-inscribed (Pro 3:3; Rom 5:5 infused into hearts), mind-engaged (Mat 22:37 — love with all your mind; Joh 15:15 — love as knowledge-sharing), and body-expressed (kiss, embrace, tears, womb-movement across multiple groups). The constitutional movement pattern is consistently downward: Spirit origin → heart reception → soul experience → body expression. Love's heart-inscription (Pro 3:3) is the closest evidence to a constitutional deposit — the metaphorical writing of chesed into the heart's deepest register produces a lasting dispositional quality (the chasid person-type). The primary finding: love is not confined to any single constitutional level but operates across all levels in an integrated movement from deepest to most outward. This comprehensive constitutional architecture is consistent with love's function as the programme's organising characteristic.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-103-007: Love's constitutional architecture and its faculty engagement are structurally aligned. The heart's engagement with love (Q&A-044, Q&A-045) corresponds to the heart's known integrating function across…
findings.finding_value: Love's constitutional architecture and its faculty engagement are structurally aligned. The heart's engagement with love (Q&A-044, Q&A-045) corresponds to the heart's known integrating function across the programme: the heart is the location of knowing (Joh 15:15 — knowledge-disclosure as love's act), willing (Mat 22:37 — love commanded), feeling (Song 5:2 — heart awake in love-awareness), and moral awareness (Pro 3:3 — chesed inscribed). Each of the heart's functions corresponds to a faculty: knowing → reason and memory; willing → will; feeling → emotion; moral awareness → moral sensitivity. The soul-level constitutional location (Song 5:6 — soul failing at beloved's absence) corresponds to the identity and relational capacity faculties: the soul whose vitality is partly constituted by the love-object is the soul whose identity (T3.10) and relational capacity (T3.11) are most deeply invested in love. The Spirit-sourced origin of love (implied) corresponds to the deep pre-reflective faculty level (L-005 — love below conscious attention): the Spirit's infusion produces love at a depth below ordinary faculty-awareness. Constitutional depth and faculty depth are directly correlated.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-002: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level …
findings.finding_value: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level (chesed as covenantal-soul character), heart-level (Hos 11:8 — "my heart recoils"), and somatic-level (re.chem, splanchnon) are all richly evidenced. The constitutional architecture is bottom-up: the womb and entrails are the originating ground; the soul and heart are the engagement points; the act is the constitutional expression. Four body-part functions are identified: constitutive (womb — the generative image of compassion), expressive (gut — the felt movement), indicative (Synoptic pattern — splanchnizō signals the compassion-event), and mediating (heart in Hos 11:8 — the deliberative locus where compassion and judgment contend). The four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) is uniquely evidenced in this registry — consistently inside-out and bottom-up. T2.8 established no body deposit; T5.7 is formally closed. The constitutional portrait confirms the sb_classification (soul-body interface) and extends it: compassion is the most somatically grounded characteristic in the programme, with its originating logic residing in the body's deepest interior.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-014: T2's four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) maps directly onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The somatic-arousal s…
findings.finding_value: T2's four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) maps directly onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The somatic-arousal stage (T2.6 — gut stirring, splanchnizō) corresponds to T3.1's perceptive-trigger stage (sight activates the somatic response) and T3.4's affect stage (the stirring is the affective movement). The soul-engagement stage (T2.2 — chesed as soul-character) corresponds to T3.8 moral evaluation (the soul assesses the need) and T3.9 conscience (the conscience activates the response). The volitional-engagement stage (T2.3 — heart-locus as deliberative site) corresponds to T3.6 volition (the will directs the action). The outward-action stage corresponds to T3.7 agency. T2 and T3 describe the same movement sequence from two perspectives: T2 maps the constitutional levels; T3 maps the faculties active at each level.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-002: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary…
findings.finding_value: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary point of reception (Zec 12:10 — spirit of grace poured out), not the point of generation (grace originates with God — T2.9). The soul level is the site of standing (Rom 5:2 — "this grace in which we stand") and identity (1Cor 15:10 — "by the grace of God I am what I am"). The constitutional movement follows the SD021 four-faces model: divine disposition received at spirit level → relational standing established at soul level → specific capacity gifted → character expressed outward. Heart-location is partially evidenced via eusplanchnos (Eph 4:32 — the tenderheartedness that grace produces, reaching the affective-somatic interface). T2.7 produces a new finding: grace operates bidirectionally through the body-soul interface — soul-to-body (inner posture enacted somatically in prostration, fasting, sackcloth) and body-to-soul (somatic enactment deepening and confirming the inner posture). T2.8 remains open (body deposit question unresolved); T5.7 is left open accordingly. The constitutional origin analysis (T2.9) is the most analytically significant T2 finding: grace does not originate in the human constitutional system at any level — it arrives from outside. This is confirmed at T6 as the structural uniqueness of grace: the only characteristic that is not produced by any other inner-being characteristic.

findings.session_b_note: The heart-location evidence reveals that covenant engages all four aspects of the heart's integrating function: (1) Willing: "with all his heart" covenant-making (2Ki 23:3) — the heart as the seat of volitional commitment. (2) Knowing: "they shall all know me" follows from God writing on the heart (Jer 31:34) — heart-inscription produces knowing. The heart is the seat of covenantal knowing of God. (3) Moral awareness: Psa 78:37 — "their heart was not steadfast... they were not faithful" — covenant faithlessness is a heart-integrity failure; the heart as moral evaluation centre assesses covenant obligation. (4) Feeling/affective: Psa 25:14 direction — "the friendship of the Lord is for those who fear him, and he makes known to them his covenant" — the relational-affective dimension of knowing God's covenant is a heart reality. All four aspects of the heart's integrating function are engaged: covenant writes on the knowing heart, calls the willing heart, evaluates the moral-faithful heart, and is experienced in the affective-relational heart.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-099-002: T2 reveals a clear and important constitutional asymmetry for kindness: the heart is its named constitutional site (Pro 3:3 — explicitly inscribed there), while the soul, mind, and body are not named …
findings.finding_value: T2 reveals a clear and important constitutional asymmetry for kindness: the heart is its named constitutional site (Pro 3:3 — explicitly inscribed there), while the soul, mind, and body are not named locations — the soul appears as beneficiary, the mind as instrument, the body as the direction of outward expression. This asymmetry is not a gap in the evidence but a structural feature: kindness is a heart-level characteristic. Its constitutional movement is a coherent downward-outward trajectory — Spirit-formation produces the heart-level disposition, which in turn generates deliberate relational acts. The origin of kindness is triple: divinely initiated (in God's own character), Spirit-mediated (Gal 5:22), and humanly formed (the chasid's character accumulated through covenantal faithfulness). These three are not competing explanations but sequential layers of the same formation process. T2's most significant intra-tier finding: the body-deposit question (T2.8) closes formally — no deposit evidence exists — which confirms that kindness does not transmit generationally through biological means but through covenantal-formative means (Exo 20:6 — "to a thousand generations" = covenantal, not biological).

findings.finding_value: T2's finding that kindness is located in the heart and moves outward through a constitutional trajectory (Spirit → heart → disposition → acts) connects structurally with T3's finding that kindness engages the heart's integrating faculties — volition, agency, conscientiousness, moral evaluation, relational capacity, and conscience. The heart in T2 is not merely a location label but the integrating site where all these faculties converge (T2.3.2 — Q&A-045). The constitutional movement pattern in T2 (downward-outward from Spirit to acts) is powered by the multi-faculty engagement that T3 documents: the Spirit-formation produces the heart-level disposition, but the heart exercises volition (choosing to be kind), agency (enacting kindness), and conscientiousness (sustaining kindness reliably over time) to move the disposition into action. The T3 finding that kindness engages taste as the primary perceptive faculty (1Pet 2:3 — "tasted that the Lord is good") is the perceptive entry point for the T2 constitutional movement: the person first tastes divine kindness, then the Spirit forms it in the heart, then the heart's faculties exercise it outward. The two tiers together describe a complete inner-to-outer movement with both location (T2) and mechanism (T3) identified.

findings.session_b_note: The heart-location of peace engages all four of the heart's integrating functions: (1) Knowing (cognitive): Rom 8:6 ("to set the mind/heart on the Spirit is life and peace") — the heart's cognitive orientation toward God produces peace; the directed heart knows what produces peace; (2) Willing (volitional): Psa 120:7 ("I am for peace") — the heart's volitional orientation toward peace as identity; Isa 30:15 ("but you were unwilling") — the refusal of peace is a heart-act of will; (3) Feeling (affective): Joh 14:27 ("let not your hearts be troubled") — the troubled heart as the experiential opposite of peace; the heart as the seat of distress or rest; (4) Moral awareness (conscience): Deu 29:19 — the heart's stubbornness as the moral condition that generates false shalom; Psa 28:3 — evil in the heart contrasted with speaking peace. The heart is the integrating centre of peace's constitutional address: peace must be received, held, directed, and expressed from the heart. The heart-peace connection is the most comprehensive single-location engagement in the data.

findings.session_b_note: Heart-location in Hos 11:8 engages the feeling/willing aspect of the heart's integrating function: "My heart recoils" (haphak libbi) — the heart turns, moves, is overturned in compassionate response. This is an affective-volitional movement: the heart feels the pull of compassion and the will is determined by it, overriding the logic of deserved judgement. The heart's integrating function here is the resolution of internal tension: judicial logic (give over) versus compassionate orientation (cannot give up) — the heart is the location where this conflict is resolved. The Neh 9:8 reference ("heart faithful") engages moral awareness: Abraham's heart is assessed as faithful — the heart as the seat of moral character is the ground of the covenantal giving. Together: the heart engages both the affective-volitional dimension (Hos 11:8) and the moral-character dimension (Neh 9:8) in connection with this characteristic.

The heart in Lev 19:17 is the integrating centre where intention, planning, and relational orientation converge. The prohibition "not in your heart" is precise: hatred at the heart level is the problem, even before any act. This means hatred is culpable as an inner state, not only as a behaviour. Pro 26:24 shows the heart as the hiding place — hatred can be active in the heart while the lips present false peace, revealing that the heart is where the real disposition lives, prior to and independent of speech or action. The heart's hatred is the primary moral problem; the act is its secondary expression.

**[CLUSTER]** E. The heart-location of righteousness reveals that it is not primarily a behavioral category but an inner-being reality. "Law written on the heart" (Jer 31:33, VSG M26-A2-005) shows that righteousness is inscribed at the integrating center of the person — the place where knowing, willing, and feeling converge. This means righteousness shapes not just what a person does but who they are at the core. The heart-location also reveals the depth of the resistance: the hard heart (Rom 2:5) is not resistant at the surface level of behavior but at the integrating center. The location in the heart explains both the transformative depth of received righteousness (it shapes the person from the inside) and the seriousness of its rejection (it is the heart that refuses, not merely the will or the behavior).
Pro 16:23: wisdom in the heart engages the heart's governing function — the heart produces judicious speech and governs the whole person's output. M15-A engages the heart as the governing centre.

findings.finding_value: M01-A's heart-location engages the heart's willing and moral-awareness functions primarily. Deu 5:29 (heart disposed to fear — volitional); Jer 5:24 (people do not say in their hearts "let us fear" — the heart as the seat of moral self-direction, the decision to fear or not to fear); Jer 32:40 (fear implanted in the heart "preventing them from turning away" — the heart as the seat of covenant faithfulness). The heart's knowing function is also engaged: Psa 86:11 (heart integration required for genuine reverence — the heart must be unified in its knowing to produce authentic fear).

M01-B's heart-location engages the heart's feeling function primarily: Psa 27:3 (the heart "yields to dread" — the affective registration of threat); Neh 2:2 (fear "seated in the heart, visible in his countenance" — the heart as the source of the emotional experience that then appears on the face); 1Sa 28:5 ("Saul's visual perception of the enemy army triggers an inner collapse of courage, with the emotion immediately registered in his heart" — the heart as the affective registration center).

M01-D's heart-location engages the knowing and feeling functions together. Dan 5:10 (dismay "originates in the inner life of thought and then visibly destabilizes the body" — the knowing function disrupted); Job 23:16 ("God has made Job's heart faint" — the feeling/sustaining function of the heart).
M01-E's heart-location (Isa 21:4; Job 37:1) engages the feeling function — the trembling expresses the heart's emotional state through the body.

M01-F's heart-location engages the feeling function (Deu 28:67: unbearable anguish) and the moral-awareness function (Pro 12:25: anxiety as a burden on the heart relieved by an encouraging word — the heart's capacity to receive and be moved by speech).

The heart's three primary functions engaged by M01 are: (1) the willing function — M01-A's reverential fear governs the heart's moral choices; (2) the feeling function — M01-B, E, F locate the emotional experience of fear in the heart; (3) the moral-awareness function — M01-A's absence-of-fear is moral blindness (Psa 36:1), and M01-F's Deu 28:67 dread is located in the heart's awareness of its exposure. The knowing function is secondary across the cluster.

Heart-location reveals that anger engages the knowing, willing, and feeling dimensions of the heart's integrating function simultaneously. Ecc 7:9 (anger as heart-resident of fools) shows it engaging the moral-evaluative dimension of the heart — foolishness and anger are linked through the heart. Pro 19:3 (heart raging against the Lord) shows anger as a directing force in the heart — the will's energy is misdirected through the heart's anger. The heart-location reveals anger as an integrating inner-being condition, not a peripheral emotion.
