Heart-location in M03 engages the feeling and integrating function of the heart — the heart as the centre of the person's inner experience, the site at which grief is received and carried. Two specific heart functions are engaged. First, the affective-integrating function: grief settles in the heart as the seat of inner emotional life (Psa 13:2; Jer 8:18; 2Cor 2:4). The heart is where grief is experienced as a totality, not merely as a passing feeling. Second, the volitional function: grief presses on the heart and affects what the person can will and do — the heart wrung within (Lam 1:20) is disabled in its will; godly grief reshapes the heart's moral energy (2Cor 7:11). Heart-location means grief is not peripheral but central to the person's integrating inner life.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The heart in OT anthropology is the integrating centre of the person — encompassing knowing, willing, feeling, and moral orientation. Heart-location for exultation reveals that this is not a peripheral emotion but an integrated inner state engaging the whole person's central faculty. Psa 32:11's "upright in heart" as the precondition for rejoicing shows exultation is not morally neutral — it is the appropriate inner expression of a heart aligned with God. The heart both originates exultation (Psa 13:5 — "my heart shall rejoice") and sustains it (Psa 89:16 — "exult in your name all the day").

**[CHAR-2]** E — The heart's integrating role means Joy at the heart level is not a peripheral emotion but an inner state engaging the whole person's central volitional-affective-knowing faculty. Pro 15:13 directly connects heart-gladness to countenance (the outer expression of inner state) and contrasts it with sorrow crushing the spirit — showing the heart as the nexus where Joy or its absence determines the whole person's inner condition. The heart's Joy is the productive source of the person's orientation to the world: Deu 28:47's failure to "serve the Lord with joyfulness and gladness of heart" as the root cause of judgment reveals that the heart's inner posture before God is the most fundamental thing about the covenant person's standing.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Act 2:26's heart-gladness followed by tongue-rejoicing shows the characteristic moving from the inner constitutional centre (heart) outward to expressive declaration — consistent with the broader inner-to-outer pattern across M04. The heart as the seat of the initial gladness (even in the Peter-quoting-David context) confirms that Suffering-Joy is not purely spirit-level but has a heart-level component in its expressed form.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Heart-location confirms that Gladness is not purely a cognitive judgment external to the person but an inner-being state that settles in the integrating centre. The heart is where Gladness takes up residence: in Jer 15:16 the word becomes "the delight of my heart" — it is received and held inwardly, not merely assessed externally. Pro 12:25's heart weighed down by anxiety that is relieved by a good word shows the heart as the seat where Gladness's presence or absence is most directly felt.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Heart-location reveals that Delight is the integrating faculty of the heart — it is how the heart orients itself toward its object. Psa 40:8 is paradigmatic: the law within the heart is what the heart delights in, and that delight drives the will to do God's will. The heart does not first decide and then delight; it first delights (law within) and thereby wills rightly. Delight is therefore the heart's orientation-faculty — it is the mechanism by which the heart chooses its object and aligns the will toward it.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Heart-location reveals that Pleasure is heart-mediated: the state of the heart determines the quality of Pleasure received. Pro 2:10's sequence (wisdom enters heart → knowledge pleasant to soul) shows the heart as the gateway: when the heart is rightly constituted by wisdom, the soul receives Pleasure in what is genuinely good. Pro 15:15's "cheerful of heart" confirms the heart as the seat whose positive orientation produces a continuous feast-quality of inner life — the inner disposition of the heart generates the felt pleasantness of daily experience. Gen 8:21 confirms: even divine Pleasure is located in God's heart.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Psa 9:1's "whole heart" in response to Wonder's proclamation shows that genuine Wonder produces whole-hearted engagement — the heart is fully involved in the thanksgiving that Wonder overflows into. Psa 131:1's "my heart is not lifted up" shows that the rightly-ordered heart is the condition for genuine Wonder: the humble heart does not overreach. Heart-location reveals Wonder as requiring heart-humility as an enabling condition and producing heart-wholeness as an effect.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Heart-location across all seven characteristics confirms the heart's function in M04 as the integrating centre through which positive inner states are constituted and expressed. Three cluster-level findings: (1) **Joy's heart-centrality** (Char 2) confirms Deu 28:47's diagnostic weight — the failure to serve "with joyfulness and gladness of heart" is the root cause of covenant curse; the heart's posture before God is the most fundamental diagnostic of the covenant person's standing; (2) **The heart-gladness/heart-exultation gradient** — Joy (heart primary) and Exultation (heart strongly evidenced but soul equally primary) are both heart-characteristics but at different intensities; the heart's gladness is the steady state; its exultation is the elevated event; (3) **Heart as the gateway** — in Delight (Char 4) and Pleasure (Char 5), the heart is explicitly the gateway: wisdom enters the heart (Pro 2:10) enabling Pleasure in knowledge; the law within the heart (Psa 40:8) produces Delight-in-obedience. The heart here is the receiving-and-constituting organ rather than merely the seat of affect.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Heart-location reveals that shame engages the integrating centre of the inner person — the faculty of moral knowing, feeling, and willing simultaneously. Psa 119:80's "blameless heart" as the shame-shield means that what protects against shame is not merely righteous behaviour but the inner orientation of the heart's full faculty. This places shame within the heart's moral-evaluative and volitional system: shame is what the heart experiences when its moral integrity is compromised or threatened, and a heart that is whole is the inner condition that protects against it.

**[CHAR-2]** S — CHAR-2's evidence does not specifically locate the characteristic in the heart. The heart is implicated as the locus of the proud disposition CHAR-2 corrects, but CHAR-2 itself as enforced humiliation is not explicitly heart-located. Silent.

---

**[CHAR-3]** E — The self-contradicting inner stance of Rom 2:23 — boasting in the law while breaking it — engages the heart as the integrating centre of moral consistency (or inconsistency). The heart that boasts in the law while the will breaks it is a divided heart, and from this inner division the dishonoring of God flows. Jam 2:6's failure of moral perception — treating the poor man as if he had no worth — is a failure of the heart's integrating moral vision.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — The heart is implicated in CHAR-4's VCG-03 inversion: Phili 3:19's "minds set on earthly things" and "their god is their belly" suggest a heart-level orientation that corrupts the evaluative faculty. The heart as the integrating moral centre is the location from which the evaluative faculty operates and from which its inversion flows.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — The contempt-er's heart is engaged: Luk 18:9 — "trusted in themselves that they were righteous" — is a heart-disposition of self-sufficiency that generates contempt. The heart as the integrating centre of self-assessment is the location from which the contemptuous dismissal of others flows. For the recipient, the heart as the worth-sensing faculty is the target of CHAR-5's damage.

---

**[CHAR-6]** E — The heart is CHAR-6's primary explicit constitutional location: "integrity of my heart" (Gen 20:5, vc=22817/22821). The heart as the integrating centre of moral knowing, willing, and feeling is the location from which CHAR-6 operates. Psa 73:13's "I have kept my heart clean" names the heart as the specific locus of the moral purity that CHAR-6 describes. The heart-location confirms CHAR-6 as a heart-level moral characteristic — it is the condition of the heart's moral integrity.

---

**[CLUSTER]** E — Five of six characteristics locate at the heart; the exception is Char 2 (which does not explicitly heart-locate, reflecting its social-bodily primary dimension). The heart-location across Chars 1, 3, 4, 5, and 6 consistently engages the heart as the integrating centre of moral awareness, willing, and feeling. Key evidence: Char 1's "may my heart be blameless in your statutes, that I may not be put to shame" (Psa 119:80) — the blameless heart as shame's protective faculty; Char 3's divided heart as the dishonour-generator (Rom 2:23 — boasting in the law while breaking it); Char 4's heart corrupted by earthly orientation (Phili 3:19); Char 5's self-righteous heart generating contempt (Luk 18:9); Char 6's "integrity of my heart" (Gen 20:5). Cluster-level: the heart is the primary constitutional location for the shame-field's moral producing and protective conditions.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — Heart-location engages multiple aspects of the heart's integrating function. Volitional: Dan 11:36 (vc=34235, M08-A1-VCG-02) — the king exalts himself "by his own will"; Isa 14:13 (vc=34233, M08-A4-VCG-05) — "you said in your heart, 'I will ascend to heaven'" — the heart as the seat of volitional self-declaration. Cognitive/knowing: Jer 48:29 (vc=34603, M08-A1-VCG-03) — pride is the "culminating inner attitude in a list of pride's expressions," the heart naming the identity-claim; Eze 28:17 (vc=34047, M08-A1-VCG-02) — pride in the heart corrupts wisdom — the heart's discernment function is distorted. Moral assessment: Pro 16:5 (vc=12083, M08-A1-VCG-03) — "an abomination to the Lord" — the heart's moral condition evaluated by God as abomination. Identity formation: Eze 28:2 (vc=34040, M08-A1-VCG-02) — "your heart is proud, and you have said, 'I am a god'" — the heart as the seat of the most fundamental self-understanding, CHAR-1 distorting it into a claim of divine status.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Heart-location engages the heart's self-assessment function: Obd 3 (vc=34108, M08-B-VCG-02) — "inner conviction of invulnerability that pride has planted in the heart" — the heart's self-evaluative capacity is distorted by CHAR-2 into a false assessment of the self's power and safety. Jer 49:16 (vc=34115, M08-B-VCG-02) — "the arrogance of your heart has deceived you" — the heart's directional knowledge function is corrupted by CHAR-2 into self-deception. 1Sa 17:28 (vc=34112) — "arrogance and evil of heart together" — the heart as the seat of morally disordered disposition. CHAR-2 in the heart engages the heart's knowing/assessment faculty, distorting it into overconfidence in the self's autonomy.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Heart-location reveals that CHAR-3 has two distinct relationships to the heart: in its condemned form (VCG-01), the heart's prideful orientation (CHAR-1 substrate) generates CHAR-3's self-directed boasting; in its examined form (VCG-02), the heart's integrity and conscience are the ground of legitimate self-commendation (2Cor 1:12, vc=33912: "the testimony of our conscience"). The heart is CHAR-3's interior origin-point for its condemned form and its integrity-ground for its examined form.

**[CHAR-4]** S — The silence on heart-location for CHAR-4 is analytically significant: it confirms CHAR-4's distinctive constitutional location in the cognitive/mind register, distinguishing it from CHAR-1 (whose primary seat is the heart). The mind (nous) and the cognitive thinking-faculty (froneō) are CHAR-4's named locations, not the heart.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Heart-location reveals that CHAR-5's structural-power medium (wealth, might, height) generates an inner heart-level pride that is constitutionally located at the same depth as CHAR-1's dispositional self-elevation. Eze 28:5 (vc=34046, M08-E-VCG-02): the wealth-triggered heart-pride confirms that CHAR-5 follows CHAR-1's constitutional location (heart) while being distinguished by the specific medium (structural goods) that triggers it. The heart is the seat of the inner pride that the structural goods generate; without the structural goods, the heart-pride of CHAR-5 specifically would not have been triggered.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The heart-location across four characteristics reveals that M08's pride is constitutively deep — it originates in the inner person's integrating centre (the heart as the seat of will, evaluation, and orientation) rather than at the periphery of behaviour or social presentation. The cluster comparison also reveals that the heart-location serves different functions per characteristic: in CHAR-1 it is the dispositional seat of the elevated posture; in CHAR-2 it is the seat of the self-deceptive overconfidence that enables transgression; in CHAR-3 it is the integrity-ground of legitimate versus illegitimate boasting; in CHAR-5 it is the seat of the pride that structural goods generate. CHAR-4's absence from the heart-location set confirms its distinctive cognitive-mind location as genuinely distinct from the other four.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The heart-location engages the heart's *integrating moral and volitional function*. Rom6:17 — "obedience from the heart" contrasts with enslaved-to-sin; the heart's integrating moral orientation (whose authority rules the person) is what is at stake. Eph6:5 — "sincere heart" engages the heart's authenticity-function — the undivided inner person whose will and motive are aligned. Col3:22 — "sincerity of heart and fear of the Lord" engages the heart's moral-reverential orientation. The characteristic engages the heart as the integrating centre that determines: (a) whose authority the person genuinely serves (volitional-allegiance function); (b) whether compliance is whole-hearted or divided (sincerity function); (c) what moves the person at their deepest level (motivational function).

**[CHAR-3]** E — The heart's breaking (Psa34:18) reveals that contrition engages the heart's *integrating function comprehensively*: the heart as the centre of knowing, willing, feeling, and moral awareness is broken — not one function only but the integrating centre itself. When the heart is broken, the integrating function that holds the person together before God is genuinely disrupted. Isa57:15's "revive the heart" indicates that the restoration God provides is equally comprehensive — reaching the heart's integrating function to restore it. The heart-location confirms that contrition is a whole-person inner event, not a compartmentalised emotional state.

**[CHAR-4]** S — Heart-location is not explicitly evidenced in §3.C. The characteristic's grounding in shared weakness (Heb5:2) implies a heart-level self-awareness, but the heart is not named as the constitutional site.
**[CHAR-5]** S — Heart-location is not explicitly evidenced in §3.D.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The heart's location reveals that willing-heartedness engages the heart's *integrating volitional-affective function*. The "generous/willing heart" (Exo35:5) is one whose integrating centre is freely-moved toward giving — the heart's knowing, willing, and feeling are all aligned in the direction of free offering rather than in conflict (reluctance would be the heart's conflicted state). The characteristic in its heart-location is the whole-person inner integration that produces the uncoerced external act of giving.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The heart in biblical usage integrates knowing, willing, feeling, and moral awareness — all of which are engaged by humility. The Lev26:41 "uncircumcised heart" language suggests the heart's moral-knowing function: the hardened heart is one that does not genuinely receive or register the moral reality of its situation before God. The 2Ki22:19 "penitent heart" engages the heart's affective and moral-awareness dimensions — genuine inner grief over one's condition. Mat11:29 "lowly in heart" engages the heart's dispositional-volitional function — the settled posture of the whole person. Phili2:3 ("in humility count others more significant") engages the heart's cognitive-evaluative function — the reassessment of relative worth. The characteristic engages the heart's integrating function comprehensively: knowing (accurate self-assessment), willing (the act of self-lowering), feeling (the grief and tenderness that accompany genuine humbling), and moral awareness (recognition of one's true standing before God).

**[CLUSTER]** E — The heart's integrating function (knowing, willing, feeling, moral awareness) is engaged differently by each of the four heart-located characteristics. CHAR-1 Humility engages all four functions comprehensively — the humble heart is cognitively reordering (Phili2:3), volitionally self-lowering (Jam4:10), affectively tender (2Ch34:27), and morally aware (Lev26:41). CHAR-2 Submission engages primarily the volitional-allegiance function — the heart determines whose authority rules (Rom6:17). CHAR-3 Contrition engages the heart's integrating centre comprehensively — the heart broken means the integrating centre itself is disrupted (Psa34:18 — nishbar-lev). CHAR-6 Willing-heartedness engages the heart's integrating volitional-affective function — the willing heart is one whose integrating centre is freely-moved (Exo35:5). The cluster-level finding: CHAR-1 and CHAR-3 are the two characteristics that engage the heart's *full integrating function*; CHAR-2 and CHAR-6 engage the heart's *primary volitional-directional function*. This heart-engagement taxonomy distinguishes the characteristics that are comprehensive (whole-person) from those that are primarily directional (will-directed).

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — Heart-location engages the heart's *willing and moral-evaluating* functions. Job 1:5 shows sinning in the heart as a heart-orientation (cursing God) — the heart's alignment with or against God is the register. Psa 119:11 shows the heart as the site where the word is stored and where the will-to-not-sin is formed — the heart's *holding* and *deciding* function. The heart here is integrating function in the sense that it is where the person's stance before God is formed: the heart that curses God (Job 1:5) is the heart that has turned its deepest orientation against him, while the heart that stores his word (Psa 119:11) is the heart aligned with him. Sinning in the heart is thus sinning at the person's deepest evaluative and volitional centre.

**[CHAR-10]** E — Heart-location (2Pe 2:14 — "hearts trained in greed") reveals that the enticement mechanism reaches the constitutional centre of the person: the heart is not merely performing sinful appetite but has been *trained* into it — the training implies sustained formation of the heart's motivational centre toward sin. The heart's training is what makes the enticement self-generating: the heart has become the bait-mechanism itself, not merely a passive recipient of external lures.

**[CHAR-11]** E — Heart-location (Heb 3:13 — hardening through deceit; Rom 6:17 — heart-enslavement preceding heart-obedience) reveals that the universal sin-condition is not merely behavioural or cognitive but penetrates to the person's moral-volitional centre. The heart's hardening (Heb 3:13) means sin's deceitfulness progressively closes the heart's capacity to respond to God's voice — the more thoroughly the condition operates on the heart, the less the person can hear and respond to correction. This is why the remedy addresses the heart: the forgiveness-declaration (VCG-02) reaches the heart level, and the Spirit's conviction (Joh 16:8/9) addresses the heart's resistance to acknowledging the condition.

**[CHAR-12]** S — The absence of explicit heart-language reflects the corpus's focus on the will's captivity (Joh 8:34), the universal structural imprisonment (Gal 3:22), and the allegiance-level identity (1Jo 3:8). The heart's implicit engagement is through the will's captivity, but the vocabulary does not name it directly in this corpus.

**[CHAR-13]** E — Heart-location (Jer 17:1 — iron pen, diamond point engraving on the heart's tablet) reveals that the divine record has a dual location: before God externally and within the person internally. The engraving metaphor is the most analytically significant image in the 205-verse corpus for constitutional location: the sin is inscribed in the person's innermost moral core with such permanence ("iron pen... diamond point") that it cannot be self-erased. The heart bears the record as an internal impression while God maintains it as an external account. The record's internal inscription explains why it persists even when hidden from others: the engraving is within.

**[CHAR-14]** E — Heart-location (Lev 10:19 — inner state affecting offering's validity; Lev 23:27 — affliction as inner-posture) reveals that the seeking dimension of the characteristic is not merely formal (bringing the prescribed offering) but requires an appropriate inner orientation at the heart level. The priestly officiants' inner state matters (Lev 10:19); the individual seeker's self-affliction matters (Lev 23:27); and in the NT register, Luk 7:47 — the woman's love is the heart's response to forgiveness received, confirming that the heart is the primary relational-receptive faculty engaged throughout.

**[CHAR-15]** E — Heart-location (1Ki 8:47 — "turn their heart") reveals that generational sin has penetrated to the person's moral-volitional centre: the heart must turn, which implies it was previously oriented in a wrong direction sustained by the generational pattern. The heart's turning is the required reversal of what the generational sin-condition has made the heart's default orientation. The heart is thus both the site of the condition's hold and the site of the potential turning that addresses it.

**[CHAR-16]** E — Heart-location (Jam 4:8 — heart requiring purification alongside the sinner's hand-cleansing; Pro 23:17 — heart tempted toward sinners' prosperity) reveals that the sinner-identity operates through and on the heart in complementary ways: the sinner's own heart requires purification (Jam 4:8 — the heart is the inner dimension of the sinner's condition); and the observing person's heart is at risk of envy toward sinners (Pro 23:17 — the sinner-identity's apparent prosperity can misdirect the onlooker's heart). The heart is thus both the site of the sinner's internal condition and a faculty vulnerable to the sinner's external situation.

**[CHAR-17]** E — Heart-location (Hos 10:2 — "false heart... must bear guilt") reveals that the guilt-state is rooted in the heart's dispositional condition: it is not merely the result of isolated acts but flows from the heart's sustained false-orientation. The heart generates the acts that create guilt entries, and the guilt-bearing is thus the heart's consequence. This connects CHAR-17 to CHAR-16 (sinner as moral character): the false heart that generates guilt is the heart of the sinner-type.

**[CHAR-18]** E — Heart-location (Eze 14:3/4/7 — idols taken into the heart; Job 31:33 — iniquity hidden in the heart) reveals two distinct heart-iniquity functions. (1) *The heart as iniquity's origin*: Eze 14:3 — the will chooses to receive idols inward; the heart is the site of the originating criminal allegiance that produces all subsequent iniquity; (2) *The heart as iniquity's hiding-place*: Job 31:33 — the heart can conceal acknowledged iniquity to avoid accountability; the hiding is a deliberate inner act. VCG-08's heart-seated register is thus the most foundational: it locates iniquity at the person's innermost will-level, making it the source-register from which other VCGs flow.

**[CHAR-19]** E — Heart-location (Psa 36:1 — "deep in his heart"; Isa 59:13 — "conceiving from the heart"; Eze 18:31 — new heart as remedy) reveals that CHAR-19's transgression is not primarily an external act but an inner-heart condition that drives external behaviour. Psa 36:1's "transgression speaks deep in the heart" is the single most important inner-being statement in the entire 147-verse corpus: it personifies transgression as an internal counsellor installed at the heart's deepest level, displacing the fear of God and steering the will toward rebellion. The heart is both the origin of transgression (where it speaks from) and the site requiring renewal when transgression is addressed (Eze 18:31).

**[CHAR-2]** E — The absence of heart-language (T2.3.1) is a defining structural feature of unintentional sinning. The heart, as the integrating moral centre of the inner person (knowing, willing, feeling), is *not engaged* at the moment of unintentional sinning — which is precisely why the sinning is unintentional. The heart's absence from the act confirms that the characteristic operates below the level of heart-engagement: it is an act that proceeds without the heart's informed moral consent. Lev 4:2 ("sins unintentionally") — the absence of heart-language signals that the heart's moral-evaluation function did not process the act as prohibited. The heart engages *after* realisation (Lev 5:5 — guilt realised and confessed), not during the sinning itself.

**[CHAR-20]** E — Heart-location (2Ch 29:6 — turning away from God; 2Ch 26:16 — proud heart producing faithlessness; Psa 73:15 — heart's inner deliberation as potential betrayal) reveals that faithlessness operates at the heart's allegiance-level: the heart that has turned its face and back toward God (2Ch 29:6) is the heart in the faithlessness-condition. The heart's disposition of allegiance — toward God or away — is the constitutional location of faithlessness. When the heart turns away from God (2Ch 29:6 — "turned their backs"), the turn is faithlessness at its heart-origin.

**[CHAR-21]** E — Heart-location (Pro 6:14 — "perverted heart"; Pro 23:33 — heart uttering perverse things; Deu 32:20 — perverse generation) reveals that perversion-as-inner-inversion originates at the heart's deep centre. Pro 6:14's "perverted heart devises evil continually" is the corpus's defining inner-being statement: the heart is both the origin and the continual driver of perversity; the perversion is not episodic but continuous because it is seated in the heart's dispositional centre. The heart is the characteristic's primary constitutional location.

**[CHAR-22]** E — Heart-location (Psa 58:2 — "in your hearts you devise wrongs"; Psa 64:6 — "inward mind and heart... deep"; Psa 53:1 — heart-atheism) reveals that CHAR-22 originates in the heart's deliberating function: the heart does not passively receive injustice but actively *devises* it. The heart is the scheming centre — the same faculty that, when rightly oriented, devises justice, is here engaged in the deliberate planning of wrongs. Psa 64:6's "diligent search" confirms the deliberateness.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Heart-location (2Sa 24:10) reveals that genuine confession is not primarily a social or religious obligation performed externally but an inner event initiated by the heart's own moral witness. The heart here functions in its *moral-awareness and conscience* capacity: it registers that a wrong was done and responds by striking — producing inward conviction before external prompt. This confirms that CHAR-3's deepest constitutional seat is the heart: the heart confesses first (within itself, in the form of conviction), then the mouth confesses second (externally, in the form of speech). The heart-initiation distinguishes genuine confession from its hollow form — where the heart has not struck but the mouth still speaks.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The absence of explicit heart-language in this corpus is analytically significant. In CHAR-3 (Confession), "David's heart struck him" — the heart is where genuine conscience-engagement originates. The absence of heart-language in CHAR-4 may reflect that conscience suppression operates *below* the heart's full moral engagement — the heart's warning function is what is suppressed, which is why it does not appear actively in the corpus. Tit 3:11's "warped" (*exestraptai* — to be distorted/turned inside out) may imply a heart-level distortion that the term "warped" carries, though the heart is not explicitly named.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Heart-location (2Ki 10:31) reveals that refusal to repent is seated in the heart's *incomplete volitional commitment*. "Not with all his heart" — the heart is the integrating centre of the will's commitment to God and his law; where the heart is not wholehearted, a portion of it remains available for the sinful course to continue unchallenged. The refusal to repent is thus not located in a single moment of will-act but in the heart's ongoing failure to commit entirely — the characteristic is as deep as the heart's partial alignment.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Heart-location (Exo 9:34) reveals that habitual defection is seated at the heart's *dispositional-volitional centre* and produces a progressive deformation of that centre. The hardening of the heart is both the mechanism and the symptom: each sinning act hardens the heart, and the hardened heart drives the next sinning act. The heart in habitual defection is not merely passively shaped but actively hardens itself ("hardened his heart" — the Hiphil causative suggests the agent is Pharaoh himself, not an external force). Habitual defection thus represents the heart's own participation in its constitutional deformation.

**[CHAR-7]** E — The absence of explicit heart-language in this corpus is analytically significant. The Jeroboam-formula focuses on the leader's conduct (walking in the way, making Israel to sin) and the community's outcome (sinning, provoking God) rather than on the leader's inner heart-state. This contrasts with CHAR-5 (2Ki 10:31 — "not with all his heart") where the heart is explicitly named as the site of incomplete commitment. CHAR-7's evidence base is behavioural-relational rather than introspective — the corpus describes what the leader does and what the community undergoes rather than the internal heart-condition that drives the leader.

**[CHAR-8]** E — The absence of explicit heart-language reflects the corpus's focus on the outer political acts rather than the inner generating conditions. The one verse that comes closest to inner location is 2Ch 21:10's "forsaken the Lord" — forsaking is a heart-level act — but the heart is not named directly. The corpus is descriptive at the political-social level; the inner heart-conditions that produce revolt (such as the decision to break submission) are not named. This is consistent with the corpus's literary form (regnal narrative) which describes political outcomes rather than inner states.

**[CHAR-9]** E — Heart-location (Mat 15:19; Mar 7:22) reveals that sinful speech is not primarily a failure of speech-regulation but a *diagnostic of the heart's moral condition*. The speech does not corrupt the heart — the corrupted heart produces the speech. This is the characteristic's most theologically significant finding: addressing sinful speech by regulating the mouth (without addressing the heart) is insufficient; the mouth speaks what the heart contains. Eph 4:31's "put away from you" and Col 3:8's "put them all away" are therefore ultimately heart-level renunciation commands, not merely verbal-hygiene commands.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Heart-location reveals that wickedness-as-settled-person-identity specifically engages the heart's integrating and self-governing function. The heart in Scripture is the integrating centre of the person — where knowing, willing, feeling, and moral awareness converge. In the wicked person: (1) the knowing function is corrupted — the heart's moral compass is inverted (Pro 10:32); (2) the willing function is misoriented — the heart renounces God actively (Psa 10:13); (3) the governing function is occupied — transgression speaks as an internal voice in the heart (Psa 36:1), displacing the God-fear that should govern. The heart is not merely the location of wickedness — it is the site where wickedness has replaced the rightful governance structure of the person with its own alternative governance (transgression-as-inner-voice).

**[CHAR-2]** E — Heart-location reveals that evil as constitutional inner nature engages the heart's generative and integrating function — the heart as the source from which all inner-being outputs flow. The treasury metaphor (Mat 12:35 — VCG-03) captures this precisely: the heart does not merely host the characteristic but actively generates outputs from it. The knowing function is corrupted (Mat 9:4 — evil in your hearts as corrupt cognition), the willing function is misoriented (Heb 3:12 — unbelieving heart leading to apostasy), and the generative function is redirected (Mat 15:19 — out of the heart come the vice list). The heart-location reveals the characteristic as occupying the central integrating organ of the person — not a peripheral faculty but the generative core from which speech, thought, and action all flow.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Heart-location reveals that abomination engages three of the heart's integrating functions simultaneously. (1) The moral-orientation function — the heart's basic directional bent (crooked — Pro 11:20; straight/blameless as opposite) determines whether the person is abominable or delightful to God. (2) The affective-pride function — arrogance in heart (Pro 16:5 — VCG-02) is an affective orientation of self-elevation that the heart harbours. (3) The cognitive-hidden function — seven abominations in the heart (Pro 26:25 — VCG-02) describes the heart as the location of concealed corrupt motivations that the person hides beneath smooth speech. The heart-location reveals the characteristic as operating at the central integrating point of the person — the place where orientation, affect, and hidden motivation converge, all of which God perceives directly (Luk 16:15 — "God knows your hearts").

**[CHAR-4]** E — Heart-location reveals that idolatrous abomination engages specifically the heart's directional-devotional function — the function by which the heart orients itself toward an object of worship and allegiance. Eze 11:21 (vc=1631 — VCG-05): "heart goes after" — the going-after is the heart's directional function misdirected. Eze 6:9 (vc=1697 — VCG-05): "whoring heart that has departed from me" — the departure is the directional function moving away from God. The characteristic does not engage the heart's cognitive function (knowing) or the moral-awareness function (right and wrong) primarily; it engages the allegiance-devotion function — the capacity by which the heart binds itself to an object of ultimate loyalty. This is the heart's most fundamental function as image-bearer: the choice of what to love and worship.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Heart-location reveals that iniquity as scheming engages all three of the heart's primary integrating functions simultaneously. (1) Cognitive/planning function: Isa 32:6 (vc=38181 — VCG-02): the heart "busy with iniquity" in a planning, scheming mode — the heart's knowing-planning capacity generates the schemes. (2) Moral awareness function — inverted: Psa 28:3 (vc=38232 — VCG-03): "evil is in their hearts" while speaking outward peace — the heart knows the evil it harbours, enabling the deception; the moral awareness is present but co-opted for concealment. (3) Volitional function: the heart as chooser — Psa 36:4 (vc=38235 — VCG-02): "he sets himself in a way that is not good; he does not reject evil" — the heart's willing is the faculty through which iniquity is retained. Heart-location shows the characteristic as engaging the full integrating centre of the person.

**[CHAR-6]** S — Heart-location is not explicitly evidenced in this corpus (T2.3.1). The nearest equivalent to heart-location is the hardened-will evidence in VCG-01 — Rev 16:9 (vc=14352): "they did not repent and give him glory" — the refusal is at the deepest volitional-moral centre, which in the programme's framework corresponds to heart-level function even without the explicit vocabulary. This engagement is with the heart's volitional-moral function (the will's choice of orientation) without heart-vocabulary being used.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Heart-location across all six characteristics reveals that M10b inner evil is constitutionally central — it occupies the integrating organ of the inner person (the heart as the seat of knowing, willing, feeling, and moral awareness). The cluster's heart-location evidence shows each characteristic engaging a different face of the heart's integrating function. Char 1 engages the heart's moral-directional function (the way the heart is oriented). Char 2 engages the heart's generative-treasury function (what it stores and outputs). Char 3 engages the heart's moral-character quality (the crooked, arrogant, abomination-filled heart). Char 4 engages the heart's devotion-directional function (the heart going after idols). Char 5 engages the heart's cognitive-productive function (the heart busy with iniquity, conceiving evil). Char 6 engages the heart's volitional-refusing function (the will refusing repentance). The cluster reveals that the six forms of inner evil correspond to six functions of the heart — together constituting a comprehensive portrait of the heart's full failure-profile under the influence of M10b characteristics.
**[CHAR-1]** S — Not evidenced from the 133-verse corpus. See T2.3.3.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The heart-location engages the heart's allegiance-forming function — the faculty by which the heart orients itself toward or away from God. Rom 1:24 (VCG-02): the heart's lusts are the engine of defilement; the heart has oriented its desires toward corrupted objects. Eph 5:5 (VCG-04): the impure person is equated with an idolater — "covetous (that is, an idolater)" — the heart's allegiance has been displaced from God to corrupt desire. The heart-location reveals the characteristic as a condition of allegiance disorder: the integrating function of the heart, which should orient all inner faculties toward God, has been redirected toward desire-objects that defile.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The implicit heart-allegiance dimension reveals that the corporate/covenantal defilement-state originates in the community's disordered allegiance — the heart that should be directed toward God (covenant fidelity) has been directed toward idols (Eze 20:7/18/30/31 — the repeated commands not to defile with Egypt's idols and fathers' idols, which the community persistently ignores). This reveals the characteristic as flowing from the heart's most fundamental function: the setting of ultimate loyalty and allegiance. When corporate loyalty is disordered, the defilement extends to the entire sacred relational environment.
**[CHAR-4]** S — Not evidenced. See T2.3.3.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The heart-location in Characteristics 2 and 3 reveals the cluster's most fundamental inner-being insight: at the deepest point where defilement is generated by the person's own constitution, the mechanism is heart-allegiance disorder — the heart directed toward corrupted desire (Char 2: Rom 1:24 — "lusts of their hearts") or toward idolatrous attachment (Char 3: Eze 23:7 — "all the idols of everyone after whom she lusted"; implicit in the Ezekiel idolatry corpus throughout VCG-02). The heart-allegiance disorder in Characteristic 2 is individual; in Characteristic 3 it is corporate. Both reveal that self-generated defilement originates in the heart's fundamental misdirection — the faculty that should orient the person and community toward God has been redirected toward corrupting alternatives. This confirms the alignment of the M10c cluster with the broader biblical diagnosis of sin: its deepest root is in the heart's allegiance.

findings.finding_value: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level (chesed as covenantal-soul character), heart-level (Hos 11:8 — "my heart recoils"), and somatic-level (re.chem, splanchnon) are all richly evidenced. The constitutional architecture is bottom-up: the womb and entrails are the originating ground; the soul and heart are the engagement points; the act is the constitutional expression. Four body-part functions are identified: constitutive (womb — the generative image of compassion), expressive (gut — the felt movement), indicative (Synoptic pattern — splanchnizō signals the compassion-event), and mediating (heart in Hos 11:8 — the deliberative locus where compassion and judgment contend). The four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) is uniquely evidenced in this registry — consistently inside-out and bottom-up. T2.8 established no body deposit; T5.7 is formally closed. The constitutional portrait confirms the sb_classification (soul-body interface) and extends it: compassion is the most somatically grounded characteristic in the programme, with its originating logic residing in the body's deepest interior.

findings.finding_value: T2's four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) maps directly onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The somatic-arousal stage (T2.6 — gut stirring, splanchnizō) corresponds to T3.1's perceptive-trigger stage (sight activates the somatic response) and T3.4's affect stage (the stirring is the affective movement). The soul-engagement stage (T2.2 — chesed as soul-character) corresponds to T3.8 moral evaluation (the soul assesses the need) and T3.9 conscience (the conscience activates the response). The volitional-engagement stage (T2.3 — heart-locus as deliberative site) corresponds to T3.6 volition (the will directs the action). The outward-action stage corresponds to T3.7 agency. T2 and T3 describe the same movement sequence from two perspectives: T2 maps the constitutional levels; T3 maps the faculties active at each level.

findings.finding_value: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary point of reception (Zec 12:10 — spirit of grace poured out), not the point of generation (grace originates with God — T2.9). The soul level is the site of standing (Rom 5:2 — "this grace in which we stand") and identity (1Cor 15:10 — "by the grace of God I am what I am"). The constitutional movement follows the SD021 four-faces model: divine disposition received at spirit level → relational standing established at soul level → specific capacity gifted → character expressed outward. Heart-location is partially evidenced via eusplanchnos (Eph 4:32 — the tenderheartedness that grace produces, reaching the affective-somatic interface). T2.7 produces a new finding: grace operates bidirectionally through the body-soul interface — soul-to-body (inner posture enacted somatically in prostration, fasting, sackcloth) and body-to-soul (somatic enactment deepening and confirming the inner posture). T2.8 remains open (body deposit question unresolved); T5.7 is left open accordingly. The constitutional origin analysis (T2.9) is the most analytically significant T2 finding: grace does not originate in the human constitutional system at any level — it arrives from outside. This is confirmed at T6 as the structural uniqueness of grace: the only characteristic that is not produced by any other inner-being characteristic.

findings.session_b_note:
The mind is not the primary locus of forgiveness in the verse evidence, but a cognitive dimension is present and significant:

- **Jer 31:34** — "I will remember their sin no more." The divine cognitive act of ceasing to remember is the most direct mind-location in the corpus. God's mind — specifically the memory/cognition function — is the locus of the cognitive component of forgiveness. OBS-064-017 names this: "the completeness of divine forgiveness is measured... by the permanent cessation of the legal/cognitive claim."
- **Three-registry shared anchor:** Jer 31:34 is shared with thought/knowledge (R160), confirming the cognitive intersection of forgiveness in this verse.
- **The calculative logic of Mat 18:** The parable involves numerical reckoning — debts calculated, amounts compared. The cognitive tracking of the debt-account is what forgiveness cancels.

The mind-location is **partial and secondary** — it appears primarily in the cognitive-cessation of Jer 31:34 (divine side) and in the implicit debt-accounting logic (human side). It is not named as the primary locus of forgiveness in the human person.

findings.session_b_note:
The evidence partially addresses the mind in the context of compassion, primarily through the 1 Pet 3:8 community list and the metriopatheō term.

1 Pet 3:8 places sumpathēs (sympathetic/compassionate) alongside "unity of mind" (homophrōn) — the same verse positions compassion and cognitive unity as companion virtues. The mind (phronēma) is implicated but not as the seat of compassion itself — rather as a co-operating faculty.

G3356 metriopatheō (Heb 5:2) — "deal gently" — draws on the Stoic metriopatheia tradition of moderating the passions through reasoned self-governance. The term places a form of calibrated compassion in proximity to the mind's regulating function: compassion that is wise rather than raw. However, Heb 5:2 regrounds this in shared vulnerability rather than cognitive mastery — the moderation comes from knowing human weakness from the inside, not from philosophical reasoning (SD-013).

**What is missing (P):** The data does not locate compassion directly in the mind using nous or equivalent terms. Mind-engagement is evidenced as secondary and co-operative rather than primary.
findings.finding_value:
The evidence partially addresses the mind in the context of compassion, primarily through the 1 Pet 3:8 community list and the metriopatheō term.

1 Pet 3:8 places sumpathēs (sympathetic/compassionate) alongside "unity of mind" (homophrōn) — the same verse positions compassion and cognitive unity as companion virtues. The mind (phronēma) is implicated but not as the seat of compassion itself — rather as a co-operating faculty.

G3356 metriopatheō (Heb 5:2) — "deal gently" — draws on the Stoic metriopatheia tradition of moderating the passions through reasoned self-governance. The term places a form of calibrated compassion in proximity to the mind's regulating function: compassion that is wise rather than raw. However, Heb 5:2 regrounds this in shared vulnerability rather than cognitive mastery — the moderation comes from knowing human weakness from the inside, not from philosophical reasoning (SD-013).

**What is missing (P):** The data does not locate compassion directly in the mind using nous or equivalent terms. Mind-engagement is evidenced as secondary and co-operative rather than primary.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-067-002: T2 as a whole reveals that goodness has a comprehensive multi-level constitutional presence — from Spirit-level origin through soul-orientation, heart-engagement, and mind-evaluative functions to outw…
findings.finding_value: T2 as a whole reveals that goodness has a comprehensive multi-level constitutional presence — from Spirit-level origin through soul-orientation, heart-engagement, and mind-evaluative functions to outward expression — but with a marked asymmetry in evidence quality. Spirit-level (Q&A-037-039), soul-level (Q&A-040-041), and heart-level (Q&A-043-044) are all substantively evidenced. Mind-level is partially evidenced through cognitive dimensions. Body-level is thin — the gladness-of-heart compound (tov-lev) and the taste-and-see perceptual metaphor are the somatic markers, but no constitutional body deposit is evidenced (T2.8 silent). The most structurally significant T2 finding is the six-step constitutional movement (Q&A-064): Spirit-level origin → soul reorientation → heart engagement → volitional alignment → agentive resolve → outward expression. This movement is top-down and outward, with no evidenced reversal from body to inner being. Goodness is constitutionally deep but does not leave a somatic deposit.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-103-002: Love is the programme's most constitutionally comprehensive characteristic — it occupies all five constitutional levels simultaneously: spirit-sourced (implied via Spirit-as-agent, Rom 5:5, Gal 5:22),…
findings.finding_value: Love is the programme's most constitutionally comprehensive characteristic — it occupies all five constitutional levels simultaneously: spirit-sourced (implied via Spirit-as-agent, Rom 5:5, Gal 5:22), soul-located (Song 5:6 — soul failing at beloved's absence; Mat 22:37 — love with all your soul; Joh 15:13 — laying down the soul), heart-inscribed (Pro 3:3; Rom 5:5 infused into hearts), mind-engaged (Mat 22:37 — love with all your mind; Joh 15:15 — love as knowledge-sharing), and body-expressed (kiss, embrace, tears, womb-movement across multiple groups). The constitutional movement pattern is consistently downward: Spirit origin → heart reception → soul experience → body expression. Love's heart-inscription (Pro 3:3) is the closest evidence to a constitutional deposit — the metaphorical writing of chesed into the heart's deepest register produces a lasting dispositional quality (the chasid person-type). The primary finding: love is not confined to any single constitutional level but operates across all levels in an integrated movement from deepest to most outward. This comprehensive constitutional architecture is consistent with love's function as the programme's organising characteristic.

findings.finding_value: T2 reveals mercy as a whole-person constitutional reality. No single level contains it: mercy originates at the spirit-soul interface, operates on the soul (addressing the nephesh-guilt), engages the heart through the visceral compassion vocabulary (splanchna), engages the mind through the memory-erasure mechanism (Heb 8:12), and operates through the body as both the medium of mercy-seeking (embodied posture) and the mechanism of mercy's effect (blood-atonement). Body deposit: none. T5.7: formally closed.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-002: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level …
findings.finding_value: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level (chesed as covenantal-soul character), heart-level (Hos 11:8 — "my heart recoils"), and somatic-level (re.chem, splanchnon) are all richly evidenced. The constitutional architecture is bottom-up: the womb and entrails are the originating ground; the soul and heart are the engagement points; the act is the constitutional expression. Four body-part functions are identified: constitutive (womb — the generative image of compassion), expressive (gut — the felt movement), indicative (Synoptic pattern — splanchnizō signals the compassion-event), and mediating (heart in Hos 11:8 — the deliberative locus where compassion and judgment contend). The four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) is uniquely evidenced in this registry — consistently inside-out and bottom-up. T2.8 established no body deposit; T5.7 is formally closed. The constitutional portrait confirms the sb_classification (soul-body interface) and extends it: compassion is the most somatically grounded characteristic in the programme, with its originating logic residing in the body's deepest interior.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-002: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary…
findings.finding_value: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary point of reception (Zec 12:10 — spirit of grace poured out), not the point of generation (grace originates with God — T2.9). The soul level is the site of standing (Rom 5:2 — "this grace in which we stand") and identity (1Cor 15:10 — "by the grace of God I am what I am"). The constitutional movement follows the SD021 four-faces model: divine disposition received at spirit level → relational standing established at soul level → specific capacity gifted → character expressed outward. Heart-location is partially evidenced via eusplanchnos (Eph 4:32 — the tenderheartedness that grace produces, reaching the affective-somatic interface). T2.7 produces a new finding: grace operates bidirectionally through the body-soul interface — soul-to-body (inner posture enacted somatically in prostration, fasting, sackcloth) and body-to-soul (somatic enactment deepening and confirming the inner posture). T2.8 remains open (body deposit question unresolved); T5.7 is left open accordingly. The constitutional origin analysis (T2.9) is the most analytically significant T2 finding: grace does not originate in the human constitutional system at any level — it arrives from outside. This is confirmed at T6 as the structural uniqueness of grace: the only characteristic that is not produced by any other inner-being characteristic.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-034-002: T2 as a whole reveals that covenant operates across the full constitutional range of the inner person with no single exclusive location. The heart is the primary site (Q&A-044), the mind is co-located…
findings.finding_value: T2 as a whole reveals that covenant operates across the full constitutional range of the inner person with no single exclusive location. The heart is the primary site (Q&A-044), the mind is co-located (Q&A-047), the soul gives totality of engagement (Q&A-041), the mouth is the expressive-constitutive organ (Q&A-050), and the body participates through blood and circumcision (Q&A-053). The single most structurally significant T2 finding is the constitutional movement shift from OT to NT covenantal mode: OT covenant moves outer→inner→outer; new covenant moves inner→inner→outer (Q&A-066). This movement-shift is the constitutional-level expression of the Sinai-to-new-covenant transformation — it places the origin of covenant faithfulness at the level of God's own interior action within the person rather than the person's compliance with external demand. T2 confirms that covenant is constitutively somatic as well as inner — it cannot be reduced to a purely invisible spiritual reality because it is enacted, sealed, and transmitted through bodily acts and substances.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-034-014: T2 locates covenant in the constitutional organs (heart, mind, soul, mouth, body). T3 reveals which inner faculties operate within and through those locations. The T2 × T3 synthesis: the constitutiona…
findings.finding_value: T2 locates covenant in the constitutional organs (heart, mind, soul, mouth, body). T3 reveals which inner faculties operate within and through those locations. The T2 × T3 synthesis: the constitutional location (T2) and the faculty operation (T3) are not separate realities but different analytical views of the same inner-being reality. The heart (T2) is where the integrating functions of willing, knowing, moral evaluation, and affect operate (T3.6 volition, T3.2 cognition, T3.8 moral evaluation, T3.4 affect). The mind (T2) is where cognition (T3.2) and memory (T3.3) operate. The soul-totality (T2) corresponds to the conscientiousness and relational capacity (T3.10, T3.11) that engage the whole person. The constitutional location and the faculty operation are two descriptions of the same inner reality: location is where the faculty is housed; faculty is what the location does. The new covenant writes on the heart/mind (T2) and thereby transforms cognition toward knowing God (T3.2) — the constitutional location is the mechanism for the faculty transformation.

findings.session_b_note: Yes — explicitly and centrally. The primary mind-location: Isa 26:3 ("You keep him in perfect peace whose mind [yetser — formed thought/disposition] is stayed on you, because he trusts in you") — OBS-117-144. This is the most direct mind-peace statement in the corpus: perfect peace (shalom shalom) is the condition of the mind that is directed toward and stayed upon God. The yetser is the formed inclination or disposition of the mind — its sustained directedness. In the NT: Phili 4:7 — "the peace of God... will guard your hearts and your minds [noema — thoughts, understanding]" — the mind is jointly named as the territory peace guards alongside the heart; Rom 8:6 — "to set the mind [phronema] on the Spirit is life and peace" — the mind's orientation determines whether peace is present. The mind is the second major constitutional location of peace after the soul, and the most explicitly causal: directing the mind toward God produces peace; directing the mind elsewhere forfeits it.

findings.finding_value: T2 establishes the constitutional location of peace; T4 establishes the relational directions through which peace moves into and out of those locations. The synthesis: God gives peace (T4.1 → T2) by addressing the constitutional locations directly — the Aaronic blessing (Num 6:26) addresses the whole person; Joh 14:27 ("let not your hearts be troubled") addresses the heart specifically; Phili 4:7 ("peace will guard your hearts and minds") names both heart and mind as the guarded locations. The human receives peace (T4.4) through the same constitutional locations — the receptive soul (Psa 131:2, T2.2) and the directed mind (Isa 26:3, T2.4) are the reception points. The relational and constitutional analyses converge: peace moves through relational channels (T4) into constitutional locations (T2).

findings.finding_value: T2's body evidence (Psa 38:3 — no sha.lom in bones because of sin) connects directly to T6's finding that reconciliation constitutes relational peace (Col 1:20, Eph 2:14) — the same sha.lom that is absent from bones when sin is present is the sha.lom that reconciliation restores. The SHA.L root (T6.4.2) names completeness — and Psa 38:3's use of sha.lom for somatic soundness is directly rooted in this: sha.lom IS somatic completeness, sha.lom IS relational completeness, sha.lom IS covenantal completeness — one root, all dimensions. The constitutional and structural analyses confirm the same root-level truth from different angles.

findings.finding_value: T2's soul, heart, and mind location findings are each lexically grounded in T7's vocabulary analysis. Psa 131:2 (soul quieted — T2.2 evidence) features the same weaned-child posture named as the best human science image (T7.3.2). The heart location (T2.3 — Phili 4:7, Joh 14:27) uses the kardia vocabulary that T7 identifies as the Greek heart term carrying the full Hebrew lev range. The mind location (T2.4 — Isa 26:3 yetser, Rom 8:6 phronema, Phili 4:7 noema) uses three distinct vocabulary terms for different aspects of the mind's engagement — T7.1.4 confirms that the vocabulary distinguishes state/disposition/act. The constitutional analysis is lexically grounded at every point.

**[A1 — God Righteousness]** God's righteousness is not located in the human mind in A1's verse evidence. The mind is addressed by the standard of God's righteousness (Felix's mind was alarmed, Act 24:25, VSG M26-A1-006), but this is the mind as the organ affected, not the location of God's righteousness.

**[A2 — Human Righteousness]** Indirectly — the mind is addressed by the renewal that produces righteousness. The "renewing of your mind" (Rom 12:2, not directly in this cluster's verses but contextually adjacent to the righteousness material in Rom 12) enables the testing of what is right. The discernment material in A2-011 (speech and discernment as expressions of righteousness) implicates the mind as the organ of discernment. Not explicitly named but functionally engaged.

**[B — Moral Uprightness]** The uprightness material in Pro 2:9 — "then you will understand righteousness and justice and equity, every good path" (VSG 1212-002) — locates the capacity for moral understanding in the mind. Understanding is a mind-function; uprightness in B produces understanding. The mind is functionally engaged even if not explicitly named as the constitutional seat of uprightness.
**[C — Justification]** Justification is not located in the mind in the verse evidence. It is a judicial declaration affecting standing, not a cognitive event in the mind. Silence.
**[D — Avenging Justice]** Silence.
**[E — Condemnation]** Silence on explicit mind-location for condemnation.

**[F — Moral Reckoning]** Yes — explicitly. The logizomai faculty is cognitive-rational: it involves deliberation (Mar 11:31: "they discussed it with one another"), reasoning (Rom 4:3–11: the argument about credited righteousness), and inner self-address (Rom 6:11: "consider yourselves"). The reckoning faculty is a mind-function: its primary constitutional location is the mind as the organ of reasoning and deliberation. This is the sub-group most clearly and explicitly located in the mind.

**[G — Structural Opposites]** Indirectly — "they do not know how to do right" (Amo 3:10, VSG 1214-001) — the failure to know what is right is a mind-function failing. Wickedness includes a cognitive failure: the wicked do not understand (Dan 12:10, VSG 1225-001: "none of the wicked shall understand"). The mind is implicated in wickedness as the organ of moral cognition that has been shut down or distorted.

**[CLUSTER — T2.4]** E. The mind is a secondary constitutional location in M26, primarily engaged by F (the reckoning faculty's cognitive nature), and secondarily by A2 (discernment and understanding as expressions of righteousness) and G (the failure of moral cognition in wickedness). The primary location remains the heart; the mind is specifically the seat of F (moral reckoning) and the organ through which righteousness in A2 expresses itself in discernment.

findings.finding_value: M01-A reverential fear is not explicitly located in the mind in the programme's dimension vocabulary. The cognitive engagement (Pro 1:7: wisdom's foundation) describes the mind's orientation but does not locate fear in the mind as a constitutional site. The heart is the primary location.

M01-B has limited mind-location. Dan 4:5 (M01-B-VCG-01: "fear is produced by a dream that targets the mind — the visions of the head alarm the inner person, showing that dread can be generated internally through the mind's nocturnal experience"). This is a clear mind-location for one form of acute fear. Job 22:10 (M01-D boundary: "sudden terror overwhelms Job because snares surround him" — the inner shock strikes without conscious mind engagement).

M01-D has significant mind-location. Dan 4:19 (D-VCG-03: "dismay holds Daniel for a moment as **his thoughts** race — the inner impact of understanding a terrible message temporarily overrides speech and composure, with alarmed thoughts pressing on the inner person"); Dan 5:10 (dismay "originates in the inner life of thought"); Dan 7:28 ("dismay works through **Daniel's thoughts**"). The mind is a significant secondary constitutional location for M01-D.

M01-F has the strongest mind-location. The de.a.gah terms (H1674 — anxiety, worry) carry a cognitive-ruminating quality: Jer 49:23 ("anxiety seizes Damascus as troubled restlessness on hearing bad news — the inner state is compared to a churning sea unable to be still, showing anxiety as an agitated, **uncontrollable inner condition**"); 2Cor 12:20 anchor ("Paul's fear is an anticipatory dread rooted in **thought** about what he may find — engaging the mind with anxious expectation before the visit even happens"). The M01-F-VCG-05 pastoral anxiety is explicitly cognitive-anticipatory: it is rooted in thinking about a future encounter, not in present perception of threat.

The mind is a secondary but evidenced constitutional location for M01, primarily in: M01-D (dismay disrupting thought, Dan 4:19; 7:28) and M01-F (anxiety as cognitive rumination, de.a.gah; 2Cor 12:20). The mind is not the primary location for fear across the cluster — the heart is dominant — but M01-D and M01-F have clear mind-engagement.

Isa 42:25 (M02-B-VCG-06) provides the key evidence: "the people failed to perceive or take it to heart — the inner faculty of understanding is closed off, blocking recognition of divine wrath." This is not a location of anger in the mind but reveals the mind as the faculty through which the anger's significance is processed (or failed to be processed). The characteristic engages the mind as the faculty of recognition and understanding.

Isa 42:25 (M02-B-VCG-06) provides the key evidence: "the people failed to perceive or take it to heart — the inner faculty of understanding is closed off, blocking recognition of divine wrath." This is not a location of anger in the mind but reveals the mind as the faculty through which the anger's significance is processed (or failed to be processed). The characteristic engages the mind as the faculty of recognition and understanding.

Psa 37:1–8 (M02-B-VCG-05) suggests that fretting anger operates in the mind through comparison and evaluation of the wicked's prosperity — it is a cognitive-emotional state that begins with mental observation of perceived injustice.

The M03 corpus does not prominently evidence grief located in the mind. The mind as a constitutional site is not explicitly named in the verse meanings for M03's sub-groups. The characteristic is consistently located in soul, heart, spirit, and body — not in the cognitive/discerning mind as such.

One partial exception: godly grief in 2Cor 7:9-11 (M03-C-VCG-02) produces a "change of mind" (metanoia — repentance), indicating that grief engages the mind's capacity to revise its orientation. But the grief itself is not located in the mind; it reaches the mind through the transformative pathway.

**[CHAR-1]** S — No verse in the M04-A corpus explicitly names the mind (leb as rational faculty, dianoia, nous) as the constitutional locus of exultation. The leb-heart is named, but as the integrative affective-volitional centre rather than the rational-cognitive mind specifically.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Partially, as a precondition rather than the seat. Neh 8:12 — "great rejoicing, because they had understood the words that were declared to them" — comprehension (a mind-faculty act) produces joy; the joy is in the heart and expressed in eating and celebration, but the mind's understanding is its direct cause. The Ecclesiastes investigations (Ecc 2:1 — "I said in my heart, come now, I will test you with pleasure") show the mind directing the inner experiment, but the joy itself is located in the heart. No verse explicitly names the mind (as distinct from the heart-as-rational-faculty) as the seat of Joy.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Partially, through the cognitive-reframing acts: Jas 1:2 ("count it all joy") is a cognitive act — the counting/considering is a mental operation; Heb 12:2 ("for the joy that was set before him endured the cross") involves Christ's cognitive orientation toward the eschatological joy as the mental ground for endurance. These are not explicit mind-location statements but show cognitive involvement in sustaining Suffering-Joy.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes — more prominently than for any other M04 characteristic. The M04-L-VCG-02 corpus is essentially an exercise of the evaluative-cognitive faculty: weighing, comparing, judging. Exo 18:17 (Jethro's experienced assessment); Rut 2:22 (Naomi's prudential reasoning); Job 34:4 ("let us know among ourselves what is good" — explicitly cognitive discernment); Mic 6:8 ("he has told you, O man, what is good" — knowing is the precondition for doing). The evaluative "better than" comparatives throughout M04-L-VCG-02 and M04-O-VCG-02 are cognitive acts of comparison.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Partially, in the volitional-cognitive dimension: (1) **Job 34:4** — "let us know among ourselves what is good" — though this is in M04-L (Gladness), the adjacent wisdom-comparative corpus in M04-H-VCG-03 (Pro 3:15; 8:11 — "nothing you desire can compare with her" — wisdom as the surpassing object of che.phets) engages the mind's evaluative faculty; (2) **Ecc 12:10** — "the Preacher sought to find words of delight" — the mind's aesthetic-intellectual search for truth expressed in pleasurable form; (3) **1Ch 28:9** — "a willing mind" (cha.phets adj) as the cognitive-volitional inner orientation for serving God; (4) **Psa 111:2** — "great are the works of the Lord, studied by all who delight in them" — Delight engaging the mind toward sustained inquiry. Mind-location is present but secondary to soul and heart.

**[CHAR-5]** S — No verse in the M04-J or M04-K corpus explicitly names the mind as the constitutional seat of Pleasure. The wisdom-comparative register (M04-K-VCG-03) engages the evaluative faculty which is cognitively located, but the better-than comparatives operate through the heart-soul rather than naming "mind" explicitly. (2) Self-deceptive cognition: Jer 2:23 (VCG-02) — "how can you say, 'I am not unclean, I have not gone after the Baals'?" — the corporate community's cognitive self-assessment is distorted; they cannot correctly cognise their own defilement-state.

**[CHAR-4]** S — The 21-verse corpus does not explicitly name the mind (nous) as the site of the characteristic. The suppression of speech and hearing (Mar 9:25) impairs the communicative faculties adjacent to the mind, but the mind itself is not named as the site of inhabitation or suppression.

**[CLUSTER]** E — All four characteristics evidence mind-level engagement, but the mode differs significantly. Characteristic 1 engages the mind-adjacent discernment faculty: Lev 10:10/11:47 (M10c-B-VCG-01) require the cultivation of categorical distinction (clean/unclean) as a cognitive-moral capacity; Act 10:14 (M10c-B-VCG-05) shows this categorical knowledge as fully internalised in Peter's cognitive framework. Characteristic 2 engages the mind as a site of defilement: the Tit 1:15 cross-reference in VCG-03 names "both their minds and their consciences are defiled" — the mind's moral-assessment function is compromised. Characteristic 3 engages the mind through priestly cognitive failure: Eze 22:26 (VCG-05) — the priests' failure to distinguish holy from common is a collapse of institutional cognitive-discernment; and through self-deceptive cognition: Jer 2:23 (VCG-02) — the community cannot correctly cognise its own condition. Characteristic 4 is silent on mind-location: the spirit suppresses adjacent faculties (speech/hearing) but does not directly target the cognitive domain.

findings.session_b_note:
From the evidence available:

- **Memory function:** The most clearly engaged cognitive function. Jer 31:34 names memory specifically — God's memory of sin is what forgiveness terminates. The human analogue: the withheld grievance is a form of retained memory (the mind holds the record of the wrong); forgiveness releases the cognitive grip.
- **Accounting/reckoning:** The debt-language of the parable (Mat 18) engages the mind's calculative function — the account is kept, the sum is reckoned, then cancelled. Forgiveness is the cognitive act of closing the account.
- **Discernment:** Mar 2:7 — the scribes' failure to recognise Jesus's forgiveness-authority is a discernment failure. Genuine forgiveness requires the mind to recognise its source and nature correctly.

The mind's engagement with forgiveness is primarily through **memory and accounting** — both of which forgiveness terminates or resets rather than deepens. This distinguishes forgiveness from characteristics that primarily enhance cognition.

findings.session_b_note:
From the metriopatheō evidence: compassion engages the mind's function of discernment — knowing how to respond appropriately to the one who is weak or wayward, calibrating the expression of compassion to the situation. This is compassion shaped by understanding of the other's condition rather than by raw visceral response alone.

From the Hos 11:8 evidence: the divine inner deliberation involves something mind-like — the inner contest between judgment and compassion is not purely affective but involves a form of reasoning through competing claims. Whether this belongs strictly to the "mind" in the programme's framework or to the heart's integrating function is not resolved in the data.

**What is missing (P):** The mind's role in compassion — whether discernment, understanding of need, or moral reasoning — is not developed in the data beyond these partial signals. This is a gap; no SD pointer addresses it specifically.

findings.session_b_note:
Where fellowship engages the mind, it does so primarily through two pathways:

**Rhetorical construction:** The Job 16:4 group (cognitive construction) names a mental-linguistic activity — the deliberate joining of words for argumentative effect. This is the mind's constructive, productive function engaged in the service of fellowship vocabulary.

**Discernment of fellowship compatibility:** 2Cor 6:14's rhetorical structure (*what fellowship has righteousness with lawlessness?*) requires cognitive discernment — the mind evaluates relational compatibility based on moral categories. The person must reason through who can and cannot be in fellowship with them.

The mind's role in fellowship is therefore primarily discernment (evaluating compatibility) and construction (joining words, proclamation). It is not the primary constitutional home of fellowship, but it is engaged in its discernment and communicative extension.

findings.session_b_note: Mind-engagement reveals that love has a genuine cognitive dimension — it is not sub-cognitive. The cognitive dimension operates in three ways: (a) **knowledge as love's medium** — friendship/love constituted by mutual knowledge-sharing (Joh 15:15) means love opens access to the inner world of the other and requires the mind's engagement to receive what is shared; (b) **cognitive direction toward the lovely** — Phili 4:8 makes the mind's attentiveness to what is lovely a cognitive act in service of love's orientation; (c) **knowledge of God as love's fruit** — Hos 6:6 and Jer 31:34 (OBS-103-072) place knowledge of God as the companion of love, with the new covenant completing the knowledge that love currently mediates. Love is cognitively demanding in the biblical data — it requires and produces knowledge.

findings.session_b_note: Mercy engages the memory aspect of the mind — specifically the capacity to retain or release records of wrong. Divine mercy's operation in Heb 8:12 is a wilful memory-release: God will no longer remember sins. This is not cognitive failure but an active choice of memory-erasure as the concrete form of mercy. For the human recipient, the Eze 16:63 sequence (mercy received → remember → be confounded → silence) shows human memory of one's own guilt activated by received mercy, not erased. The mind's two memorial directions — the divine forgetting and the human remembering — are mercy's two memorial faces. OBS-111-035, OBS-111-039.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-111-002: T2 reveals mercy as a whole-person constitutional reality. No single level contains it: mercy originates at the spirit-soul interface, operates on the soul (addressing the nephesh-guilt), engages the …
findings.finding_value: T2 reveals mercy as a whole-person constitutional reality. No single level contains it: mercy originates at the spirit-soul interface, operates on the soul (addressing the nephesh-guilt), engages the heart through the visceral compassion vocabulary (splanchna), engages the mind through the memory-erasure mechanism (Heb 8:12), and operates through the body as both the medium of mercy-seeking (embodied posture) and the mechanism of mercy's effect (blood-atonement). The triadic constitutional movement (Q&A-065): inner disposition → soul-transformation → embodied expression. The key finding reading T2 as a whole is the receiving-before-generating origin structure (Q&A-062): mercy cannot be generated from within the person but must be received from outside and then expressed through the constitutional architecture. Body deposit: none. T5.7: formally closed.
