findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-002: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level …
findings.finding_value: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level (chesed as covenantal-soul character), heart-level (Hos 11:8 — "my heart recoils"), and somatic-level (re.chem, splanchnon) are all richly evidenced. The constitutional architecture is bottom-up: the womb and entrails are the originating ground; the soul and heart are the engagement points; the act is the constitutional expression. Four body-part functions are identified: constitutive (womb — the generative image of compassion), expressive (gut — the felt movement), indicative (Synoptic pattern — splanchnizō signals the compassion-event), and mediating (heart in Hos 11:8 — the deliberative locus where compassion and judgment contend). The four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) is uniquely evidenced in this registry — consistently inside-out and bottom-up. T2.8 established no body deposit; T5.7 is formally closed. The constitutional portrait confirms the sb_classification (soul-body interface) and extends it: compassion is the most somatically grounded characteristic in the programme, with its originating logic residing in the body's deepest interior.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-002: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary…
findings.finding_value: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary point of reception (Zec 12:10 — spirit of grace poured out), not the point of generation (grace originates with God — T2.9). The soul level is the site of standing (Rom 5:2 — "this grace in which we stand") and identity (1Cor 15:10 — "by the grace of God I am what I am"). The constitutional movement follows the SD021 four-faces model: divine disposition received at spirit level → relational standing established at soul level → specific capacity gifted → character expressed outward. Heart-location is partially evidenced via eusplanchnos (Eph 4:32 — the tenderheartedness that grace produces, reaching the affective-somatic interface). T2.7 produces a new finding: grace operates bidirectionally through the body-soul interface — soul-to-body (inner posture enacted somatically in prostration, fasting, sackcloth) and body-to-soul (somatic enactment deepening and confirming the inner posture). T2.8 remains open (body deposit question unresolved); T5.7 is left open accordingly. The constitutional origin analysis (T2.9) is the most analytically significant T2 finding: grace does not originate in the human constitutional system at any level — it arrives from outside. This is confirmed at T6 as the structural uniqueness of grace: the only characteristic that is not produced by any other inner-being characteristic.

findings.session_b_note: Mind-location engages two distinct aspects of the mind's function: (1) Reception and inscription: Heb 8:10 / 10:16 — the mind receives the inscribed law of the new covenant. The mind is not merely the organ of intellectual processing but the constitutional site where God places his covenant content. This is not understanding in the sense of cognitive effort but reception in the sense of constitutional change — the mind becomes the location in which covenantal truth is resident. (2) Hardening and blockage: 2 Cor 3:14 — the mind can be hardened against the covenant's content. The veil over the mind when reading the old covenant is a cognitive-constitutional blockage. The mind's function of discernment and understanding is impaired by this hardening; only Christ removes it (2 Cor 3:16). Together: the mind is the site of both covenantal inscription (when open and transformed) and covenantal blindness (when hardened). Covenant engages the mind's discerning and receiving functions in opposite directions depending on the person's covenantal standing.

findings.session_b_note: Although the mind is not explicitly named as kindness's constitutional location, the verse evidence shows kindness engaging the mind's cognitive-discernment function in two specific ways. First, Hos 6:6 — "I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings" — pairs chesed with knowledge of God (da'at Elohim). Genuine chesed requires a cognitive grasp of who God is; without this knowledge, the person substitutes ritual for the real inner disposition. The mind's function of knowing and discerning is therefore prerequisite to genuine kindness [OBS-099-088]. Second, Rom 2:4 — "not knowing that God's kindness is meant to lead you to repentance" — names cognitive failure as the mechanism by which received kindness is misappropriated. A correctly functioning cognitive faculty recognises the purpose of divine kindness; a failing one presumes on it [OBS-099-076]. What this reveals: kindness is not a mind-level characteristic but it requires the mind's knowing-function to operate correctly — it is cognitively dependent without being cognitively located.

findings.session_b_note: The mind-peace connection primarily engages the mind's directional function — the capacity of the mind to fix itself upon an object. Isa 26:3 (yetser) — the "stayed" or "fixed" mind: peace requires the mind to be anchored, not drifting. The mental act that produces peace is not thought-content (what the mind thinks about) but mental orientation (what the mind is stayed upon). Rom 8:6 (phronema — the mind's settled disposition/inclination) — the mind's habitual orientation toward the Spirit produces peace; toward the flesh produces death. Phili 4:7 (noema — the products of thought, understanding) — the mind's thoughts are what peace guards: peace stands sentinel over the mind's outputs. Three aspects: (1) Orientation (Isa 26:3) — where the mind is directed; (2) Disposition (Rom 8:6) — what the mind is habitually inclined toward; (3) Output (Phili 4:7) — the contents of thought that peace protects. The mind's peace is a total engagement — orientation, disposition, and output are all in view.

findings.session_b_note: Mind-location in Job 38:36 and group 872-003 engages the understanding and discernment aspect of the mind's function, not merely information-processing. God gives wisdom to the "inward parts" (tukhoth — hidden inner seat of understanding) and understanding to the "mind" (sekhwi). The cognitive function engaged is the capacity to perceive rightly — wisdom and understanding as the inner ability to process and interpret reality from within. The giving of wisdom/Spirit-to-instruct (Neh 9:20) also confirms this: the giving targets the formative-cognitive capacity, producing the ability to understand God's ways. Mind-location therefore reveals that this characteristic can deposit cognitive capacity: giving is not only material or relational — it can constitute the person's ability to know and discern.

Mind-location reveals that fellowship has a cognitive-evaluative dimension — the community of shared mind (homofrōn) is not merely emotional agreement but cognitive-evaluative alignment. The community thinks together.

The mind is a secondary but real constitutional location across M05. Where evidenced, it serves as: the faculty that discerns what each characteristic demands (M05-A, D); the faculty whose shared orientation constitutes communal life (M05-G); and the faculty that receives scriptural encouragement toward hope (M05-F). The cluster's characteristics are not sub-cognitive but neither are they primarily cognitive — they operate from the heart through the mind into relational expression.

**[F — Moral Reckoning]** The mind-location of the reckoning faculty reveals that moral reckoning is not primarily an affective or intuitive function — it is a rational-deliberative function. The person is called to think about their moral standing, to reason about what God has declared, and to apply that reasoning to action (Rom 6:11: count, then act). This gives righteousness in its F-mode a distinctively cognitive character that is different from the heart-located modes (A2, B). The cognitive-moral dimension of righteousness operates through the mind's deliberative capacity.

**[CLUSTER]** The dual location (heart as primary, mind as secondary for F) reveals that righteousness in M26 engages both the integrating-affective center (heart) and the deliberative-cognitive capacity (mind). The characteristic is neither purely affective nor purely cognitive — it requires both. The heart receives the inscribed law and generates the inner orientation of uprightness; the mind reckons, deliberates, and applies the declared reality to lived experience.

This is not the mind's proper function (trust-grounded discernment) but its distortion under anxiety.

Grace does not bypass the mind but reshapes what the mind knows about itself and its standing.

findings.finding_value: Pro 18:11's "in his imagination" reveals that inner closure operates partly through the mind's constructive function — the imagination (mas.kith — from a root meaning to look at, to view) is the faculty through which the wealthy person builds their mental stronghold. The mind creates the security that the material goods only nominally support. This is the mind's constructive-imaginative function being misdirected toward a false security.

findings.finding_value: M01-D's mind-location reveals fear engaging the thought function primarily: Dan 4:19 (alarmed thoughts overwhelming the ability to speak), Dan 7:28 (thoughts as the originating site of dismay-agitation). The dismay begins in the mind as comprehension and then destabilizes body and composure. This is the reverse of M01-E (where the body registers the inner state): in M01-D, the mind processes the terrible message and the processing produces the inner collapse.

M01-F's mind-location reveals anxiety engaging the thought function in its anticipatory mode: 2Cor 12:20 (anxious expectation before the visit — the mind projecting forward and processing possible negative outcomes). The de.a.gah terms describe a mind that cannot be stilled, circling around potential threats. This engages the understanding function (assessing what might happen) but in a disordered mode (unable to rest).

Mind-engagement by M01 is primarily in the thought function (M01-D: comprehending a terrible message; M01-F: anticipating a threatening future). The discernment and understanding functions are engaged indirectly — fear both enables and distorts discernment, depending on whether it is reverential (M01-A, which opens the mind to genuine knowledge) or anxious (M01-F, which distorts by excessive projection).

Isa 42:25 reveals that the mind's recognitive function (understanding, perception, heart-taking) is the faculty through which anger's significance must be processed. When this faculty is closed, the anger passes unrecognised. The mind engaged is the discernment-and-recognition faculty — not analytical reasoning but the deeper moral-perceptive function that reads the significance of what is happening.

Isa 42:25 reveals that the mind's recognitive function (understanding, perception, heart-taking) is the faculty through which anger's significance must be processed. When this faculty is closed, the anger passes unrecognised. The mind engaged is the discernment-and-recognition faculty — not analytical reasoning but the deeper moral-perceptive function that reads the significance of what is happening.

Where grief engages the mind (2Cor 7:9-11 — M03-C-VCG-02), it does so through the pathway of moral self-recognition: grief produces a change of mind (repentance) by enabling the person to see their situation differently — to recognise the moral weight of what has occurred. This is cognition in service of moral renovation, not cognition as the seat of grief.

**[CHAR-1]** S — Not directly evidenced. The cognitive element of exultation (knowing the ground of exultation — God's salvation, reign, presence) is present in the evidence but is the precondition for exultation rather than exultation's constitutional seat.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The mind's role in Joy is as a precondition and director: the person who understands God's acts (Neh 8:12), perceives divine goodness (Psa 97:8 — "Zion hears and is glad"), or comprehends the gospel (Act 13:48 — "the Gentiles heard this, they began rejoicing") has the cognitive reception that enables the heart's joy. The mind provides the true account of what is happening; the heart responds with joy. The two are consistently sequenced: perception/comprehension → heart's gladness → expressed rejoicing.

**[CHAR-7]** E — The mind's role in Suffering-Joy is specifically in the **eschatological reorientation** that sustains it: by cognitively holding the future joy (reward in heaven, glory to be revealed) as more real than present suffering, the mind enables the spirit's joy to hold. This is the specific cognitive contribution: not reasoning one's way into joy but orienting one's cognitive frame around eschatological truth that grounds the Spirit's work.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Mind-location reveals Gladness as uniquely cognitively-constituted among M04 characteristics. The evaluative-gladness faculty is a function of the person's reasoning, discerning, and comparing capacities. This explains why Gladness is less susceptible to direct command than Joy (Phili 4:4) — one cannot simply be commanded to evaluate correctly; one must be formed in the capacity for accurate moral and relational assessment. The cognitive dimension is why the wisdom literature is the primary carrier of M04-L: Proverbs and Ecclesiastes are fundamentally training texts for the evaluative faculty.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Mind involvement in Delight reveals the characteristic as having a wisdom-generating dimension when the object is God's works or truth: Psa 111:2 shows Delight driving study; Ecc 12:10 shows it driving the search for words. Delight in God's law (Psa 1:2 — meditation day and night) engages the mind as the instrument through which the heart's delight sustains itself. Delight does not bypass the mind but channels the mind toward its object — it is the heart-level orientation that directs the mind's engagement.

**[CHAR-5]** S — Not directly evidenced; the cognitive-evaluative engagement with Pleasure (M04-K-VCG-03) operates through wisdom-formation of the heart and soul rather than through an explicitly named mind. The absence of explicit mind-location confirms Pleasure as primarily affective-receptive rather than cognitively-mediated (unlike Gladness whose primary dimension is cognitive-evaluative).

**[CHAR-6]** E — Mind-location reveals Wonder as the characteristic that specifically arises at the cognitive boundary — it is the response when the mind's comprehension reaches its limit. This makes Wonder unique in M04: it is the only characteristic that is constitutively defined by the cognitive faculty's encounter with what exceeds it. The mind is both the faculty that encounters Wonder (by trying to comprehend what is incomprehensible) and the faculty that is formed by Wonder (into humility and sustained contemplation). Isa 29:14 shows that human wisdom/discernment can actually become an obstacle to Wonder when it becomes presumptuous — the formed mind must be humble to remain genuinely wonder-capable.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Mind-location reveals the cluster's cognitive architecture. Three findings: (1) **Gladness and Wonder as cognitive poles** — Gladness (Char 3) is the most cognitively-constituted positive characteristic in M04; Wonder (Char 6) is the most cognitively-challenged. They represent the two ends of the cluster's cognitive range: Gladness where cognition functions correctly and produces settled brightness; Wonder where cognition reaches its limit and produces arrested astonishment; (2) **Joy's cognitive prerequisite** — the Neh 8:12 pattern (comprehension → Joy) confirms that Joy is cognitively grounded but not cognitively primary; the mind provides the true account; the heart responds with Joy; (3) **Delight as cognitive-driver** — Delight (Char 4) is uniquely positioned among the primarily-affective characteristics as the one whose sustained presence drives cognitive engagement (Psa 1:2's meditation; Psa 111:2's study). Delight in God is the most powerful driver of theological and spiritual cognition in the cluster.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Mind-location reveals that shame is not merely emotional — it involves cognitive assessment of one's standing and the cognitive crash when false beliefs are exposed. The idolatry-shame passages evidence a specific cognitive pattern: when the mind's confident belief in a false object is suddenly exposed as groundless, the cognitive disorientation (confusion, bewilderment) is the shame-experience. This means shame can be the cognitive-emotional response to cognitive failure — the inner collapse of a worldview that cannot sustain the weight of reality.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The cognitive dimension is evidenced in the confusion/disorientation register: the defeated and humiliated "go in confusion" (Isa 45:16), are "dismayed and confounded" (2Ki 19:26; Isa 37:27). The cognitive faculty of confident orientation collapses under enforced humiliation — the person loses their bearings. This is a mind-level effect of CHAR-2.

---

**[CHAR-3]** E — CHAR-3 engages the cognitive faculty in the worth-assessment process: to dishonour another is to make a cognitive judgment about their worth (assigning them less worth than they have). The Luk 18:4 judge "acknowledges to himself" that he lacks fear and regard — the cognitive self-recognition of the absent-faculty.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — The mind (nous/dianoia) is CHAR-4's primary constitutional location: the moral-evaluative judgment is a cognitive act, assessing conduct against a standard. Phili 3:19 — "minds set on earthly things" — names the mind as the site of the evaluative inversion. Rom 1:26-27's "dishonorable passions" engage the cognitive faculty in assessing whether desires are properly ordered.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — The contempt-er's cognitive faculty is engaged: the worth-assessment judgment (this person is of no account) is a cognitive act. 1Cor 6:4 — "those who have no standing in the church" — is a cognitive assessment about standing. Rom 14:3/10 — despising a brother who eats or abstains — is a cognitive-evaluative judgment about the other person's worth or standing before God.

---

**[CHAR-6]** S — CHAR-6 does not specifically engage the mind (nous/dianoia) as its primary constitutional location — the emphasis throughout is on the heart and the hands rather than cognitive operations. Silent on mind as the specific locus of CHAR-6.

---

**[CLUSTER]** E — All six engage the cognitive faculty, with varying prominence. Char 4 is primarily cognitive (the evaluative operation is a cognitive act). Chars 1, 3, 5 engage cognition primarily in worth-assessment and self-assessment. Char 2 engages it in the cognitive collapse of the humiliated (confusion, dismay — Jer 49:23; Isa 37:27). Char 6 engages it in the cognitive self-assessment that constitutes the innocence-claim. Cluster-level cognitive theme: every M07 characteristic involves some assessment of standing — of one's own standing before God (Chars 1, 6), of another's worth (Chars 3, 5), of conduct's moral quality (Char 4), of one's position relative to others (Char 2). The shame-field is irreducibly cognitive: it cannot be reduced to pure affect or pure social mechanics but involves ongoing assessment of standing, worth, and moral quality.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — Mind-location reveals that CHAR-1 operates in the cognitive faculty primarily through distorted self-assessment — the mind evaluating the self as above others or above God. Psa 10:4 (vc=34074, M08-A2-VCG-02): pride restructures the cognitive content so completely that "all his thoughts are, 'there is no God'" — CHAR-1 in the mind produces a total reorientation of the cognitive field, displacing God from the inner horizon and replacing him with the self's own self-sufficient assessment. Eze 28:17 (vc=34047, M08-A1-VCG-02): "you corrupted your wisdom for the sake of your splendour" — CHAR-1 damages the mind's highest function (wisdom/discernment). Luk 1:51 (vc=33930, M08-A1-VCG-03): arrogance located in the "thoughts" confirms the cognitive register — CHAR-1 is not merely a feeling or impulse but a structured pattern of self-elevating thought.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The partial mind-location evidence reveals that CHAR-2 involves a cognitive distortion of the self's actual standing: Obd 3 (vc=34108, M08-B-VCG-02) and Jer 49:16 (vc=34115, M08-B-VCG-02) both name "self-deception" as the cognitive consequence of CHAR-2's heart-location — the mind evaluates the self as secure when it is not. Psa 86:14 (vc=34097): the mind's failure to "set God before" it means CHAR-2 operates in a cognitive vacuum where divine authority is absent from the inner perceptual field.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Mind-location reveals that CHAR-3 requires a cognitive process (self-assessment, self-comparison, attribution) to generate its content. The boaster's cognitive faculty evaluates the self as worth boasting about — a specific cognitive act of self-assessment that produces the content of the boast. The failure of this cognitive process (lack of understanding in self-comparison; misattribution of received goods as self-generated) is what makes the VCG-01 boast morally wrong.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Mind-location reveals that CHAR-4 is constitutively an epistemic failure: the mind's self-assessment function is the specific faculty that CHAR-4 distorts. Col 2:18 (vc=33941): "his sensuous mind" — the mind in its fleshly orientation inflates without factual basis. Rom 12:3 (vc=60866): "think with sober judgment, each according to the measure of faith" — the commanded alternative identifies accurate cognitive self-referencing as what CHAR-4 denies. CHAR-4 engages the mind's self-assessment, self-comparison, and self-definition functions — the very faculties that should produce accurate self-knowledge.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The partial mind-location evidence reveals that CHAR-5's structural-power medium generates a specific cognitive claim of self-sufficiency: the nation or person with structural power makes an inner cognitive assessment of themselves as complete, secure, and above external threat (Obd 3: "who will bring me down?"). This cognitive claim is the mind-level expression of CHAR-5's heart-level pride — and like CHAR-4's fusioō, it is self-deceptive (Obd 3: "the pride of your heart has deceived you").

**[CLUSTER]** E — The universal mind-engagement across all five confirms that M08 is constitutively a cognitive disorder cluster — not in the sense that all five are primarily cognitive (only CHAR-4 is), but in the sense that every form of pride involves a distortion of the mind's self-assessment and perception functions. The cluster comparison reveals that the cognitive distortion takes different forms per characteristic: perceptive closure to God (CHAR-1), self-deceptive overconfidence (CHAR-2), misattribution of received goods (CHAR-3), inflated self-picture (CHAR-4), ontological self-sufficiency claim (CHAR-5). All five corrupt the mind's capacity to perceive accurately — making M08 as a whole a cluster that targets the mind's truth-processing faculty across its five sub-forms.

**[CHAR-2]** E — 2Cor10:5 reveals that submission engages the mind's *evaluative and reasoning function*. The "arguments and lofty opinions raised against the knowledge of God" are intellectual-evaluative constructs — the mind's capacity to generate self-justifying reasoning that resists divine authority. Submission requires capturing this evaluative capacity and reorienting it under Christ's authority. The mind's function in this characteristic is not merely to understand the command but to surrender its own reasoning to the authority's claim — which is a higher-level cognitive act. 2Cor10:6 ("when your obedience is complete") positions the community's collective cognitive-volitional state as the determining factor.

**[CHAR-3]** S — The evidence is silent on explicit mind-location (see T2.4.1). The cognitive dimension is implied by the characteristic's requirement for genuine moral self-knowledge, but the mind is not named as a constitutional site in this corpus.

**[CHAR-4]** S — Mind-location is not explicitly evidenced in §3.C. The enabling cognitive self-assessment (awareness of shared weakness) is implied but not located in the mind as a named constitutional site.
**[CHAR-5]** S — Mind-location is not evidenced in §3.D.
**[CHAR-6]** S — Mind-location is not evidenced in §3.E.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The Phili2:3 evidence reveals that humility engages the mind's evaluative function: the cognitive act of *counting* (hēgeomai — reckoning, considering, evaluating) others as more significant is a deliberate cognitive operation. The Col2:18 evidence reveals that the mind can be the site of false humility's corruption: the "sensuous mind" inflated while performing humility. Together these evidences reveal that humility engages the mind's capacity for honest self-assessment and other-evaluation — the function of realistic comparative judgment. The mind's role is to arrive at an accurate rather than self-inflated assessment of relative worth; humility is the disposition that enables this accurate assessment.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The two characteristics with explicit mind-engagement reveal that when M09 characteristics engage the mind, it is specifically the evaluative and reasoning function rather than the perceptive or imaginative function. Submission (CHAR-2) engages the mind most explicitly: 2Cor10:5 — "take every thought captive to obey Christ" — the mind's reasoning capacity generates self-justifying arguments against God's authority; submission requires capturing the evaluative mind and reorienting it under Christ's claim. This is the highest-level cognitive act the cluster evidences: not merely understanding a command but surrendering the mind's own reasoning apparatus to legitimate authority. Humility (CHAR-1) engages the mind's evaluative function through the cognitive act of counting others more significant (Phili2:3 — hēgeomai), and the corrupt sensuous mind (Col2:18) is the site of false humility's distortion. The four characteristics without explicit mind-location (CHAR-3, CHAR-4, CHAR-5, CHAR-6) imply cognitive engagement but do not name the mind as a constitutional site. Cluster-level: the mind as distinct constitutional faculty is most clearly a battleground in the submission register of M09 — the cluster's most cognitively explicit characteristic is CHAR-2.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — The evidence implicates the mind's *discernment and deliberative* function: sinning occurs when the will acts without adequate moral deliberation. Psa 4:4 — pondering (reflective deliberation) is the remedy; the absence of pondering allows anger to become sinful action. Ecc 5:6 — the mouth outrunning the mind produces sinful speech. Joseph in Gen 39:9 shows the opposite: the mind actively deliberates ("how then can I do this?") and the named moral content (great wickedness, sin against God) provides the deliberative check. The mind's deliberative function — its capacity to name an act as wrong before committing it — is what wilful sinning must overcome or bypass.

**[CHAR-10]** S — The absence of mind-location vocabulary is consistent with the mechanisms' character: enticement operates through the sub-rational desire-faculty (below the level of explicit cognitive deliberation); hypocrisy operates through social-identity performance (not primarily cognitive); apostasy operates through the will's departure (not primarily cognitive). The mechanisms characteristically bypass or operate below the level of explicit rational deliberation.

**[CHAR-11]** E — Mind-location (Rom 7:23/25 — mind versus law of sin; Rom 3:20 — knowledge of sin through the law) reveals a critical distinction within the condition's operation: the mind can know God's law and even will to comply with it (Rom 7:25 — "I myself serve the law of God with my mind") while the condition operates in the members against what the mind knows. This produces the characteristic divided-person experience of Romans 7: the condition is not ignorance (the mind knows) but constitutional incapacity (the members do not comply). The condition thus operates *around* the mind rather than exclusively *through* it — which is why knowledge alone (intellectual) cannot resolve the condition.

**[CHAR-12]** S — The absence of mind-location reflects that sin's enslaving power in this corpus operates at the constitutional-volitional and allegiance levels rather than primarily through cognitive processes. The mind may know the enslaved condition (intellectually aware) but the enslaving power is not primarily a cognitive phenomenon in this corpus.

**[CHAR-13]** E — Mind-location (Gen 41:9 — remembering offenses; Job 13:23 — seeking to know the record; Pro 24:9 — devising folly as sin) reveals that the divine record engages the mind at two points: (1) the mind's acts can create entries in the record (Pro 24:9 — cognitive devising of folly is sin); (2) the mind can partially access the record through memory (Gen 41:9) but cannot fully enumerate it without divine disclosure (Job 13:23 — needing God to "make me know my transgression and my sin").

**[CHAR-14]** E — Mind-location (Lev 4:14 — recognition as prerequisite; Act 2:38 — repentance as metanoia) reveals that the seeking dimension requires a cognitive component: the mind must recognise the sin and reorient toward God. Metanoia (repentance) is precisely the mind's change of direction — the mind that was directed toward sin now turns toward God. The mind does not merely register the seeking intellectually; it undergoes the directional reorientation that is the seeking's volitional dimension.

**[CHAR-15]** E — Mind-location (Psa 78:32 — unbelief despite wonders) reveals that the generational sinning pattern operates partly through the mind's persistent refusal to draw the correct cognitive conclusion from God's actions. The mind that has witnessed divine wonders and still does not believe is exhibiting a constitutively resistant cognitive orientation — a mind-level component of the generational pattern that makes it self-perpetuating: even extraordinary evidence does not break the inherited unbelief-pattern in the mind.

**[CHAR-16]** E — Mind-location (Amo 9:10 — cognitive self-deception about consequences; Joh 9:25 — cognitive uncertainty about sinner-label) reveals that the sinner-identity engages the mind in its self-assessment function: the habitual sinner's mind generates false security (Amo 9:10), while the observer's mind must exercise careful judgment about applying the sinner-label (Joh 9:25 — "I do not know"). The mind is the faculty through which the sinner either correctly or incorrectly assesses their own moral status.

**[CHAR-17]** E — Mind-location (Lev 5:2/3/4 — "comes to know"; Gen 42:21 — cognitive retrospection) reveals that the guilt-state requires a cognitive trigger: the person must come to know the violation before guilt-recognition occurs. Guilt is not merely the feeling of having done wrong but requires the mind's engagement with the knowledge of what was done. This is why Lev 5:17/19 is significant: "though he did not know it, then realizes his guilt" — even guilt from unknown violations becomes subjectively active once the mind acquires knowledge.

**[CHAR-18]** E — Mind-location (Psa 36:2 — self-flattery; Hos 12:8 — false self-assessment; Job 13:23 — need for divine disclosure) reveals that the mind's self-assessment of iniquity is constitutively unreliable without divine input. The mind flatters itself (Psa 36:2), generates false confidence (Hos 12:8), and requires God to reveal what it cannot see on its own (Job 13:23 — "make me know"). This unreliability is a symptom of the iniquity's effect on the mind itself: the accumulated crime distorts the very cognitive faculty that would assess it.

**[CHAR-19]** E — Mind-location (Rom 4:15 — knowledge-prerequisite; Isa 46:8 — recall failure; Job 13:23 — needs divine disclosure) reveals that transgression engages and distorts the cognitive faculty at two levels: (1) it requires the mind's prior knowledge of the law to be technically possible (Rom 4:15); (2) it progressively suppresses the mind's capacity to accurately assess its own transgression-state (Isa 46:8 — transgressors need to "recall it to mind"). The mind is both the prerequisite for transgression and a casualty of its sustained operation.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The mind's pattern of engagement — present in realisation, absent during the sinning — reveals that unintentional sinning is constitutively a *knowledge-gap event*. The act and the mind's available information are out of alignment at the moment of sinning. When the mind's knowledge catches up to the act's moral reality (Lev 5:5 — realises; Num 22:34 — did not know, now knows), the sinning becomes retrospectively identified and the conscience engages. The characteristic thus operates in the space between what the mind knows and what the act requires — a space that the prescribed education in God's commandments (Lev 4:2 — "the Lord's commandments about things not to be done") is designed to narrow over time.

**[CHAR-20]** E — Mind-location (Psa 73:15 — deliberating whether to speak; Psa 59:5 — plotting evil) reveals that faithlessness engages the cognitive-deliberative faculty in two ways: (1) the mind can deliberate whether to speak (Psa 73:15) and thereby either commit or avoid betrayal through speech; (2) the mind can plan treachery (Psa 59:5 — those who treacherously plot evil). The mind is both the faculty that can restrain faithlessness through honest deliberation and the faculty that can plot and execute it.

**[CHAR-21]** E — Mind-location (1Ti 6:5 — mind depraved; 2Cor 11:3 — thoughts led astray; Isa 29:16 — cognitive inversion) reveals that CHAR-21's perversion operates at the level of the mind's basic cognitive function: the capacity to know God as creator (Isa 29:16), to hold truth (1Ti 6:5 — "deprived of the truth"), and to maintain sincere devotion (2Cor 11:3). When the mind is corrupted, the person cannot accurately perceive the most fundamental realities (creator-creature relationship, truth). This makes CHAR-21's mind-corruption the most epistemically devastating dimension.

**[CHAR-22]** E — Mind-location (Psa 64:6 — inward mind devising; Job 18:21 — not knowing God) reveals that injustice operates at the cognitive level through two mechanisms: (1) *active deliberation toward wrong* (Psa 64:6 — "diligent search" for injustice — the mind's analytical capacity deployed toward planning wrong); (2) *God-knowledge deficit* (Job 18:21 — "knows not God") — the mind's failure to know God produces the characteristic's enabling condition.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Mind-location (2Sa 19:20; Dan 9:5) reveals that confession is partly a *cognitive differentiation event*: the mind must identify the sin, name its character (foolishness — Num 12:11; betrayal of innocent blood — Mat 27:4; rebellion against commandments — Dan 9:11), and articulate its dimensions. The more complete the cognitive articulation, the more complete the confession. Dan 9:5's cascade ("sinned... done wrong... acted wickedly... rebelled... turning aside") shows the mind's differentiating function at full operation within confession — not merely "I did something wrong" but a precise taxonomy of what the wrong involved. The mind provides the vocabulary and the structure through which conscience's recognition is named.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Mind-location reveals that conscience suppression has a *cognitive dimension*: the failure to register sin is not only a conscience-faculty failure but a knowledge failure. 1Cor 15:34 — "no knowledge of God" — the mind's knowledge of God is the prerequisite for the moral discernment that conscience suppression lacks. Without knowing God, the standard against which sin is measured is absent from the mind, making conscience-activation impossible. Jer 16:10 — the mind that asks "what sin?" genuinely does not know — its cognitive-moral categories have been so deformed that the question is sincere. The mind-location shows that conscience suppression affects the cognitive faculty's ability to process moral reality accurately.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Mind-location (Heb 10:26; 1Ki 16:31) reveals that refusal to repent can operate through a corrupt cognitive assessment (minimising the sin's gravity — 1Ki 16:31) and through deliberate choice against available knowledge (Heb 10:26 — knowing the truth and sinning deliberately). The mind's evaluative function either produces false verdicts that enable the refusal (minimisation) or is bypassed/overridden by the will in its deliberate sinning mode. In Heb 10:26, the knowledge is present and correct; the will acts against it. The mind-location reveals that refusal to repent is not always a problem of ignorance (cf CHAR-4 — Conscience suppression) but can involve the will acting against what the mind knows.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Mind-location (1Jo 3:6; 1Sa 2:25) reveals that habitual defection produces *epistemic consequences*: the sustained sinning pattern either reveals or produces the inability to know and see God. 1Jo 3:6's "never seen him or known him" is not a momentary perceptual failure but a fundamental epistemic blindness correlating with the habitual sinning — the mind's capacity for theological-relational knowledge is impaired by or indicative of the habitual sinning condition. Similarly, 1Sa 2:25's non-listening shows the mind's receptive capacity being closed against corrective input.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Mind-location (Deu 20:18 — teaching mode) reveals that contagious sin can operate through the cognitive-instructional channel: the sinning practices are transmitted as *knowledge* to the recipient community, whose mind receives and internalises the content. The teaching mode is particularly insidious because it operates through the mind's designed learning capacity — the God-given ability to learn from others is turned toward learning sinning practices. This differs from the authority-structural mode (Kings corpus) in that it is explicitly cognitive-pedagogical: the Canaanite nations are not just modelling but actively teaching.

**[CHAR-8]** S — The absence of mind-location reflects the corpus's action-reporting literary form. The political decision-making process (what the revolting parties thought and calculated) is not addressed; only the action and its consequences are named.

**[CHAR-9]** E — Mind-location (1Ti 6:4 — "understands nothing"; Mat 15:19 — "evil thoughts") reveals that sinful speech is accompanied by and enabled by cognitive failure: the slanderer does not properly understand the moral reality of what they are doing or the nature of the God they are speaking against. 1Ti 1:13 — Paul's blasphemy was from "ignorant unbelief" — cognitive-epistemic ignorance as the enabling condition. The mind's role is not the origin of sinful speech (the heart is) but the cognitive framework within which sinful speech is enabled or constrained.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Mind-location reveals that wickedness-as-settled-person-identity engages and corrupts the deliberative and perceptive functions of the mind. The deliberative corruption is most visible in Pro 12:5 (deceptive counsels), Job 21:16 (morally alien counsel-frame), and Isa 5:23 (VCG-05 — the corrupt judicial mind that acquits the guilty for a bribe). The perceptive corruption is visible in Pro 4:19 (blindness to what causes stumbling), Dan 12:10 (the wicked "cannot understand" in the eschatological refining process), and Isa 26:10 ("does not see the majesty of the Lord"). The mind-location reveals that wickedness corrupts not only what the person chooses but what they can perceive and reason about — the characteristic progressively disables the cognitive apparatus through which moral reality would otherwise be apprehended.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Mind-location reveals that evil as constitutional inner nature engages and corrupts the cognitive functions of understanding and discernment. Col 1:21 (vc=14424 — VCG-06) names the mind as "hostile" — the relational-cognitive orientation of the mind is the point of corruption. 1Ti 6:4 (vc=14470 — VCG-06) shows the mind as "devoid of understanding" when inflated with conceit — the characteristic occupies the cognitive space where understanding should reside, producing evil suspicions in its place. The mind-location reveals the characteristic corrupting two mind functions: the evaluative-relational function (making the mind hostile to others) and the epistemic function (replacing understanding with evil suspicions). The mind-location is secondary to the heart-location but directly evidenced.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Mind-location reveals that abomination specifically engages the deliberative-planning function of the mind. Pro 15:26 (vc=1679 — VCG-02) targets "thoughts" (machashevot) — deliberate planned thought rather than involuntary passing cognition. The wicked person's deliberate moral reasoning is itself an abomination. The cognitive failure of Isa 44:19 (vc=65961 — VCG-05) — "no one considers" — reveals that the absence of reflective moral cognition enables abomination: the person who does not stop to consider what they are doing proceeds into abomination through cognitive abdication. Mind-location shows the characteristic engaging the evaluative-deliberative mind rather than mere perceptual cognition.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Mind-location reveals that idolatrous abomination corrupts the cognitive-evaluative function that assesses gravity. Eze 8:17 (vc=65980 — VCG-05): treating abomination as a light thing shows that the evaluative cognitive faculty — the capacity to assess moral and spiritual weight — has been dulled. The characteristic also suppresses the memory function: Eze 16:22 (vc=65985 — VCG-05) — not remembering origins; Eze 16:43 (vc=65987 — VCG-05) — failure to remember youth. The mind-location reveals the characteristic as corrupting specifically the evaluative and memorial cognitive functions — the person can no longer correctly assess the gravity of what they do or recall the covenantal history that should check their idolatrous attachment.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Mind-location reveals that iniquity as active scheming engages the deliberative-planning function of the mind — specifically the capacity for premeditated scheming and devising. Mic 2:1 (vc=38217 — VCG-02): "those who devise wickedness and work evil on their beds" — the devising is nocturnal planning, using the quiet of the night for deliberate mental scheming. Eze 11:2 (vc=38193 — VCG-02): "devise iniquity and give wicked counsel" — the cognitive-planning function produces both the inner scheme and the social counsel that extends it. Isa 59:7 (vc=38203 — VCG-02): "thoughts are thoughts of iniquity" — the thought-life is entirely colonised by iniquitous content. The mind-location reveals the characteristic as one that specifically co-opts the deliberative-planning faculty — the mind's highest-level cognitive function — for the production of evil.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Jude 10 (vc=14355 — VCG-01) reveals that the characteristic specifically engages the mind's comprehension-and-discernment function — but through its failure. The characteristic fills the gap left by absent understanding with contemptuous speech: what is not understood is blasphemed rather than humbly acknowledged as unknown. The mind's discernment function (the capacity to accurately recognise and assess what one encounters) has been bypassed — replaced by the instinctual level of unreasoning animals. Mind-location reveals the characteristic as a cognitive-regressive phenomenon: it operates below the level of rational discernment, expressing itself through contempt where understanding should be.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Mind-location across the cluster reveals the cognitive faculty's corruption in three distinct modes: (a) cognitive bypass — Char 6 (Jude 10): blasphemy filling the gap where understanding should be; (b) cognitive colonisation — Char 5 (Isa 59:7): thoughts wholly constituted by iniquity; (c) cognitive inversion — Char 3 (Pro 15:26) and Char 6's false-attribution mode (Rom 3:8 — VCG-02): deliberate cognitive misrepresentation producing false verdicts. The cluster reveals that the mind's engagement with inner evil spans from complete bypass (contempt substituting for absent understanding) through active colonisation (thoughts of iniquity) to strategic inversion (producing false moral verdicts). Chars 5 and 6 share the cognitive-scheming dimension; Chars 3 and 6 share the cognitive-inversion dimension.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The relevant mind-function is discernment — the capacity to distinguish, categorise, and apply the clean/unclean boundary correctly. The purity laws function as a training curriculum for this faculty: sustained engagement with the clean/unclean distinction in its many sub-categories (which animals are clean, what transmission patterns produce defilement, which conditions are permanent and which temporary) forms the person in a structured pattern of categorical perception. Peter's Act 10:14 conviction ("I have never eaten anything that is common or unclean") shows this categorical knowledge as fully internalised — not a rule consulted but a deeply embedded inner judgment.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The mind-location (via Tit 1:15 reference in VCG-03) reveals the characteristic as engaging the mind's moral-assessment function: the defiled mind cannot correctly assess what is pure, because the standard for moral evaluation has itself been compromised. The defiled mind produces defiled moral judgement. This is the deepest cognitive impact of the characteristic: it does not merely distort behaviour but corrupts the inner instrument of moral perception and judgement. Within §3, 1Cor 8:7 (VCG-03) shows the conscience (the mind's moral-witness function) as the locus of defilement from acting against inner conviction.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The mind-location reveals that the corporate/covenantal defilement-state both requires cognitive formation (the clean/unclean distinction must be taught — Eze 44:23 VCG-05, Eze 22:26 VCG-05) and corrupts cognitive self-assessment (Jer 2:23 — the community cannot see its own condition). The priestly failure at Eze 22:26 is cognitive: the priests who should maintain and teach the clean/unclean framework have failed in their cognitive-formative role. This reveals the characteristic as inhabiting the cognitive domain at two levels: the knowledge-formation dimension (teaching discernment) and the self-knowledge dimension (recognising one's own condition).
**[CHAR-4]** S — Not evidenced. See T2.4.3.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's mind-location findings reveal two functions of the cognitive faculty in relation to defilement: the categorical-discernment function (Chars 1, 3) and the self-assessment function (Chars 2, 3). The categorical-discernment function is what the defilement-state requires for proper management: knowing the clean/unclean distinction (Char 1 — Lev 10:10), and knowing the holy/common distinction to prevent defilement (Char 3 — Eze 22:26/44:23). The self-assessment function is what the advanced defilement-state corrupts: the ability to correctly assess one's own moral condition (Char 2 — Tit 1:15: "nothing is pure to the defiled"; Char 3 — Jer 2:23: self-deceptive denial). The cluster's mind-level insight: the cognitive faculty is both the tool for managing defilement (categories of clean/unclean) and the victim of advanced defilement (inability to assess one's own condition). The characteristic simultaneously requires cognitive formation and corrupts the cognitive capacity it requires.

findings.finding_value: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level (chesed as covenantal-soul character), heart-level (Hos 11:8 — "my heart recoils"), and somatic-level (re.chem, splanchnon) are all richly evidenced. The constitutional architecture is bottom-up: the womb and entrails are the originating ground; the soul and heart are the engagement points; the act is the constitutional expression. Four body-part functions are identified: constitutive (womb — the generative image of compassion), expressive (gut — the felt movement), indicative (Synoptic pattern — splanchnizō signals the compassion-event), and mediating (heart in Hos 11:8 — the deliberative locus where compassion and judgment contend). The four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) is uniquely evidenced in this registry — consistently inside-out and bottom-up. T2.8 established no body deposit; T5.7 is formally closed. The constitutional portrait confirms the sb_classification (soul-body interface) and extends it: compassion is the most somatically grounded characteristic in the programme, with its originating logic residing in the body's deepest interior.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-002: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary…
findings.finding_value: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary point of reception (Zec 12:10 — spirit of grace poured out), not the point of generation (grace originates with God — T2.9). The soul level is the site of standing (Rom 5:2 — "this grace in which we stand") and identity (1Cor 15:10 — "by the grace of God I am what I am"). The constitutional movement follows the SD021 four-faces model: divine disposition received at spirit level → relational standing established at soul level → specific capacity gifted → character expressed outward. Heart-location is partially evidenced via eusplanchnos (Eph 4:32 — the tenderheartedness that grace produces, reaching the affective-somatic interface). T2.7 produces a new finding: grace operates bidirectionally through the body-soul interface — soul-to-body (inner posture enacted somatically in prostration, fasting, sackcloth) and body-to-soul (somatic enactment deepening and confirming the inner posture). T2.8 remains open (body deposit question unresolved); T5.7 is left open accordingly. The constitutional origin analysis (T2.9) is the most analytically significant T2 finding: grace does not originate in the human constitutional system at any level — it arrives from outside. This is confirmed at T6 as the structural uniqueness of grace: the only characteristic that is not produced by any other inner-being characteristic.

findings.session_b_note: Explicitly noting: the evidence does not locate the kindness disposition in the mind. The heart is the named constitutional site (Pro 3:3). This distinction — between a characteristic's location and the faculties it engages — is analytically important: kindness is heart-located, mind-dependent, and Spirit-produced.

findings.session_b_note:
The data surfaces one additional soul-level location not captured under heart or mind:

**Conscience:** The guilt-forgiveness structural pairing (54 shared verses with R073 guilt) implies that forgiveness operates in relation to the conscience — the inner witness that registers the moral debt. Q089 (partial answer not in this data, but Q035 full answer) establishes guilt as the "accumulated debt-state" that forgiveness cancels. The conscience is the faculty that holds and registers the guilt-state; forgiveness therefore operates at the conscience level as the resolution of what conscience has registered.

OBS-064-030 also names the visceral compassion (*splagchnizomai*, Mat 18:27) as the felt origin of the act of forgiving — the gut-level compassion that moves the master to release the debt. This is close to the affective/conscience boundary.

*New finding:* The conscience as the site at which guilt is held and forgiveness is received has not been assembled as an observation in the existing analysis. The tight structural pairing with guilt (R073) strongly implies this, but it has not been named explicitly. This may be a fruitful observation for Session B or Session D synthesis.

findings.session_b_note:
Yes — the will and the conscience are both implicated by the data, though not named in those terms explicitly.

**Will as soul subset:** The chus (pity) vocabulary — "your eye shall not pity" (Deut 19:13; Ezek 7:4) — locates the compassion-impulse in a place that the will can engage or override. The phrase "your eye shall not pity" addresses an inner faculty that sees and responds — a seeing-faculty that generates a compassion-impulse which can then be volitionally suppressed. This implies a soul-level layer at which compassion arises prior to volitional engagement. The will is then the faculty that either acts on or suppresses this arising impulse.

**Tender heart as a named soul subset:** 1 Pet 3:8 names "a tender heart" (eusplanchnos — literally: of good entrails/affections) as a distinct soul-level quality alongside sympathy. This is a named inner-being orientation that the verse treats as a separate faculty or quality from sympathy itself — the predisposing inner tenderness from which sumpathēs flows.

findings.session_b_note:
**Conscience:** Mat 23:30 — the Pharisees' moral self-assessment (*we would not have taken part*) engages the conscience — the inner faculty of moral self-evaluation. Moral complicity-fellowship creates or suppresses conscience activity.

findings.session_b_note: Yes — emphatically. The commanded form of love ('you shall love' — Mat 22:37, Lev 19:18) requires the will's exercise — love cannot be merely a spontaneous feeling if it is commanded. Enemy-love (Mat 5:44, OBS-103-143) is the clearest evidence: loving enemies requires volitional engagement against natural preference. The ranking of loves (Mat 10:37, OBS-103-151) requires a deliberate choice-act — placing love of Christ above natural love of family. Ruth's chesed (Rut 3:10, OBS-103-089) — choosing the elderly Boaz over young men — is love expressed through will against self-interest. The will's engagement is not peripheral but central to love in its highest form (agapē, chesed). The affective forms (phileō, dod) may be less volitionally constituted, but the command-forms require the will.

The four modes (T1) each engage different constitutional levels (T2): covenantal-objective mode engages no named inner-being locus (external mechanism); divine relational-personal mode engages the full constitutional range (spirit, heart, cognition — via the access-postures of faith, repentance, confession); human horizontal mode explicitly requires the heart (Mat 18:35); intercessory mode requires the dependence-posture at the constitutional level of the plea. The somatic compassion origin-point (T2.5 — splagchnizomai) is the constitutional expression of the volitional-release act (T1.4.1 — the act must be chosen). Definition and constitutional location are co-determining: the mode of forgiveness determines which constitutional level is engaged.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-014: T2's constitutional locations map onto T3's faculty engagements. The heart-locus (T2.3 — Mat 18:35) corresponds to T3's volition, moral evaluation, and conscience faculties — all heart-level. The cogn…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional locations map onto T3's faculty engagements. The heart-locus (T2.3 — Mat 18:35) corresponds to T3's volition, moral evaluation, and conscience faculties — all heart-level. The cognition-locus (T2.4 — Jer 31:34) corresponds to T3's cognition and memory faculty engagements. The somatic-compassion locus (T2.5 — splagchnizomai) corresponds to T3's affect faculty at its somatic depth. The constitutional movement (T2.10 — guilt-bearing → forgiveness → love) is the sequence in which T3's faculties are engaged: conscience identifies the guilt → volition releases the claim → affect produces the love-response. Constitutional location determines faculty engagement sequence.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-015: T2's constitutional origin (divine character as the source — Psa 86:5, Psa 130:4) explains T4's God-to-human directional dominance. Because forgiveness originates exclusively in divine character at th…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional origin (divine character as the source — Psa 86:5, Psa 130:4) explains T4's God-to-human directional dominance. Because forgiveness originates exclusively in divine character at the deepest level, the primary relational direction is necessarily God-initiated toward the human. T2's heart-locus requirement (Mat 18:35) explains T4's giving-direction requirement: genuine horizontal forgiveness requires the same constitutional depth as the received vertical (heart-level in both cases). The somatic-compassion origin (T2.5) is the constitutional enabler of the horizontal-giving direction (T4.3): the person who genuinely gives forgiveness does so from a somatic-affective inner origin (splagchnizomai), not merely a verbal performance.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-002: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level …
findings.finding_value: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level (chesed as covenantal-soul character), heart-level (Hos 11:8 — "my heart recoils"), and somatic-level (re.chem, splanchnon) are all richly evidenced. The constitutional architecture is bottom-up: the womb and entrails are the originating ground; the soul and heart are the engagement points; the act is the constitutional expression. Four body-part functions are identified: constitutive (womb — the generative image of compassion), expressive (gut — the felt movement), indicative (Synoptic pattern — splanchnizō signals the compassion-event), and mediating (heart in Hos 11:8 — the deliberative locus where compassion and judgment contend). The four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) is uniquely evidenced in this registry — consistently inside-out and bottom-up. T2.8 established no body deposit; T5.7 is formally closed. The constitutional portrait confirms the sb_classification (soul-body interface) and extends it: compassion is the most somatically grounded characteristic in the programme, with its originating logic residing in the body's deepest interior.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-002: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary…
findings.finding_value: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary point of reception (Zec 12:10 — spirit of grace poured out), not the point of generation (grace originates with God — T2.9). The soul level is the site of standing (Rom 5:2 — "this grace in which we stand") and identity (1Cor 15:10 — "by the grace of God I am what I am"). The constitutional movement follows the SD021 four-faces model: divine disposition received at spirit level → relational standing established at soul level → specific capacity gifted → character expressed outward. Heart-location is partially evidenced via eusplanchnos (Eph 4:32 — the tenderheartedness that grace produces, reaching the affective-somatic interface). T2.7 produces a new finding: grace operates bidirectionally through the body-soul interface — soul-to-body (inner posture enacted somatically in prostration, fasting, sackcloth) and body-to-soul (somatic enactment deepening and confirming the inner posture). T2.8 remains open (body deposit question unresolved); T5.7 is left open accordingly. The constitutional origin analysis (T2.9) is the most analytically significant T2 finding: grace does not originate in the human constitutional system at any level — it arrives from outside. This is confirmed at T6 as the structural uniqueness of grace: the only characteristic that is not produced by any other inner-being characteristic.

findings.finding_value: T2 maps the constitutional territory; T3 maps the faculties engaged. The synthesis: every constitutional level (T2) corresponds to faculty engagement (T3) in the peace data. Soul-level (T2.2) ↔ Affect (T3.4) — the soul's peace is primarily affective (Lam 3:17, Psa 62:5); Heart-level (T2.3) ↔ Moral evaluation + Volition + Conscience (T3.8/6/9) — the heart engages the moral-volitional-conscience cluster; Mind-level (T2.4) ↔ Cognition (T3.2) — the mind's directed orientation; Body-level (T2.6) ↔ Agency (T3.7) — the body's actions express inner peace; Hidden-person (T2.5) ↔ Conscientiousness (T3.10) — the hidden person of the heart is the site of the most integrated response. The constitutional and faculty maps are not independent but interlocking descriptions of the same whole-person reality.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-060-002: T2 as a whole reveals that this characteristic has no single constitutional home — it operates across the full spirit-soul-body register through different modes. Spirit is the location in two modes: a…
findings.finding_value: T2 as a whole reveals that this characteristic has no single constitutional home — it operates across the full spirit-soul-body register through different modes. Spirit is the location in two modes: as the object of endowing giving (Neh 9:20) and as the faculty transformed eschatologically (Isa 61:3). Soul (nephesh/nafshi) appears in divine self-reference in the giving-over context (Jer 12:7). Heart (leb) is the faculty where the giving decision is made (Hos 11:8). Hidden inner parts (tukhoth) are the target of wisdom-giving (Job 38:36). Rahamim (visceral compassion) is the inner-being quality that determines giving direction. Body appears as the expressive medium of self-giving (Isa 50:6) and as constituted by breath-giving (Isa 42:5). No constitutional body deposit is confirmed. Three movement patterns — constitutive (spirit→mind), expressive (inner→body), transformative (outside-in→inside renewed→inside-out) — show the characteristic is constitutionally dynamic. What T2 reveals as a whole: this characteristic operates at every constitutional level not because it is superficially distributed but because giving as an inner-being act can reach the spirit (endowing), the heart (deciding), the soul (attaching), the hidden inner parts (forming), and the body (expressing and constituting). It is constitutionally pervasive.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-007: The constitutional locations (T2 — spirit, heart, soul, hidden inner parts, body) and the inner faculties (T3 — perception, cognition, memory, affect, volition, agency, moral evaluation, relational ca…
findings.finding_value: The constitutional locations (T2 — spirit, heart, soul, hidden inner parts, body) and the inner faculties (T3 — perception, cognition, memory, affect, volition, agency, moral evaluation, relational capacity) are not independent — they occupy the same inner-being territory from two different analytical perspectives. T2 asks where; T3 asks which faculty. Reading them together reveals: the heart (leb, T2.3) is the location of affect-volition integration (T3.4, T3.6) — where compassion (affect) determines giving (volitional act). The hidden inner parts (tukhoth, T2.5) are the constitutional home of the cognitive-formative faculty (T3.2 — the wisdom that is given there). The body (T2.6-7) is the somatic site of agentive expression (T3.7 — agency expresses through the body). The spirit (ruach, T2.1) is both the object of constitutive giving and the faculty whose depletion the eschatological giving addresses — connecting to the agency and relational capacity faculties that cannot operate from a faint spirit. What this pair reveals: constitutional location and faculty engagement are two descriptions of the same inner-being event. The characteristic is located constitutionally precisely where the relevant faculties operate.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-010: The constitutional pervasiveness of the characteristic (T2 — it reaches every constitutional level through distinct modes) and the hub position it occupies in the structural landscape (T6 — connecting…
findings.finding_value: The constitutional pervasiveness of the characteristic (T2 — it reaches every constitutional level through distinct modes) and the hub position it occupies in the structural landscape (T6 — connecting multiple adjacent characteristics across all five dimensions) are causally related. The characteristic can occupy the hub position precisely because it is constitutionally pervasive: it is not anchored to a single constitutional level that would limit its relational scope. A purely spirit-level characteristic would only relate structurally to other spirit-level characteristics; a purely somatic characteristic would only relate somatically. This characteristic, moving across all levels, can relate structurally to characteristics at every level. What this pair reveals: constitutional breadth enables structural breadth. The connecting-hub position is a structural consequence of the constitutional polymorphism of giving as an inner-being act.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-011: The constitutional evidence (T2 — spirit, heart, soul, hidden inner parts, body all engaged) and the lexical/literary evidence (T7 — na.tan as exclusively verbal, Hos 11:8 as primary anchor) mutually …
findings.finding_value: The constitutional evidence (T2 — spirit, heart, soul, hidden inner parts, body all engaged) and the lexical/literary evidence (T7 — na.tan as exclusively verbal, Hos 11:8 as primary anchor) mutually confirm. The lexical finding that na.tan is grammatically a verb (T7, Q&A-171) is the lexical expression of the constitutional finding that the characteristic moves across constitutional levels through distinct movement patterns (T2.10) — a verb in motion describes constitutional movement in language. Hos 11:8 as primary anchor (T7.2.5) identifies precisely the verse that shows the deepest constitutional engagement: leb (heart) and rahamim (visceral inner parts) both named in a single verse showing inner-being movement. The verse evidence and constitutional analysis converge on the same verse for the same reason: it is the verse where constitutional depth and inner-being movement are most explicitly disclosed. What this pair reveals: the lexical and constitutional evidence are independently converging on the same structural reality.

The volitional sub-dimension of the soul. Gen 27:41: Esau's hatred produces a resolution — "then I will kill my brother Jacob" — the volitional resolution is explicit and internal. The settled hatred has organised the volitional capacity around a future act. The hatred does not merely exist as feeling; it has become an intention. The will as a soul-subset is engaged by hatred — hatred recruits the will into a hostile plan.

The volitional faculty: Gen 25:34 (Esau's despising of the birthright) — "and he ate and drank and rose and went his way" — the will acts in accordance with the contemptuous evaluation. Once the worth-verdict is rendered, the will acts as if the thing truly has no claim. Job 12:5: "in the *thought* of one who is at ease there is contempt for misfortune" — the word "thought" (Hebrew: 'ashton) names a cognitive-reflective faculty: the person's comfortable thought-life generates contempt.

The conscience as a soul-level organ is the most central sub-location for abhorrence. The characteristic operates at the level of the conscience's deepest reactions — the visceral recoil precedes and is then named by the moral evaluation faculty. The conscience (as the acute inner witness of moral reality) is abhorrence's most natural constitutional home.

The absence of fear of God as a soul-subset is the key constitutional observation. Fear of the Lord is a soul-level orientation governing the whole person. Its absence (Psa 54:3) is what M06-D names as the constitutional ground of cruelty and ruthlessness. The characteristic is defined by a soul-level absence rather than a soul-level presence.

The identity-level of the soul. Sa.ni (group 1664-001, Deu 21:15) names reproach as a total relational identity condition — the disfavoured wife is not merely experiencing episodes of reproach but inhabiting a position of permanent relational identity that shapes every legal and relational dimension of her existence. Isa 54:4 — "you will forget the shame of your youth, and the reproach of your widowhood you will remember no more" — the memory faculty (as a soul-subset) is named as the location where reproach persists after the external condition has changed, requiring active forgetting for restoration.

**[A2 — Human Righteousness]** The will is implicated as a distinct soul-subset: the hunger for righteousness (Mat 5:6, VSG M26-A2-006) involves a dispositional-volitional orientation — not merely knowing what is right or feeling drawn to it, but actively desiring and seeking it. The will is the organ of desire and intent; hunger and thirst name an active orientation of the will toward righteousness.

**[B — Moral Uprightness]** Speech and expression are implicated in the uprightness vocabulary — not as constitutional location but as expression-channel. The uprightness of B expresses itself through speech (Pro 8:6; Isa 33:15; Pro 23:16). This is not a soul-subset in the strict constitutional sense, but the vocal/speech expression of an inner state.

**[D — Avenging Justice]** The zeal faculty is implicated in D — 2Cor 7:11 (VSG 945-001) names "zeal" (zēlos) as one of the inner responses produced by godly grief that issues in the desire for justice. Zeal as an inner faculty (intense inner purposefulness) is engaged in the avenging justice sub-group as the emotional-volitional charge behind the cry for justice.

**[F — Moral Reckoning]** The deliberative will is engaged alongside the mind — the instruction to "count yourselves dead to sin" (Rom 6:11) is not merely a cognitive act but a volitional commitment: the person is told to reckon AND to not let sin reign (Rom 6:12). The will executes what the mind has reckoned. The reckoning faculty in F sits at the junction of mind and will.

**[CLUSTER — T2.5]** E. Beyond heart and mind, the verse evidence surfaces the will (volitional orientation toward righteousness, A2-006; F-execution of reckoning conclusions) and zeal (D: the intense purposeful charge behind the cry for justice). These are not primary constitutional locations but functional engagements — secondary soul-subsets engaged by specific modes of righteousness in the cluster.

Rev 18:14 (liparos — "your soul longed for all your delicacies") names psuchē (soul) and the longing/desire of the soul for material luxury. 1Ti 6:9 ("those who desire [boulomai] to be rich fall into temptation... and many senseless and harmful desires [epithumiai]") names the desire-faculty as the location of the wealth-drive that produces ruin. The desire-subset of the soul is the location where the wealth-orientation and insatiability are seated in M46-A and M46-B.

findings.finding_value: Rev 18:14 also evidences the soul's longing/desire in M46-B context (the soul that longed for Babylon's luxurious goods). The soul as the seat of desire is present in both M46-B (desire for material luxury) and M46-D (in its inverted form — the soul oriented toward God rather than goods).

Luk 12:19-20 context uses "soul" in the sense of life-centre — not directly M01 but adjacent. The BOUNDARY term ademoneo (Mat 26:37) engages "his soul" (psychē) in the Gethsemane distress.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes: the **whole being** (Psa 16:9 — "my whole being rejoices"; the Hebrew uses the term for "glory" or "my honour/innermost self" as a designation for the whole inner person). This suggests exultation, while arising from the heart and soul, extends to encompass the totality of the person's inner being.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes: (1) **The whole being / whole inner self** — Psa 16:9 ("my heart is glad, and my whole being rejoices") — Joy extends from the heart to encompass the totality of the inner person; (2) **The mouth and tongue as expressive organs** — Act 2:26 ("my tongue rejoiced") — in this agalliao verse, the tongue is named as the rejoicing organ, showing Joy's primary inner state (heart-gladness) expressing itself through the first inner-to-outer organ of speech; (3) **The bones** — Psa 51:8 ("let the bones that you have broken rejoice") — Joy's restoration is requested at the deepest somatic level.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Yes: **tongue** — Act 2:26 ("my tongue rejoiced") — the tongue as the expressive organ of inner exultation; **flesh/body** — Act 2:26 ("my flesh also will dwell in hope") — the body as the recipient of the hope that accompanies the rejoicing; **face** — Job 9:27 ("put off my sad face") — the face as the somatic expression of the inner struggle with cheerfulness; Psa 39:13 ("that I may smile again") — the face/countenance as the visible indicator of the barely-attainable brightening.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes: **bones** — Pro 15:30 ("good news refreshes the bones") — the deepest somatic structure is the recipient of gladness in the good-news register; the refreshment of good news penetrates to the body's depths. **[CHAR-1]** E — Conscience is the most prominent additional soul-location for CHAR-1. The M07-B seared-conscience register (VCG-04) is entirely about the conscience's relation to shame: "they did not know how to blush" — the loss of the shame-registering conscience. The M07-C-VCG-03 material (entropē — 1Cor 6:5; 15:34) presents shame as directly awakening the conscience toward God. 2Ch 30:15 (vc=38506) — the priests' shame moving them to consecration — is a conscience-activated response. Conscience is the specific inner faculty that receives the moral signal that shame carries; when it is functional, shame can be received; when seared, it cannot.

The conscience is the faculty that registers the presence or absence of guilt — and CHAR-6 is the condition in which the conscience registers no guilt because no deliberate wrongdoing has occurred. **[CLUSTER]** E — Conscience is the cluster's most important soul-subset, integrating three of the six characteristics (1, 4, 6) at their primary constitutional location. Char 1: conscience-shame identity — shame is what the functioning conscience feels when it registers failure; the loss of shame (Jer 6:15) is the loss of conscience. Char 4: conscience as constitutively the evaluative mode — identifying the shameful is conscience's primary operation in the shame-field. Char 6: conscience as integrity mode — the condition of the conscience when it is clean and blameless before God. Cluster-level finding: the seared conscience (Char 1's absence-mode), the inverted conscience (Char 4's corruption-mode), and the incapacity for innocence (Char 6's loss-mode) are three faces of the same inner-being catastrophe: the conscience's failure as the primary shame-registering and shame-countering faculty. These three failure-modes are the cluster's most critical diagnostic findings.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The conscience is surfaced as a distinct soul-level location. Phili2:12 — sustained obedience rooted in "fear of God rather than social pressure" — the conscience functions as the internal accountability when external accountability is absent. Eph6:1 — "in the Lord, for this is right" — the moral-rightness evaluation that grounds the obedience is a conscience-function. Col3:22 — "fearing the Lord" as the inner motivational ground — fear of God as a conscience-orientation. The conscience is the inner faculty that evaluates the legitimacy of the authority claim and sustains the submission when external supports are withdrawn.
