**[CHAR-4]** E — The will is surfaced as the primary constitutional location by the evidence (T1.8.1): both metriopatheō and okneō evidence volitional qualities — the will's manner of engaging (measured, calibrated) and the will's kinetic quality (without hesitation). The will is the most directly evidenced constitutional faculty, even though it is not named explicitly as a distinct location in these two verses.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The character-level is the most directly evidenced constitutional location. All three verses locate semnotēs as a *character quality* — the stable property of the person's whole inner person that expresses itself comprehensively: "in every way" (1Ti2:2), "all dignity" (1Ti3:4), as a quality of teaching character (Tit2:7). The constitutional site is the character as a whole — the settled, comprehensive disposition of the inner person that shapes all their social expression — rather than a specific soul-faculty (heart, mind, will).

**[CHAR-6]** E — The will is the most directly evidenced soul-level faculty beyond the heart as an integrating location. 1Ch28:21 — "every willing man" — names the person by the orientation of their will (nadav = freely-willing); Exo35:5 — the "willing heart" is the heart whose will is freely-oriented. The will as distinct soul-level faculty is engaged and evidenced throughout the corpus even where the word "will" is not separately named.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The evidence surfaces the will as a distinct soul-level location beyond heart and mind. The characteristic is repeatedly framed as an act of the will: "humble yourselves" (Jam4:10; 1Pe5:6) — reflexive imperatives addressed to the volitional capacity; Phili2:8 — Christ "humbled himself" — the volitional self-determination of the kenotic act. The will's engagement with humility is as a primary faculty, not merely as the instrument of the heart's orientation. Additionally, the affect — weeping, tenderness, grief (2Ki22:19; 2Ch34:27; 2Cor12:21) — surfaces as a soul-level location in which the characteristic finds its expression.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Three additional soul-level locations surface across the cluster. *Conscience* (CHAR-2): Phili2:12 — the conscience functions as the internal sustainer of submission when external accountability is removed; the conscience is the M09-C register's most distinctive secondary constitutional location. *Will* (CHAR-4, CHAR-6): 1Ch28:21 — na.div names the person by the orientation of their will; metriopatheō and okneō evidence the will as the primary constitutional location for CHAR-4. *Character* (CHAR-5): semnotēs is the comprehensive character quality — the character as a whole-person constitutional property rather than a specific faculty. Cluster-level: M09 evidences the following constitutional locations in order of frequency: heart > will > conscience > character > spirit. The dominance of heart and will confirms the cluster's volitional character; the presence of conscience (CHAR-2) confirms that submission requires not only the will but an internal moral evaluator sustaining it; the character-level (CHAR-5) confirms that the cluster includes at least one characteristic that is constitutionally comprehensive rather than faculty-specific.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes. The *conscience* is evidenced as a distinct soul-subset engaged by wilful sinning. The VCG-03 corpus (deterrence/restraint) presupposes conscience as the faculty that recognises the moral quality of a potential act before commission: Gen 39:9 (Joseph's conscience names "great wickedness"), Psa 39:1 (the conscience-driven resolve to guard the mouth). Post-act, conscience appears in Gen 42:22 (Reuben's conscience connects past sinning to present reckoning). The conscience operates as the inner moral witness that either deters sinning (pre-act) or registers it as wrong (post-act). This is distinct from the heart's volitional function and the mind's deliberative function.

**[CHAR-10]** E — *Desire/appetite (epithumia)* as a distinct soul-level faculty is the primary location beyond heart and mind. Jam 1:14 — "his own desire" — the desire-faculty (epithumia) is the mechanism's operative site for enticement. 2Pe 2:14 — "insatiable for sin" — the appetite-faculty is named through its insatiability. 2Pe 2:18 — "sensual passions of the flesh" — the sensual-desire register of the epithumia faculty. This is the desire-faculty operating as a constitutional location distinct from (though related to) the heart.

**[CHAR-11]** E — *Will/volition* as a distinct soul-level faculty is evidenced. Rom 7:15 (implied in the corpus's broader argument — the specific verse is outside the 112 but the pattern is evidenced within it): the condition operates at the will level through the split between intending good and doing evil — Rom 7:17/20 — "it is no longer I who do it, but sin that dwells within me" — the "I" (volitional self) is distinguished from the sin-force that operates within; (2) Rom 6:16 — "you are slaves of the one whom you obey" — the obedience is a volitional act; the condition operates by capturing the volitional obedience and directing it toward sin rather than God; (3) Gen 4:7 — "you must rule over it" — the will is addressed as the faculty that must exercise ruling authority against the sin-force.

**[CHAR-12]** E — *Will/volition in its captive mode* is the primary evidenced soul-level location beyond heart and mind. Joh 8:34 — "a slave to sin" — the slavery is specifically the will's captivity (the definition explicitly names "governing the will so it cannot freely choose otherwise"). The will as the enslaved faculty is the distinctive soul-level location of CHAR-12. Additionally, *identity/allegiance* as a constitutional soul-level dimension: 1Jo 3:8 — "of the devil" — the person's deepest identity-belonging is the soul-level location of the allegiance captured by the enslaving power.

**[CHAR-13]** E — *Conscience* as a distinct soul-level faculty is evidenced. Psa 51:3 — "my sin is ever before me" — the conscience's persistent awareness of the record is the primary soul-level location beyond heart and mind. Num 5:6 — "that person realizes his guilt" — the conscience's realisation of guilt is the moment the divine record becomes accessible to inner awareness. The conscience is the faculty that mediates between the objective divine record and the subjective inner-being experience of it.

**[CHAR-14]** E — *Faith/trust* as a distinct soul-level faculty is evidenced. Act 10:43 — "everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name" — the believing (*pisteúōn* — present participle) is the soul-level receptive act through which forgiveness is received; faith is the faculty of trust-directed-toward-Christ through which the receiving dimension is completed. Faith is not merely cognitive (mind) or affective (heart) but a distinct trust-orientation of the whole person toward the forgiver.

**[CHAR-15]** E — *Will* as a distinct soul-level faculty is evidenced through the rebellion dimension. Psa 78:17 — "yet they sinned still more against him, rebelling against the Most High in the desert" — rebellion (*mārāh* — to be contentious, to rebel) is a volitional act: the will actively sets itself against God rather than passively drifting. The "still more" indicates an escalating volitional commitment to the sinning pattern. The will's active rebellion is the soul-level faculty through which the generational pattern is individually sustained.

**[CHAR-16]** E — *Conscience* as a distinct soul-level faculty is evidenced. Luk 5:8 — "I am a sinful man, O Lord" — Peter's spontaneous recognition of his sinner-identity is a conscience-operation: the moral self-assessment arises unbidden in the presence of holiness. Luk 18:13 — "would not even lift up his eyes to heaven, but beat his breast" — the tax collector's bodily self-abasement is the physical expression of conscience's internal verdict about the sinner-identity. Rom 3:7 — "why am I still being condemned as a sinner?" — the rhetorical question engages the conscience's assessment of moral status even when one's act produced divine glory.

**[CHAR-17]** E — *Conscience* as the primary soul-level faculty of CHAR-17 is the defining element of the characteristic. 1Sa 25:31 (pu.qah) — "pangs of conscience" — the term directly names the conscience-faculty's experience of guilt-stagger; Lev 4:13/22/27; 5:2/3/4/5 — "realizes his guilt" (a.sham) — the repeated guilt-realisation pattern names the conscience as the recognition-faculty; Hos 5:15 — "until they acknowledge their guilt" — the acknowledgment is the conscience's output. The conscience is the primary inner-being faculty constituting the characteristic (per the definition: "conscience in its guilt-awareness mode").

**[CHAR-18]** E — *Conscience* as a distinct soul-level faculty is evidenced. 2Sa 24:10 — "David's heart struck him after he had numbered the people" — the heart-strike is a conscience event: the moral self-assessment faculty activates spontaneously in response to the iniquity; Psa 38:18 — "I confess my iniquity; I am sorry for my sin" — the conscience produces both confession and sorrow as its output; Lev 26:40/41 — "confess their iniquity... if then their uncircumcised heart is humbled" — the confession presupposes conscience engaging through heart-humiliation.

**[CHAR-19]** E — *Will* as the primary soul-level faculty is the defining location of CHAR-19. The entire characteristic is built on the wilful act of crossing a known boundary — the will is the primary inner faculty. Isa 31:6 — "turn to him from whom people have deeply revolted" — the turning (the will's reversal) is the prescribed remedy, confirming the will is the primary locus. Eze 18:28 — "he considered and turned away from all the transgressions" — the turning of the will is the act that reverses the transgression's consequence. *Conscience* also appears: Pro 28:13 — "whoever conceals his transgressions will not prosper" — the concealment is a conscience-suppression act.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The *conscience* is the primary soul-subset evidenced beyond heart and mind. Lev 5:5 ("when he realizes his guilt... and confesses") — the realization of guilt is a conscience-event: the moral witness within the person registers that a wrong was done, even though no deliberate defiance occurred. The conscience here operates *retrospectively*: it engages after the fact, processing the moral reality of a past act once the relevant information is available. Num 22:34 (Balaam's immediate confession) shows the same retrospective conscience pattern: knowledge arrives → conscience fires → verbal acknowledgment follows.

**[CHAR-20]** E — *Will* as the primary soul-level faculty is central to CHAR-20. 1Ch 5:25 — "broke faith with the God of their fathers, and whored after the gods of the peoples" — the will's active transfer of allegiance is the volitional core; Eze 18:24 — "when a righteous person turns away from his righteousness" — the turning is a volitional act; Lev 26:40 — "treachery that they committed against me, and also in walking contrary to me" — the will walking contrary. *Conscience* appears in Ezr 9:4 — "all who trembled at the words of the God of Israel... sat appalled" — the conscience-engaged response to observed faithlessness; Ezr 10:6 — mourning over the exiles' faithlessness.

**[CHAR-21]** E — *Desire* as a distinct soul-level faculty is explicitly the corruption-agent in the NT. Eph 4:22 — "old self... corrupt through deceitful desires (*epithumiais*)"; 2Pe 1:4 — "corruption that is in the world because of sinful desire (*epithumia*)"; Gal 6:8 — "sows to his own flesh" — the fleshly desire-orientation. *Will* is also engaged: Pro 6:14 — "devises evil" — the will drives the devising; 2Pe 2:19 — "slaves of corruption" — the will is captured. *Conscience* appears in Job 33:27 — "I sinned and perverted what was right" — the conscience producing the confession of perversion.

**[CHAR-22]** E — *Will* is the primary operative faculty. Eze 18:8 — "withholds his hand from injustice" — the will's active restraint; Eze 3:20 — "a righteous person turns from his righteousness and commits injustice" — the volitional turn; Job 34:32 — "if I have done iniquity, I will do it no more" — the will's capacity to cease. *Conscience* is engaged through the shame-dimension: Zep 3:5 — "the unjust knows no shame" — the conscience's shame-response is the relevant faculty, absent in the unjust; Job 6:29 — "let no injustice be done" — appeal to the conscience of Job's interlocutors.

**[CHAR-3]** E — *Will/volition* emerges as a distinct soul-subset beyond heart and mind in the CHAR-3 corpus. The contrast between genuine and hollow confession is precisely a will-contrast: in Deu 1:41 (VCG-03), the will proceeds autonomously despite the spoken words — the will is not aligned with the confession. In 1Ch 21:17, the will is fully engaged: "It is I who have sinned" — the will claims ownership without deflection. The will's alignment or misalignment with the confessional content is what distinguishes genuine from hollow confession — which makes the will a distinct inner location that confession either fully engages or only partially reaches.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The *will* is evidenced as a distinct soul-subset engaged in conscience suppression's active-denial mode. Jer 2:35 — "you say, 'I am innocent'" — the saying involves the will's active commitment to the false claim. The will is not merely passive in the face of suppressed conscience; it is the faculty that chooses to voice and maintain the denial. This distinguishes the active-denial mode (will engaged in suppression) from the perceptual-blindness mode (will not specifically engaged — Jer 16:10) and the habituated mode (will habituated to sinning — Ecc 8:12).

**[CHAR-5]** E — The *will* as a distinct volitional faculty beyond the heart's integrating function is the primary soul-subset evidenced. The corpus's persistent "did not depart... did not turn... would not obey" formulations all name the will directly. Heb 10:26's *hekousiōs* (deliberately/willingly) is the most explicit naming of the will as the operative faculty. The will is what clings (2Ki 3:3 — *davaq*), refuses to depart, and stubbornly persists against correction (Neh 9:29 — "would not obey").

**[CHAR-6]** E — *Will/disposition* as a distinct volitional-dispositional faculty is the primary soul-subset beyond heart and mind. The continuous-present forms — "keeps on sinning" (1Jo 3:6), "they would not listen" (1Sa 2:25), "there they have continued" (Hos 10:9) — all name the will's settled directional commitment rather than discrete choices. The will has been formed into a disposition that produces sinning as its default: this is will-as-disposition, distinct from will-as-moment-of-choice (CHAR-1/CHAR-5).

**[CHAR-7]** E — *Will/volition* is the primary soul-level faculty evidenced. The corpus's dominant form — "walked in the way of Jeroboam and... made Israel to sin" — is constitutively volitional in the leader (walked = volitional commitment; made Israel to sin = volitional causative action). The community's will is redirected: 2Ki 17:21 — "drove Israel from following the Lord" — the driving-away is an act against the community's volitional orientation. The will operates at both ends of the transmission: the leader's will causes, the community's will is redirected.

**[CHAR-8]** E — *Will/volition* is the primary evidenced soul-level location. Pa.sha — the deliberate act of breaking submission — is constitutively volitional: 2Ki 8:20 — "revolted from the rule of Judah and set up a king of their own" — the combined act of breaking from and establishing requires volitional decision and action. 2Ch 21:10 — "because he had forsaken the Lord" — *forsook* (*azav* H5800) is a volitional act of abandonment.

**[CHAR-9]** E — *Will/volition* as a distinct soul-level faculty is clearly engaged. Jude 9 — Michael "did not *presume* to pronounce a blasphemous judgment" — the presume (*epitolmaō* — to dare) names the will's act of over-reaching. Rev 13:5 — the beast's blasphemous utterances are a willed, permitted, sustained act ("it was allowed to exercise authority for forty-two months") — the will exercises sustained blasphemous speech over time. 1Ti 6:4 — the "craving for controversy" is a volitional appetite. The will is engaged as the faculty that either restrains or enacts sinful speech.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The evidence surfaces "way" (derek) as a directional-volitional location beyond heart and mind — it names the person's overall trajectory and life-direction. This is the VCG-07 corpus's dominant language: "his wicked way" (Eze 3:18; 33:8; 33:11; Isa 55:7; Pro 4:14). While "way" is not a faculty but a directional concept, it describes the totality of the person's volitional thrust — which in the programme's framework is a soul-level phenomenon. The eyes also appear in Pro 21:4 (VCG-03): "haughty eyes and a proud heart, the lamp of the wicked, are sin" — the eyes as the vehicle of pride's inner disposition expressing outward. Beyond this, the "belly" (Pro 13:25) as the seat of insatiable appetite is a sub-soul location in the Hebrew anthropological tradition.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes. The conscience (syneidēsis) is explicitly evidenced as a location of this characteristic. Heb 10:22 (vc=14426 — VCG-06): "hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience" — the conscience is named as a location where evil constitutionally resides, and its "evil" state makes approach to God impossible. The conscience is the specific faculty named in Heb 10:22 as the primary barrier between the constitutionally evil inner person and the holy God. The whole-body/whole-person framing of Mat 6:23 (vc=14458 — VCG-03 — "your whole body will be full of darkness") implies the characteristic is not localised to a single faculty but permeates the whole inner person.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes. The conscience is the most significant additional constitutional locus. VCG-04 (11 verses) is entirely devoted to the conscience's relationship with abomination across its states — wholly silenced (Jer 6:15; Jer 8:12), grieving and active (Eze 9:4), callable to repentance (Eze 14:6), awakened to produce self-loathing (Eze 36:31), bearing permanent shame (Eze 44:13), and rebelling (Eze 44:6). The conscience as a distinct inner faculty is the most extensively evidenced constitutional locus beyond heart and mind in this characteristic. Additionally, Pro 13:19 (vc=1687 — VCG-05) evidences the soul's desire faculty as a locus (T2.2.1).

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes. The eyes (as the perceptive-desire faculty) are explicitly evidenced. Eze 20:7 (vc=1634 — VCG-05): "the detestable things your eyes feast on" — the eyes are the perceptive-desire faculty through which idolatrous attachment is sustained and fed. Eze 20:8 (vc=65911 — VCG-05): "none of them cast away the detestable things their eyes feasted on" — the eyes' feasting habit is the mechanism of the characteristic's perpetuation. Eze 6:9 (vc=1697 — VCG-05): "eyes that go whoring after their idols" — the eyes are specifically named as going whoring, paralleling the heart's whoring. The eyes in this context are not merely physical organs but the inner-perceptive faculty of desire — the capacity for morally-weighted visual attention that feeds the soul's attachment.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Yes. The tongue/mouth as the expressive-concealment faculty is directly evidenced. Psa 10:7 (vc=38225 — VCG-04): "under his tongue are mischief and iniquity" — the iniquity is located beneath the tongue as a hidden reservoir. This is an inner-sub-set location: the tongue/mouth as the site where iniquity waits for deployment. Additionally, Isa 58:9 (vc=38201 — VCG-04): "speaking wickedness" — the vocal-expressive faculty is named as a location of iniquitous expression. These tongue-mouth references are expressive-concealment locations: iniquity stored beneath the tongue ready to flow outward.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Yes. Jude 8 (vc=14354 — VCG-01) evidences the volitional faculty as a distinct constitutional location: "relying on their dreams, they defile the flesh, reject authority, and blaspheme the glorious ones." The will (rejection of authority) is the constitutional location of the characteristic's source. Additionally, the body's speech-instruments are specifically named: Rev 13:6 (vc=14356 — VCG-01): "opened its mouth to utter blasphemies" — the mouth as the body's speech-instrument is the constitutional locus through which the characteristic becomes operative. The will (refusing, rejecting) and the mouth (uttering) are the two additional constitutional locations beyond heart and mind in this corpus.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Yes. The cluster reveals multiple soul-sub-set locations across its six characteristics: (a) the conscience (Chars 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 — all evidence conscience-engagement through its silencing or suppression); (b) the devotion-faculty/eyes as desire-perceptive mechanism (Char 4 — Eze 20:7-8: eyes feasting on idol-objects; Eze 6:9: eyes going whoring); (c) the speech-concealment layer (Char 5 — Psa 10:7: iniquity under the tongue; Char 6 — Rev 13:6: mouth as the constitutional bridge); (d) the will as distinct from the heart (Chars 1, 4, 5, 6 — the will's volitional orientation named separately from the heart's dispositional state). The conscience is the most universally evidenced soul-sub-set location across the cluster — all six characteristics engage with conscience through its suppression or bypass.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes: the affective dimension. Num 9:7 (M10c-A-VCG-07) — the men's grief at exclusion from worship — shows affect (grief, desire for worship) as a soul-level response to the condition. The grief is specifically named: "why are we kept from bringing the Lord's offering?" — the grief of a worship desire blocked by the defilement-state. Lev 13:45 (M10c-B-VCG-03) — the public cry "Unclean, unclean" — shows the social-relational soul-dimension engaged: the declaration is simultaneously a ritual act and a social-relational act of self-naming before the community. The social exclusion of Lev 13:46 ("he shall live alone; his dwelling shall be outside the camp") shows the relational soul-dimension as the site of the condition's most sustained impact.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes: the will and desire are additional soul-level locations. Rom 6:19 (VCG-02): "slaves to impurity" — the will is specifically named as the faculty bound by the defilement-state; the person's volitional capacity is in bondage. Rom 1:24 (VCG-02): "lusts of their hearts" — desire (epithumia) as the soul-level faculty through which the characteristic operates. Eph 4:19 (VCG-02): "given themselves up to sensuality, greedy to practice every kind of impurity" — the volitional self-surrender and the appetitive desire are both named.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes: the memory faculty and the affect faculty. Memory: Eze 20:43 (VCG-02) — "there you shall remember your ways and all your deeds with which you have defiled yourselves" — the corporate memory of the defilement-state is the named inner mechanism of future repentance; memory is explicitly engaged as the faculty through which defilement becomes the generative force of self-loathing and moral grief. Affect: Gen 34:5 (VCG-01) — Jacob's "restrained, simmering awareness of wrong done" is an affective response; Num 5:14 — jealousy as the immediate affective inner response to suspected covenantal betrayal.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes: the will and the speech/hearing communicative-perceptive complex. Will: Luk 8:29 (VCG-01) — "driven by the demon into the desert" — the person's will is completely overridden; the spirit drives where the person's will would not go. Mar 9:25 (VCG-01): the spirit suppresses speech (a volitional-expressive faculty) and hearing (a perceptive faculty).

**[CLUSTER]** E — All four characteristics surface additional soul-level locations, collectively mapping the full range of inner-being faculties engaged by the M10c cluster. Characteristic 1: affect (Num 9:7 — grief at exclusion) and social-relational capacity (Lev 13:45-46 — enforced isolation). Characteristic 2: will (Rom 6:19 — "slaves to impurity") and desire (Rom 1:24 — "lusts of their hearts"). Characteristic 3: memory (Eze 20:43 — memory of defilement as the mechanism of repentance) and affect (Gen 34:5 — simmering grief; Num 5:14 — jealousy). Characteristic 4: will (Luk 8:29 — "driven by the demon") and the speech/hearing communicative-perceptive complex (Mar 9:25 — "mute and deaf spirit"). Together the cluster engages all major soul-level locations: will (Chars 1, 2, 3, 4), desire (Chars 2, 3), affect (Chars 1, 3, 4), memory (Char 3), conscience (Chars 1, 2, 3), and speech/hearing (Char 4). The cluster's coverage is comprehensive: every major soul-level faculty is engaged by at least two characteristics.

findings.session_b_note:
The tender heart (eusplanchnos) reveals that compassion is not only a disposition that engages with the other when they appear — it is grounded in a prior inner softness or receptivity. The person who has a tender heart (eusplanchnos) is constitutionally open to being moved. This is the pre-dispositional condition for compassion-movement: a heart that has not been hardened, calloused, or closed against the suffering of others.

This is analytically significant: it implies a gradient of inner receptivity to compassion. The fully compassionate person is eusplanchnos AND sumpathēs — internally tender AND actively sympathetic. The hardened person (implied by the judicial-eye-that-will-not-pity) lacks the eusplanchnos quality at the soul-subset level. This inner tenderness is a constitutional precondition, not merely an incidental quality.

The affective forms (phileō, dod) may operate without explicit volitional initiation, but they too produce will-acts (Peter's fileō generates faithful mission-response, Joh 21:17, OBS-103-153).

findings.finding_value: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level (chesed as covenantal-soul character), heart-level (Hos 11:8 — "my heart recoils"), and somatic-level (re.chem, splanchnon) are all richly evidenced. The constitutional architecture is bottom-up: the womb and entrails are the originating ground; the soul and heart are the engagement points; the act is the constitutional expression. Four body-part functions are identified: constitutive (womb — the generative image of compassion), expressive (gut — the felt movement), indicative (Synoptic pattern — splanchnizō signals the compassion-event), and mediating (heart in Hos 11:8 — the deliberative locus where compassion and judgment contend). The four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) is uniquely evidenced in this registry — consistently inside-out and bottom-up. T2.8 established no body deposit; T5.7 is formally closed. The constitutional portrait confirms the sb_classification (soul-body interface) and extends it: compassion is the most somatically grounded characteristic in the programme, with its originating logic residing in the body's deepest interior.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-002: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary…
findings.finding_value: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary point of reception (Zec 12:10 — spirit of grace poured out), not the point of generation (grace originates with God — T2.9). The soul level is the site of standing (Rom 5:2 — "this grace in which we stand") and identity (1Cor 15:10 — "by the grace of God I am what I am"). The constitutional movement follows the SD021 four-faces model: divine disposition received at spirit level → relational standing established at soul level → specific capacity gifted → character expressed outward. Heart-location is partially evidenced via eusplanchnos (Eph 4:32 — the tenderheartedness that grace produces, reaching the affective-somatic interface). T2.7 produces a new finding: grace operates bidirectionally through the body-soul interface — soul-to-body (inner posture enacted somatically in prostration, fasting, sackcloth) and body-to-soul (somatic enactment deepening and confirming the inner posture). T2.8 remains open (body deposit question unresolved); T5.7 is left open accordingly. The constitutional origin analysis (T2.9) is the most analytically significant T2 finding: grace does not originate in the human constitutional system at any level — it arrives from outside. This is confirmed at T6 as the structural uniqueness of grace: the only characteristic that is not produced by any other inner-being characteristic.

findings.session_b_note: The mouth/lips as a soul-level location reveals two things: (1) Covenant is constituted through speech — the spoken oath is what brings the covenant into being (Q&A-024); the mouth is not merely expressive but constitutive. When God puts his words in the mouth (Isa 59:21), the covenant content is carried forward through speech across generations ("shall not depart out of your mouth, or out of the mouth of your offspring"). (2) The mouth's use of covenant vocabulary carries moral weight — taking the covenant "on your lips" (Psa 50:16) without inner integrity is an act of hypocrisy that God explicitly challenges. The mouth as covenant-location is not neutral; it is morally evaluated. The soul-level expressive organ (mouth/lips) is thus the site of covenant's public expression and also the site of its possible falsification.

Its significance: restlessness and peace penetrate below the level of deliberate consciousness to the visceral core of the person. This deepens the somatic evidence (T2.6 below). Peace at this level is not performance but being. The hidden-person location connects to the T1 finding about the formed character of peace (Q&A-029) — the peace that is formed becomes the hidden person's defining quality.

findings.finding_value: The soul-location (nefesh) in Psa 6:3 reveals that dismay penetrates to the personal-life center of the person. The nefesh in Hebrew anthropology is the seat of the person's own experienced aliveness — hunger, desire, vitality. When dismay seizes the nefesh, the person's capacity to sustain their own inner life is disrupted. This is constitutionally deeper than heart-disturbance: it is the person's experienced existence itself that is shaken.

The "within" location (Est 1:12 — inner fire located explicitly "within him") and the somatic-inner convergence (Dan 3:19 — filling visible on the face) reveal that anger is experienced as a whole-inner-person phenomenon that defies precise anatomical assignment to a single faculty. The characteristic saturates the inner person — spirit, heart, mind, and the felt bodily interior — simultaneously.
No additional soul subset beyond heart is evidenced with sufficient specificity to distinguish from the general soul-as-seat. Not applicable.

**[CHAR-1]** E — "My whole being" (Psa 16:9) suggests exultation does not remain confined to a single constitutional sub-level but radiates through the whole inner person. This is consistent with the characteristic's expressive dimension (the surging inner state overflows into voice and body) and its comprehensive scope (the person is not divided in exultation but wholly engaged).

**[CHAR-2]** E — The whole-being location (Psa 16:9) reveals that Joy at its fullest does not stay confined to the heart but radiates through the entire inner person. This is consistent with the characteristic's expressive quality — Joy that truly takes hold of the heart moves through the whole being and out into voice, body, and action. The tongue-rejoicing (Act 2:26) shows Joy constitutively moving toward proclamation as its natural expression channel.

**[CHAR-7]** E — The tongue-rejoicing (Act 2:26) shows Suffering-Joy moving from the deepest inner level (spirit/heart) outward to expressive declaration — consistent with agalliao's leaping-expressive root meaning. The face's smile (Psa 39:13; implied in Job 9:27) as the desired visible sign of ba.lag shows the characteristic's outward-expressive quality even in its fragile form: the inner brightening seeks a visible form even when barely attainable.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The "bones refreshed" by good news (Pro 15:30) reveals that Gladness in its most intense experiential form reaches the person at their deepest physical level. The bones are the body's inner framework; their refreshment by good news shows Gladness as a holistic inner-being phenomenon — not merely cognitive or affective but reaching to the body's structural level. This is consistent with the somatic imagery of restoration in the broader M04 cluster (Psa 51:8 — bones asked to rejoice).

**[CHAR-4]** E — Rom 7:22's "inner being" (esō anthrōpos) is the most constitutionally significant location for Delight in the entire corpus. It reveals that the deepest layer of the person — below and beneath what the flesh does — genuinely delights in God's law. This creates the Pauline inner conflict: the deepest self (Delight in God's law) and the flesh (doing what the law prohibits) are in opposition. Delight's location at the "inner being" level means it is the constitutional orientation of the regenerate person's deepest self, not merely a surface preference.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The whole-person and sense-perceptive locations reveal Pleasure as the most holistically distributed characteristic in M04 — it registers across the whole person (life-quality, inheritance-condition), through the senses (sight, taste, smell/aroma), in the soul (Pro 2:10), and in the body (Pro 16:24). No other M04 characteristic is as explicitly multi-level in its constitutional distribution.

**[CHAR-6]** E — **Eyes**: Wonder in its VCG-01 register is specifically perceptual — it requires seeing (Psa 118:23 — "marvellous in our eyes") and the petition to see (Psa 119:18 — "open my eyes"). This visual emphasis is unique to Wonder among M04 characteristics. Wonder begins with a perceptive encounter. **Mouth**: Wonder consistently produces proclamation — the mouth as the organ through which inner Wonder overflows into speech. The proclamatory character of Wonder (tell of, sing of, declare, recount) is its most distinctive expressive mode, consistently using the mouth.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Two cluster-level findings: (1) **The esō anthrōpos (inner being) location of Delight** — Rom 7:22 places Delight at the deepest constitutional level named anywhere in the cluster. The "inner being" is below and beneath both heart and mind, below the level at which the flesh operates. This makes Delight the characteristic with the deepest constitutional grounding in the cluster — it is the orientation of the person's deepest self. This explains why Delight's corruption (Isa 66:3's soul delighting in abominations) is so catastrophic: the person's deepest constitutional level has been inverted; (2) **The bones as the deepest somatic level** — both Gladness (Pro 15:30) and Joy (Psa 51:8) reach the bones. In the OT, the bones represent the body's deepest structural experience. When good news "refreshes the bones," the gladness is not superficial but penetrates to the physical depths. This somatic depth-reaching is part of the cluster's embodied character.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Conscience as the additional soul-subset location reveals that CHAR-1 has a specific moral-registration function beyond the general heart/mind framework. Shame is the primary experiential output of the conscience when it registers moral failure or exposure. The functional conscience = shame-capable; the non-functional (seared) conscience = shame-incapable. This means CHAR-1 and the conscience are structurally linked: shame is what the conscience feels when it registers failure, and the loss of shame is the sign that the conscience has ceased to function. The conscience is both the faculty that receives the shame signal and the faculty through which shame can be deployed correctively (1Cor 6:5).

**[CHAR-2]** S — No additional soul-subset location beyond the general soul and the cognitive/affective dimensions is evidenced in the 72-verse corpus. Silent.

---

**[CHAR-3]** S — No additional soul-subset location beyond the above is evidenced in the 15-verse corpus. Silent.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — Conscience (suneidēsis, implied in 2Cor 4:2 — "commend ourselves to everyone's conscience") is the specific soul-subset location of CHAR-4. The conscience is the moral-recognitive faculty that specifically identifies the shameful as shameful. CHAR-4 is conscience's primary output in its evaluative mode.

---

**[CHAR-5]** S — No additional soul-subset location beyond the above is clearly evidenced in the 24-verse corpus. Silent.

---

**[CHAR-6]** E — Conscience is the additional soul-subset location of CHAR-6: the clean conscience is what CHAR-6's innocence produces and what blameless hands reflect. The conscience is the faculty that registers the presence or absence of guilt — and CHAR-6 is the condition in which the conscience registers no guilt because no deliberate wrongdoing has occurred. The conscience and CHAR-6 are functionally linked: functioning conscience + no deliberate wrongdoing = CHAR-6's inner condition.

---

**[CLUSTER]** E — Conscience is the cluster's most important soul-subset, integrating three of the six characteristics (1, 4, 6) at their primary constitutional location. Char 1: conscience-shame identity — shame is what the functioning conscience feels when it registers failure; the loss of shame (Jer 6:15) is the loss of conscience. Char 4: conscience as constitutively the evaluative mode — identifying the shameful is conscience's primary operation in the shame-field. Char 6: conscience as integrity mode — the condition of the conscience when it is clean and blameless before God. Cluster-level finding: the seared conscience (Char 1's absence-mode), the inverted conscience (Char 4's corruption-mode), and the incapacity for innocence (Char 6's loss-mode) are three faces of the same inner-being catastrophe: the conscience's failure as the primary shame-registering and shame-countering faculty. These three failure-modes are the cluster's most critical diagnostic findings.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — The spirit-location (confirmed T2.1) reveals that CHAR-1 penetrates to the deepest constitutional stratum of the person. Ecc 7:8 (vc=12087, M08-A4-VCG-04) most directly names the spirit as the seat of a dispositional orientation: "proud in spirit" vs "patient in spirit" — two contrasting fundamental orientations at the spirit level. Dan 5:20 (vc=34129, M08-A1-VCG-02) reveals the most entrenched form of CHAR-1: simultaneous heart-lifting and spirit-hardening, producing the behavioural pattern that led directly to Belshazzar's deposition. The spirit-level location confirms that CHAR-1 is not a surface phenomenon of the outer person but can reach the innermost constitutional depth.
**[CHAR-2]** S — No additional soul-level location evidenced. See T2.5.1.
**[CHAR-3]** S — No additional soul-level location evidenced. See T2.5.1.
**[CHAR-4]** S — No additional soul-level location evidenced. CHAR-4 is constitutionally headquartered in the mind/cognitive faculty alone within §3.C.
**[CHAR-5]** S — No additional soul-level location evidenced. See T2.5.1.

**[CLUSTER]** E — CHAR-1's spirit-level evidence, in conjunction with its heart-level and eye-level location, reveals CHAR-1 as the cluster's most constitutionally comprehensive characteristic — it penetrates across spirit, heart, and eyes/outward-bearing in a way that no other characteristic matches. The cluster-synthesis: constitutional depth in M08 is characteristic-specific, not cluster-uniform.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The conscience as distinct soul-level location reveals that genuine submission has an *internal evaluative sustainer*: the person who genuinely submits does so not only from heart-orientation but from a conscience that has assessed the authority as legitimate and the submission as right. This is the difference between Phili2:12's sustained obedience (conscience-grounded, without external accountability) and mere social compliance (which cannot survive without external support). The conscience in this register is what makes submission resilient and sustainable — it internalises the authority's legitimacy and the submission's rightness so that neither requires constant external reinforcement.
**[CHAR-3]** S — No additional soul-level location beyond heart and spirit is evidenced in §3.B. Prompt closed.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The will as the primary constitutional location reveals that meekness and gentleness are fundamentally volitional in their constitutional ground — not primarily emotional or cognitive but the quality and kinetics of the will itself. Metriopatheō (Heb5:2 — "can deal gently") names a volitional capacity; okneō (Act9:38) names volitional readiness. The will's quality — calibrated, non-hesitating — is the constitutional site of the characteristic.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The character as constitutional location reveals that semnotēs is a *comprehensively characterological* quality — it shapes the whole person's manner of inhabiting their existence rather than operating through a single faculty. 1Ti2:2 — "in every way" — the comprehensiveness confirms that the characteristic's constitutional reach is the whole character rather than a single internal faculty. This makes dignity one of the most broadly-reaching inner-being characteristics in M09: it is not located in one constitutional faculty but pervades the person's entire characterological being.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The will as distinct soul-level faculty reveals that willing-heartedness is constitutively volitional — it is the will's quality and direction (free, uncoerced) that defines the characteristic. The will in this characteristic is not the neutral capacity to choose but specifically the will in its freed, non-resistant, gladly-oriented posture toward God. The will's quality (willing vs unwilling) is the constitutional essence of the characteristic.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The will as distinct soul-level location reveals that humility is not merely felt or understood but chosen and enacted. The repeated imperative form ("humble yourselves") addresses the person's capacity to initiate the act of self-lowering; the characteristic is not passively received but actively performed by the will. This reveals that humility, unlike conditions received from outside (such as comfort or peace), is fundamentally the person's own volitional contribution to their inner state — though it is also the appropriate response to divine initiative (the ka.na pattern, where God's word or judgment creates the occasion). The will is the constitutional faculty through which the person responds to divine address with the act of self-lowering.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Three distinct additional soul-level locations surface across the six characteristics. The will as distinct soul-level location: Humility (CHAR-1 — imperative form "humble yourselves" addresses the volitional capacity), Meekness and Gentleness (CHAR-4 — metriopatheō and okneō name the quality and kinetics of the will itself), and Willing-heartedness (CHAR-6 — na.div names the will's freed, gladly-oriented posture). The conscience as distinct location: Submission (CHAR-2 — Phili2:12's sustained conscience-grounded obedience without external accountability distinguishes genuine submission from social compliance). Character as comprehensive location: Dignity (CHAR-5 — semnotēs is the whole-person characterological quality, not located in a single faculty). What these locations reveal: the will as the primary constitutional battleground and expression-site for M09 characteristics (three of six), the conscience as the internal sustainer that distinguishes genuine from performed submission (CHAR-2 distinctively), and character as the comprehensive location that cannot be reduced to any single faculty (CHAR-5 distinctively). Together the additional locations confirm M09's range: from the most faculty-specific (will in CHAR-4 and CHAR-6) to the most comprehensive (character in CHAR-5).

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — The conscience location (T2.5.1) reveals that wilful sinning involves a three-way inner dynamic: (1) the *will* as the faculty that commits the act, (2) the *conscience* as the faculty that witnesses it as wrong (either before, deterring it, or after, registering guilt), and (3) the *heart* as the deep-orientation centre from which both proceed. The relationship between conscience and will is antagonistic in the resistance register (VCG-03): conscience deters what the will is tempted to commit. When conscience fails to deter, sinning occurs — which is precisely why Psa 119:11 (word in the heart) and Exo 20:20 (fear of God before the eyes) function as conscience-strengthening mechanisms.

**[CHAR-10]** E — The desire/appetite location (Jam 1:14; 2Pe 2:14/18) reveals that enticement operates through a constitutional faculty below the level of explicit volition: desire draws the person before the will has made a conscious decision. The desire-faculty is the *pre-volitional* motivational field within which enticement operates. 2Pe 2:14's "insatiable for sin" shows what happens when this faculty is not governed by the will but governs it: the desire becomes constitutionally uncontrollable ("insatiable"), reshaping the person's entire motivational structure.

**[CHAR-11]** E — Will-level location (Rom 7:17/20 — the "I" distinguished from the indwelling sin-force; Rom 6:16 — volitional obedience as the site of the master-choice; Gen 4:7 — the will addressed as the ruling faculty) reveals that the condition engages the will at both ends of its operation: the will is the target sin seeks to capture (Gen 4:7 — "its desire is for you, and you must rule over it") and the faculty through which the condition's enslavement operates (Rom 6:16 — whoever you obey is your master). The condition is not fully separate from the will — it operates through the will's captivity — but it is also not identical with the will — Rom 7:17/20's distinction between "I" and "sin that dwells within me" preserves the person's identity even within the condition's operation.

**[CHAR-12]** E — Will-level captivity (Joh 8:34 — slave to sin) and identity-allegiance level (1Jo 3:8 — of the devil) reveal that sin's enslaving power penetrates to the two deepest soul-level faculties: the will (the faculty that chooses) and the identity (the faculty that constitutes who the person is). The enslaving power is thus comprehensive in soul-depth: it captures both the directive capacity (will) and the constitutive identity (allegiance-belonging).

**[CHAR-13]** E — Conscience-level location (Psa 51:3 — "my sin is ever before me"; Num 5:6 — "realizes his guilt") reveals that the divine record has a conscience-facing dimension: the objective record held by God has a corresponding inner signal in the conscience that (when functioning) makes the record accessible to the person's own awareness. The characteristic's definition ("the person carries this record whether they feel it or not") notes the conscience's optional engagement: the record is objective; conscience engagement is variable. When conscience functions, it mirrors the divine record internally; when suppressed, the record remains but the inner signal is silenced.

**[CHAR-14]** E — The faith-level location (Act 10:43 — "everyone who believes... receives") reveals that the receiving dimension of the characteristic has a specific inner faculty through which it is received: trust directed toward Christ is the mechanism of reception. The OT parallel is faith-through-the-prescribed-means (bringing the animal, laying hands — 2Ch 29:23); the NT crystallises this as explicit personal faith in Christ's name. Faith is thus the soul-level faculty that bridges seeking and receiving: the one who believes is simultaneously seeking (expressing trust in the forgiving God) and receiving (the forgiveness comes to those who believe).

**[CHAR-15]** E — Will-level location (Psa 78:17 — rebellion; Psa 78:32 — "they still sinned" — volitional persistence) reveals that generational sin, though transmitted through lineage, is actively maintained by each generation's own volitional choices: the inherited pattern requires individual volitional engagement to persist. The "still sinned" language (Psa 78:17/32 — "still more," "still sinned") names the will's active continuation of the inherited pattern rather than passive reception of it.

**[CHAR-16]** E — Conscience-level location (Luk 5:8 — spontaneous recognition; Luk 18:13 — penitential self-abasement; Rom 3:7 — conscience's condemnation-assessment) reveals that the sinner-identity is not only externally assigned (social-stigma VCG-01) or constitutionally imputed (VCG-02) but is also registered internally by the conscience when functioning correctly. The conscience is the faculty that can most precisely assess and name the sinner-identity: Luk 5:8's recognition is accurate; Luk 18:13's plea is appropriate. The conscience's correct engagement with the sinner-identity is the first step toward the repentance that the identity calls for (Luk 5:32 — "sinners to repentance").

**[CHAR-17]** E — Conscience-level location (1Sa 25:31 — pu.qah; Lev 4/5 sequences; Hos 5:15) reveals that CHAR-17 is constitutively a conscience-characteristic: the inner experience of guilt-as-inner-state IS the conscience operating in its guilt-awareness mode. The conscience is not merely a secondary faculty that registers guilt after it exists elsewhere; guilt-as-inner-state is the conscience's specific form of operation when moral liability is recognised. The conscience's stagger (pu.qah — 1Sa 25:31) is the single-term expression of what the guilt-state does to the conscience when it fully engages.

**[CHAR-18]** E — Conscience-level location (2Sa 24:10 — heart-strike; Psa 38:18 — confession and sorrow; Lev 26:40/41 — confession with humbled heart) reveals that conscience is the inner faculty that detects and responds to iniquity-as-accumulated-crime. However, unlike CHAR-17 where conscience is the primary faculty (the characteristic IS conscience in guilt-awareness mode), in CHAR-18 conscience is a secondary responder: the iniquity exists in the divine record independently of conscience (Hos 13:12 — "bound up" whether Ephraim recognises it or not); conscience detects what is already there. The conscience-engagement is productive when it produces confession (Psa 38:18) and suppressed when self-flattery operates (Psa 36:2).

**[CHAR-19]** E — Will-level location (Isa 31:6 — "turn... from whom you revolted"; Eze 18:28 — "considered and turned away"; Eze 18:30 — "repent and turn from all your transgressions") reveals that CHAR-19 is the will-characteristic of M10: the defining inner-being faculty of transgression-as-deliberate-boundary-crossing is the will's volitional capacity to turn (in either direction — toward or away from God). Every remedy-call in the corpus addresses the will's turning: "turn from transgression" (multiple verses in VCG-06). Conscience-level is also engaged (Pro 28:13 — concealment suppresses conscience; Psa 36:1 — transgression speaks in place of conscience's God-fear).

**[CHAR-2]** E — The retrospective conscience location reveals a distinctive feature of CHAR-2: the conscience is not engaged *during* the sinning (which is why the sinning is unintentional) but engages *upon disclosure*. This temporal gap between sin and conscience-engagement is the defining inner-being structure of unintentional sinning. It contrasts with CHAR-1, where the conscience is engaged (and overridden) during the sinning act itself. CHAR-2's conscience functions in a reactive, retrospective mode — it responds to information rather than deterring an act-in-progress.

**[CHAR-20]** E — Will-level location (1Ch 5:25 — allegiance-transfer; Eze 18:24 — turning away from righteousness; Lev 26:40 — walking contrary) reveals that faithlessness is a will-act at the level of covenant-allegiance: the will that breaks covenantal loyalty (the definition). Conscience-level location (Ezr 9:4/10:6 — appalled, mourning) reveals that a functioning conscience is deeply troubled by faithlessness — both in the self and in others. The conscience's response is grief rather than guilt-suppression when faithlessness is recognised.

**[CHAR-21]** E — Desire-level location (Eph 4:22; 2Pe 1:4) reveals the most analytically significant inner-being finding for CHAR-21: desire (*epithumia*) is named as the active mechanism of corruption — "corrupt through deceitful desires." The desire-faculty is not merely associated with perversion but is identified as its engine: the deceitful desire is what the corruption operates through. This makes CHAR-21 M10's characteristic that most precisely locates sin's mechanism in the desire-faculty — a finding not present in any other M10 characteristic studied with this precision.

**[CHAR-22]** E — Will-level location (Eze 18:8 — withholding; Eze 3:20 — turning; Job 34:32 — will-to-cease) reveals CHAR-22 as a will-governed characteristic: the will that chooses to withhold its hand from injustice (Eze 18:8) is the same will that, in the unjust person, deploys the hand in wrong. Conscience-level absence (Zep 3:5 — "knows no shame") is CHAR-22's most distinctive inner-being feature: the shamelessness diagnostic names the conscience's complete non-functioning as the marker of the thoroughly constituted unjust person.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The will-location reveals that confession has a *volitional threshold*: the conscience may have registered (producing the words) without the will being fully reoriented toward the moral reality named. Genuine confession crosses this threshold — the will agrees with the conscience's verdict and the confession expresses that agreement. Hollow confession (VCG-03; Pharaoh; Saul) stays below the threshold — the conscience has registered enough to produce words but the will remains self-directed. The characteristic thus requires not just the heart's striking and the mind's naming but the will's submission to what is being named as wrong.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The will-location (Jer 2:35) reveals that in its active-denial mode, conscience suppression is a *volitional act*: the person chooses to maintain the claim of innocence against the available evidence (God's prophetic word has already declared judgment). This is not innocent ignorance but active refusal. The will's engagement makes the active-denial mode the most culpable form of conscience suppression: the person knows enough to be held to account (Jer 2:35 — God will judge for "saying") but chooses the false claim over honest acknowledgment.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Will-location throughout the corpus reveals that refusal to repent is constitutively and irreducibly a will-event: it is the will's persistent non-departure that constitutes the characteristic. No other faculty can produce refusal to repent — the conscience may register the need to turn (otherwise it would be CHAR-4), the mind may know the truth (Heb 10:26), but it is the will's non-departure that makes it CHAR-5. The will-location is the essential constitutional site of the characteristic.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Will-as-disposition location reveals that habitual defection is the condition where the will no longer needs to make a fresh choice to sin — the disposition has become the default, producing sinning naturally. 1Jo 3:6's "keeps on sinning" describes this: the present continuous is not a series of discrete choices but a sustained directional flow. Hos 8:11 — altars for sinning becoming altars that produce more sinning — shows how the will's settled sinning disposition generates structural supports that make continued sinning the natural path of least resistance. The will is engaged as its dispositional capacity to form habits rather than its episodic capacity to choose.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Will-location reveals that contagious sin is both a leader's volitional act and a community-reshaping volitional force. The leader's will must be committed to the sinning course and must exercise its authority causatively; the community's will is reshaped by the transmitted sinning direction. The key insight from will-location: the community's sinning after contagious sin transmission is volitionally real — the community members are not forced to sin; their will has been shaped toward the sinning direction by the leader's authority. The will is the target of the transmission, not just the instrument.

**[CHAR-8]** E — Will-location reveals that political revolt is constitutively an act of the will: the decision to break submission and assert independence is a volitional act that cannot occur without the will's decisive engagement. The pa.sha root confirms this volitional character — it is not a passive drifting but an active wilful breaking-away. 2Ch 21:10's forsaking (the inner volitional act preceding the revolts) shows that the will's abandonment of God precedes and enables the political will's revolting.

**[CHAR-9]** E — Will-location reveals that sinful speech requires the will's consent to externalise the heart's corruption through the mouth. The heart generates the corrupted content; the will determines whether that content is externalised as speech. Jude 9 — Michael's restraint shows the will can withhold the blasphemous word even where the inner might to say it exists; the will's exercise of restraint is what prevents sinful speech. This confirms the will as the decisive inner faculty that mediates between the corrupted heart and the spoken word.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The "way" (derek) as directional-volitional location reveals that wickedness-as-settled-person-identity is not merely an interior state but an entire life-orientation — the person's direction of travel as a whole. This is analytically important: it means the characteristic is not localised to a discrete faculty but has organised the entire person's movement through life. The "belly" location (Pro 13:25) reveals that wickedness operates at the level of basic appetite — the person's most fundamental need-structure is corrupted (their hunger is perpetually unsatisfied by evil, which cannot nourish). The "eyes" location (Pro 21:4 — haughty eyes) reveals that wickedness occupies even the perceptive-relational faculty by which one relates to others and assesses one's own relative position.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The conscience location (Heb 10:22 — VCG-06) reveals that evil as constitutional inner nature occupies the specifically relational-moral faculty — the conscience that should mediate between the person and God, making approach possible. When the conscience is constitutionally evil ("an evil conscience"), it does not function as a clear channel for approach to God but as a barrier. This reveals the characteristic's most profound relational consequence: it corrupts the very faculty (conscience) whose designed function is to enable the human person's access to God. The characteristic in the conscience is the characteristic at its most theologically consequential location.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The conscience location (VCG-04, 11V) reveals that abomination has a specific and privileged relationship with the conscience as the inner-being faculty designed to register moral violations and produce the appropriate shame-response. The conscience's normal function in relation to abomination is grief and shame: Eze 9:4 (vc=1698 — VCG-04): grieving; Eze 36:31 (vc=1681 — VCG-04): self-loathing upon restored memory. When the conscience is functional, it registers abomination. When it is silenced (Jer 6:15; 8:12 — VCG-04), the abomination proceeds without inner check. The conscience location reveals the characteristic as one whose normal inner-being containment mechanism is specifically the shame-producing conscience — and whose most dangerous form is when that mechanism has been rendered inoperative.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The eyes-as-perceptive-desire faculty (Eze 20:7 — VCG-05; Eze 6:9 — VCG-05) reveal that idolatrous abomination operates through a sustained visual-desire loop: the eyes feast on the detestable things, feeding the soul's attachment to them, which directs the heart further toward them. This is a distinct inner-being mechanism: perception feeding desire feeding attachment feeding further perception. The character of the shiq.quts (idol-objects as things the eyes feast on) shows that the idolatrous objects are presented as attractive to the perceptive faculty — the visual-desire loop is a specific mechanism through which idolatrous attachment deepens.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The tongue-as-location (Psa 10:7 — VCG-04: "under his tongue are mischief and iniquity") reveals that iniquity has a specific concealment-deployment mechanism within the inner person. Iniquity is not only stored in the heart but positioned under the tongue — the speech-faculty's anteroom — ready to be released as harmful speech (cursing, deceit, oppression in the same verse: "his mouth is filled with cursing and deceit and oppression"). This tongue-location reveals the characteristic as having a built-in social delivery mechanism: it generates inwardly (heart-mind), stores sub-lingually, and deploys outwardly through speech. The tongue-location is thus the constitutional bridge between the inner scheming and the outer harm.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The will-location (Jude 8 — VCG-01) reveals that the characteristic's inner source is volitional rather than merely cognitive or affective: the authority-rejection is an act of will that precedes and enables the blasphemous expression. The mouth-location (Rev 13:6 — VCG-01) reveals the characteristic as constitutively embodied in its expression: the mouth is the necessary instrument through which inner wickedness becomes socially operative blasphemy. These two locations — inner will (source) and mouth/speech-instrument (expression) — define the characteristic's constitutional range: it spans from the deepest volitional-inner level to the body's speech-expressing surface.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The conscience is the cluster's most significant beyond-heart-and-mind constitutional location. Char 3 (VCG-04 — 11V Jer 6:15/Jer 8:12/Eze 9:4/Eze 36:31 etc.) provides the richest conscience-evidence: shame present (Eze 9:4 — grieving), shame silenced (Jer 6:15/8:12 — no blush), shame restored (Eze 36:31 — self-loathing). Char 5 (Pro 30:20 — "I have done no wrong") and Char 6 (Rev 16:9/11 — "they did not repent") show the conscience silenced at maximum depth. Char 4 (Eze 8:17 — treating abomination as trivial) shows cognitive-conscience failure. Char 2 (Heb 10:22 — VCG-06: sprinkling of the conscience) and Char 1 (Psa 36:1 — no fear of God) show conscience in its failed state. The conscience is the cluster's primary internal-arresting mechanism — its health or suppression determines whether M10b characteristics can take hold and deepen.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The affective and social-relational dimensions are the other soul-level locations. Affect: the defilement-state activates grief at exclusion and desire for restored access (Num 9:7). Social-relational capacity: the characteristic structurally impairs the person's ability to participate in communal worship and communal life (Lev 13:46, Num 5:2, M10c-A-VCG-07 and M10c-B-VCG-03). This reveals that the characteristic is not only a condition of the body but a condition that restructures the person's social-relational standing within the covenant community.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Will and desire. The will's location reveals the characteristic as a condition that actively constrains freedom — it is not merely a passive colouring of the inner life but a bondage of the willing capacity (Rom 6:19: "slaves"). The desire-location (epithumia) reveals the characteristic as rooted in a specific distortion of the appetitive faculty: desire has been detached from its proper orientation toward God and redirected toward corrupting objects (Rom 1:24 — "lusts of their hearts to impurity"; Col 3:5, VCG-02 — "passion, evil desire, and covetousness").

**[CHAR-3]** E — The memory location (Eze 20:43) reveals the characteristic's most distinctive inner-being contribution: corporate memory of defilement is the mechanism of repentance. Unlike Characteristic 2, where memory is present but ineffective in the hardened state (2Cor 12:21), Characteristic 3 envisions memory as the precisely appointed instrument of corporate moral transformation — the community's future self-loathing will be generated by the memory of its own defilement. This reveals the characteristic as having a built-in eschatological repentance function: the very condition of defilement, when remembered in the context of restoration, becomes the generative force of the community's humility before God.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The will-location and speech/hearing-location reveal the characteristic as targeting the specific soul-level faculties that enable the person's relationship with God (prayer/hearing divine speech) and with others (speech/hearing in community). The suppression of these faculties reveals the characteristic as attacking the person at precisely the soul-level points where their relational-covenantal existence is constituted.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's additional soul-level locations reveal each characteristic's distinctive inner-being signature. Characteristic 1's affect-grief (Num 9:7) reveals the ritual defilement-state as existentially costly — the condition is not emotionally neutral but generates grief at blocked worship desire. Characteristic 2's will-bondage (Rom 6:19 — "slaves to impurity") and desire-misdirection (Rom 1:24 — lusts of the heart) reveal the moral-inner defilement-state as a bondage of the person's motivational core. Characteristic 3's memory function (Eze 20:43 — memory of defilement as repentance mechanism) is the cluster's most analytically distinctive additional location: memory here is not incidentally engaged but specifically appointed as the divinely designed instrument of future corporate repentance — uniquely in the cluster, a soul-level faculty is built into the resolution structure of the characteristic itself. Characteristic 4's speech/hearing suppression (Mar 9:25) reveals the most targeted faculty-suppression: the communicative faculties that enable relationship are specifically attacked.

findings.finding_value: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level (chesed as covenantal-soul character), heart-level (Hos 11:8 — "my heart recoils"), and somatic-level (re.chem, splanchnon) are all richly evidenced. The constitutional architecture is bottom-up: the womb and entrails are the originating ground; the soul and heart are the engagement points; the act is the constitutional expression. Four body-part functions are identified: constitutive (womb — the generative image of compassion), expressive (gut — the felt movement), indicative (Synoptic pattern — splanchnizō signals the compassion-event), and mediating (heart in Hos 11:8 — the deliberative locus where compassion and judgment contend). The four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) is uniquely evidenced in this registry — consistently inside-out and bottom-up. T2.8 established no body deposit; T5.7 is formally closed. The constitutional portrait confirms the sb_classification (soul-body interface) and extends it: compassion is the most somatically grounded characteristic in the programme, with its originating logic residing in the body's deepest interior.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-002: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary…
findings.finding_value: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary point of reception (Zec 12:10 — spirit of grace poured out), not the point of generation (grace originates with God — T2.9). The soul level is the site of standing (Rom 5:2 — "this grace in which we stand") and identity (1Cor 15:10 — "by the grace of God I am what I am"). The constitutional movement follows the SD021 four-faces model: divine disposition received at spirit level → relational standing established at soul level → specific capacity gifted → character expressed outward. Heart-location is partially evidenced via eusplanchnos (Eph 4:32 — the tenderheartedness that grace produces, reaching the affective-somatic interface). T2.7 produces a new finding: grace operates bidirectionally through the body-soul interface — soul-to-body (inner posture enacted somatically in prostration, fasting, sackcloth) and body-to-soul (somatic enactment deepening and confirming the inner posture). T2.8 remains open (body deposit question unresolved); T5.7 is left open accordingly. The constitutional origin analysis (T2.9) is the most analytically significant T2 finding: grace does not originate in the human constitutional system at any level — it arrives from outside. This is confirmed at T6 as the structural uniqueness of grace: the only characteristic that is not produced by any other inner-being characteristic.

findings.session_b_note:
The body is present in the corpus but not as a primary locus. Q038 answer identifies four body-related appearances:

1. **Blood of Christ (Eph 1:7; Heb 9:22):** The physical body as the site of the atoning act that enables forgiveness — "redemption through his blood." Blood is the specific body-element named.

2. **The woman's bodily acts (Luk 7:47):** Weeping and anointing as the bodily expression of received forgiveness — "the body as the surface on which inner transformation becomes visible."

3. **The paralytic's healing (Mat 9:2-6):** Forgiveness pronounced, then healing follows — a body-part connection implied (the healed body as downstream of the forgiveness act), though not mechanically stated.

4. **Visceral compassion (splagchnizomai, Mat 18:27):** The gut/spleen as the bodily location of the compassion that precedes the act of forgiving. Q038 names this: "the body's visceral response (gut, spleen) as the felt origin of the act of forgiving."

The specific body parts implied: **blood** (mechanism), **eyes/hands/feet** (the woman's bodily acts — though not individually named), **the diseased body** (the paralytic), **the gut** (splagchnizomai).

findings.session_b_note:
Yes — and this is among the strongest and most explicit body-part links in the programme. Two primary anatomical anchors:

**The womb (re.chem / ra.cham):** H7358 re.chem and H7356A ra.cham link compassion directly and etymologically to the womb. The word for compassion (ra.cham) is the same root as the word for womb (re.chem). This is not a metaphorical extension — the lexical relationship is built into the language. Isa 46:3 ("carried from the womb") and Psa 22:10 ("from my mother's womb you have been my God") use the womb as the originating space of divine care and compassion.

**The entrails / gut (splanchnon / splanchnizō):** G4697 splanchnizō names the gut-movement of compassion. Its root is G4698 splanchnon (entrails, affections). The abdominal organs were understood in the ancient world as the seat of the deepest emotions. Jesus's compassion movements in the Synoptics are all named through this gut-vocabulary. Jas 5:11 (polusplanchnos — "of great gut-compassion") intensifies the somatic grounding.

**The heart (lev):** Hos 11:8 — "my heart recoils within me." The heart is a secondary body-part link, functioning here as the organ of inner deliberation and feeling rather than as the primary etymological ground.

findings.session_b_note:
Yes — two body-part references appear in the verse evidence:

1. **Bones** (Psa 51:8): "let the bones that you have broken rejoice." The bones are the skeletal structure — the body's deepest physical core. God is said to have broken the psalmist's bones (H1794 — da.khah, the same term used of contrite heart). The bones function as the somatic image for the innermost structural integrity of the person — when the bones are broken, the whole person is structurally undone.

2. **Somatic embodiment of inner states** (Jer 46:5): "turned backward... fled in haste... terror on every side." The warriors' inner terror (H3807) is expressed through their bodily behaviour — turning, fleeing. The body expresses the inner state. This is a behavioural/somatic expression rather than a named body-part link.

findings.session_b_note:
Yes. The wound-fellowship vocabulary links fellowship explicitly to the body:

- **Pro 20:30** — *blows that wound* (H2250 chabbûrāh — the wound-joining term) — the *innermost parts* are named as the site of purification through wounding. Physical blows are the fellowship mechanism; the innermost parts of the body are the site.
- **Isa 53:5** — *with his wounds we are healed* — the wounds (H2250) of the servant produce healing in others. The body of the servant bears the fellowship of suffering; the inner-being of the recipient receives healing.
- **Phili 3:10** — *share his sufferings, becoming like him in his death* — somatic language (sufferings, death) is used for the deepest fellowship with Christ.

The chavar/chabbûrāh root family's physical joining vocabulary also establishes structural body-links: the tabernacle curtain joinings (identified in DIM-062-SD001 as analogically significant) use the same root as the fellowship vocabulary for inner-being joining.

No other specific body part is explicitly linked to goodness in the anchor verse evidence. The Psa 34:8 "taste and see" metaphor uses perceptual language (taste, see) that implies sensory or quasi-physical engagement, but this is figurative language for inner perception rather than a literal body-part linkage. The data is thin here. (OBS-067-OBS-007, OBS-067-OBS-041)

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-103-002: Love is the programme's most constitutionally comprehensive characteristic — it occupies all five constitutional levels simultaneously: spirit-sourced (implied via Spirit-as-agent, Rom 5:5, Gal 5:22),…
findings.finding_value: Love is the programme's most constitutionally comprehensive characteristic — it occupies all five constitutional levels simultaneously: spirit-sourced (implied via Spirit-as-agent, Rom 5:5, Gal 5:22), soul-located (Song 5:6 — soul failing at beloved's absence; Mat 22:37 — love with all your soul; Joh 15:13 — laying down the soul), heart-inscribed (Pro 3:3; Rom 5:5 infused into hearts), mind-engaged (Mat 22:37 — love with all your mind; Joh 15:15 — love as knowledge-sharing), and body-expressed (kiss, embrace, tears, womb-movement across multiple groups). The constitutional movement pattern is consistently downward: Spirit origin → heart reception → soul experience → body expression. Love's heart-inscription (Pro 3:3) is the closest evidence to a constitutional deposit — the metaphorical writing of chesed into the heart's deepest register produces a lasting dispositional quality (the chasid person-type). The primary finding: love is not confined to any single constitutional level but operates across all levels in an integrated movement from deepest to most outward. This comprehensive constitutional architecture is consistent with love's function as the programme's organising characteristic.

findings.finding_value: The evidential foundation supports and grounds the constitutional location claims. Each constitutional level identified in T2 has specific vocabulary evidence in T7: Spirit-level origin — Gal 5:22 (fruit of the Spirit), Rom 5:5 (poured into hearts through the Spirit); soul-level — Song 5:6 (soul failing), Mat 22:37 (all your soul), Joh 15:13 (lay down the soul); heart-level — Pro 3:3 (heart inscription), Rom 5:5 (into our hearts); mind-level — Mat 22:37 (all your mind), Joh 15:15 (knowledge disclosure); body-level — kiss/embrace/tears/inner-organ-movement vocabulary across multiple groups. The lexical range of the primary terms (Q&A-122 — chesed, racham, agapē, dod, phileō) corresponds precisely to the five constitutional levels: each term carries a different constitutional register as its primary habitat. The evidential foundation thus not only confirms the constitutional claims but shows them to be lexically grounded in the vocabulary's own structure.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-111-002: T2 reveals mercy as a whole-person constitutional reality. No single level contains it: mercy originates at the spirit-soul interface, operates on the soul (addressing the nephesh-guilt), engages the …
findings.finding_value: T2 reveals mercy as a whole-person constitutional reality. No single level contains it: mercy originates at the spirit-soul interface, operates on the soul (addressing the nephesh-guilt), engages the heart through the visceral compassion vocabulary (splanchna), engages the mind through the memory-erasure mechanism (Heb 8:12), and operates through the body as both the medium of mercy-seeking (embodied posture) and the mechanism of mercy's effect (blood-atonement). The triadic constitutional movement (Q&A-065): inner disposition → soul-transformation → embodied expression. The key finding reading T2 as a whole is the receiving-before-generating origin structure (Q&A-062): mercy cannot be generated from within the person but must be received from outside and then expressed through the constitutional architecture. Body deposit: none. T5.7: formally closed.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-111-015: T2 establishes the receiving-before-generating constitutional principle (Q&A-062) and T4 establishes the asymmetric relational chain (God→received human→extended human mercy). These are the constituti…
findings.finding_value: T2 establishes the receiving-before-generating constitutional principle (Q&A-062) and T4 establishes the asymmetric relational chain (God→received human→extended human mercy). These are the constitutional and relational descriptions of the same structural requirement: mercy cannot be generated from within the person (T2) and mercy cannot be extended without prior receipt (T4). T2 explains why T4's relational chain is necessary: the constitutional principle of receiving-before-generating is what creates the structural necessity of the T4 relational chain. The body-soul interface through which mercy's mechanism operates (T2 — blood atonement on nephesh) is the constitutionally specific expression of the God→human directional mercy (T4.1).
