findings.finding_value: T2's soul-level atoning operation (the nephesh addressed by kipper) maps to T6's sequential positioning of mercy (mercy as bridge from negative condition to positive outcome). The constitutionally specific operation on the nephesh (T2) is what makes mercy the bridge across the most fundamental negative condition (guilt as soul-condition addressed by atonement). T6's co-occurrence with guilt (R073 at 75) and its cross-registry sequential bridging function are the relational expression of T2's constitutional operation at the soul level. Mercy bridges guilt to forgiveness (T6) because it operates constitutionally on the soul-level guilt-condition (T2).

findings.finding_value: T7's vocabulary arc maps lexically to T2's constitutional architecture. The womb-root vocabulary (T7 — racham/rechem) corresponds to T2's spirit-soul interface location. The soul-level atonement vocabulary (kipper/kaphar) corresponds to T2's soul-level operation on the nephesh. The embodied seeking vocabulary (hilaskomai in Luk 18:13) corresponds to T2's body-level expression. The mercy seat vocabulary (kapporet/hilastērios) corresponds to T2's spatial locus. T7's finding that the vocabulary arc is a theological narrative (Q&A-180) is confirmed by T2: the vocabulary traces the constitutional journey mercy makes through the inner-being structure.

findings.finding_value: T2 establishes that contrition operates at the deepest constitutional level (spirit as primary locus) with secondary engagement at heart, soul, and body. The constitutional portrait is comprehensive: spirit broken at the innermost level, heart broken at the moral-evaluative level, nephesh crushed at the whole-self level, and bones as the somatic expression of the inner breaking. What T2 reveals as a whole is the embodied depth of contrition — it is not a disembodied inner experience but a constitutional event that traverses all levels of the person. The bidirectional constitutional movement (downward through divine confrontation, upward through reviving) is the structural frame within which contrition functions: it reaches the bottom and creates the conditions for movement back upward. The T2.8 finding (no body deposit) means contrition does not leave a permanent somatic trace — it is a passing constitutional event, not a permanent constitutional mark.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-064-002: T2 reveals that forgiveness engages multiple constitutional levels but with a distinctive constitutional pattern. The heart is the one explicitly named locus — Mat 18:35 ("from your heart") names the …
findings.finding_value: T2 reveals that forgiveness engages multiple constitutional levels but with a distinctive constitutional pattern. The heart is the one explicitly named locus — Mat 18:35 ("from your heart") names the heart as the required depth of genuine forgiveness-giving. The cognition-faculty (Jer 31:34 — "remember no more"; "they shall know me") is the most clearly evidenced constitutional engagement alongside the heart. The somatic compassion faculty (splagchnizomai — Mat 18:27) is the named somatic-affective origin-point of the forgiving act. Spirit and soul levels are inferred from the guilt-forgiveness structural relationship and the Spirit's mediating role (Mar 3:29, Joh 20:23) rather than explicitly named. The body-deposit question is data-silent (T2.8); T5.7 closes formally. The constitutional movement is explicit (Luk 7:47 — guilt-bearing → forgiveness received → love generated; Jer 31:34 — forgiveness → direct knowledge of God). T2's key finding: the constitutional structure of forgiveness is act-centred, not state-centred — it is a constitutional event (the moment of release) that produces constitutional consequences (love, reverence, direct access).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-008: T1 establishes forgiveness as an act; T2 maps where the act is constitutionally located. The four modes (T1) each engage different constitutional levels (T2): covenantal-objective mode engages no name…
findings.finding_value: T1 establishes forgiveness as an act; T2 maps where the act is constitutionally located. The four modes (T1) each engage different constitutional levels (T2): covenantal-objective mode engages no named inner-being locus (external mechanism); divine relational-personal mode engages the full constitutional range (spirit, heart, cognition — via the access-postures of faith, repentance, confession); human horizontal mode explicitly requires the heart (Mat 18:35); intercessory mode requires the dependence-posture at the constitutional level of the plea. The somatic compassion origin-point (T2.5 — splagchnizomai) is the constitutional expression of the volitional-release act (T1.4.1 — the act must be chosen). Definition and constitutional location are co-determining: the mode of forgiveness determines which constitutional level is engaged.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-015: T2's constitutional origin (divine character as the source — Psa 86:5, Psa 130:4) explains T4's God-to-human directional dominance. Because forgiveness originates exclusively in divine character at th…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional origin (divine character as the source — Psa 86:5, Psa 130:4) explains T4's God-to-human directional dominance. Because forgiveness originates exclusively in divine character at the deepest level, the primary relational direction is necessarily God-initiated toward the human. T2's heart-locus requirement (Mat 18:35) explains T4's giving-direction requirement: genuine horizontal forgiveness requires the same constitutional depth as the received vertical (heart-level in both cases). The somatic-compassion origin (T2.5) is the constitutional enabler of the horizontal-giving direction (T4.3): the person who genuinely gives forgiveness does so from a somatic-affective inner origin (splagchnizomai), not merely a verbal performance.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-017: T2's cognitive-locus finding (Jer 31:34 — forgiveness engages and enables cognition) explains the R160 thought co-occurrence at Jer 31:34. T2's somatic-compassion locus (splagchnizomai — Mat 18:27) ex…

T2's heart-locus requirement (Mat 18:35) explains the R073 guilt co-occurrence at the heart level — guilt is the heart-level prior condition that forgiveness addresses at the heart level. Constitutional location and co-occurrence signals are mutually confirming: every major constitutional locus of forgiveness corresponds to a co-occurrence registry that operates in the same constitutional space.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-018: T2's constitutional levels are each evidenced by specific grammatical forms in T7. Heart-locus (Mat 18:35 — heart-level requirement) is carried by the G0863H imperative forms in the horizontal command…

Cognition-locus (Jer 31:34) is carried by the H5545 Niphal passive (the worshipper as receiver) and the se.li.chah noun (forgiveness as the quality God has, which enables the cognitive-relational access). T7 provides the grammatical evidence base for T2's constitutional account.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-002: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level …
findings.finding_value: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level (chesed as covenantal-soul character), heart-level (Hos 11:8 — "my heart recoils"), and somatic-level (re.chem, splanchnon) are all richly evidenced. The constitutional architecture is bottom-up: the womb and entrails are the originating ground; the soul and heart are the engagement points; the act is the constitutional expression. Four body-part functions are identified: constitutive (womb — the generative image of compassion), expressive (gut — the felt movement), indicative (Synoptic pattern — splanchnizō signals the compassion-event), and mediating (heart in Hos 11:8 — the deliberative locus where compassion and judgment contend). The four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) is uniquely evidenced in this registry — consistently inside-out and bottom-up. T2.8 established no body deposit; T5.7 is formally closed. The constitutional portrait confirms the sb_classification (soul-body interface) and extends it: compassion is the most somatically grounded characteristic in the programme, with its originating logic residing in the body's deepest interior.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-008: T1's four-kind structure (character quality, inner event, condition of object, externalised act) maps precisely onto T2's constitutional levels. The character-quality kind (ra.chum — dispositional com…
findings.finding_value: T1's four-kind structure (character quality, inner event, condition of object, externalised act) maps precisely onto T2's constitutional levels. The character-quality kind (ra.chum — dispositional compassionate character) operates at the soul level (T2.2 — chesed as soul-character). The inner-event kind (splanchnizō — the moment of being-moved) operates at the somatic level (T2.6 — the gut as the site of the stirring). The condition-of-object kind (eleeinos — the pitiable state) is the constitutional trigger that activates the somatic-constitutional movement. The externalised-act kind is the constitutional endpoint of T2.10's four-stage movement sequence. T1's definition and T2's constitutional account are co-determining: the characteristic cannot be adequately defined without specifying the constitutional levels at which its four kinds operate.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-014: T2's four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) maps directly onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The somatic-arousal s…
findings.finding_value: T2's four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) maps directly onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The somatic-arousal stage (T2.6 — gut stirring, splanchnizō) corresponds to T3.1's perceptive-trigger stage (sight activates the somatic response) and T3.4's affect stage (the stirring is the affective movement). The soul-engagement stage (T2.2 — chesed as soul-character) corresponds to T3.8 moral evaluation (the soul assesses the need) and T3.9 conscience (the conscience activates the response). The volitional-engagement stage (T2.3 — heart-locus as deliberative site) corresponds to T3.6 volition (the will directs the action). The outward-action stage corresponds to T3.7 agency. T2 and T3 describe the same movement sequence from two perspectives: T2 maps the constitutional levels; T3 maps the faculties active at each level.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-015: T2's constitutional origin analysis (somatic-relational-covenantal triple ground) and T4's relational direction analysis are structurally aligned. The somatic origin (womb, gut) grounds the cross-boun…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional origin analysis (somatic-relational-covenantal triple ground) and T4's relational direction analysis are structurally aligned. The somatic origin (womb, gut) grounds the cross-boundary relational direction in T4: splanchnizō's somatic immediacy is precisely what enables it to cross covenantal boundaries — the gut-movement toward the suffering other precedes any covenantal assessment of the relationship. The covenantal origin (chesed) grounds the within-bond sustaining direction in T4. The constitutional origin therefore predicts the relational direction: somatic = cross-boundary; covenantal = within-bond. T2's soul-body interface classification explains T4's scope-by-need finding: because compassion originates at the soul-body interface (before covenantal-rational assessment), its scope is determined by the pre-rational recognition of need rather than the post-rational assessment of covenantal standing.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-017: T2's somatic-constitutional location explains several T6 structural connections. The shared anchor at Isa 53:5 (with R030 contrition) confirms that the somatic wound vocabulary intersects both compass…
findings.finding_value: T2's somatic-constitutional location explains several T6 structural connections. The shared anchor at Isa 53:5 (with R030 contrition) confirms that the somatic wound vocabulary intersects both compassion and contrition at the constitutional-somatic level — both characteristics have somatic-body language as part of their evidential ground. The CHASAD root's crossing of compassion and shame clusters (T6.4 — most unexpected structural finding) is partly explainable from T2: if CHASAD names a covenantal-soul disposition, it can operate in both the positive register (chesed — steadfast love/compassion) and the negative register (bōsheth — shame as the opposite soul-condition of exposed vulnerability). T2's constitutional portrait (soul-body interface) is the constitutional ground for the root-level cluster-crossing that T6 identifies.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-018: T2's constitutional levels are each carried by specific vocabulary families in T7. The somatic-body level (T2.6 — gut, womb) is carried by the RACHAM/SPLANCHN root families — the body's interior as th…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional levels are each carried by specific vocabulary families in T7. The somatic-body level (T2.6 — gut, womb) is carried by the RACHAM/SPLANCHN root families — the body's interior as the etymological ground of both. The soul-character level (T2.2) is carried by the CHASAD family — chesed as the settled covenantal character disposition. The heart-deliberative level (T2.3) is evidenced most richly in Hos 11:8 (T7's primary anchor for divine compassion). T7's vocabulary arc (womb to almsgiving) traverses exactly the constitutional range T2 maps: from the most interior somatic level (womb) through the character-soul level to the externalised action level. The dual primary anchor (T7) maps onto T2's constitutional depth: Hos 11:8 evidences constitutional depth (heart-level deliberation of compassion over judgment); Luke 10:33 evidences constitutional breadth (the full four-stage movement from sight to action).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-002: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary…
findings.finding_value: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary point of reception (Zec 12:10 — spirit of grace poured out), not the point of generation (grace originates with God — T2.9). The soul level is the site of standing (Rom 5:2 — "this grace in which we stand") and identity (1Cor 15:10 — "by the grace of God I am what I am"). The constitutional movement follows the SD021 four-faces model: divine disposition received at spirit level → relational standing established at soul level → specific capacity gifted → character expressed outward. Heart-location is partially evidenced via eusplanchnos (Eph 4:32 — the tenderheartedness that grace produces, reaching the affective-somatic interface). T2.7 produces a new finding: grace operates bidirectionally through the body-soul interface — soul-to-body (inner posture enacted somatically in prostration, fasting, sackcloth) and body-to-soul (somatic enactment deepening and confirming the inner posture). T2.8 remains open (body deposit question unresolved); T5.7 is left open accordingly. The constitutional origin analysis (T2.9) is the most analytically significant T2 finding: grace does not originate in the human constitutional system at any level — it arrives from outside. This is confirmed at T6 as the structural uniqueness of grace: the only characteristic that is not produced by any other inner-being characteristic.

findings.session_b_note: Yes — two body-part links are evidenced. (1) Blood: the covenant is sealed and constituted through blood in multiple traditions — "the blood of the covenant" (Exo 24:8, echoed in Mat 26:28, Mar 14:24, Heb 9:20, Heb 13:20 — OBS-034-058, OBS-034-074). The blood of sacrifice (OT) and of Christ (NT) is the physical substance through which the covenant is enacted and confirmed. Blood is the bodily medium of covenant-making and covenant-sealing. (2) Circumcision: Act 7:8 — "he gave him the covenant of circumcision" — circumcision as the bodily sign of the Abrahamic covenant. The covenant is physically inscribed on the male body as its permanent sign. Both blood and circumcision are body-part links that carry distinct significances — blood as the sealing substance, circumcision as the identifying mark.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-034-002: T2 as a whole reveals that covenant operates across the full constitutional range of the inner person with no single exclusive location. The heart is the primary site (Q&A-044), the mind is co-located…
findings.finding_value: T2 as a whole reveals that covenant operates across the full constitutional range of the inner person with no single exclusive location. The heart is the primary site (Q&A-044), the mind is co-located (Q&A-047), the soul gives totality of engagement (Q&A-041), the mouth is the expressive-constitutive organ (Q&A-050), and the body participates through blood and circumcision (Q&A-053). The single most structurally significant T2 finding is the constitutional movement shift from OT to NT covenantal mode: OT covenant moves outer→inner→outer; new covenant moves inner→inner→outer (Q&A-066). This movement-shift is the constitutional-level expression of the Sinai-to-new-covenant transformation — it places the origin of covenant faithfulness at the level of God's own interior action within the person rather than the person's compliance with external demand. T2 confirms that covenant is constitutively somatic as well as inner — it cannot be reduced to a purely invisible spiritual reality because it is enacted, sealed, and transmitted through bodily acts and substances.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-034-015: T2 reveals that covenant operates constitutionally in the heart, mind, soul, mouth, and body. T4 reveals that covenant operates relationally through God-to-human, human-to-God, and horizontal interfac…
findings.finding_value: T2 reveals that covenant operates constitutionally in the heart, mind, soul, mouth, and body. T4 reveals that covenant operates relationally through God-to-human, human-to-God, and horizontal interfaces. The T2 × T4 synthesis: the constitutional locations and the relational interfaces are not separate registers — they are the same inner reality viewed from different angles. The soul's engagement in covenant (T2 — "with all his heart and all his soul") is precisely the inner posture required for genuine human-to-God movement (T4.2 — Q&A-106). The mouth as constitutional location (T2 — Isa 59:21) is the organ through which the human-to-God relational direction is enacted (oath as speech act — Q&A-024, T1.4). The blood as somatic covenant-medium (T2 — Q&A-053) is the mediating substance through which the God-to-human interface is constituted (the blood of the covenant — Q&A-101). Constitutional location and relational interface are two views of the same inner-being dynamic.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-034-018: T2 identifies blood and circumcision as the primary somatic covenant locations. T7 establishes the lexical arc showing covenant as simultaneously relational, bodily, oral, legal, moral, transformative…
findings.finding_value: T2 identifies blood and circumcision as the primary somatic covenant locations. T7 establishes the lexical arc showing covenant as simultaneously relational, bodily, oral, legal, moral, transformative, and eschatological. The T2 × T7 synthesis: the bodily dimension identified in T2 is confirmed and deepened by the lexical analysis of T7. The root meaning of karat (to cut — Q&A-170) and the blood-of-the-covenant vocabulary are etymologically embedded in the bodily-somatic dimension of the covenant vocabulary arc. The LXX translation choice (diathēkē — Q&A-177) adds the death/inheritance dimension to the somatic vocabulary: the blood is the means of mediation, and the testator's death is required for the testament to take effect. T2's somatic findings are not incidental features but are inscribed in the etymology and semantic development of the vocabulary itself (T7).

Soul-level (T2.2) ↔ Affect (T3.4) — the soul's peace is primarily affective (Lam 3:17, Psa 62:5); Heart-level (T2.3) ↔ Moral evaluation + Volition + Conscience (T3.8/6/9) — the heart engages the moral-volitional-conscience cluster; Mind-level (T2.4) ↔ Cognition (T3.2) — the mind's directed orientation; Body-level (T2.6) ↔ Agency (T3.7) — the body's actions express inner peace; Hidden-person (T2.5) ↔ Conscientiousness (T3.10) — the hidden person of the heart is the site of the most integrated response. The constitutional and faculty maps are not independent but interlocking descriptions of the same whole-person reality.

The body's somatic evidence (T2.6/7) connects directly to T5's suffering-and-discipline findings: the bones wasting (Psa 32:3) is the T5 suffering-as-formation pathway reversed — where sustained peace-withholding produces deterioration, the discipline of Heb 12:11 produces peace-in-body over time. The constitutional movement patterns (T2.10) are the spatial description of what T5 describes temporally: the cascading gift pattern (God → spirit → soul/mind → body) is the sequence by which peace is received and formed over time (T5.2) through the mechanisms of divine word, Spirit, and discipline (T5.3).

findings.finding_value: T2's body evidence (Psa 38:3 — no sha.lom in bones because of sin) connects directly to T6's finding that reconciliation constitutes relational peace (Col 1:20, Eph 2:14) — the same sha.lom that is absent from bones when sin is present is the sha.lom that reconciliation restores. The SHA.L root (T6.4.2) names completeness — and Psa 38:3's use of sha.lom for somatic soundness is directly rooted in this: sha.lom IS somatic completeness, sha.lom IS relational completeness, sha.lom IS covenantal completeness — one root, all dimensions. The constitutional and structural analyses confirm the same root-level truth from different angles.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-060-002: T2 as a whole reveals that this characteristic has no single constitutional home — it operates across the full spirit-soul-body register through different modes. Spirit is the location in two modes: a…
findings.finding_value: T2 as a whole reveals that this characteristic has no single constitutional home — it operates across the full spirit-soul-body register through different modes. Spirit is the location in two modes: as the object of endowing giving (Neh 9:20) and as the faculty transformed eschatologically (Isa 61:3). Soul (nephesh/nafshi) appears in divine self-reference in the giving-over context (Jer 12:7). Heart (leb) is the faculty where the giving decision is made (Hos 11:8). Hidden inner parts (tukhoth) are the target of wisdom-giving (Job 38:36). Rahamim (visceral compassion) is the inner-being quality that determines giving direction. Body appears as the expressive medium of self-giving (Isa 50:6) and as constituted by breath-giving (Isa 42:5). No constitutional body deposit is confirmed. Three movement patterns — constitutive (spirit→mind), expressive (inner→body), transformative (outside-in→inside renewed→inside-out) — show the characteristic is constitutionally dynamic. What T2 reveals as a whole: this characteristic operates at every constitutional level not because it is superficially distributed but because giving as an inner-being act can reach the spirit (endowing), the heart (deciding), the soul (attaching), the hidden inner parts (forming), and the body (expressing and constituting). It is constitutionally pervasive.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-008: The constitutional locations where the characteristic operates (T2 — heart, soul/nephesh, spirit, body) and the relational interfaces through which it operates (T4 — God-to-human, human-to-God) reveal…
findings.finding_value: The constitutional locations where the characteristic operates (T2 — heart, soul/nephesh, spirit, body) and the relational interfaces through which it operates (T4 — God-to-human, human-to-God) reveal a mirroring structure. God's giving proceeds from his leb (heart, Hos 11:8) and his nafshi (soul, Jer 12:7) — the deepest divine inner-being locations are engaged in the God-to-human direction. The human's giving toward God is expressed through the body (back, cheeks, face — Isa 50:6) and from the deepest inner orientation (Job 1:21 — recognition of divine sovereignty). The constitutional depths engaged in both directions are commensurate: God gives from his heart and soul; the human gives from the whole self, expressed bodily. What this pair reveals: the divine-human relational correspondence (DHC dimension, group 872-006) has a constitutional depth structure — the correspondence is not merely behavioural but engages the deepest constitutional levels of both parties. The giving that constitutes the correspondence is heart-to-body deep.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-011: The constitutional evidence (T2 — spirit, heart, soul, hidden inner parts, body all engaged) and the lexical/literary evidence (T7 — na.tan as exclusively verbal, Hos 11:8 as primary anchor) mutually …
findings.finding_value: The constitutional evidence (T2 — spirit, heart, soul, hidden inner parts, body all engaged) and the lexical/literary evidence (T7 — na.tan as exclusively verbal, Hos 11:8 as primary anchor) mutually confirm. The lexical finding that na.tan is grammatically a verb (T7, Q&A-171) is the lexical expression of the constitutional finding that the characteristic moves across constitutional levels through distinct movement patterns (T2.10) — a verb in motion describes constitutional movement in language. Hos 11:8 as primary anchor (T7.2.5) identifies precisely the verse that shows the deepest constitutional engagement: leb (heart) and rahamim (visceral inner parts) both named in a single verse showing inner-being movement. The verse evidence and constitutional analysis converge on the same verse for the same reason: it is the verse where constitutional depth and inner-being movement are most explicitly disclosed. What this pair reveals: the lexical and constitutional evidence are independently converging on the same structural reality.

**BOUNDARY characterisation — Category 1: Physical locations and acts of relational expression.** Terms: H2436G cheq (bosom/embrace), G5370 filēma (kiss), G2705 katafileō (to kiss). These terms name the bodily, spatial, and somatic register through which the cluster's inner characteristics are expressed outward. The bosom is the physical location of intimacy — the space where cherishing is enacted in the body (Rut 4:16; 2Sa 12:3; Isa 40:11). The kiss is the enacted outward sign of the inner relational state: holy kiss of greeting (Rom 16:16; 1Cor 16:20; 2Cor 13:12; 1Th 5:26; 1Pe 5:14); kiss of Judas (Mat 26:49; Mar 14:45; Luk 22:48). Why BOUNDARY: these terms name the expressive act or spatial location — the point where the inner characteristic contacts the body and the social world. Cheq is where love is held, not love itself; filēma is what love does with the face, not what love is. What this reveals: the cluster's inner characteristics are not merely cognitive or volitional but seek embodied expression.
**[A1 — God Righteousness]** No body-part link for God's righteousness.

**[A2 — Human Righteousness]** Yes — mouth/lips as the body part through which righteousness expresses itself (VSG M26-A2-011: speech and discernment). "The mouth of the righteous brings forth wisdom" (Pro 10:31) and "the tongue of the righteous is choice silver" (Pro 10:20, implied in A2-011). The mouth is the body-part channel of righteous speech. Additionally, "hands" — the righteous person "shakes his hands, lest they hold a bribe" (Isa 33:15, B-group, also relevant here): the hands as the body-part expression of the decision not to receive bribes.

**[B — Moral Uprightness]** Yes — lips and tongue. "Speak uprightly" (Isa 33:15, VSG 1212-002); "from my lips will come what is right" (Pro 8:6, VSG 1212-002); "my inmost being will exult when your lips speak what is right" (Pro 23:16, VSG 1212-002). The lips/tongue are the body-part link for uprightness — the inner disposition of straightness expresses itself through the organ of speech.
**[C — Justification]** No body-part link for justification.
**[D — Avenging Justice]** No direct body-part link for avenging justice in the verse evidence.

**[E — Condemnation]** Yes — the mouth/words. "By your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned" (Mat 12:37, VSG 3201-001). The mouth is the instrument of self-condemnation — the words that come from the person become the ground of the verdict. "Your own mouth condemns you, and not I; your own lips testify against you" (Job 15:6, VSG 1225-002, in G-subgroup but directly relevant). The mouth as the body-part that produces the self-condemning evidence.
**[F — Moral Reckoning]** The reckoning faculty is a cognitive-internal function. No body-part link evidenced.

**[G — Structural Opposites]** Yes — mouth/lips (as per E above: Job 15:6, "your own mouth condemns you"). The wicked person's own words bear witness against them. Also implicated: "hands" in a negative sense — the unjust grasp of the unjust and cruel man (Psa 71:4, VSG 5617-001: "from the grasp of the unjust and cruel man"). The hands as the instrument of the unjust act.

**[CLUSTER — T2.6]** E. The primary body-part link in M26 is the mouth/lips/tongue — the organ of speech through which righteousness expresses itself (A2-011, B) and through which condemnation is generated (E, G). The secondary body-part link is the hands — the instrument of righteous or unjust action. The body-part links in this cluster are consistently expressive: the inner state of righteousness or wickedness manifests through the speech-organ and the action-organ.

findings.finding_value: M01-A has one explicit body-part link: Psa 119:120 (M01-E-VCG-02, but relevant to the reverential dimension): "Fear of God's judgments produces a somatic response — **the psalmist's flesh trembles**." The flesh is the body-part named. Lev 19:14's prohibition against exploiting "the deaf and the blind" implies bodily vulnerability as the context for fear's ethical restraint, but the fear itself is not located in a specific body part.

M01-B has body-part links through the trembling-in-the-heart pattern: 1Sa 28:5 (Saul's trembling "explicitly located in **his heart**" — the heart as a body-organ), Neh 2:2 (fear "visible in his countenance" — the face as the body-part expressing the inner fear).

M01-C-VCG-04 has an explicit body-part link: Psa 55:4 (anchor: "terror is located **in the heart** — the terrors of death fall upon the psalmist, causing inner anguish so intense it is felt as a physical collapse within **the chest**"). **[CHAR-19]** E — Yes — three body-part links. (1) *Lips and mouth*: Pro 10:19 — "when words are many, transgression is not lacking" — the lips/mouth as the body-part through which transgression overflows; Pro 12:13 — "ensnared by the transgression of his lips"; Isa 59:13 — "uttering from the heart lying words"; (2) *Neck/shoulders*: Lam 1:14 — "transgressions were bound into a yoke... set upon my neck" — the neck/shoulders as the body-part bearing the yoke-burden of transgression; (3) *Head*: Isa 1:5 — "the whole head is sick" — sustained revolt-transgression incapacitates the whole head.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The corpus contains limited body-part evidence. The ritual actions described in VCG-02 involve specific body-located acts: Lev 8:15 ("Moses took the blood, and with his finger put it on the horns of the altar") — the finger as the instrument of purification. Lev 9:15 (Aaron killing the goat of the sin offering) involves hands. However, these are priestly body-parts performing the remedial ritual, not body parts of the sinner. Within the personal-moral register (VCG-01), no specific body part is named in connection with unintentional sinning. The act occurs without a specified body-part instrument (unlike CHAR-1's tongue/lips/hands). The 1Sa 14:33/34 context (eating with blood) involves the mouth as the instrument — "eating" — but the Pass A meaning does not foreground the body-part specifically.

**[CHAR-20]** E — Yes — two body-part links. (1) *Face and back*: 2Ch 29:6 — "they have forsaken him and have turned away their faces from the habitation of the Lord and turned their backs" — the face and the back are the body-parts through which the inner faithlessness is expressed; turning the back on God is the bodily enactment of the heart's turning; (2) *Womb and thigh*: Num 5:27 — "her womb shall swell, and her thigh shall fall away" — the faithless wife's reproductive organs are the body-parts on which the curse of faithlessness falls; the bodily consequence is located at the very organ that embodied the covenant of marriage.

**[CHAR-21]** E — Yes — three body-part links. (1) *Mouth, lips, tongue*: Pro 4:24 — "put away from you crooked speech, put devious talk far from you"; Pro 10:31 — "the perverse tongue will be cut off"; Pro 10:32 — "the mouth of the wicked, what is perverse"; (2) *Eyes*: Pro 16:30 — "whoever winks his eyes plans dishonest things" — the eye-wink as the bodily signal of perverse inner plotting; Exo 23:8 — "a bribe blinds the clear-sighted" — the eyes as the faculty blinded by bribery-perversion; (3) *The bowed/bent back*: Psa 38:6 — "I am utterly bowed down and prostrate" — the body bent by sin's weight.

**[CHAR-22]** E — Yes — three body-part links. (1) *Hands*: Psa 58:2 — "your hands deal out violence on earth"; Psa 7:3 — "if there is wrong in my hands"; Eze 18:8 — "withholds his hand from injustice"; (2) *Tongue/lips/mouth*: Isa 59:3 — "your tongue mutters wickedness"; Job 6:30 — "is there any injustice on my tongue?"; Zep 3:13 — "speak no lies"; Mal 2:6 — "no wrong was found on his lips"; (3) *Fingers*: Isa 59:3 — "your hands are defiled with blood and your fingers with iniquity."

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes. The *mouth and lips* are the body-part link for confession as a speech-act. The entire corpus is composed of spoken acts: "Pharaoh sent and called Moses and Aaron and *said*" (Exo 9:27), "the son *said* to him" (Luk 15:21), "he *sings* before men and says" (Job 33:27). The mouth/lips are the terminal organ through which the inner confession is externalised. Neh 1:6 — "confessing the sins... that I now *pray* before you" — prayer-speech as the mode. No body part other than the speech organs is evidenced in direct connection with the confessional act itself.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes — in the active-denial mode. Jer 2:35 — "you *say*, 'I am innocent'" and "'I have not sinned'" — the mouth/speech organs are the body-part through which the inner suppression externalises. The speech-act of false innocence-claiming is the body-level expression of conscience suppression's denial mode. Judg 20:16 — literal physical *missing* of a target with a sling — physical body context, but no moral inner-being content.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Yes. Neh 9:29 — "they turned a *stubborn shoulder* and *stiffened their neck*" — two body parts are used as constitutional metaphors. The *shoulder* (kateph) — giving a stubborn shoulder was the gesture of refusing to carry a yoke, refusing to submit to the burden of obedience. The *neck* (oreph) — stiffening the neck was the gesture of an animal resisting the yoke of control. Both are bodily-metaphor expressions of the will's refusal to submit to God's direction.

**[CHAR-6]** S — The 14-verse corpus contains no explicit body-part link for habitual defection. The characteristic operates through the heart (Exo 9:34 — inner organ metaphor rather than external body part), the ears (1Sa 2:25 — "would not listen" implies ear-reception, but ears are not named explicitly), and through outer practices (altars — Hos 8:11) rather than through a named external body-part.

**[CHAR-7]** S — The 19-verse corpus contains no explicit body-part link for contagious sin. The characteristic operates through the volitional-institutional level (walking, building, driving) without named body-part connection.
**[CHAR-8]** S — The 9-verse corpus contains no body-part link for political revolt. The characteristic operates through political-social action without named body-part connection.

**[CHAR-9]** E — Yes — the mouth is the body-part link throughout the corpus. Col 3:8 — "slander... *from your mouth*" — the mouth is explicitly named as the body-part of externalisation. Rev 13:5 — "a *mouth* uttering haughty and blasphemous words" — the beast's mouth is named as the instrument. Rev 13:6 — "It opened its *mouth* to utter blasphemies" — the mouth-opening is the bodily act. Jude 9 — Michael "did not presume to pronounce" — the pronouncing is a mouth-act. The mouth is the defining bodily instrument of sinful speech throughout.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes. The evidence links wickedness-as-settled-person-identity to multiple body parts as expressive instruments. The mouth is the most prominent: Pro 10:6 and 10:11 ("the mouth of the wicked conceals violence"), Pro 10:32 ("the mouth of the wicked knows what is perverse"), Pro 11:11 ("by the mouth of the wicked [a city] is overthrown"), Pro 12:6, 15:28, 19:28 — the wicked person's mouth is the primary body-level marker. The arm/hand appears in Psa 10:15 (VCG-05 — "break the arm of the wicked"), Eze 7:21 (VCG-03 — the wicked used as instruments of plunder — their "hand"), Job 38:15 ("their uplifted arm is broken"). The "feet" / "path" are implied in Psa 1:1 (walking in counsel) and Pro 4:14 (entering the path). Pro 21:4: "haughty eyes and a proud heart" — the eyes carry the expression of inner pride.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes. The eye and the mouth are the primary body-part links. Eye: Mat 6:23 (vc=14458 — VCG-03): "if your eye is bad, your whole body will be full of darkness" — the eye as the body part through which the constitutional inner evil expresses its perceptive corruption. Mouth: Mat 12:34 (vc=14419 — VCG-03): "out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks" — the mouth as the expressive instrument of the heart-treasury of evil. Luk 6:45 (vc=14421 — VCG-03): the same mouth-as-overflow-of-heart-treasury pattern. 3Jo 10 (vc=14454 — VCG-04): "talking wicked nonsense against us" — the mouth as the instrument of domineering inner malice. Body members in general: Rom 6:13 (vc=14340 — VCG-06): "do not present your members to sin as instruments for unrighteousness" — the body's members as potential instruments for the constitutional unrighteousness.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes. Multiple body parts appear. Lips: Pro 8:7 (vc=65953 — VCG-02): "wickedness is an abomination to my lips" — Wisdom's lips are the body part that expresses the divine faculty of moral revulsion; Pro 12:22 (vc=65955 — VCG-02): "lying lips are an abomination to the Lord" — the lips as the instrument of deceptive speech that is abominable. Ear: Pro 28:9 (vc=65958 — VCG-03): "if one turns away his ear from hearing the law" — the ear as the faculty of receptive hearing is the body part whose turning away renders prayer abominable. Forehead: Rev 17:5 (vc=65878 — VCG-05): the name of abomination written on the forehead — the forehead as the site of public identity disclosure. Face: Eze 14:6 (vc=65984 — VCG-04): "turn away your faces from all your abominations" — the face as the direction-of-orientation indicator.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes. Eyes and hands are the primary body parts. Eyes: Eze 20:7 (vc=1634 — VCG-05): "the detestable things your eyes feast on"; Eze 6:9 (vc=1697 — VCG-05): "eyes that go whoring after their idols." Hands (implied through craftsmanship and installation): Eze 7:20 (vc=65909 — VCG-05): "His beautiful ornament they used for pride, and they made their abominable images and their detestable things of it" — making with hands; Deu 29:17 (vc=65897 — VCG-02): "idols of wood and stone, of silver and gold" — crafted objects. Mouth/teeth: Zec 9:7 (vc=65918 — VCG-04): "I will take away its blood from its mouth, and its abominations from between its teeth" — abominations lodged in the mouth as physical-metaphorical location. The installation of idols in sacred space (Jer 7:30 — vc=65904 — VCG-04; Jer 32:34 — vc=65907 — VCG-04) implies bodily agency (hands placing).

**[CHAR-5]** E — Yes. Multiple body parts appear. Hand: Job 11:14 (vc=38207 — VCG-04): "if iniquity is in your hand, put it far away" — iniquity located in the hand as the active-agency instrument. Isa 59:6 (vc=38202 — VCG-04): "deeds of violence are in their hands" — the hand as the body part where iniquity's deeds reside. Tongue/mouth: Psa 10:7 (vc=38225 — VCG-04): "under his tongue are mischief and iniquity"; Pro 6:12 (vc=38223 — VCG-03): "goes about with crooked speech." Feet: Isa 59:7 (vc=38203 — VCG-02): "their feet run to evil" — the feet as the body part through which the will's eager movement toward iniquity is expressed; Pro 6:18 (vc=38224 — VCG-02): "feet that make haste to run to evil." Face/heart juxtaposition: Psa 28:3 (vc=38232 — VCG-03): "speak peace" (face/mouth) while "evil is in their hearts" — the face/outward expression vs. heart/inner condition.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Yes. The mouth is the primary body part. Rev 13:6 (vc=14356 — VCG-01): "opened its mouth to utter blasphemies against God" — the mouth as the body's primary speech-instrument is explicitly named as the vehicle through which the characteristic operates. The opening of the mouth is the act through which inner defiant contempt becomes operative blasphemy. The entire characteristic is constitutively mouth-mediated: evil must be "expressed through speech" — the speech-faculty, located in the mouth, is the necessary constitutional bridge between inner wickedness and its social expression.

**[CLUSTER]** E — All six characteristics link their respective evil-forms to body parts, revealing a comprehensive body-part map of inner evil's expression. The mouth is the most universal body-part across the cluster — evidenced in Chars 1 (Pro 10:6/11/32 — the wicked person's mouth), 2 (Mat 12:34 — mouth as overflow of heart-treasury), 3 (Pro 8:7 — lying lips; Pro 12:22), 5 (Psa 10:7 — under the tongue; Pro 6:12), and 6 (Rev 13:6 — "opened its mouth"). The eyes appear in Chars 2 (Mat 6:23), 4 (Eze 20:7 — feasting eyes), and 1 (Pro 21:4 — haughty eyes). The hand appears in Chars 1 (Psa 10:15 — arm/hand), 4 (Eze 7:20 — hands making idols), and 5 (Job 11:14 — iniquity in the hand). The feet appear in Chars 1 (Psa 1:1 implied — the wicked person's path) and 5 (Isa 59:7; Pro 6:18 — feet running to evil). The cluster reveals the mouth as the body's primary site of inner evil's social expression — confirming Char 6's constitutive speech-focus as expressing the cluster's deepest body-part pattern.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes, several body-part linkages are explicit. Skin: the leprous-disease verdict system (M10c-B-VCG-02, Lev 13 corpus) is entirely skin-focused — the priest examines "the diseased area on the skin of his body" (Lev 13:3); the skin's surface is both the site of the condition and the medium of assessment. Head: Lev 13:44-45 (M10c-B-VCG-02/03) — disease on the head receives a specific verdict; the head is the locus of the public self-declaration. Mouth/saliva: Lev 15:8 (M10c-A-VCG-06) — spitting by the discharge-person defiles. Hand: Lev 15:11 (M10c-A-VCG-06) — the unwashed hand is the vector of defilement-transmission. Lips: implied in the self-declaration cry (Lev 13:45 — "cover his upper lip and cry out"). Genitals/bodily fluids: the entire discharge register (M10c-A-VCG-05 and -06) is anchored in bodily-fluid emission — menstrual blood, seminal fluid, abnormal discharge.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes. Isa 6:5 (VCG-01): "I am a man of unclean lips" — the lips are named as the bodily organ in which the inner moral defilement is expressed and perceived; the prophet's mouth/lips are the body part that articulates the inner condition. Rom 1:24 (VCG-02): "to the dishonoring of their bodies among themselves" — the body as a whole receives the consequence of the impurity, though no specific body part is named here beyond "bodies." 2Cor 7:1 (VCG-03): "defilement of body and spirit" — the body (soma) as a whole is named alongside the spirit as the constitutional locus of the defilement.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes. Num 5:27 (VCG-01): the ordeal water produces consequences in the body — "her womb shall swell, and her thigh shall fall away" — when defilement through broken covenant faith is real; the body is the site of the judicial consequence of the covenantal defilement. The womb and thigh (probably genitals/reproductive organs) are the specific body parts named as the site of the physical judgment. Eze 22:10 (VCG-01): men violating women "in their menstrual impurity" — the body's menstrual state defines the boundary being transgressed; the female body's specific physiological condition is the boundary marker.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes. (1) Speech organs: Mar 1:26 (VCG-02) — "crying out with a loud voice" — the spirit uses the person's voice; Mar 9:25 (VCG-01) — "mute and deaf spirit" — the mouth/voice is the specifically suppressed speech organ. (2) Body as a whole: Luk 8:29 (VCG-01) — "bound with chains and shackles, but he would break the bonds" — the body's limbs are the sites of both restraint and supernatural strength; Luk 9:42 (VCG-01) — "threw him to the ground and convulsed him" — the whole body is the instrument of the spirit's violent self-expression.

**[CLUSTER]** E — All four characteristics evidence body-part linkages, but the specific body parts differ by characteristic in revealing ways. Characteristic 1 has the most extensive body-part links: skin (the leprous-disease corpus of Lev 13 — the primary diagnostic site), head (Lev 13:44-45 — disease location and self-declaration site), mouth/lips (Lev 13:45 — "cover his upper lip and cry out"), hand (Lev 15:11 — vector of transmission), genitals/reproductive organs (Lev 15 discharge corpus), and the body's fluids as vehicles. Characteristic 2: lips (Isa 6:5 — "I am a man of unclean lips"), body as a whole (Rom 1:24 — "dishonoring of their bodies"; 2Cor 7:1 — "defilement of body and spirit"). Characteristic 3: womb/thigh (Num 5:27 — the judicial consequence in the ordeal), the female body's menstrual state (Eze 22:10 — the boundary being transgressed). Characteristic 4: speech organs (Mar 1:26 — "crying out with a loud voice" — the spirit uses the voice; Mar 9:25 — "mute and deaf spirit"), body as a whole (Luk 8:29 — breaking chains; Luk 9:42 — convulsed). The body-part distribution reveals the characteristic's operational domain in each case: the body surface (Char 1), the inner-expressing-outer complex (Char 2), the reproductive-covenantal boundary zone (Char 3), and the communicative and motoric apparatus (Char 4).

findings.session_b_note:
The body-links serve different functions across the four instances:

- **Blood of Christ (Eph 1:7):** **Mediating** — the body/blood of Christ is the mechanism through which forgiveness becomes possible. The body here is not the locus of forgiveness but the instrument of the atoning act that grounds it.
- **The woman's bodily acts (Luk 7:47):** **Expressive** — the body externalises what the inner being has received. The weeping and anointing are the visible surface of an inner transformation. Scripture uses the body here as evidence of inner reality.
- **The paralytic's healing (Mat 9:2-6):** **Indicative** — the healing of the body indicates the reality of the inner forgiveness. Jesus uses the physical healing as proof of his authority to forgive ("which is easier — to say 'your sins are forgiven' or 'rise and walk'?"). The body-sign validates the inner-being act.
- **Visceral compassion (Mat 18:27):** **Functional** — the gut-level compassion is named as the felt origin of the forgiving act. The body's visceral response functions as the motivating impulse from which the volitional act of forgiving flows.

*Adds structure:* The data contains four distinct body-functions in relation to forgiveness (mediating, expressive, indicative, functional) that have not been assembled as a typology in the existing observations.

findings.session_b_note:
- **The eye** (SD041): **constitutive** significance — the divine gaze constitutes the person's standing. Grace is being-seen by the one whose seeing matters.
- **The supplication body** (prostration, weeping, fasting — SD001, SD039): **expressive and indicative** — "the body enacts what the inner person is doing... the whole person brought into alignment with the inner posture of plea."
- **Eusplanchnos** (Eph 4:32, SD030): **functional** — the inner parts function as the mediating organ through which grace received flows outward as grace extended.
- **The flesh of the incarnation** (Joh 1:14, SD042): **paradigmatic** — the supreme somatic expression of grace; grace takes bodily form at its fullest.

*Adds structure: all significance types (constitutive, expressive, indicative, functional, paradigmatic) are present across the grace corpus — an unusually complete somatic coverage.*

findings.session_b_note:
Scripture is doing several distinct things simultaneously through these body-part links:

**Etymological / constitutive (womb):** The womb-link is not a rhetorical device added to an abstract concept — it is the etymological ground of the abstract concept. Scripture did not choose to illustrate compassion with a womb metaphor; the language itself was built from the womb upward. The body-part link in the RACHAM vocabulary is constitutive of the meaning, not expressive of it. This makes the womb-link unique in its depth: it does not merely describe what compassion feels like — it is what compassion is named after.

**Expressive (splanchnizō):** The gut-movement vocabulary names what compassion feels like from the inside — where in the body one experiences being moved by another's suffering. This is expressive: it communicates the somatic texture of the inner experience.

**Indicative (splanchnizō in the Gospels):** Jesus's splanchnizō-movements are consistently visible to the observers — they precede his actions and are reported as inner events that explain the external actions. The body-movement is indicative of the inner state: it shows the observers (and the reader) what is happening inside before the action takes place.

**Mediating (heart in Hos 11:8):** The heart's recoiling mediates between the divine knowledge of Israel's condition and the compassion-response. The heart is the organ of inner deliberation at which compassion overcomes judgment.

findings.session_b_note:
The bone-link at Psa 51:8 is **constitutionally intensive**: God is described as breaking the psalmist's bones — using the same crushing vocabulary applied to the contrite heart and spirit. The rhetorical effect is to convey that the divine chastisement has reached to the deepest physical level. The bones are the structurally foundational body part — when they are broken, nothing remains intact. This is emphatic intensification: contrition is not skin-deep but reaches to the structural core of the person's embodied existence.

The request that the broken bones rejoice (Psa 51:8) then becomes a petition for total restoration — not merely inner-being revival but somatic rejoicing at every level, including the deepest physical structure. This is the verse evidence's most complete picture of what total divine reviving of the contrite person would look like: spirit, heart, and bones rejoicing together.

*New finding: the bones at Psa 51:8 function constitutionally rather than merely metaphorically — they represent the deepest physical layer of the person's constitutional structure. Contrition in this verse has reached to the somatic foundation, making the petition for rejoicing a petition for total (spirit-heart-body) restoration. This three-level picture (spirit, heart, bones) has not been assembled in prior analysis.*

findings.session_b_note:
The body-link functions differently in different groups:

**Mediating (Pro 20:30):** The wound-blows are the *medium* through which inner purification reaches the innermost parts. The body mediates what the inner person receives through disciplinary wounding. The wound is the instrument of purification.

**Expressive-indicative (Isa 53:5):** The servant's wounds are the visible, somatic expression of the redemptive fellowship undertaken on behalf of others. The body *shows* what the inner-being transaction contains: the fellowship of suffering, the bearing of others' transgressions.

**Participatory (Phili 3:10):** The fellowship of Christ's sufferings (*koinōnia tōn pathēmatōn autou*) is explicitly entered through somatic experience — suffering and death are the form in which the person participates in Christ's path. The body is the site of participation.

**New finding:** The fellowship characteristic uses the body in three distinct ways: as *mediator* of inner purification (Pro 20:30), as *expression* of inner fellowship-reality made visible (Isa 53:5), and as *site* of participation in the fellowship trajectory (Phili 3:10). These are three distinct body-functions, not one.

findings.session_b_note: For "glad of heart" (tov-lev, Est 5:9): the heart-compound is emphatic — locating the inner well-being state specifically in the heart gives it a constitutive rather than circumstantial character. For Psa 34:8 ("taste and see"): the perceptual language is experiential and invitational — Scripture is using sensory vocabulary to name a quality of inner encounter that has a quasi-perceptual character. The "tasting" of goodness is not abstract cognition but participatory encounter. Scripture is inviting an embodied-in-principle inner perception — the kind of knowledge that comes from experience rather than inference. Beyond these two instances the somatic evidence is limited. (OBS-067-OBS-025, OBS-067-OBS-041)

findings.finding_value: T2 reveals mercy as a whole-person constitutional reality. No single level contains it: mercy originates at the spirit-soul interface, operates on the soul (addressing the nephesh-guilt), engages the heart through the visceral compassion vocabulary (splanchna), engages the mind through the memory-erasure mechanism (Heb 8:12), and operates through the body as both the medium of mercy-seeking (embodied posture) and the mechanism of mercy's effect (blood-atonement). The triadic constitutional movement (Q&A-065): inner disposition → soul-transformation → embodied expression. The key finding reading T2 as a whole is the receiving-before-generating origin structure (Q&A-062): mercy cannot be generated from within the person but must be received from outside and then expressed through the constitutional architecture. Body deposit: none. T5.7: formally closed.

findings.finding_value: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level (chesed as covenantal-soul character), heart-level (Hos 11:8 — "my heart recoils"), and somatic-level (re.chem, splanchnon) are all richly evidenced. The constitutional architecture is bottom-up: the womb and entrails are the originating ground; the soul and heart are the engagement points; the act is the constitutional expression. Four body-part functions are identified: constitutive (womb — the generative image of compassion), expressive (gut — the felt movement), indicative (Synoptic pattern — splanchnizō signals the compassion-event), and mediating (heart in Hos 11:8 — the deliberative locus where compassion and judgment contend). The four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) is uniquely evidenced in this registry — consistently inside-out and bottom-up. T2.8 established no body deposit; T5.7 is formally closed. The constitutional portrait confirms the sb_classification (soul-body interface) and extends it: compassion is the most somatically grounded characteristic in the programme, with its originating logic residing in the body's deepest interior.

findings.finding_value: T1's four-kind structure (character quality, inner event, condition of object, externalised act) maps precisely onto T2's constitutional levels. The character-quality kind (ra.chum — dispositional compassionate character) operates at the soul level (T2.2 — chesed as soul-character). The inner-event kind (splanchnizō — the moment of being-moved) operates at the somatic level (T2.6 — the gut as the site of the stirring). The condition-of-object kind (eleeinos — the pitiable state) is the constitutional trigger that activates the somatic-constitutional movement. The externalised-act kind is the constitutional endpoint of T2.10's four-stage movement sequence. T1's definition and T2's constitutional account are co-determining: the characteristic cannot be adequately defined without specifying the constitutional levels at which its four kinds operate.

findings.finding_value: T2's four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) maps directly onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The somatic-arousal stage (T2.6 — gut stirring, splanchnizō) corresponds to T3.1's perceptive-trigger stage (sight activates the somatic response) and T3.4's affect stage (the stirring is the affective movement). The soul-engagement stage (T2.2 — chesed as soul-character) corresponds to T3.8 moral evaluation (the soul assesses the need) and T3.9 conscience (the conscience activates the response). The volitional-engagement stage (T2.3 — heart-locus as deliberative site) corresponds to T3.6 volition (the will directs the action). The outward-action stage corresponds to T3.7 agency. T2 and T3 describe the same movement sequence from two perspectives: T2 maps the constitutional levels; T3 maps the faculties active at each level.

findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional origin analysis (somatic-relational-covenantal triple ground) and T4's relational direction analysis are structurally aligned. The somatic origin (womb, gut) grounds the cross-boundary relational direction in T4: splanchnizō's somatic immediacy is precisely what enables it to cross covenantal boundaries — the gut-movement toward the suffering other precedes any covenantal assessment of the relationship. The covenantal origin (chesed) grounds the within-bond sustaining direction in T4. The constitutional origin therefore predicts the relational direction: somatic = cross-boundary; covenantal = within-bond. T2's soul-body interface classification explains T4's scope-by-need finding: because compassion originates at the soul-body interface (before covenantal-rational assessment), its scope is determined by the pre-rational recognition of need rather than the post-rational assessment of covenantal standing.

findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional levels are each carried by specific vocabulary families in T7. The somatic-body level (T2.6 — gut, womb) is carried by the RACHAM/SPLANCHN root families — the body's interior as the etymological ground of both. The soul-character level (T2.2) is carried by the CHASAD family — chesed as the settled covenantal character disposition. The heart-deliberative level (T2.3) is evidenced most richly in Hos 11:8 (T7's primary anchor for divine compassion). T7's vocabulary arc (womb to almsgiving) traverses exactly the constitutional range T2 maps: from the most interior somatic level (womb) through the character-soul level to the externalised action level. The dual primary anchor (T7) maps onto T2's constitutional depth: Hos 11:8 evidences constitutional depth (heart-level deliberation of compassion over judgment); Luke 10:33 evidences constitutional breadth (the full four-stage movement from sight to action).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-002: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary…
findings.finding_value: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary point of reception (Zec 12:10 — spirit of grace poured out), not the point of generation (grace originates with God — T2.9). The soul level is the site of standing (Rom 5:2 — "this grace in which we stand") and identity (1Cor 15:10 — "by the grace of God I am what I am"). The constitutional movement follows the SD021 four-faces model: divine disposition received at spirit level → relational standing established at soul level → specific capacity gifted → character expressed outward. Heart-location is partially evidenced via eusplanchnos (Eph 4:32 — the tenderheartedness that grace produces, reaching the affective-somatic interface). T2.7 produces a new finding: grace operates bidirectionally through the body-soul interface — soul-to-body (inner posture enacted somatically in prostration, fasting, sackcloth) and body-to-soul (somatic enactment deepening and confirming the inner posture). T2.8 remains open (body deposit question unresolved); T5.7 is left open accordingly. The constitutional origin analysis (T2.9) is the most analytically significant T2 finding: grace does not originate in the human constitutional system at any level — it arrives from outside. This is confirmed at T6 as the structural uniqueness of grace: the only characteristic that is not produced by any other inner-being characteristic.

findings.session_b_note: The two body-part links serve different scriptural functions: (1) Blood as mediating: the blood of the covenant is the covenant's constitutive medium — it does not merely represent the covenant but enacts and seals it. "The blood of the covenant that God commanded for you" (Heb 9:20). The blood mediates between the parties: it is shed, sprinkled on the people (Exo 24:8) or on the altar (Lev context), creating a bond through shared life-substance. In the NT, Christ's blood is the mediation of the new covenant — it enacts the covenant by providing the death of the testator (Heb 9:16–17 — OBS-034-069). Blood's function is mediating: constituting the covenant bond through bodily sacrifice. (2) Circumcision as indicative/expressive: the sign of circumcision on the body indicates covenant membership and expresses bodily belonging to the covenant community. It does not constitute the covenant (which is God's prior promise — Gal 3:17 context) but marks the body as belonging to the covenant people. Circumcision is the bodily inscription of covenantal identity. Function: indicative and expressive. Together, blood (mediating) and circumcision (indicative) show that covenant has two distinct somatic modes: constituting-through-sacrifice and marking-through-sign.

findings.finding_value: T2 identifies blood and circumcision as the primary somatic covenant locations. T7 establishes the lexical arc showing covenant as simultaneously relational, bodily, oral, legal, moral, transformative, and eschatological. The T2 × T7 synthesis: the bodily dimension identified in T2 is confirmed and deepened by the lexical analysis of T7. The root meaning of karat (to cut — Q&A-170) and the blood-of-the-covenant vocabulary are etymologically embedded in the bodily-somatic dimension of the covenant vocabulary arc. The LXX translation choice (diathēkē — Q&A-177) adds the death/inheritance dimension to the somatic vocabulary: the blood is the means of mediation, and the testator's death is required for the testament to take effect. T2's somatic findings are not incidental features but are inscribed in the etymology and semantic development of the vocabulary itself (T7).

The most significant body-link is Psa 38:3: the explicit naming of shalom as soundness-of-bones under sin's influence establishes that inner peace and somatic integrity are structurally connected — not metaphorically but causally.

**BOUNDARY characterisation — H0887 ba.ash (to stink / make offensive).** The stench / offensiveness term — the social-sensory mark of being made repugnant to others. The root BASH names the condition of being regarded as a stench, which is the social register of M06-C's abhorrence. Where ta.av names the inner visceral recoil (M06-C), ba.ash names what the rejected person becomes in others' perception. The BOUNDARY role: ba.ash marks the outer social result of abhorrence being directed at a person or community — the social form of what M06-C names as an inner-being response. Recorded under T2.6.2 (body-link purpose — what Scripture is doing by making a body-link) because the stench metaphor is the body-sensory form Scripture uses for the abhorrence-recipient condition.

findings.finding_value: 2Cor 4:16's naming of the outer self wasting away is functional — it names the most extreme possible bodily deterioration (the body literally decaying) as insufficient to produce inner collapse when the inner person is renewed. The link is contrastive and emphatic: the body's visible decline cannot reach the heart's inner capacity for renewal. This is not the body expressing the characteristic but the body's deterioration being named as the context in which the characteristic is overcome.

findings.finding_value: The face link (Pro 15:13) is **indicative** — the inner state shows on the face; the body reveals the inner quality. The bones link (Pro 17:22) is **functional** — the inner state produces a physical effect; the body is not merely revealing the inner state but being shaped by it. The bones drying up is not a metaphor for mood but a claim about physical consequence. This is Scripture making a physiological-functional link between inner goodness and bodily health.

findings.finding_value: The fat-organ link (Isa 6:10) is functioning emphatically: the physical metaphor of fattened ears and eyes captures the spiritual-perceptual closure in a visceral, unavoidable image. The fat organ cannot perform its function — the fat ear cannot hear, the fat eye cannot see. Scripture is using the body's failure-through-excess to name the soul's failure-through-abundance. The body-link is metaphorical but grounded in the physical reality of obesity impairing function.

findings.finding_value: Pro 15:30 ("good news refreshes the bones") is functioning mediatively: the received blessing (good news) reaches the bones — the deepest structural level of the body — as the sign of comprehensive inner renewal. The bones are not merely the outer frame; in wisdom literature they are the location of the deepest inner vitality. Da.shen (to refresh/make fat) applied to bones names a renewal that is total — from the centre of the person outward.

findings.finding_value: The flesh-trembling link in Psa 119:120 is **expressive**: the trembling of flesh expresses the inner reverential dread; it shows the inner state reaching outward to the body.

The heart/chest link in Psa 55:4 (M01-C-VCG-04 anchor) is **indicative**: it locates the experience of divine-majesty terror in a specific constitutional site (the heart as the centre of inner life), indicating where the terror is felt.

The body-part links in M01-D (Dan 5:6: limbs giving way, knees knocking; Isa 21:3: cannot see; Job 32:15: speechlessness) are **expressive** — they show the completeness of the inner collapse by its bodily manifestation. They also function as **indicative** of the severity: color change, limb-failure, and eye-failure indicate that the dismay has overwhelmed the person's ability to sustain basic bodily function.

M01-E's body-part links are primarily **expressive** — the bones, flesh, hair, and lips register the inner fear by their involuntary response. But the Isa 66:2 anchor (trembling located in the spirit) suggests that for E-VCG-02 the direction is different: the spirit-posture expresses through the body, making the body-link **mediating** — the body mediates the spirit's reverence into visible form.

M01-F's body-link in Eze 12:18 (quivering while drinking) is **functional**: it shows that anxiety is not merely a conscious experience but has colonised the body's automatic activities. The link is functional because it shows how the inner state affects the person's ordinary functioning.

Scripture's body-part linking in M01 serves multiple functions: expressive (showing inner states through bodily manifestation), indicative (locating the experience in specific bodily sites), and functional (showing the inner state's effect on bodily activity). The preponderance of expressive and indicative links confirms that Scripture is attending to fear as a whole-person experience, not merely an internal mental event.

The face-link in Gen 4:5 and Dan 3:19 is expressive and indicative: the face reveals what is happening inwardly, making the inner state readable — the fallen countenance is the inner anger's external signal. Scripture uses this link to show that anger cannot be hidden — it discloses itself.

[E] The bones-link in Psa 38:3 and Pro 14:30 is mediating and deposit-making: the indignation/envy penetrates to the structural interior of the body, leaving a consequence that goes beyond the immediate emotional episode. Scripture uses this link to show that anger received or harboured has a deep somatic consequence.

---

[E] The lips-and-tongue link in Isa 30:27 is expressive and functional: the divine indignation takes a communicative form through speech-organs, showing that anger's most characteristic expression is verbal judgment. Scripture uses this link to show anger's communicative form.

In M03-A and M03-E, the body-part link is primarily expressive: grief is shown overflowing from the inner being through the body — tears from the eyes, groans from the chest, sighs from the breath. The body is the medium through which inner grief becomes visible and audible. In M03-F, the link is phenomenological: pain is felt in the body (bones wasting, heart aching, bodily deterioration) — grief is experienced as a somatic reality, not merely a psychic one. Scripture's use of body-part language for grief signals the totality of grief as a whole-person event — grief is not confined to the "inner world" as if the body were uninvolved, but saturates the entire person, inner and outer together.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Three functions are evidenced: (1) **Emphasis** — bones as the seat of deepest suffering being asked to rejoice (Psa 51:8) intensifies the characteristic's restoring power: if even the crushed bones can rejoice, the restoration is total; (2) **Indicator** — flesh dwelling secure (Psa 16:9) shows the body as the indicator of the soul's exultation — the person's bodily security is evidence of the inner joy's reality; (3) **Expression** — the mouth and lips are the natural expressive channel through which inner exultation moves outward into the world.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Three functions: (1) **Extension** — the joy that begins in the heart reaches through the whole person and out into the body (Psa 16:9; Pro 15:13) — showing Joy as a characteristic that encompasses the whole human being, not only the inner; (2) **Depth-emphasis** — bones and womb are the body's most hidden and deep levels; joy reaching to the bones (Psa 51:8) and leaping in the womb (Luk 1:44) signals that this inner state penetrates to the deepest physical levels of human existence; (3) **Expression** — tongue, hands, face, and dance are the body's expressive surfaces; their involvement shows Joy as a characteristic that naturally overflows from within outward into visible, audible expression.

**[CHAR-7]** E — (1) The tongue-link (Act 2:26) is **expressive** — the inner exultation of Suffering-Joy moves outward through the body's speech organ into declaration; (2) The flesh/hope-link (Act 2:26) is **indicative** — the body's hoped-for security is the outward evidence that the inner Suffering-Joy has a bodily dimension and is not merely abstract; (3) The face-smile-link (Job 9:27; Psa 39:13) is **emphatic** — the barely-sought smile is both the goal of ba.lag and the visible evidence of its presence; seeking to smile is seeking the somatically-visible form of inner cheerfulness.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Pro 15:30's bones-connection serves an **emphatic** function: it insists that genuine good news does not remain at a surface emotional level but penetrates to the person's physical depths. This is a similar rhetorical strategy to Psa 51:8's "bones that you have broken" — the bones stand for the deepest inner experience. Scripture links Gladness to the bones to convey its thoroughgoing, holistic character: genuine gladness-from-good-news restores the whole person.

**[CHAR-4]** E — (1) The food/mouth/nursing images (Isa 55:2; 66:11) are **emphatic** — they insist that Delight in God and in his restoration is as physically real and deeply satisfying as nourishing food and the infant's nursing; the body's own experience of satisfaction is the image chosen to convey what soul-level Delight in God is like; (2) The ni.cho.ach aroma link is **mediating** — the physical aroma rises from the altar and reaches God (or in M04-P, the idol), conveying the inner disposition of the worshipper through a physical medium; the external aroma represents the inner orientation of obedient Delight (or its corrupt counterpart); (3) The bounced-on-knees image (Isa 66:12) is **expressive** — it gives somatic form to the quality of carefree, entirely-held, resting Delight in divine peace.

**[CHAR-5]** E — (1) **Nose (ni.cho.ach)** — the olfactory link is **mediating**: the physical aroma rises from the altar and reaches God through the olfactory dimension, making the sensory physical act the medium of the worship-Pleasure relationship; the physical smell mediates a spiritual-relational reality (God's reception of the worshiper's offering); (2) **Mouth/honey-sweetness** — Pro 16:24's honey simile is **emphatic**: it insists that genuinely pleasant speech nourishes as concretely and immediately as honey nourishes the body; the bodily taste-image serves to communicate the soul-level impact; (3) **Eyes** — Psa 27:4's "gaze" is **constitutive**: gazing upon God's beauty is the act that receives divine Pleasure; the eyes are not merely metaphorical but are the appropriate organ for encountering beauty; (4) **Body overall** — Pro 16:24's "health to the body" is **integrative**: pleasant speech heals the whole person, demonstrating that genuine Pleasure penetrates from word to soul to body.

**[CHAR-6]** E — (1) **Eyes** — the link is **constitutive**: Wonder at God's acts begins with seeing (Psa 118:23 — "it is marvellous in our eyes") and Psa 119:18 asks for opened eyes specifically to behold wonders. The eyes are not merely metaphorical — genuine Wonder requires genuine perceptual encounter. (2) **Mouth** — the link is **expressive**: Wonder consistently overflows through speech into proclamation. The mouth-link reveals that Wonder is constitutively oral-doxological — it characteristically moves from inner astonishment to voiced declaration. The inner state seeks outward expression through the body's speech organ.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Three functions appear across the cluster: (1) **Emphatic** — bones and womb are the body's deepest and most hidden levels; linking the cluster's characteristics to bones (Psa 51:8; Pro 15:30) and womb (Luk 1:44) insists that these inner states penetrate to the physical depths — they are not surface emotions; (2) **Expressive** — mouth, tongue, hands, face, and dance are the body's expressive surfaces; their involvement across Joy, Exultation, Wonder, and Suffering-Joy confirms that M04 characteristics characteristically move from inner to outer — the inner state seeks a bodily form; (3) **Mediating** — the ni.cho.ach aroma (Pleasure Char 5 and Delight Char 4 M04-M) is the most distinctive mediating body-link in the cluster: a physical sensory-act mediates a spiritual-relational reality between the human worshiper and God. The olfactory sense as the medium of the worship-Pleasure relationship is unique to M04 among the programme's clusters.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The face-link is both *indicative* (showing shame's outward visibility — it is seen in the face) and *expressive* (the covering of the face is the body acting out the inner shame). The head-link is primarily *postural* — the head-down posture is the body enacting the inner collapse of dignity. The blush-link is *physiological* — it names the involuntary body-response that indicates the inner state. The face/head/blush links together reveal that shame's inner state is not hidden — it expresses itself through the body even when the person tries to conceal it (covering the face is itself a shame-expression). Scripture is showing that shame is a whole-person event: the inner collapse has a necessary bodily expression that cannot be fully suppressed.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Multiple prominent body-part links: (1) The beard (2Sa 10:5; 1Ch 19:5) — shaving as the enacted sign of humiliation. (2) The face (2Ch 32:21 — "shame of face"; Mic 3:7 — "cover their lips"). (3) The crown and turban (Eze 21:26 — "remove the turban and take off the crown"). (4) The back (Jer 48:39 — "turned his back in shame"). (5) The eyes (Isa 2:11; 5:15; Psa 18:27 — haughty eyes brought down). The links are indicative, expressive, and juridical.
