**[CHAR-3]** E — The head-covering symbolic-disrespect register (1Cor 11:4-5, vc=35009/35010) is CHAR-3's most prominent body-part link: the covered or uncovered head is the bodily sign through which the symbolic disrespect of divinely ordered authority is communicated. The body-part link here is symbolic and communicative — the head functions as the sign of relational honour/dishonour.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — The body-part link is present in VCG-01 and VCG-02. 1Cor 11:6 (vc=34983) — the wife's cut or shaved hair is disgraceful — links shamefulness to hair as the bodily sign of social-moral propriety. Rom 1:27 (vc=34966) — "shameless acts with men" — links shamefulness to specific bodily conduct. Rev 16:15 (vc=34967) — naked exposure — links shamefulness to the body's unguarded state. The body-part links in CHAR-4 are indicative (the body reveals the inner moral-disorder) and symbolic (hair as the sign of propriety).

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — VCG-02's violent-contempt register (Mar 12:4 — "struck him on the head and treated him shamefully"; Luk 20:11 — "beat and treated him shamefully") links CHAR-5 to the body through physical violence as the enactment of contemptuous dismissal. The body is the site where contemptuous rejection is enacted against the person — the body receives the contempt physically. Bartimaeus's cloak (Mar 10:50) is a bodily-item carrying the identity of contempt-shaped shame; throwing it off is a bodily act of shame-identity abandonment.

---

**[CHAR-6]** E — The hands are CHAR-6's most prominent body-part link: "the innocence of my hands" (Gen 20:5); "I wash my hands in innocence" (Psa 26:6). The hands function as the external expression of the internal moral condition: hand-cleanness is the outward evidence of the inner moral integrity. The hand-washing gesture (Psa 26:6) is both the ritual enactment of CHAR-6's claim and the symbolic communication of the inner state to God and community. The body-part link is indicative (the hands show the moral condition), ritual (hand-washing enacts the moral claim), and communicative (the gesture declares innocence).

---

**[CLUSTER]** E — The body-part links across the six reveal a concentrated body-map of shame's expression. The face is the most prominent body-part: face-covering, face-hiding, blushing, inability to lift the face (Chars 1, 2), the head's symbolic-disrespect register (Char 3 — 1Cor 11:4-5). The hands appear in the cluster's positive pole: the innocent hands of Char 6 (Gen 20:5; Psa 26:6). The back appears in the retreat-pattern of Chars 1 and 2 (backward turning — Psa 35:4; 129:5; Jer 48:39). The eyes appear in Char 2's haughty-eyes-brought-down pattern (Isa 5:15; Psa 18:27). The beard and crown appear in Char 2's social-demotion register (2Sa 10:5; Eze 21:26). Cluster-level finding: the face-hand polarity is the cluster's primary body-axis. Shame collapses the face (preventing the upright forward presentation that confidence requires); innocence is expressed through the hands (the clean hands that enable approach to God's altar). This asymmetry — shame on the face, innocence on the hands — is a cluster-level pattern not visible at the per-characteristic level.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The body-part links are consistently expressive and indicative: the bodily register makes visible the inner pride that the heart and spirit hold. Pro 6:17 (vc=34247, M08-A2-VCG-01) — "haughty eyes... an outward expression of an inward elevation of self that God finds abominable" — the eye-link is expressive: it renders CHAR-1 visible and morally legible for divine assessment and judgment. Isa 2:11 (vc=34089, M08-A2-VCG-01) — "the haughty looks of man shall be brought low" — the looks both express the inner disposition and become the specific target of divine judgment, functioning as indicators of what is being addressed. Isa 3:16 (vc=34052, M08-A2-VCG-02) — "outstretched necks... wanton glances... mincing along" — the body in motion as the full indicative display of the inner haughtiness. The body-part links do not mediate CHAR-1 into the person; they express and indicate it outward.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The stiff-neck body-part link is expressive and indicative: the neck's stiffening is how CHAR-2's inner resistance to divine authority becomes physically visible and narratively legible. Neh 9:16 (vc=34120, M08-B-VCG-01): "stiffened their neck" pairs with "acted presumptuously" as the somatic expression of the inner volitional refusal. The body-part links in §3.A function as indicators — making the inner will's defiant orientation readable through a physical sign (the stiff neck), a physical action (going up to battle), or a physical instrument (the hand in murder). The bodily expression confirms that CHAR-2 is not merely a cognitive position but a willed act that moves into physical space.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The mouth-link is functional: CHAR-3 requires speech to be expressed; the boast that remains interior is not yet CHAR-3 in its characteristic form — it becomes CHAR-3 when it is given voice. The mouth-link makes CHAR-3 accountable and addressable: what comes from the mouth can be heard, evaluated, and corrected. Pro 27:1 (vc=33359, M08-C-VCG-01): "do not boast about tomorrow" — the prohibition addresses the speech-act. The mouth is CHAR-3's functional expression-point.
**[CHAR-4]** S — No body-part link evidenced. See T2.6.1.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Physical height functions as the expressive and indicative form of CHAR-5's structural-power pride: the physical elevation of the high hill, the fortified nest, and the towering stature are what CHAR-5 looks like at the structural level. Obd 3 (vc=65674, M08-E-VCG-02): "lofty dwelling expresses the outward form of inner pride — living in inaccessible heights reinforces the proud heart's conviction of invulnerability." The physical height is both a chosen position (self-securing strategy) and a visible indicator of CHAR-5's inner posture — the same soul-to-body directionality as CHAR-1's haughty eyes but at the structural/architectural rather than the individual body-part level.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Across the cluster, the body-part links serve two functions. First, indicative: the body-part expression makes the inner pride externally legible and publicly identifiable (the haughty eyes of CHAR-1's M08-A2, the stiff neck of CHAR-2, the mouth of CHAR-3, the fortified height of CHAR-5). Second, accountable: the bodily expression makes the inner pride judicially assessable — it creates a publicly evidenced form of the inner characteristic that can be named, addressed, and judged. The absence of body-part links in CHAR-4 is consistent with its exclusively inner-cognitive register: CHAR-4 does not primarily express through a body-part but through speech (controversy-craving) and relational disorder.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Two different functions. In Rom6:12, the link is *diagnostic*: the body's passions are named as the point of competition — submission to God versus submission to bodily desire are rival claims on the will. The body-link diagnoses where the competing submission operates and therefore where the battle for genuine submission must be fought. In Eph6:5, the link is *expressive*: the bodily service rendered to earthly masters is the outward form of the inner submission — the body-soul link here shows how inner submission necessarily takes outward form in the person's active conduct. Both functions confirm that the characteristic is not merely mental or spiritual but is engaged with the person's whole embodied existence.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Two different functions are at work. The weeping/clothes-tearing link (2Ki22:19; 2Ch34:27) is *expressive*: the body expresses the genuine inner state, and God confirms he has heard (the inner act is the criterion, the bodily expression is its outward correlate). The emphasis is that genuine humbling has bodily expression — the body is not the site but the indicator. The Phili3:21 "lowly body" link is *indicative*: the body's creaturely lowliness points to the constitutional condition of the believer in the present age — mortal, suffering, lowly — which awaits its transformation. Here the body *is* the site of the condition rather than merely expressing it.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Only Humility (CHAR-1) and Submission (CHAR-2) have evidenced body-characteristic links; both evidence two distinct functions simultaneously. For Humility (CHAR-1): the weeping/clothes-tearing link (2Ki22:19; 2Ch34:27) is expressive — the body expresses the genuine inner state, and God confirms he has heard (the bodily expression is the outer correlate of the inner act). The Phili3:21 "lowly body" link is indicative — the body's creaturely lowliness points to the constitutional condition of mortal embodiment awaiting transformation. Scripture makes the link differently in each register: expressively (M09-A — inner → bodily expression → divine hearing); indicatively (M09-B — bodily condition as constitutional indicator of the creaturely state). For Submission (CHAR-2): the body link in Rom6:12 is diagnostic — naming the body's passions as the specific site of competing submission; the body link in Eph6:5 is expressive — bodily service as the outer form of inner submission. Cluster-level: both body-linked characteristics use the body link in two distinct functional modes simultaneously, confirming that M09's engagement with the body is functional and purposive rather than incidental.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The body-part links serve distinct functions. For the mouth/lips/tongue (Psa 39:1; Job 2:10; Ecc 5:6), the function is *expressive and mediating* — the mouth is the organ through which inner sinful impulse externalises and through which restraint can intercept the act. The body-part is both the problem (it leads the person into sin, Ecc 5:6) and the solution-site (guarding it prevents the sin, Psa 39:1). For soma in 1Cor 6:18, the function is *indicative* — Paul indicates that sexual sin uniquely damages the very body through which it is committed, making the body both instrument and victim. For hands in 1Sa 24:11, the function is *instrumental* — hands are the agents of action (killing) that David specifically restrains.

**[CHAR-10]** E — 2Pe 2:14's eyes-link does two things. (1) *Names the perceptive channel of enticement*: the eyes are the sensory pathway through which the lure enters — "eyes full of adultery" names a gaze that has been formed to see through the lens of adulterous desire; the perceptive faculty has been captured by the desire-object. (2) *Connects the inner appetite to outer physical sensation*: the eyes bridge the inner desire and the outer world of visible lures — the body's sensory capacity is the interface through which external enticements engage the inner desire-faculty.

**[CHAR-11]** E — The members/flesh body-link (Rom 6:12/13; 7:5/23; 8:3/10) does four things. (1) *Locates the condition's operational site*: sin operates through the body's concrete physical capacities — not as an ethereal abstraction but through the members' actual motions; (2) *Explains the mind-flesh split*: the body-link explains why knowing what is right (Rom 7:23 — the mind's law) does not produce doing what is right (the members serving sin's law) — the condition has colonised the physical constitution; (3) *Establishes what the condition must be condemned in*: Rom 8:3 — God "condemned sin in the flesh" — the body-level is where the condition had to be addressed; (4) *Reveals the body's mortality as the condition's consequence*: Rom 8:10 — "the body is dead because of sin" — the physical body bears the terminal consequence of the universal condition.
**[CHAR-12]** S — No body-part link is evidenced. This prompt is not applicable.

**[CHAR-13]** E — The body-part links (bones — Psa 38:3; lips — Isa 6:7; Psa 59:12; hands — Isa 31:7) perform three functions. (1) *Naming the instrument of sin*: the hands (Isa 31:7), the mouth (Psa 59:12) are named as the body-parts through which specific sins are enacted and the record entries are created; (2) *Naming the site of consequence*: the bones and flesh (Psa 38:3) are where the record's weight registers physically — the body bears the evidence of the record's moral cost; (3) *Naming the site of atonement*: Isa 6:7 — the lips are the specific body-part where the divine action of atonement addresses the sin; the coal touches the place of the sin's origination.

**[CHAR-14]** E — The hands-link (2Ch 29:23) does two things. (1) *Enacts identification*: laying hands on the animal identifies the person (or community) with the offering — the sin is symbolically transferred to the substitute through the physical contact; the seeking is not purely inner but requires bodily engagement to be complete. (2) *Grounds the seeking in the body*: the bodily act of hand-laying makes the inner seeking externally visible and communally enacted — the king and assembly together lay hands, making the corporate seeking a shared bodily act.
**[CHAR-15]** S — No body-part link is evidenced. This prompt is not applicable.

**[CHAR-16]** E — Jam 4:8's hands-link does two things. (1) *Names the outer expression of the sinner-identity*: the hands are the visible instrument of sinful conduct; the call to cleanse them is a call to address the outer behavioural expression of the inner sinner-identity; (2) *Grounds the inner-identity in bodily action*: the parallel "cleanse your hands... purify your hearts" establishes that the sinner-identity has both an outer (hands — conduct) and an inner (heart — disposition) dimension that must both be addressed. The bodily expression is not separable from the inner identity.

**[CHAR-17]** E — Three distinct body-part functions. (1) *Face-avoidance* (Ezr 9:6): the downcast face before God names the body's expression of the guilt-state's shame dimension; the face cannot be lifted because the guilt precludes the standing-before-God that face-lifting implies; (2) *Forehead-bearing* (Exo 28:38): the forehead as the visible body-part that bore guilt before God establishes the priestly guilt-bearing as a physical and visible act — the guilt literally rests on the person's face/head in the representative's bearing; (3) *Lips-location* (Isa 6:7): the lips as the body-part of Isaiah's guilt names the speech-faculty as the site of his specific form of guilt (unclean lips before the holy God — Isa 6:5).

**[CHAR-18]** E — Three distinct body-part functions. (1) *Hands as instruments of iniquity* (Isa 59:3): the hands name the body-part of active wrongdoing; iniquity is enacted through the body's working members; the moral crime has a bodily-enactment dimension; (2) *Bones as iniquity's permanent mark* (Eze 32:27): iniquity clings to the bones even in death, naming the body as the permanent carrier of the iniquity-record into Sheol; (3) *Head/shoulders as overwhelmed bearer* (Psa 38:4): the head-overflowing image names the body-part through which the accumulated weight is expressed; the burden metaphor uses the body's carrying capacity to name iniquity's weight.

**[CHAR-19]** E — Three distinct body-part functions. (1) *Lips as transgression's instrument* (Pro 10:19; Pro 12:13; Isa 59:13): the mouth is the outer organ through which the heart's transgression is expressed; "transgression of the lips" names the body's speaking-organ as the conduit for inner rebellion becoming outer act; (2) *Neck as transgression's burden-point* (Lam 1:14): the yoke on the neck images the transgression as an enslaving weight physically borne; the neck is the body-part that carries what the transgression has imposed; (3) *Head as revolt's victim* (Isa 1:5): the head incapacitated by sustained revolt names the body's commanding faculty as the location of systemic deterioration from persistent transgression.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The finger in Lev 8:15 (Moses applying blood to altar horns) functions as the *mediating instrument* of purification — the precise physical action that conveys the atoning remedy to the defiled object. This is a functional body-part link in the remedial direction: the priest's finger is the means by which the unintentional defilement is addressed. The body-part here is in the remedy, not in the sinning act. This is the inverse of CHAR-1, where the body-part (tongue, lips, hands) is in the sinning act itself.

**[CHAR-20]** E — Two distinct body-part functions. (1) *Face and back as bodily expression of inner allegiance-direction* (2Ch 29:6): turning the face toward God or away is the body's expression of the heart's covenant-orientation; the face-direction images the inner will's God-direction; turning the back is the bodily expression of the heart that has definitively turned away; (2) *Womb and thigh as the site of covenant-embodied consequence* (Num 5:27): the marriage covenant was embodied in the marital relationship; faithlessness in that embodied covenant produces bodily consequences at the embodied organs of the covenant's expression — the curse falls on what expressed the covenant.

**[CHAR-21]** E — Three distinct body-part functions. (1) *Mouth/tongue as perversity's primary expressive organ*: Pro 10:31/32 — the tongue and mouth are the body-parts through which inner perversity is most immediately expressed outward; the perverse tongue is the inner corruption's most visible bodily instrument; (2) *Eyes as perversity's corrupted perceptive organ*: the blinded eyes (Exo 23:8 — bribery) and the winking eyes (Pro 16:30 — planned dishonesty) name the eyes as the body-part through which perversity distorts perception and signals intent; (3) *The bowed body as perversity's consequence*: Psa 38:6 — the whole body bent and prostrate is the bodily expression of what sin's perversion has done to the person's inner posture.

**[CHAR-22]** E — Three distinct body-part functions. (1) *Hands as injustice's primary enacting organs* (Psa 58:2; Psa 7:3; Eze 18:8): the hands are the body-parts through which the heart's devised injustice is enacted in the world; "withholds his hand from injustice" (Eze 18:8) confirms the hand as the conduct-level instrument the will either deploys or restrains; (2) *Tongue/lips as injustice's verbal instrument* (Isa 59:3; Job 6:30; Zep 3:13): the tongue expresses inward injustice verbally — "mutters wickedness" (Isa 59:3); (3) *Fingers as injustice's detailed-action organs* (Isa 59:3): the fingers represent the precision instruments of the wrongdoing — "your fingers with iniquity" naming the detailed physical execution of the unjust act.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The mouth-link is *expressive and constitutive*: the mouth expresses the inner conscience-recognition, and the expression is constitutive of confession — without the speaking, the inner state is guilt (CHAR-17) but not yet confession (CHAR-3). Scripture consistently shows confession happening through speech because speech is what makes the inner moral reality public — before God (prayer-confession), before persons (Shimei before the king — 2Sa 19:20; Judas before the priests — Mat 27:4), or before a community (corporate confessions — VCG-02). The body-part link is thus *necessary but not sufficient*: the mouth must speak, but what the mouth speaks must arise from conscience and will engaged, not merely from social calculation.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The mouth-link in Jer 2:35 is *expressive and constitutive* — the spoken claim is not merely a symptom of the inner suppression but constitutes and reinforces it. God's judgment falls specifically on the speech-act: "I will bring you to judgment for *saying*, 'I have not sinned'" — the speaking of the denial is itself the judged act. The body-part link is emphatic: the mouth, which should confess (CHAR-3), instead denies, and God holds the person accountable for the specific speech-act of denial.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The body-part link (Neh 9:29) is *expressive and emphatic*: the shoulder and neck metaphors embody the inner attitude of refusal in physical-gesture language. The imagery is drawn from animal behaviour (the ox refusing the yoke) and applied to the human will: the person's inner refusal to repent takes the physical form of an animal's resistance to being guided. This is emphatic because it makes the inner disposition viscerally visible — refusal to repent is not an intellectual position but a physical posture of resistance. The link also makes the characteristic's active nature unmistakable: a stiffened neck is not passive but actively resistant.
**[CHAR-6]** S — No explicit body-part link is evidenced. This prompt is not applicable.
**[CHAR-7]** S — No body-part link is evidenced. This prompt is not applicable.
**[CHAR-8]** S — No body-part link is evidenced. This prompt is not applicable.

**[CHAR-9]** E — The mouth-link is *constitutive*: sinful speech is definitionally a mouth-act. Without the mouth, the inner corruption remains unexpressed as CHAR-9. The mouth-link also functions *diagnostically*: Col 3:8 — "from your mouth" — addresses the command of renunciation at the point of externalisation; the mouth is where the characteristic either occurs or is prevented. Rev 13:5/6 — the beast's mouth as the instrument of its constitutive blasphemy — the mouth is the beast's defining operative faculty for its anti-God identity. The body-part link is the most consistent and constitutive in the entire M10 corpus.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The mouth-link (the dominant body connection) is primarily expressive and indicative: the wicked person's speech reveals and enacts the inner orientation. The mouth does not cause wickedness — it discloses and extends it outward into social space (Pro 12:6: "lie in wait for blood" — the words as instruments; Pro 10:6: "conceals violence" — the mouth masking and enabling). The arm/hand link is functional and mediating: the wicked person's capacity for harm is located in their physical power (Psa 10:15 — "break the arm" = dismantle their harm-capacity; Job 38:15 — "their uplifted arm is broken" = divine termination of their agency). The eyes link (Pro 21:4) is expressive and indicative: haughty eyes display the inner pride that constitutes the wicked person's characteristic orientation. The body-links are consistently diagnostic (displaying inner character) and instrumental (enacting inner orientation outward).

**[CHAR-2]** E — The eye-link (Mat 6:23 — VCG-03) is indicative and functional: the eye's moral state (bad vs. good) is indicative of the whole inner person's condition, and functionally it is the perceptive channel through which inner darkness is spread to the whole body. Scripture's use here is diagnostic — the quality of the eye reveals and expresses the constitutional inner condition. The mouth-link (Mat 12:34; Luk 6:45 — VCG-03) is expressive and revelatory: the mouth does not cause the constitutional evil but reveals and enacts it. Scripture is using the mouth as the diagnostic instrument — what overflows from the mouth reveals the state of the heart-treasury. The body-members link (Rom 6:13 — VCG-06) is functional-mediating: the body's members are the means through which constitutional unrighteousness is enacted outward in the world; the link is about instrumentality.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The lip-links (Pro 8:7; Pro 12:22 — VCG-02) are expressive and indicative: the lips reveal and enact the inner character — lying lips disclose a heart of deception. The ear-link (Pro 28:9 — VCG-03) is functional and mediating: the ear's turning away from the law is the volitional act that corrupts the worship relationship, making prayer abominable. The function here is the reverse of the normal: the ear should mediate receptivity to divine instruction; its deliberate turning away mediates the corruption of the person's access to God. The forehead-link (Rev 17:5 — VCG-05) is emphatic and identifying: public disclosure of inner identity. The face-link (Eze 14:6 — VCG-04) is directional and indicative: the face shows the direction the person is oriented; turning the face from abominations is the commanded inner-volitional act expressed through the body's directional faculty.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The eyes-link (Eze 20:7; 6:9 — VCG-05) is expressive and functional: the eyes as the body's perceptive-desire faculty express the inner attachment to idolatrous objects; they also function as the mechanism through which the characteristic deepens (feasting on the idols feeds the inner attachment). The link is both diagnostic and causal: the eyes reveal the inner state and contribute to its perpetuation. The hands-link (making idols from beautiful ornament — Eze 7:20 — VCG-05) is expressive and mediating: the bodily act of craft production enacts the inner idolatrous disposition outward. The mouth/teeth-link (Zec 9:7 — VCG-04) is emphatic and vivid: abominations lodged in the mouth/teeth show how thoroughly the characteristic has penetrated the physical person, requiring divine extraction.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Three distinct functions are evidenced. The hand-link (Job 11:14 — VCG-04) is functional and expressive: the hand as the instrument of agency; iniquity in the hand is the inner condition enacted through the body's primary work-instrument. The commanded response ("put it far away") shows the hand-link as indicating active-enactment requiring volitional reversal. The tongue/mouth-link (Psa 10:7 — VCG-04) is concealment-deployment: the iniquity hidden beneath the tongue is positioned for strategic release through speech; Scripture's naming of the sub-lingual location is emphatic — the evil is not merely in the abstract inner life but positioned in the speech mechanism. The feet-link (Isa 59:7 — VCG-02; Pro 6:18 — VCG-02) is directional-indicative: feet running to evil shows the whole embodied person moving eagerly toward iniquity — the eagerness of the body's locomotion reveals the will's inner orientation.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Rev 13:6 (vc=14356 — VCG-01): "opened its mouth to utter blasphemies" — the mouth-link is functional and mediating: the mouth is the specific constitutional instrument through which the beast's inner defiant contempt becomes social reality. The mouth-link is not merely emphatic (this is how it works) but constitutive (without the mouth, the inner evil cannot become operative blasphemy). The deliberate "opened its mouth" also reveals agency and intention: the mouth is not involuntarily venting but deliberately opened — the volitional act of opening the mouth is part of the characteristic's inner-being operation. The mouth functions as both mediating instrument and indicator of deliberate agency.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Across the cluster, three functions of body-part links emerge. (1) Expressive-indicative: the body part reveals the inner condition (mouth revealing wicked inner character — Chars 1, 2, 5); eyes revealing the inner orientation (Char 4 — feasting eyes revealing inner idol-attachment; Char 2 — bad eye revealing constitutional inner darkness). (2) Functional-mediating: the body part is the instrument through which inner evil is enacted (hands making idols — Char 4; feet running to evil — Char 5; mouth opening to utter blasphemy — Char 6). (3) Bidirectional feedback: the body-characteristic link runs both inner-to-outer AND outer-to-inner in two characteristics specifically — Char 4 (the eye-feast on idols reinforces inner attachment) and Char 5 (the mouth devouring iniquity feeds back into the inner appetite). This bidirectional feedback is a distinctive cluster-level finding: two characteristics show the body-expressive act as not merely diagnostic but formative — the expression deepens the inner condition.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The body-part links serve distinct functions. The skin linkage (Lev 13 leprosy corpus) is diagnostic and indicative: the skin's condition is the external indicator of the defilement-state's presence and severity. The hand linkage (Lev 15:11) is functional: the unwashed hand is the transmission vector — washing the hand could prevent the transfer, making the hand's cleansing the moral act. The bodily-fluid linkages (Lev 15 discharge) are mediating: the fluid is the medium through which the defilement-state transmits from person to person and to objects. The head linkage (Lev 13:44-45) is both indicative (the disease location) and expressive (the self-declaration involves the whole visible head — "let the hair hang loose, cover the upper lip, cry out").

**[CHAR-2]** E — The lips-link at Isa 6:5 (VCG-01) is expressive and indicative: the lips are the organ of confession, prophecy, and speech before God — naming them as unclean is both the prophet's self-recognition (expressive) and an indication that the defilement extends to his primary instrument of divine service (indicative). The body-link at Rom 1:24 (VCG-02) is consequential: the body receives the dishonour that results from the defilement-state; the body mediates the moral consequence outwardly. The body-link at 2Cor 7:1 (VCG-03) is constitutional: defilement of body and spirit together names the full extent of the condition — neither bodily nor spiritual is excluded; the link is comprehensive rather than specific.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The body-part links serve distinct functions. The womb/thigh link at Num 5:27 (VCG-01) is judicial-consequential: the specific body parts associated with reproduction and covenant-sexual integrity receive the physical consequence of covenantal infidelity — the defilement of a sexual covenant bond is judged in the bodily domain most directly associated with that bond. The menstrual-impurity link at Eze 22:10 (VCG-01) is boundary-indicative: the body's physiological state defines a relational-moral boundary whose transgression constitutes covenantal defilement.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The speech/mouth link (Mar 1:23, Mar 1:26, Mar 9:25) is functional and expressive: the spirit uses the person's voice as its instrument of declaration and protest; and the spirit suppresses speech to isolate the person from relational communication. The body-as-a-whole link (Luk 8:29 — breaking chains; Luk 9:42 — convulsions) is emphatic and indicative: the spirit's expression through the body demonstrates the power of the domination — the body is no longer the person's own instrument but the spirit's.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The four body-part links serve distinct theological functions that together reveal the cluster's theology of embodiment. Characteristic 1's skin link (Lev 13) is diagnostic: the body surface is the readable text that encodes sacral status — the priest reads the skin to determine the person's condition. Characteristic 1's hand link (Lev 15:11) is functional: the unwashed hand is the transmission vector — the body part is the mechanism of defilement's spread. Characteristic 2's lips link (Isa 6:5) is expressive and indicative: the lips are the organ of prophetic speech before God, making the defilement of the lips particularly revealing of inner moral condition. Characteristic 3's womb/thigh link (Num 5:27) is judicial-consequential: the body parts most directly associated with the violated covenant bond (reproductive-sexual) receive the physical consequence of that violation — the defilement of a covenant relationship is judged in the body that enacted the betrayal. Characteristic 4's voice link (Mar 1:26, Mar 9:25) is appropriative: the spirit uses the person's communicative apparatus for its own declarations — and suppresses it when it serves the spirit's isolating purposes. The cluster's theology of the body: the body is simultaneously a diagnostic surface (Char 1), an expressive medium (Chars 2, 4), a judicial site (Char 3), and a transmission vector (Chars 1, 4).

findings.session_b_note: Love is not primarily emotional in the biblical data, though it has a rich emotional dimension. The evidence positions love as primarily dispositional/constitutional — an inner orientation that produces emotional states rather than consisting in them. Chesed is the clearest evidence: it persists without depending on emotional states (Lam 3:22 — 'the steadfast love of the Lord never ceases' despite Israel's devastating judgment). Agapē of enemies (Mat 5:44) operates where positive feeling is absent or where it must overcome negative feeling. The emotional states (joy, grief, rest, yearning) are love's products and evidence, not its constitutive substance. If love were primarily emotional, its commanded form ('you shall love') would be incoherent — emotions cannot be commanded. The commanded form confirms that love's primary operation is dispositional-volitional; the emotional dimension is real but secondary.

findings.finding_value: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level (chesed as covenantal-soul character), heart-level (Hos 11:8 — "my heart recoils"), and somatic-level (re.chem, splanchnon) are all richly evidenced. The constitutional architecture is bottom-up: the womb and entrails are the originating ground; the soul and heart are the engagement points; the act is the constitutional expression. Four body-part functions are identified: constitutive (womb — the generative image of compassion), expressive (gut — the felt movement), indicative (Synoptic pattern — splanchnizō signals the compassion-event), and mediating (heart in Hos 11:8 — the deliberative locus where compassion and judgment contend). The four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) is uniquely evidenced in this registry — consistently inside-out and bottom-up. T2.8 established no body deposit; T5.7 is formally closed. The constitutional portrait confirms the sb_classification (soul-body interface) and extends it: compassion is the most somatically grounded characteristic in the programme, with its originating logic residing in the body's deepest interior.

findings.finding_value: T1's four-kind structure (character quality, inner event, condition of object, externalised act) maps precisely onto T2's constitutional levels. The character-quality kind (ra.chum — dispositional compassionate character) operates at the soul level (T2.2 — chesed as soul-character). The inner-event kind (splanchnizō — the moment of being-moved) operates at the somatic level (T2.6 — the gut as the site of the stirring). The condition-of-object kind (eleeinos — the pitiable state) is the constitutional trigger that activates the somatic-constitutional movement. The externalised-act kind is the constitutional endpoint of T2.10's four-stage movement sequence. T1's definition and T2's constitutional account are co-determining: the characteristic cannot be adequately defined without specifying the constitutional levels at which its four kinds operate.

findings.finding_value: T2's four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) maps directly onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The somatic-arousal stage (T2.6 — gut stirring, splanchnizō) corresponds to T3.1's perceptive-trigger stage (sight activates the somatic response) and T3.4's affect stage (the stirring is the affective movement). The soul-engagement stage (T2.2 — chesed as soul-character) corresponds to T3.8 moral evaluation (the soul assesses the need) and T3.9 conscience (the conscience activates the response). The volitional-engagement stage (T2.3 — heart-locus as deliberative site) corresponds to T3.6 volition (the will directs the action). The outward-action stage corresponds to T3.7 agency. T2 and T3 describe the same movement sequence from two perspectives: T2 maps the constitutional levels; T3 maps the faculties active at each level.

findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional origin analysis (somatic-relational-covenantal triple ground) and T4's relational direction analysis are structurally aligned. The somatic origin (womb, gut) grounds the cross-boundary relational direction in T4: splanchnizō's somatic immediacy is precisely what enables it to cross covenantal boundaries — the gut-movement toward the suffering other precedes any covenantal assessment of the relationship. The covenantal origin (chesed) grounds the within-bond sustaining direction in T4. The constitutional origin therefore predicts the relational direction: somatic = cross-boundary; covenantal = within-bond. T2's soul-body interface classification explains T4's scope-by-need finding: because compassion originates at the soul-body interface (before covenantal-rational assessment), its scope is determined by the pre-rational recognition of need rather than the post-rational assessment of covenantal standing.

findings.finding_value: T2's somatic-constitutional location explains several T6 structural connections. The shared anchor at Isa 53:5 (with R030 contrition) confirms that the somatic wound vocabulary intersects both compassion and contrition at the constitutional-somatic level — both characteristics have somatic-body language as part of their evidential ground. The CHASAD root's crossing of compassion and shame clusters (T6.4 — most unexpected structural finding) is partly explainable from T2: if CHASAD names a covenantal-soul disposition, it can operate in both the positive register (chesed — steadfast love/compassion) and the negative register (bōsheth — shame as the opposite soul-condition of exposed vulnerability). T2's constitutional portrait (soul-body interface) is the constitutional ground for the root-level cluster-crossing that T6 identifies.

findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional levels are each carried by specific vocabulary families in T7. The somatic-body level (T2.6 — gut, womb) is carried by the RACHAM/SPLANCHN root families — the body's interior as the etymological ground of both. The soul-character level (T2.2) is carried by the CHASAD family — chesed as the settled covenantal character disposition. The heart-deliberative level (T2.3) is evidenced most richly in Hos 11:8 (T7's primary anchor for divine compassion). T7's vocabulary arc (womb to almsgiving) traverses exactly the constitutional range T2 maps: from the most interior somatic level (womb) through the character-soul level to the externalised action level. The dual primary anchor (T7) maps onto T2's constitutional depth: Hos 11:8 evidences constitutional depth (heart-level deliberation of compassion over judgment); Luke 10:33 evidences constitutional breadth (the full four-stage movement from sight to action).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-002: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary…
findings.finding_value: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary point of reception (Zec 12:10 — spirit of grace poured out), not the point of generation (grace originates with God — T2.9). The soul level is the site of standing (Rom 5:2 — "this grace in which we stand") and identity (1Cor 15:10 — "by the grace of God I am what I am"). The constitutional movement follows the SD021 four-faces model: divine disposition received at spirit level → relational standing established at soul level → specific capacity gifted → character expressed outward. Heart-location is partially evidenced via eusplanchnos (Eph 4:32 — the tenderheartedness that grace produces, reaching the affective-somatic interface). T2.7 produces a new finding: grace operates bidirectionally through the body-soul interface — soul-to-body (inner posture enacted somatically in prostration, fasting, sackcloth) and body-to-soul (somatic enactment deepening and confirming the inner posture). T2.8 remains open (body deposit question unresolved); T5.7 is left open accordingly. The constitutional origin analysis (T2.9) is the most analytically significant T2 finding: grace does not originate in the human constitutional system at any level — it arrives from outside. This is confirmed at T6 as the structural uniqueness of grace: the only characteristic that is not produced by any other inner-being characteristic.

questions.question_text: Where a body link exists (from the T2.1.1 audit), in which direction does it run — soul/spirit expressing through the body, the body feeding back to the soul, or both — and what follows from that direction? If no body link, record none.

findings.session_b_note:
The direction varies by instance, and the data supports the observation that both directions operate:

- **Soul → Body (expressive direction):** The woman's bodily acts (Luk 7:47) — the inner state of received forgiveness expresses outward through bodily action. Direction: soul to body.
- **Body → Soul (feedback direction):** The visceral compassion (splagchnizomai, Mat 18:27) — the body's gut-level response moves the inner person toward the act of forgiving. Direction: body to soul (as motivating impulse).
- **Body as mediating instrument (neither direction exclusively):** The blood of Christ (Eph 1:7) — the body/blood of Christ mediates between the divine act and human reception. This is not a simple directional relationship within the human person.
- **Body as downstream indicator:** The paralytic's healing — the body shows the effect of the inner-being act without directly feeding back to the soul.

The direction runs **both ways** across the different instances — and Scripture deploys both directions purposefully.

findings.session_b_note:
The data reveals that the body-characteristic link for compassion runs in both directions, and that the directionality differs by body part and vocabulary:

**From soul to body (expressive direction):** In the splanchnizō Gospels pattern, the inner compassion-disposition (soul level) expresses itself through the gut-stirring (body level) and then through action. The movement is: inner character → somatic event → outward act. The body is the vehicle through which the soul's compassion arrives at expression and action.

**From body to soul (constitutive direction):** In the RACHAM etymology, the direction is reversed. The body's most intimate space (womb) is the ground from which the abstract compassion concept was named. The physical reality precedes and constitutes the inner-being concept. This is the unusual etymological direction noted at T0.3 Prompt 1 — the womb feeds the meaning upward into the soul-level concept.

**Mutual / participatory direction (sumpatheō):** The classical philosophical usage of sumpatheō (soul and body sympathising with each other — Aristotle, as noted in the Pass 1 term 14 analysis) introduces a bidirectional model: the soul and body suffer-together, each affecting the other. The NT reappropriation of this term for Christian community and Christology (SD-011) carries this bidirectionality into the new context: genuine fellow-feeling involves both soul and body moving in concert.

findings.session_b_note:

1. **Soul/inner-being → Body (expressive)**: In Jer 46:5, the inner terror produces bodily behaviour (turning backward, fleeing). The inner state expresses through bodily movement. The body is the medium of expression for the inner-being crushing.

2. **Body → Soul/inner-being (indicative and constitutive)**: In Psa 51:8, the broken bones carry the image of inner divine chastisement. The body is the image through which the inner-being condition is described — somatic language is used to name the inner condition (the breaking of bones images the breaking of the inner person by God's chastisement). The somatic language is constitutive of the meaning: it conveys the depth of the inner-being breaking by invoking the deepest physical layer.

The groaning of Psa 38:8 is a third direction: **body expressing inner-being reality simultaneously** — the groan arises from both the tumult of the heart and the feeble/crushed condition of the person, and it is both somatic and inner-being at once.

**Soul expressed through body (outward direction):** Isa 53:5 — the servant's inner fellowship of substitutionary suffering is expressed outwardly through the physical wounds. The inner-being reality (bearing of transgressions, the chastisement that brought peace) is made visible through the somatic wound. Movement runs from inner to outer.

**Bidirectional (Phili 3:10):** Fellowship with Christ's sufferings engages both directions: the outward somatic experience of suffering participates in the inner transformative fellowship trajectory (inward), while the person's inner orientation toward Christ expresses itself through conformity to his death (outward). Both directions operate simultaneously.

findings.finding_value: T2 establishes that contrition operates at the deepest constitutional level (spirit as primary locus) with secondary engagement at heart, soul, and body. The constitutional portrait is comprehensive: spirit broken at the innermost level, heart broken at the moral-evaluative level, nephesh crushed at the whole-self level, and bones as the somatic expression of the inner breaking. What T2 reveals as a whole is the embodied depth of contrition — it is not a disembodied inner experience but a constitutional event that traverses all levels of the person. The bidirectional constitutional movement (downward through divine confrontation, upward through reviving) is the structural frame within which contrition functions: it reaches the bottom and creates the conditions for movement back upward. The T2.8 finding (no body deposit) means contrition does not leave a permanent somatic trace — it is a passing constitutional event, not a permanent constitutional mark.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-002: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level …
findings.finding_value: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level (chesed as covenantal-soul character), heart-level (Hos 11:8 — "my heart recoils"), and somatic-level (re.chem, splanchnon) are all richly evidenced. The constitutional architecture is bottom-up: the womb and entrails are the originating ground; the soul and heart are the engagement points; the act is the constitutional expression. Four body-part functions are identified: constitutive (womb — the generative image of compassion), expressive (gut — the felt movement), indicative (Synoptic pattern — splanchnizō signals the compassion-event), and mediating (heart in Hos 11:8 — the deliberative locus where compassion and judgment contend). The four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) is uniquely evidenced in this registry — consistently inside-out and bottom-up. T2.8 established no body deposit; T5.7 is formally closed. The constitutional portrait confirms the sb_classification (soul-body interface) and extends it: compassion is the most somatically grounded characteristic in the programme, with its originating logic residing in the body's deepest interior.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-018: T2's constitutional levels are each carried by specific vocabulary families in T7. The somatic-body level (T2.6 — gut, womb) is carried by the RACHAM/SPLANCHN root families — the body's interior as th…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional levels are each carried by specific vocabulary families in T7. The somatic-body level (T2.6 — gut, womb) is carried by the RACHAM/SPLANCHN root families — the body's interior as the etymological ground of both. The soul-character level (T2.2) is carried by the CHASAD family — chesed as the settled covenantal character disposition. The heart-deliberative level (T2.3) is evidenced most richly in Hos 11:8 (T7's primary anchor for divine compassion). T7's vocabulary arc (womb to almsgiving) traverses exactly the constitutional range T2 maps: from the most interior somatic level (womb) through the character-soul level to the externalised action level. The dual primary anchor (T7) maps onto T2's constitutional depth: Hos 11:8 evidences constitutional depth (heart-level deliberation of compassion over judgment); Luke 10:33 evidences constitutional breadth (the full four-stage movement from sight to action).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-002: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary…
findings.finding_value: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary point of reception (Zec 12:10 — spirit of grace poured out), not the point of generation (grace originates with God — T2.9). The soul level is the site of standing (Rom 5:2 — "this grace in which we stand") and identity (1Cor 15:10 — "by the grace of God I am what I am"). The constitutional movement follows the SD021 four-faces model: divine disposition received at spirit level → relational standing established at soul level → specific capacity gifted → character expressed outward. Heart-location is partially evidenced via eusplanchnos (Eph 4:32 — the tenderheartedness that grace produces, reaching the affective-somatic interface). T2.7 produces a new finding: grace operates bidirectionally through the body-soul interface — soul-to-body (inner posture enacted somatically in prostration, fasting, sackcloth) and body-to-soul (somatic enactment deepening and confirming the inner posture). T2.8 remains open (body deposit question unresolved); T5.7 is left open accordingly. The constitutional origin analysis (T2.9) is the most analytically significant T2 finding: grace does not originate in the human constitutional system at any level — it arrives from outside. This is confirmed at T6 as the structural uniqueness of grace: the only characteristic that is not produced by any other inner-being characteristic.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-008: T1's four-kind structure (disposition, standing, capacity, character quality) maps onto T2's constitutional levels. The divine-disposition kind operates at the level of grace's origin (T2.9 — God's ow…
findings.finding_value: T1's four-kind structure (disposition, standing, capacity, character quality) maps onto T2's constitutional levels. The divine-disposition kind operates at the level of grace's origin (T2.9 — God's own disposition; not a human constitutional level). The standing kind operates at the soul level (T2.2 — Rom 5:2 "this grace in which we stand"). The capacity kind operates at the spirit-soul interface — the specific enabling for specific tasks (2Cor 12:9) is received at the deepest level and expressed through specific faculties. The character-quality kind operates at the soul-to-body level (T2.7 — gracious conduct and speech expressing the received inner character outward). T1's constitutional movement finding (SD021 four-faces sequence) is the longitudinal form of T2's spatial map: T2 identifies the constitutional levels; T1 identifies the movement between them.

findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional movement (spirit reception → soul standing → capacity → character expression) maps onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The spirit-reception stage (T2.1) corresponds to T3.1 (perception — grace enabling the inner sight and hearing that receives it). The soul-standing stage (T2.2) corresponds to T3.9 (conscience — grace as the condition within which conscience can operate without destruction) and T3.8 (moral evaluation — the standing produces the clarity of moral self-assessment). The capacity-gifting stage (T2.1 — spirit level) corresponds to T3.7 (agency — capacity given constitutes agency for the task). The character-expression stage (T2.7 — outward through body-soul) corresponds to T3.10 (conscientiousness — the integrated moral-action expression of received grace-character). T2 maps the constitutional space; T3 maps the faculties active at each spatial level; the two tiers describe the same movement from orthogonal perspectives.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-016: T2's constitutional movement (SD021 sequence: disposition → standing → capacity → character) and T5's five formation mechanisms describe the same formation arc from spatial and temporal perspectives. …
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional movement (SD021 sequence: disposition → standing → capacity → character) and T5's five formation mechanisms describe the same formation arc from spatial and temporal perspectives. T2 identifies the constitutional levels through which grace moves; T5 identifies the mechanisms by which grace moves through each level in different contexts. The encounter mechanism (T5 — sudden specific relational event) produces the spirit-level reception (T2.1 — the initial point of arrival). The word mechanism (T5 — Act 20:32 — grace through proclaimed word) produces the soul-standing establishment (T2.2 — the word's sustained effect on the person's constitutive condition). The mediated-transformation mechanism (T5 — tenderheartedness → forgiving — Eph 4:32, SD030) corresponds to T2.7's bidirectional body-soul finding: the inner transformation mediates outward through the body-soul interface. T2.8's open question (body deposit) and T5.7's open status are formally aligned — both pending further investigation.

findings.finding_value: T2 establishes that peace is constitutionally mobile across all three levels (spirit, soul/mind/heart, body) in three documented patterns: (1) Cascading loss — inner disorder produces somatic deterioration (Psa 32:3, 38:3, Deu 28:65); the body is the last to fail and the indicator of deep inner disorder; (2) Cascading gift — divine peace received at the spirit level moves through heart and mind (Phili 4:7) into somatic rest (Psa 4:8); (3) Redemptive reversal — the Servant's wounded body produces inner healing in others (Isa 53:5); the primary causal direction reversed. findings.session_b_note: The direction is inner-to-body (soul expressing through body) in Isa 50:6. findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-060-002: T2 as a whole reveals that this characteristic has no single constitutional home — it operates across the full spirit-soul-body register through different modes. Spirit is the location in two modes: a…
findings.finding_value: T2 as a whole reveals that this characteristic has no single constitutional home — it operates across the full spirit-soul-body register through different modes. Spirit is the location in two modes: as the object of endowing giving (Neh 9:20) and as the faculty transformed eschatologically (Isa 61:3). Soul (nephesh/nafshi) appears in divine self-reference in the giving-over context (Jer 12:7). Heart (leb) is the faculty where the giving decision is made (Hos 11:8). Hidden inner parts (tukhoth) are the target of wisdom-giving (Job 38:36). Rahamim (visceral compassion) is the inner-being quality that determines giving direction. Body appears as the expressive medium of self-giving (Isa 50:6) and as constituted by breath-giving (Isa 42:5). No constitutional body deposit is confirmed. Three movement patterns — constitutive (spirit→mind), expressive (inner→body), transformative (outside-in→inside renewed→inside-out) — show the characteristic is constitutionally dynamic. What T2 reveals as a whole: this characteristic operates at every constitutional level not because it is superficially distributed but because giving as an inner-being act can reach the spirit (endowing), the heart (deciding), the soul (attaching), the hidden inner parts (forming), and the body (expressing and constituting). It is constitutionally pervasive.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-008: The constitutional locations where the characteristic operates (T2 — heart, soul/nephesh, spirit, body) and the relational interfaces through which it operates (T4 — God-to-human, human-to-God) reveal…
findings.finding_value: The constitutional locations where the characteristic operates (T2 — heart, soul/nephesh, spirit, body) and the relational interfaces through which it operates (T4 — God-to-human, human-to-God) reveal a mirroring structure. God's giving proceeds from his leb (heart, Hos 11:8) and his nafshi (soul, Jer 12:7) — the deepest divine inner-being locations are engaged in the God-to-human direction. The human's giving toward God is expressed through the body (back, cheeks, face — Isa 50:6) and from the deepest inner orientation (Job 1:21 — recognition of divine sovereignty). The constitutional depths engaged in both directions are commensurate: God gives from his heart and soul; the human gives from the whole self, expressed bodily. What this pair reveals: the divine-human relational correspondence (DHC dimension, group 872-006) has a constitutional depth structure — the correspondence is not merely behavioural but engages the deepest constitutional levels of both parties. The giving that constitutes the correspondence is heart-to-body deep.

**[A2 — Human Righteousness]** Soul expressing through body. The righteous person's inner state expresses itself through the mouth (speech) and through the hands (action). The direction runs from inner-to-outer: righteousness in the heart and will produces righteous speech and righteous action. The body does not generate the righteousness; it expresses it.

**[B — Moral Uprightness]** Soul expressing through body. The inner disposition of uprightness in the heart produces upright speech from the lips. Same direction as A2: inner-to-outer, soul-to-body expression.

**[E — Condemnation]** Soul expressing through body (and back). The mouth expresses the inner condition — but in E there is also a feedback loop: "by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned" (Mat 12:37). The words expressed from the inner condition become the grounds of the verdict directed back at the person. The direction here runs both ways: inner→mouth (expression) and then mouth→verdict (feedback that determines the standing). The body part (mouth) becomes the medium of both expression and judgment.

**[G — Structural Opposites]** Soul expressing through body. The wicked person's inner condition expresses itself through the mouth (Job 15:6) and through the hands (Psa 71:4). Direction: inner-to-outer.
Soul → body direction: wisdom in the heart → judicious speech from the mouth (Pro 16:23). Unidirectional: outward-expressing.

findings.finding_value: The direction in 2Cor 4:16 runs from the body upward to the soul/heart — or more precisely, the text denies that this direction reaches its apparent terminus. The body wastes away (physical deterioration) but the inner self is renewed (the inner does not follow the outer's trajectory). The characteristic (ekkakeō) is the risk of the soul following the body's declining trajectory; the text says the inner renewal prevents this. Direction: body decline does not necessarily produce inner collapse — but the assumed natural direction (body → soul vulnerability) is the risk the verse names and counters.

findings.finding_value: The sha.men body-link runs in both directions in different contexts. In Isa 6:10, the direction is soul-to-body: the inner condition of fat-heartedness is expressed in the functional impairment of the perceptual organs (cannot see, hear). In Deu 32:15 and Jer 5:28, the direction is body-to-soul: the physical condition of being fat/well-fed (material prosperity received into the body) produces the inner condition of turning from God. Both directions are evidenced.

findings.finding_value: For M01-A's somatic dimension (Psa 119:120) and M01-E-VCG-02 (trembling at God's word), the direction runs from soul/spirit → body. The reverential dread or spirit-trembling is the inner originating state; the bodily trembling is the expression. Direction: soul expressing through the body.

For M01-A's somatic dimension (Psa 119:120) and M01-E-VCG-02 (trembling at God's word), the direction runs from soul/spirit → body. The reverential dread or spirit-trembling is the inner originating state; the bodily trembling is the expression. Direction: soul expressing through the body.

For the involuntary somatic expressions in M01-B (face-expression, heart-registration), M01-D (limbs giving way, color change), and most of M01-E (theophanic trembling, military panic-trembling), the direction is complex. The triggering stimulus is external (sight of threat, divine encounter, overwhelming news); the internal state arises; the body expresses it. This is primarily soul/inner person → body, but with an important caveat: the bodily experience of trembling may itself deepen or intensify the inner fear state (the body feeding back to the soul). The Damasio somatic marker framework from the science extract is relevant here: somatic states are constitutive of emotional experience, not merely expressive.

M01-F's body link (Eze 12:18: quivering while drinking) runs from inner anxiety → body (soul expressing through body). But the ongoing somatic anxiety may deepen the inner state, suggesting bidirectional influence.

The primary direction across M01 is soul/inner person → body (inner fear expressing through somatic symptoms). The evidence is consistent with a primary expressive direction but leaves open the possibility of somatic feedback to the inner state, particularly in the chronic conditions of M01-E and M01-F. The M01-E-VCG-02 (spirit-level trembling) confirms the soul-to-body direction most clearly.
For the face-link (Gen 4:5; Dan 3:19 / M02-B-VCG-02/03): the direction is soul-to-body — the inner anger expresses outward through the face. The face is the expressive medium, not the source.

For the bones-link (Psa 38:3 / M02-C-VCG-01 and Pro 14:30 / M02-E-VCG-04): the direction may run both ways. Divine indignation penetrates the body of the recipient (soul → body, impact direction). But sustained jealousy rotting the bones (Pro 14:30) suggests that the habitual inner state deposits its consequence in the body, which then feeds back as physical deterioration affecting the person's whole condition. The bi-directional possibility is present.
For Dan 3:19 (filling visible in face): the direction is soul-to-body — the inner state of being filled with fury overflows into the face's expression.

In M03-A and M03-E, the primary direction is inner-to-outer: grief in the soul/heart overflows outward through the body — tears from the eyes (Jer 13:17 anchor M03-A-VCG-04: "the soul's hidden grief" flows outward through the eyes as tears), groaning from the heart (Psa 38:8 — M03-E-VCG-01 anchor: groaning rises from "the tumult of my heart"). The inner state produces the outward somatic expression.

The inner state produces the outward somatic expression.

The feedback direction (body feeding back to the soul) is also evidenced: sustained weeping and sighing produce bodily deterioration (bones wasting, Psa 31:10 — M03-E-VCG-03; Psa 102:5) that then deepens the sense of inner depletion. Similarly, pain on the bed is divine rebuke engaging both body and conscience (Job 33:19 — M03-F-VCG-01), showing the somatic-to-inner feedback.

The bidirectionality is theologically significant: the body is not merely the passive vehicle for inner grief but participates in the grief event as a full partner.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The primary direction is **inner to outer**: soul exults → mouth praises (Psa 63:5); heart is glad → whole being rejoices → flesh dwells secure (Psa 16:9). The bones-rejoicing (Psa 51:8) is the restoration direction — the inner state of exultation, once restored, reaches through to the body's deepest structural level. There is no clear evidence of the body feeding back into the inner exultation in this corpus — the direction is consistently soul/heart → body/voice.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The primary direction is **inner to outer**: heart gladness → cheerful face (Pro 15:13); heart rejoices → whole being rejoices → flesh dwells secure (Psa 16:9); soul rejoices → tongue rejoices (Act 2:26). The secondary direction — **outer to inner** — appears in the feast-context passages: eating, drinking, and feasting (Deu 16:13–15; 1Ki 8:66; Ecc 9:7) are outer acts prescribed to occasion inner gladness; the bodily act of feasting in God's presence is a means of producing and expressing the inner joy. Wine gladdens the heart (Psa 104:15; Ecc 10:19) — a bodily input producing an inner state. This bidirectionality is notable: Joy is not only inner-to-outer in expression but also cultivated through outer forms that produce inner states.

**[CHAR-7]** E — **Inner to outer**: spirit/heart exults → tongue rejoices (Act 2:26); inner gladness → face smiles (Psa 39:13). The direction is consistently from the deepest constitutional level (spirit) outward through heart, tongue, and face. There is no evidence in this corpus of bodily state initiating the inner Suffering-Joy.

**[CHAR-3]** E — **Inner to outer**: the good news received by the inner person (cognitively and affectively) refreshes the bones — the inner gladness moves outward to the body's structural level. There is no evidence of the body initiating gladness in this corpus (unlike some Pleasure instances where sensory input produces inner warmth). The direction is consistently: news/word/circumstance received by the inner person → inner gladness arises → body participates in the refreshment.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Both directions: (1) **Inner to outer** — the primary direction in the affective-receptive register: the soul's delight in God's restoration expresses through the body (nursing, eating, being bounced — Isa 55:2; 66:11–12); the inner orientation produces outward bodily participation; (2) **Outer to inner** — the ni.cho.ach aroma direction: the physical act of offering the correctly-prescribed sacrifice (Lev 1:17; Num 15:13) is the outer act that expresses and reinforces the inner orientation of obedient Delight toward God; the aroma is the outer form of an inner disposition; (3) **Outer as sign of inner loss** — Deu 28:56 — the delicate woman's foot touching the ground is the outward sign of the inner Delight (a.nog) destroyed by judgment; the body signals what the inner being has lost.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Both directions: (1) **Body-to-soul** — the ni.cho.ach aroma rises from the offering (physical) and reaches God's inner being (divine inner response); in the human person: the perception of a pleasant aroma, sight, or taste produces an inner soul response (the olfactory, visual, and gustatory senses feeding inward to the soul); (2) **Soul-to-body** — Pro 16:24's gracious words received by the soul produce "health to the body" — the inner reception of pleasant speech flows outward to bodily health; the soul's Pleasure produces body-benefit; (3) **Body-as-signal** — Deu 28:54, 56 (the delicate body as the sign of Pleasure in pampered ease); the body's condition signals the inner state of Pleasure or its absence.

**[CHAR-6]** E — **External-to-inner-to-outward**: God's marvellous work (external) → perceived by the eyes (perceptive body) → wonder arises in the mind/soul (inner) → proclaimed through the mouth (expressive body). The direction is: external encounter → inner arrest → outward proclamation. This is a three-stage sequence: perception → astonishment → expression.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The directionality varies across the cluster with a dominant pattern and a significant exception: (1) **Dominant direction: inner-to-outer** — the primary direction for Exultation (soul/heart → voice/body), Joy (heart → face/hands/dance/voice), Gladness (cognitive evaluation → bodily refreshment — Pro 15:30), Delight (soul → eating/nursing images), Suffering-Joy (spirit/heart → tongue/face); (2) **Bidirectional**: Joy (Char 2) is the one characteristic with strong outer-to-inner evidence: feast-food, wine (Psa 104:15; Ecc 10:19), and communal festivity produce inner gladness — the prescribed outer forms of joy shape the inner state. The feast commandments (Deu 16:11–15) work in this outer-to-inner direction; Pleasure (Char 5) is also bidirectional: the ni.cho.ach aroma rises from the body (outer) to evoke God's inner response, while gracious words received (outer through hearing) produce inner soul-sweetness; (3) **Three-stage external-inner-outer**: Wonder (Char 6) — God's marvellous work (external) → perceived by eyes (body) → wonder arises in mind/soul (inner) → proclaimed through mouth (outer). This three-stage sequence is the most fully articulated constitutional movement pattern in the cluster.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Primarily **inner → body**: the felt inner shame produces the bodily expression (face-covering, blushing, head-lowering, withdrawal). But there is also a **body → inner** feedback: the bodily expression of shame can reinforce and deepen the inner state, and the bodily posture of trust (looking to God, Psa 34:5) produces the inner radiance that shame would have destroyed. The blushing-refusal of Jer 6:15 ("they did not know how to blush") shows that the bodily signal has been disconnected from the inner state — the body no longer reflects the inner reality that should be present. In the M07-C mode (face not lifted, Ezr 9:6), the bodily posture carries the inner moral reality outward into a relational context (before God) — this is bidirectional: inner shame → bodily posture → relational stance before God.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Bidirectional. External to body to inner: military defeat strips armour and forces retreat; social community strips the beard; divine act removes crown — the outer act produces inner collapse. Inner to body: haughty eyes (inner pride-disposition) are specifically targeted and brought low.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Inner to body: the inner disposition of disrespect toward divinely ordered authority is expressed through the bodily act (the covered or uncovered head). The body is the medium through which the inner worth-denial is communicated to the relational community.

**[CHAR-4]** E — In VCG-02, the direction is inner to body: disordered inner desire (dishonorable passions, Rom 1:26) produces the shameful bodily acts (Rom 1:27). The body enacts the inner disorder. In VCG-01's hair register (1Cor 11:6), the body-sign is both indicative of inner moral propriety and constitutive of the social-moral statement.

**[CHAR-5]** E — In VCG-02, the direction is outer to inner: the physical blow and shameful treatment produce the inner experience of CHAR-5 in the person being treated. In Mar 10:50, the direction is inner to body: the decision to abandon the shame-identity is expressed through the bodily act of throwing off the cloak.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The direction is inner to body to relational: heart-integrity (inner) -> hand-cleanness (body) -> approach to God's altar (relational). The hands express and enact the inner moral condition; the relational access to God is the outcome of the inner-to-body expression. This is a consistently inner-to-outer direction: CHAR-6 originates in the heart and expresses through the hands toward the relational encounter with God.

---

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's body-characteristic link is bidirectional, following the same inner-outer pattern identified at T2.10. Inner to body is the primary direction for expressive characteristics (Chars 1, 4, 6) — the inner condition expresses through the body. Body/outer to inner is the primary direction for received characteristics (Chars 2, 3, 5) — the external event produces the inner condition through the body. The body is therefore both the site of shame's expression and the site of its reception, mediating the inner-outer exchange in both directions. This bidirectionality confirms that the shame-field is a whole-person phenomenon operating across the body-soul interface.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — The direction is consistently soul-to-body: the inner pride of the heart and spirit expresses outward through the bodily register. Pro 30:13 (vc=34249, M08-A2-VCG-01): "inner arrogance manifests in the gaze" — manifestation is from interior to exterior. Isa 2:11 (vc=34089, M08-A2-VCG-01): "the outward gaze reflects an inner disposition of self-elevation" — reflection runs from inner disposition outward to the gaze. Isa 3:16 (vc=34052, M08-A2-VCG-02): "their inner exaltation/pride expresses itself outwardly in ostentatious posture and wanton glances" — the direction is explicit. 1Sa 2:3 (vc=12084, M08-A4-VCG-05): "proud talk is the outward expression of an inner arrogance that flows from the mouth" — from inner to vocal/bodily. No verse in §3 evidences the body generating or feeding back CHAR-1 into the inner person. The body is the display surface, not the source.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The direction is consistently will-to-body: the inner volitional assertion of CHAR-2 expresses itself outward through the body's actions and posture. Neh 9:16 (vc=34120, M08-B-VCG-01): the people's inner presumption ("acted presumptuously") produces the somatic expression ("stiffened their neck") and the physical action ("did not obey your commandments") — the sequence runs from inner to outer. Deu 1:43 (vc=34123): the inner will's defiance expresses through the bodily act of going up. No verse in §3.A evidences the body generating CHAR-2 in the inner person.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Inner to outer: the inner alazoneia disposition and the soul's desires (Psa 10:3, vc=33354) and the heart's prideful orientation generate the speech-act through the mouth outward into the social field. Jam 4:16 (vc=33866): "arrogance" (inner — alazoneia) → "you boast" (outer — speech-act). 1Jo 2:16 (vc=33865): "the pride of life [alazoneia]" is the inner source that produces visible social display. The direction is consistently interior → verbal/social expression.
**[CHAR-4]** S — No body-characteristic link evidenced in §3.C. Direction question not applicable.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The direction is consistently inner-to-outer: the heart's pride (Obd 3 — "the pride of your heart has deceived you") generates the choice to occupy elevated physical positions (living in the clefts of the rock) as a structural expression and security-strategy of the inner pride. Jer 49:16 (vc=34167, M08-E-VCG-02): "the height of your dwelling, who hold the height of the hill" — the physical dwelling-height expresses and reinforces the inner CHAR-5. The structural-physical elevation is the inner pride's external form.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The direction is consistently inner-to-outer across all four characteristics with body-part links. CHAR-1: the heart's elevated posture manifests outward as the haughty eyes (M08-A2-VCG-01/02). CHAR-2: the inner boiling-will expresses through the stiff neck and the going-up act. CHAR-3: the inner alazoneia disposition generates the speech-act through the mouth. CHAR-5: the heart-pride generates the choice to occupy elevated physical positions. The cluster-synthesis: M08's inner-to-outer directionality is universal — every characteristic moves from its constitutional seat (spirit, heart, or mind) outward through body or social expression. No characteristic begins with the body and generates the inner state.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The direction differs between the two body-links. In Rom6:12 (bodily passions — competition): the direction is *body → soul* in the negative direction — the body's passions exert a pull on the will, competing with the soul's submission to God. Sin's use of the body is the mechanism by which the competing submission operates: body → will's orientation. In Eph6:5 (bodily service — expression): the direction is *soul → body* — the genuine inner submission of the heart expresses itself through the bodily act of service. Heart → bodily conduct, with the heart's genuineness determining whether the bodily conduct is authentic (sincere heart as to Christ) or performative (eye-service).
**[CHAR-3]** S — No body-characteristic link is evidenced in §3.B (see T2.6.1). This prompt is accordingly closed.
**[CHAR-4]** S — No specific body-characteristic link is evidenced in §3.C. Prompt closed.
**[CHAR-5]** S — No body-characteristic link evidenced. Prompt closed.
**[CHAR-6]** S — No body-characteristic link evidenced. The constitutional movement is heart/spirit → outward act (bringing offerings), confirmed in T2.10, but no named body-part link is evidenced.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The direction differs between the two body-links identified in T2.6. For the weeping/clothes-tearing link (2Ki22:19; 2Ch34:27): the direction is *soul → body* — the inner act of humbling produces the bodily expression. God confirms he heard the inner act, not the bodily expression per se (though the bodily expression is the sign God cites — "you have torn your clothes and wept before me"). For the Phili3:21 "lowly body": the direction is ambiguous — the body's creaturely condition (M09-B experienced lowliness) is not produced by the inner disposition but is a given condition of creaturely existence. In this instance the direction is more complex: the body's state *shapes* the inner experience of lowliness (body → soul) rather than the soul expressing through the body.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The two characteristics with body links (CHAR-1 and CHAR-2) both evidence *bidirectional* body-soul relationships, but with different emphases. CHAR-1: the M09-A voluntary register is soul→body (inner humbling produces bodily weeping — expressive direction); the M09-B imposed register is body→soul (the bodily condition of creaturely lowliness shapes the inner experience — formative direction). CHAR-2: the competition direction is body→soul (bodily passions pull on the will — Rom6:12); the expression direction is soul→body (heart-submission expresses through bodily service — Eph6:5). Cluster-level: both characteristics evidence the same bidirectionality, which confirms M09's account of the person as constitutively embodied — the characteristics are not purely inner-being states but engage the whole embodied person. The soul-to-body direction (expressive) and body-to-soul direction (formative/competitive) together map the characteristic's full constitutional engagement.
