**[CHAR-1]** E — The directional evidence is primarily *soul/will → body* for the speech-mode sinning: the inner sinful impulse (from will or heart) seeks expression through the mouth/tongue. Psa 39:1 — the will resolves to guard the tongue, implying the inner impulse would otherwise express outward. Ecc 5:6 — the mouth "leads" the person into sin, suggesting a body → soul feedback loop: undisciplined speech generates liability that then implicates the inner person's standing before God. 1Cor 6:18 shows bidirectionality: the sinful act is performed through the body (soul → body) but the damage returns to the body (body receives the consequence). The dominant direction is inner-to-outer for the commission of sinning, but the feedback (consequence returning to the person) runs outer-to-inner.

**[CHAR-10]** E — The direction for enticement's body-link runs *outer-to-inner and inner-to-outer simultaneously*. 2Pe 2:14 — "eyes full of adultery" — the outer visual world (the object of adulterous desire) enters through the eyes (outer-to-inner). But the eyes are "full of adultery" — the inner desire-state shapes what the eyes see and seek (inner-to-outer). The direction is bidirectional: desire shapes what the eyes seek; the eyes deliver what desire seeks. The body (eyes) is both receptor and projector of the enticement mechanism.

**[CHAR-11]** E — The direction is bidirectional. (1) *Outer-to-inner*: the condition uses the body's members to drive the person's inner states — Rom 6:12 — "let not sin reign in your mortal body, to make you obey its passions" — bodily passions exert pressure on the will's inner obedience; (2) *Inner-to-outer*: the condition within the person expresses itself through the body's members — Rom 6:13 — "present your members to sin as instruments" — the members are deployed by the inner condition as its external instruments. The direction is thus circular: inner condition → bodily expression → reinforced inner condition.
**[CHAR-12]** S — No body-part link is evidenced (T2.6.3). This prompt is not applicable.

**[CHAR-13]** E — The direction is bidirectional. (1) *Body-outward generating the record*: the hands making idols (Isa 31:7), the mouth producing sinful speech (Psa 59:12) — body-to-record direction; the body's acts create entries in the divine record. (2) *Record-inward affecting the body*: Psa 38:3 — "no health in my bones because of my sin" — the record's weight produces physical deterioration; the divine record (held before God) produces bodily consequences. The direction thus flows both ways: body-acts → record-entry → physical-consequences → body-deterioration.

**[CHAR-14]** E — Bidirectional. (1) *Inner-to-outer (seeking)*: the inner recognition of sin and the volitional movement toward God (inner) is expressed through the outer bodily act of hand-laying (2Ch 29:23) — the seeking moves from inner to outer; (2) *Outer-to-inner (receiving)*: the outer historical event of Christ's blood being poured out (Mat 26:28 — outer) produces the inner forgiveness (the trespasses cancelled — Eph 1:7; Col 2:13 — inner). The characteristic thus moves bidirectionally: inner → outer in seeking; outer → inner in receiving.
**[CHAR-15]** S — No body-part link is evidenced (T2.6.3). This prompt is not applicable.

**[CHAR-16]** E — Bidirectional. (1) *Inner-to-outer*: the inner sinner-character (heart — Jam 4:8) produces outer sinful conduct through the hands; the inner moral identity is expressed through bodily action; (2) *Outer-to-inner*: Luk 18:13 — the outer bodily act of beating the breast is the physical expression of the inner conscience's verdict about the sinner-identity; the body enacts what the conscience has registered. The direction is thus bidirectional: inner character → outer bodily conduct; outer bodily self-abasement ← inner conscience's assessment.

**[CHAR-17]** E — Bidirectional. (1) *Inner guilt → outer bodily expression*: Ezr 9:6 — the inner shame of guilt produces the outer bodily posture of downcast face; the inner condition is expressed through the body; (2) *Bodily location → guilt-borne*: Exo 28:38 — the guilt of Israel's holy offerings is borne specifically on Aaron's forehead; the guilt is located at the body-part as its point of representation; (3) *Body-part as guilt-site → divine removal*: Isa 6:7 — the guilt located at Isaiah's lips is removed by the coal touching that specific body-part; the removal addresses the guilt at its specific body-location.

**[CHAR-18]** E — Bidirectional. (1) *Inner crime → outer bodily enactment*: Eze 14:3 — heart-seated idolatry → Isa 59:3 — fingers with iniquity — the inner moral crime expresses through the body's active members; (2) *Outer bodily decay ← inner crime*: Psa 31:10 — "my strength fails because of my iniquity, and my bones waste away" — the inner iniquity produces outward bodily deterioration; Eze 32:27 — "iniquities upon their bones" — the inner crime attaches as a permanent bodily mark; (3) *Bodily burden image for inner weight*: Psa 38:4 — "gone over my head; like a heavy burden" — the body's carrying experience images the inner weight of accumulated iniquity.

**[CHAR-19]** E — Bidirectional. (1) *Inner heart → outer lips*: Psa 36:1 — transgression speaks deep in the heart → Isa 59:13 — "uttering from the heart lying words" — the inner transgression produces the outer speech-act through the lips; (2) *Outer transgressions → bodily burden*: Lam 1:14 — "my transgressions were bound into a yoke... set upon my neck" — the accumulated outer transgressions return as a physical-weight burden on the body; (3) *Sustained inner revolt → whole-body incapacitation*: Isa 1:5 — continued inner rebellion → "whole head is sick, whole heart faint" — the inner volitional revolt produces bodily systemic deterioration.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The body-link in VCG-02 runs in the *outer-to-outer* direction: the priest's body (finger, hands) acts upon the altar/sanctuary (external object). This is not a soul-expressing-through-body direction (as in CHAR-1's speech-mode sinning) but a body-as-instrument-of-remedy direction. For VCG-01's personal-moral register, the body direction evidence is minimal — eating with blood (1Sa 14:33/34) shows the body (mouth, eating) as the instrument of the inadvertent violation, running in the body-engaging-soul direction (the eating triggers a cultic violation whose moral reality the person did not register).

**[CHAR-20]** E — Bidirectional. (1) *Inner faithlessness → outer bodily posture*: the heart's turning away from God (inner) produces the turning of the face and back (outer bodily expression — 2Ch 29:6); the inner disposition expresses through the body's directional posture; (2) *Inner faithlessness → bodily curse*: the inner act of marital faithlessness (Num 5:27) produces the bodily curse entering the womb; the inner betrayal produces the outward bodily consequence; (3) *Outer bodily posture → inner assessment of faithlessness*: 2Ch 29:6's "turned their backs" is also the observable sign by which the faithlessness is assessed — the outer posture is both expressive of and diagnostic for the inner condition.

**[CHAR-21]** E — Bidirectional. (1) *Inner perversity → outer bodily expression*: Pro 6:14 — perverted heart → devises evil sown outward; Pro 23:33 — perverted heart → mouth utters perverse things; Pro 16:30 — inner plot → winking eye signal; (2) *Outer bodily influence → inner corruption*: Exo 23:8 — bribe (outer material) → blinds the eyes (outer faculty) → subverts inner judgment-discernment; 1Cor 15:33 — "bad company ruins good morals" — external social influence corrupts inner moral character; (3) *Inner corruption → bodily deterioration*: Psa 38:6 — inner sin producing the bowed, prostrate body; 2Cor 4:16 — "outer self is wasting away" — the bodily decay as consequence of the fallen inner condition.

**[CHAR-22]** E — Primarily *inner-to-outer*. Psa 58:2 — "in your hearts you devise wrongs; your hands deal out violence" — the explicit sequence is heart → hands; the inner devising produces the outer enacting. Isa 59:3 — "your hands are defiled... your tongue mutters wickedness" — the defilement of hands and tongue is the outward expression of the inner moral corruption. The will's restraint (Eze 18:8 — "withholds his hand") confirms the inner-to-outer direction: the will governs what the hand does. No verse clearly evidences the reverse direction (body-to-inner-corruption) for CHAR-22.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The direction is *inner-to-outer*: conscience and will (inner) express through the mouth (outer body). 2Sa 24:10 — heart struck (inner) → "David said to the Lord" (outer). Luk 15:18/21 — inner resolution ("I will say to him") → enacted speech ("and the son said"). The inner movement is prior and produces the outer speech. The reverse feedback direction is also present: Job 33:27 — the restored man who "sings before men and says 'I sinned'" — the public speaking of confession reinforces the inner moral understanding and positions the person in a social-moral reality shaped by the named truth.

**[CHAR-4]** E — In Jer 2:35, the direction runs *inner-to-outer*: the inner suppression/denial drives the spoken claim outward through the mouth. But the reinforcement loop also runs *outer-to-inner*: the spoken claim, once established, shapes the inner self-understanding and deepens the suppression. The characteristic thus uses the mouth as a bidirectional amplifier: the inner denial externalises through speech, and the external speech further entrenches the inner denial.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The body-part link in Neh 9:29 runs *inner-to-outer*: the inner volitional refusal to submit expresses outward as the physical gestures of stubbornness (stiff neck, stubborn shoulder). The metaphors describe the outward embodiment of the inner will. The reverse feedback direction is also implied: the habituation of the bodily posture of resistance (consistently giving the stubborn shoulder, consistently stiffening the neck) consolidates the inner disposition — the outer gesture-pattern of refusal shapes and deepens the inner refusal over time.
**[CHAR-6]** S — No body-part link is evidenced (T2.6.3). This prompt is not applicable.
**[CHAR-7]** S — No body-part link is evidenced (T2.6.3). This prompt is not applicable.
**[CHAR-8]** S — No body-part link is evidenced (T2.6.3). This prompt is not applicable.

**[CHAR-9]** E — The direction runs *inner-to-outer*: heart (inner) → will (consent) → mouth (body-outer). Mat 15:19 — "out of the heart come... slander" — the direction is explicitly from inner origin through the body. The reverse feedback is also evidenced: Col 3:8's renunciation command addresses the mouth as the externalisation point because stopping sinful speech at the mouth can also address the inner condition — the command to silence the mouth is part of the inner transformation process.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The direction is consistently from soul outward to body: the inner orientation of wickedness (soul, heart, will) expresses itself through the body's instruments (mouth, arm, eyes). Pro 12:6 ("the words of the wicked lie in wait for blood") evidences the soul-to-mouth directionality — the inner lethal intent flows outward through speech. Psa 36:1 (VCG-02) supports this: the transgression-voice operates "deep in his heart" first, then surfaces in the person's outward conduct and absence of fear. The body does not generate wickedness — it enacts and reveals it. There is one partial exception: Pro 5:22 ("ensnared by the cords of his sin") suggests a feedback loop — the wickedness the body enacts (acts of sin) generates constraints that deepen the inner condition. But this is a consequence-loop, not a primary body-to-soul causation.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The direction runs consistently from the inner constitutional condition outward to the body's expressive instruments. Mat 12:34 (vc=14419 — VCG-03): the heart's abundance flows to the mouth — inner to outer. Mat 6:23 (vc=14458 — VCG-03): the bad eye floods the "whole body" — a secondary inner-to-outer direction (the eye as the inner-perceptive faculty expressing outward through the body's illumination). Rom 6:13 (vc=14340 — VCG-06): the body's members become instruments for the unrighteousness — the inner condition uses the body as its channel outward. The constitutional evil (inner) → body members (outer) direction is entirely consistent across the corpus. There is no evidence of a body-feeding-back-to-soul direction in this corpus.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The direction is consistently from inner constitutional condition outward to the body's expressive and receptive instruments. The lying lips (Pro 12:22 — VCG-02) express an inner character of deception — the inner condition flows to the lips. Wisdom's lips that find wickedness abominable (Pro 8:7 — VCG-02) express an inner moral faculty of revulsion outward through speech. The ear turned from the law (Pro 28:9 — VCG-03) is the volitional inner act of rejection expressed through the body's receptive faculty — but here a nuance: the ear's turning away from the law also functions as the mechanism through which the inner person is closed to divine instruction, so there is a secondary body-to-inner feedback: deliberate ear-closing reinforces the inner closure. The face-turning of Eze 14:6 (VCG-04) is directional — the face expresses the inner orientation's direction and is also the commanded instrument of volitional redirection.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The direction is bidirectional but with the primary flow from inner to outer. Primary inner-to-outer: the inner attachment of heart and soul to idols → the eyes feast on them → the hands craft them → they are installed in sacred space. The inner devotional commitment expresses itself through the body's perceptive (eyes), productive (hands), and locative (installation) acts. Secondary outer-to-inner (feedback): the sustained feeding of the eyes on the idolatrous objects reinforces and deepens the inner attachment — Eze 20:8 (vc=65911 — VCG-05): "none of them cast away the detestable things their eyes feasted on" — the sustained visual-desire habit reinforces the inner attachment. The body-characteristic link runs in both directions here: inner desire → bodily feasting → reinforced inner desire, creating a self-perpetuating loop.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The primary direction is inner-to-outer: the inner scheming (heart-mind devising) → expressive through body parts (hand enacting, feet running, tongue deploying). Mic 2:1 (vc=38217 — VCG-02): "devise wickedness on their beds; when the morning dawns, they perform it" — the inner nocturnal devising flows outward through bodily enactment at dawn. Isa 59:7 (vc=38203 — VCG-02): "thoughts are thoughts of iniquity" → "feet run to evil" — the cognitive inner state directly drives the bodily directional movement. Pro 6:18 (vc=38224 — VCG-02): "heart devises wicked plans" → "feet make haste to run to evil" — same inner-to-outer sequence. Secondary feedback (outer-to-inner): Pro 19:28 (vc=38220 — VCG-03): "the mouth of the wicked devours iniquity" — the bodily act of devouring iniquity through speech feeds back into the inner appetite, reinforcing it.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The direction runs primarily inner-to-outer: inner will-wickedness → volitional choice to open the mouth → speech-act through the mouth → social/relational impact. Rev 13:6 (vc=14356 — VCG-01): the beast's mouth utters what originates in the inner orientation of defiant contempt. Rev 16:9 (vc=14352 — VCG-01): the inner will that refuses to repent finds expression through the cursing speech act. The sequence is consistently inner-to-outer. There is also a possible feedback dimension: the act of cursing God's name under judgment (Rev 16:9/11/21 — VCG-01) does not reduce but deepens the will's defiance — the very act of expressing blasphemy through the mouth appears to reinforce and deepen the inner hardened state rather than relieving it.

**[CLUSTER]** E — All six characteristics show inner-to-outer as the primary direction: inner will-state/moral condition → bodily expression (speech, eyes, hands, feet). This is the cluster's universal body-directionality. The secondary outer-to-inner feedback dimension appears specifically in Chars 4 (visual-desire loop) and 5 (mouth devouring iniquity reinforces inner appetite) — and arguably in Char 6 (blasphemy under judgment deepens the will's hardening). The cluster-level pattern: inner-to-outer primary, with Chars 4, 5, and 6 showing secondary feedback loops that make the body-expression self-reinforcing for its respective inner evil-form.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Primarily the body feeds to the soul. The defilement-state originates in a bodily event (carcass-contact, discharge, skin condition) and feeds back into the inner person as a condition affecting conscience, will, affect, and social standing. Lev 5:2-3 (M10c-A-VCG-01): the bodily contact creates the condition that the conscience then recognises. Lev 15:2 (M10c-A-VCG-06): the bodily discharge is the source of the unclean state that governs the person's relational and ritual standing. In M10c-B, the direction is more complex: the bodily condition (skin disease) is assessed by the priest, whose speech act then constitutes the social reality of the unclean status — so body → priestly assessment → performative speech → social condition. But also a soul-to-body direction in VCG-04: Lev 11:43-44 (M10c-A-VCG-04) — the will's refusal of defiling contact is the inner act that prevents the bodily acquisition of the state; the soul's volitional choice governs what the body does, preventing the body-to-soul contamination chain. Both directions are evidenced, with body-to-soul dominant.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Primarily soul-to-body, though with a bidirectional component. The soul's desires and will-failure are the originating force: Rom 1:24 (VCG-02) — "lusts of their hearts" leads to "dishonoring of their bodies" — the soul-level disorder (desire) produces the bodily consequence (dishonour). This is soul-to-body direction. However, at 2Cor 7:1 (VCG-03), the defilement is named as inhabiting both body and spirit simultaneously — suggesting that the body is not merely a passive recipient but a co-site of the condition; the direction is bidirectional in that the defilement inhabits both simultaneously and the cleansing must address both.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Primarily soul-to-body in consequence. The soul's covenantal betrayal (the will's volitional unfaithfulness — Num 5:20: "if you have defiled yourself... having lain with another man") produces a judgment received in the body (Num 5:27 — womb and thigh affected). The directional sequence is: volitional-covenantal betrayal (soul level) → defilement-state incurred (condition) → judicial consequence in body (body level). There is also a body-to-community movement: Eze 36:17 (VCG-04): "their ways before me were like the uncleanness of a woman in her menstrual impurity" — the bodily-impurity register (nid.dah) is the metaphor for the community's moral uncleanness, suggesting the body's impurity state provides the framework through which the corporate moral condition is understood (body informs the characterisation of the corporate soul-condition).

**[CHAR-4]** E — The direction runs from the external spirit through the person's spirit-level to the body: external unclean spirit → spirit-level invasion → soul-will domination → body as instrument (convulsed, driven, voice appropriated). There is no reverse direction — the body does not feed back to the spirit or produce the characteristic from below. The domination is entirely top-down.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The four directional profiles reveal the cluster's most analytically significant constitutional finding. Characteristic 1: primarily body-to-soul (bodily event → condition → conscience/affect/will); with a reverse direction evidenced at Lev 11:43-44 (soul's volitional choice → governs what the body contacts). Characteristic 2: primarily soul-to-body (soul's desire-disorder → bodily dishonour — Rom 1:24); bidirectional at 2Cor 7:1 (defilement inhabiting both body and spirit simultaneously). Characteristic 3: primarily soul-to-body in consequence (covenantal volitional betrayal → judicial consequence in body — Num 5:27); body metaphor to community (nid.dah as metaphor for corporate moral uncleanness — Eze 36:17). Characteristic 4: exclusively top-down from external spirit through spirit-level to soul-level to body (external spirit → spirit-level invasion → soul-will overridden → body convulsed). Cluster pattern: the direction reverses as the characteristics are compared. Characteristic 1 moves body-to-soul (embodied creaturely vulnerability as origin). Characteristic 2 moves soul-to-body (inner moral disorder as origin). Characteristic 3 moves soul-to-body-and-environment (corporate inner defection as origin). Characteristic 4 moves spirit-to-soul-to-body (external spiritual agent as origin). The four directional profiles together map the full constitutional range of the defilement domain.

findings.session_b_note:
The bidirectionality of the body-soul relationship in forgiveness has not been named as an observation in the existing analysis. Its consequence:

Forgiveness is not a purely "upward" inner-being phenomenon (soul generating, body merely expressing). The body participates in the formation of the forgiving act — the gut-level compassion (splagchnizomai) is named as the felt origin of the master's decision to forgive in Mat 18:27. This suggests that the body's affective-somatic responses (compassion, visceral response to the other's condition) are not incidental but structurally connected to the capacity and act of forgiving.

*New finding:* The body's feedback role in generating the compassion that enables forgiveness is a datum not assembled in existing observations. This may be relevant for Session D's treatment of the forgiveness-compassion relationship (DIM-064-SD002 already flags compassion as a precondition — the splagchnizomai evidence grounds this at the somatic level).

findings.session_b_note:
The bidirectionality has a significant consequence: compassion is not adequately described either as a purely interior soul-quality that incidentally uses the body as its vehicle, nor as a purely somatic reflex. It is a genuinely soul-body integrated phenomenon in which the body is both the originating ground (RACHAM etymology) and the expressive medium (splanchnizō movement) and the participatory instrument (sumpatheō — suffering with).

This means that the programme's sb_classification of **Soul-body interface** is precisely right for compassion — not merely as a category assignment but as a description of the characteristic's constitutional operation. Compassion lives at the interface in both directions simultaneously. The person who is compassionate is someone whose soul and body are integrated in their response to the suffering other: they feel it in their gut, they are moved from the inside, and that inner-bodily movement produces action.

An important implication: compassion cannot be fully present as a purely cognitive determination (a decision to act compassionately without the somatic component). The vocabulary insists on the body's participation. A compassion that bypasses the gut is, in the terms of this vocabulary, not the full phenomenon.

findings.session_b_note: The bidirectionality reveals that contrition is a **whole-person phenomenon** — it does not remain at the inner constitutional levels but integrates with the body in multiple ways. The body expresses contrition (groaning, trembling at Isa 66:2), images contrition (broken bones), and is the site of the reviving that follows contrition (the bones that are invited to rejoice). Contrition is therefore not merely an interior psychological state but one that implicates the embodied person — their voice, their structural physical integrity, their somatic expression.

findings.session_b_note:
The bidirectional body-engagement reveals that fellowship is not a purely inner phenomenon that occasionally finds somatic expression. In the wound-fellowship groups, the somatic and the inner-being are genuinely entangled: the physical wound is not a metaphor for inner purification — it *is* the mechanism (Pro 20:30). The inner healing is not a metaphor for physical recovery — it is the reality the physical wound produces (Isa 53:5). The fellowship of sufferings is not merely a spiritual orientation — it is entered through somatic experience (Phili 3:10).

This means that fellowship at the deepest register (suffering-transformation-resurrection) cannot be fully understood as a purely inner-being phenomenon. Its constitutional movement is genuinely somatic-to-inner and inner-to-somatic.

findings.session_b_note: If the direction runs soul → body (inner well-being produces gladness visible in comportment, as in Est 5:9), the consequence is that goodness is a deep inner quality that naturally expresses itself outwardly — it cannot be purely internal without visible expression. But the Haman diagnostic also confirms that the outward expression of gladness (tov-lev) can be present without genuine inner goodness-rootedness. This distinction is analytically significant: visible gladness and genuine goodness are not identical, and the body's expression of well-being can be present even in the absence of its genuine source. The directional consequence is that inner goodness properly produces outward expression but outward expression does not guarantee inner goodness. (OBS-067-OBS-040, OBS-067-OBS-041)

The conscience recognises the moral wrongness of hate-in-the-heart (Lev 19:17, OBS-103-114); love is what the conscience directs the person toward as the alternative. If conscience is the inner moral monitor, love is the inner moral orientation — the conscience identifies what violates love; love provides the positive orientation the conscience is protecting. Gap: this relationship is inferred, not directly evidenced in R103's anchor verses.

findings.finding_value: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level (chesed as covenantal-soul character), heart-level (Hos 11:8 — "my heart recoils"), and somatic-level (re.chem, splanchnon) are all richly evidenced. The constitutional architecture is bottom-up: the womb and entrails are the originating ground; the soul and heart are the engagement points; the act is the constitutional expression. Four body-part functions are identified: constitutive (womb — the generative image of compassion), expressive (gut — the felt movement), indicative (Synoptic pattern — splanchnizō signals the compassion-event), and mediating (heart in Hos 11:8 — the deliberative locus where compassion and judgment contend). The four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) is uniquely evidenced in this registry — consistently inside-out and bottom-up. T2.8 established no body deposit; T5.7 is formally closed. The constitutional portrait confirms the sb_classification (soul-body interface) and extends it: compassion is the most somatically grounded characteristic in the programme, with its originating logic residing in the body's deepest interior.

The somatic-body level (T2.6 — gut, womb) is carried by the RACHAM/SPLANCHN root families — the body's interior as the etymological ground of both. The soul-character level (T2.2) is carried by the CHASAD family — chesed as the settled covenantal character disposition. The heart-deliberative level (T2.3) is evidenced most richly in Hos 11:8 (T7's primary anchor for divine compassion). T7's vocabulary arc (womb to almsgiving) traverses exactly the constitutional range T2 maps: from the most interior somatic level (womb) through the character-soul level to the externalised action level. The dual primary anchor (T7) maps onto T2's constitutional depth: Hos 11:8 evidences constitutional depth (heart-level deliberation of compassion over judgment); Luke 10:33 evidences constitutional breadth (the full four-stage movement from sight to action).

findings.finding_value: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary point of reception (Zec 12:10 — spirit of grace poured out), not the point of generation (grace originates with God — T2.9). The soul level is the site of standing (Rom 5:2 — "this grace in which we stand") and identity (1Cor 15:10 — "by the grace of God I am what I am"). The constitutional movement follows the SD021 four-faces model: divine disposition received at spirit level → relational standing established at soul level → specific capacity gifted → character expressed outward. Heart-location is partially evidenced via eusplanchnos (Eph 4:32 — the tenderheartedness that grace produces, reaching the affective-somatic interface). T2.7 produces a new finding: grace operates bidirectionally through the body-soul interface — soul-to-body (inner posture enacted somatically in prostration, fasting, sackcloth) and body-to-soul (somatic enactment deepening and confirming the inner posture). T2.8 remains open (body deposit question unresolved); T5.7 is left open accordingly. The constitutional origin analysis (T2.9) is the most analytically significant T2 finding: grace does not originate in the human constitutional system at any level — it arrives from outside. This is confirmed at T6 as the structural uniqueness of grace: the only characteristic that is not produced by any other inner-being characteristic.

findings.finding_value: T1's four-kind structure (disposition, standing, capacity, character quality) maps onto T2's constitutional levels. The divine-disposition kind operates at the level of grace's origin (T2.9 — God's own disposition; not a human constitutional level). The standing kind operates at the soul level (T2.2 — Rom 5:2 "this grace in which we stand"). The capacity kind operates at the spirit-soul interface — the specific enabling for specific tasks (2Cor 12:9) is received at the deepest level and expressed through specific faculties. The character-quality kind operates at the soul-to-body level (T2.7 — gracious conduct and speech expressing the received inner character outward). T1's constitutional movement finding (SD021 four-faces sequence) is the longitudinal form of T2's spatial map: T2 identifies the constitutional levels; T1 identifies the movement between them.

findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional movement (spirit reception → soul standing → capacity → character expression) maps onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The spirit-reception stage (T2.1) corresponds to T3.1 (perception — grace enabling the inner sight and hearing that receives it). The soul-standing stage (T2.2) corresponds to T3.9 (conscience — grace as the condition within which conscience can operate without destruction) and T3.8 (moral evaluation — the standing produces the clarity of moral self-assessment). The capacity-gifting stage (T2.1 — spirit level) corresponds to T3.7 (agency — capacity given constitutes agency for the task). The character-expression stage (T2.7 — outward through body-soul) corresponds to T3.10 (conscientiousness — the integrated moral-action expression of received grace-character). T2 maps the constitutional space; T3 maps the faculties active at each spatial level; the two tiers describe the same movement from orthogonal perspectives.

findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional movement (SD021 sequence: disposition → standing → capacity → character) and T5's five formation mechanisms describe the same formation arc from spatial and temporal perspectives. T2 identifies the constitutional levels through which grace moves; T5 identifies the mechanisms by which grace moves through each level in different contexts. The encounter mechanism (T5 — sudden specific relational event) produces the spirit-level reception (T2.1 — the initial point of arrival). The word mechanism (T5 — Act 20:32 — grace through proclaimed word) produces the soul-standing establishment (T2.2 — the word's sustained effect on the person's constitutive condition). The mediated-transformation mechanism (T5 — tenderheartedness → forgiving — Eph 4:32, SD030) corresponds to T2.7's bidirectional body-soul finding: the inner transformation mediates outward through the body-soul interface. T2.8's open question (body deposit) and T5.7's open status are formally aligned — both pending further investigation.

findings.session_b_note: The bidirectional blood-covenant relationship reveals that covenant is not merely inner and invisible — it moves through the body and back again, using physical substance as its medium. The consequence: covenant is constitutionally somatic in its enacted form; it cannot be reduced to a purely internal or invisible inner-being reality. The body participates in covenant both as the site of covenant's expression (sacrifice, circumcision, spoken oath) and as the medium through which covenant is constituted and marked. This has implications for understanding the new covenant's sacramental forms (Eucharist, baptism): both are bodily acts that carry covenant significance — they are not merely symbolic but participate in the covenant's constituting and marking logic that runs through the body. The body is not external to covenant but is the medium through which covenant is enacted, marked, and sustained in time.

findings.session_b_note: The primary direction (inner → body) establishes peace as a genuinely somatic characteristic — its absence or presence registers in the body because the body is the outward expression of the inner state. This has two consequences: (1) Peace cannot be fully present in the inner person while the body is in somatic distress caused by inner disorder — the body is a truth-telling indicator of the inner condition (Psa 38:3, 32:3); a person who claims inner peace while their body deteriorates under the weight of unconfessed sin is in the false-shalom pattern; (2) The redemptive reversal (Isa 53:5 body → inner) is extraordinary precisely because it runs against the normal causal direction: normally inner disorder produces somatic deterioration; in the Servant's case, somatic suffering produces inner healing in others. The directionality finding deepens the T1 paradox (Q&A-023): peace comes through its opposite conditions not only experientially but physically.

findings.finding_value: T2 maps where peace is located; T5 maps how it is formed there. The body's somatic evidence (T2.6/7) connects directly to T5's suffering-and-discipline findings: the bones wasting (Psa 32:3) is the T5 suffering-as-formation pathway reversed — where sustained peace-withholding produces deterioration, the discipline of Heb 12:11 produces peace-in-body over time. The constitutional movement patterns (T2.10) are the spatial description of what T5 describes temporally: the cascading gift pattern (God → spirit → soul/mind → body) is the sequence by which peace is received and formed over time (T5.2) through the mechanisms of divine word, Spirit, and discipline (T5.3).

findings.session_b_note: The inner-to-body directionality (Isa 50:6) confirms that human self-giving in this registry is fundamentally an inner-being act that finds somatic expression — not a somatic act that generates an inner experience. This has a significant consequence: the body's suffering in Isa 50:6 (back struck, beard pulled, face spat upon) is not the source of the faithfulness but its evidence. The inner act of giving precedes and determines the somatic form. This prevents a reading in which bodily endurance is itself the virtue — the virtue is the inner orientation that produces the bodily self-offering. For the programme's spirit-soul-body mapping: the characteristic has inner-to-body directionality in its human expression, confirming its location in the inner-being register while showing somatic expression.

The body is the expression vehicle, not the origin. This is significant for understanding M01-A: reverential fear is not caused by physiological arousal (the science extract's amygdala-model) but by the person's inner recognition of God's reality. The direction is spirit/soul → body, not stimulus → body → emotion.

The soul-to-body direction for theophanic trembling and dismay confirms that these are inner events that produce somatic consequences, not somatic events that produce inner experiences. However, the feedback loop (body → soul) may be evidenced in the persistence of the condition: once trembling begins, it may intensify the inner experience. This is the somatic marker dynamic the science extract identifies.

The directionality is significant: M01 consistently describes fear as originating in the inner person's engagement with a reality (God, threat, terrible news) and expressing through the body. This distinguishes Scripture's fear-vocabulary from a purely physiological account (stimulus → body → emotion) and from a purely cognitive account (appraisal → emotion). The biblical account integrates both dimensions within a soul-body unity in which the inner person's engagement with reality produces both inner experience and somatic expression simultaneously.

The consistent soul-to-body direction for the face-link means that anger is fundamentally an inner event that cannot be concealed — it inscribes itself on the body involuntarily. This makes anger a constitutionally revealing characteristic: its presence discloses the moral state of the inner person to observers.

The possible body feedback in Pro 14:30 (envy rotting bones) means that sustained covetous jealousy deposits itself in the body, which then contributes to the degradation of the whole person. This is both a moral and a somatic consequence — the inner state damages the body, and the damaged body may reinforce the damaged inner state.

The primarily inner-to-outer direction means that the body's grief expressions (tears, groaning, sighing) are properly read as evidence and extension of genuine inner grief rather than as the grief itself. God hearing the sound of weeping (Psa 6:8 — M03-A-VCG-04) shows that the somatic expression reaches God; it is not inner grief that God hears but its outward overflow. This confirms that the somatic expressions are real and communicative — they are not symptoms to be suppressed but appropriate completions of the inner state. The body participates in the whole-person event of grief.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The soul-to-body direction shows exultation as fundamentally an inner-originating characteristic that overflows into the body and voice. The body does not produce the inner state but receives and expresses it. This means exultation cannot be manufactured from the outside — it must originate in the soul/heart's genuine orientation before it reaches the body and voice. The commanded exultations (Psa 32:11; Zec 9:9) work by addressing the will and heart, not by commanding the body.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The bidirectionality reveals that Joy is both a spontaneous inner state that seeks outward expression and a cultivated inner state that can be formed through prescribed outer practices (feasts, singing, dancing, communal eating). This is why Deuteronomy commands the feast-joy — the commanded outer form of rejoicing before God is itself a means of producing and sustaining the inner state. The implication for formation: Joy can be cultivated through embodied communal practices, not only through direct divine encounter or inner resolve. The outer-to-inner direction is the wisdom of the feast commandments.

**[CHAR-7]** E — The inner-to-outer direction confirms that Suffering-Joy cannot be manufactured by external performance — the person who forces a smile (attempting ba.lag) without the inner Spirit-work merely performs what is not present. The genuine form requires the inner-being production (Spirit-level) before the tongue and face can genuinely express it. This is the key distinction between genuine Suffering-Joy (agalliao — inner Spirit-produced, expressed outwardly) and mere cheerfulness-performance (attempted ba.lag that may fail).

**[CHAR-3]** E — The inner-to-outer direction confirms that Gladness is an inner-originating state that expresses itself in and through the body, not a bodily state that generates inner gladness. This is significant: the body's refreshment is evidence of inner gladness, not its cause. Genuine gladness must first be received inwardly (cognitively through evaluation, affectively through response) before it reaches the body.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The bidirectional link reveals Delight as fully embodied — it does not remain confined to the inner being but seeks expression through the body and can be reinforced through bodily acts. The ni.cho.ach aroma direction is particularly significant: it shows that the outer form of worship (correctly offered sacrifice) is not indifferent to the inner state but serves as the embodied expression and reinforcement of the inner orientation of Delight. This explains why misdirected ni.cho.ach (M04-P-VCG-01 — Eze 20:28) is so severe: the outer act reinforces and expresses the inner misdirection.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The bidirectional body-link reveals Pleasure as a constitutionally integrative characteristic: it is both received through bodily senses and communicated outward to bodily health. Unlike characteristics that are purely inner-being (no body link) or purely body-triggered (no inner-being consequence), Pleasure is simultaneously sensory-received and soul-expressed, body-triggered and body-healing. This bidirectionality makes Pleasure the most fully embodied positive inner-being characteristic in M04.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The external-to-inner-to-outward direction reveals Wonder as inherently relational in its full expression: it is not self-contained but moves from encounter (external) through inner astonishment to communal proclamation (outward). The person who genuinely wonders cannot simply keep it internal — it moves through the mouth into declaration. This also explains why Wonder's failure (Neh 9:17 — "not mindful") is both an inner failure (not registering) and a communal failure (not declaring to others).

**[CLUSTER]** E — Two cluster-level consequences: (1) **The outer-to-inner direction of Joy (Char 2) has formative implications** — it explains the wisdom of the Deuteronomic feast commandments. The feast is not merely the expression of pre-existing joy but a prescribed formation practice that produces and sustains the inner state. The body eating, drinking, and festively gathering before God produces the inner state of joyfulness. This is the cluster's most direct evidence that embodied communal practice forms inner-being states — the feast is formation; (2) **Wonder's three-stage pattern is the most complete** — the only characteristic where the full perceptive-inner-proclamatory sequence is so consistently documented. This confirms Wonder as the cluster's most thoroughly integrative characteristic in terms of constitutional movement: it begins in the outer world (God's acts), passes through the body (eyes/ears), reaches the inner being (cognitive arrest), and returns to the outer world (mouth/proclamation). No other M04 characteristic moves through this complete arc as consistently.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The primarily inner → body direction confirms that CHAR-1 is first an inner phenomenon whose bodily expression is the consequence, not the cause. This distinguishes shame from purely social performances of shame (which would be body → inner). However, the bidirectionality in the M07-C mode (bodily posture mediating the relational stance before God) reveals that shame is not merely private — it finds its completion in a relational posture. The person who bears shame before God completes the experience in the downward posture of the face not lifted; the person who trusts God completes their trust in the radiant face that looks toward him. Body and inner state constitute the whole shame-experience.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Bidirectional. External to body to inner: military defeat strips armour and forces retreat; social community strips the beard; divine act removes crown — the outer act produces inner collapse. Inner to body: haughty eyes (inner pride-disposition) are specifically targeted and brought low.

---

**[CHAR-3]** E — Inner to body: the inner disposition of disrespect toward divinely ordered authority is expressed through the bodily act (the covered or uncovered head). The body is the medium through which the inner worth-denial is communicated to the relational community.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — In VCG-02, the direction is inner to body: disordered inner desire (dishonorable passions, Rom 1:26) produces the shameful bodily acts (Rom 1:27). The body enacts the inner disorder. In VCG-01's hair register (1Cor 11:6), the body-sign is both indicative of inner moral propriety and constitutive of the social-moral statement.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — In VCG-02, the direction is outer to inner: the physical blow and shameful treatment produce the inner experience of CHAR-5 in the person being treated. In Mar 10:50, the direction is inner to body: the decision to abandon the shame-identity is expressed through the bodily act of throwing off the cloak.

---

**[CHAR-6]** E — The direction is inner to body to relational: heart-integrity (inner) -> hand-cleanness (body) -> approach to God's altar (relational). The hands express and enact the inner moral condition; the relational access to God is the outcome of the inner-to-body expression. This is a consistently inner-to-outer direction: CHAR-6 originates in the heart and expresses through the hands toward the relational encounter with God.

---

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's body-characteristic link is bidirectional, following the same inner-outer pattern identified at T2.10. Inner to body is the primary direction for expressive characteristics (Chars 1, 4, 6) — the inner condition expresses through the body. Body/outer to inner is the primary direction for received characteristics (Chars 2, 3, 5) — the external event produces the inner condition through the body. The body is therefore both the site of shame's expression and the site of its reception, mediating the inner-outer exchange in both directions. This bidirectionality confirms that the shame-field is a whole-person phenomenon operating across the body-soul interface.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — The soul-to-body directionality has two consequences. First, CHAR-1's origin and constitutional seat are interior — in the heart, spirit, and thought-life — and addressing it requires engaging that interior rather than merely correcting bodily expression. Correcting the haughty eyes (pro 6:17, vc=34247) without addressing the heart's elevation would reach only the symptom. Pro 16:5 (vc=12083, M08-A1-VCG-03) states the diagnostic correctly: "arrogant in heart is an abomination" — the heart is what God assesses. Second, the outward body-expression makes CHAR-1 morally visible and judicially accountable: the haughty eyes become the specific target of divine judgment (Isa 2:11, vc=34089, M08-A2-VCG-01: "the haughty looks of man shall be brought low"; Pro 6:17, vc=34247: first in the list God hates). The body-expression is not incidental — it is how CHAR-1 becomes publicly evidenced and addressable.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The will-to-body directionality means CHAR-2 originates in the inner volitional faculty and requires address there, not merely at the level of the bodily expression. The stiff neck is the indicator; the inner will is the source. Correcting the posture would not address the will's boiling-over orientation. Additionally, the bodily expression makes CHAR-2 publicly evidenced and judicially assessable — Deu 17:12 (vc=34110, M08-B-VCG-02): the presumptuous man who defies the appointed judge is identified through his acted-out defiance, which is then publicly judged.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The interior-to-exterior directionality means CHAR-3's source is the inner alazoneia disposition and the heart's prideful orientation — the verbal boasting is the expression, not the origin. Addressing only the speech-act (silencing the mouth) without addressing the inner disposition would reach only the symptom. 2Cor 5:12 (vc=33872, M08-C-VCG-02): Paul's boasting is grounded "in the heart" — the interior is what gives the exterior boast its moral quality.

**[CHAR-4]** S — Not applicable — no body-characteristic link evidenced. The consequence of the silence is that CHAR-4 operates entirely at the inner cognitive level without a somatic expression register in this corpus.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The soul-to-structural directionality means CHAR-5 must be addressed at the inner heart-level, not merely at the level of structural position-removal. Lev 26:19 (vc=33982, M08-E-VCG-01): God "breaks the pride of your power" — the breaking is of the inner pride, not merely the removal of the structural power. If the structural power is removed without the inner pride being addressed, CHAR-5 would seek new structural grounds for its arrogance.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The inner-to-outer directionality across M08 establishes a consistent implication: each characteristic must be addressed at its constitutional source (the inner person) rather than merely at the level of its bodily expression. Removing the body-expression (silencing the mouth, lowering the haughty eyes, removing the physical height) would address only the symptom. Lev 26:19 (M08-E-VCG-01): God "will break the pride of your power" — the breaking is of the inner pride, not merely the structural power. This is confirmed across the cluster as a consistent structural finding.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The bidirectionality reveals that submission is engaged in a genuine body-soul interaction. The soul → body direction (Eph6:5) shows that genuine inner submission necessarily expresses itself outwardly — submission that produces no outer conduct is suspect. The body → soul direction (Rom6:12) shows that the body's passions are a genuine constitutional force competing with the soul's submission to God — the body is not neutral territory. The characteristic must be held at the soul/will level against the bodily-passion pull (Rom6:12), while also flowing into and expressing through bodily conduct (Eph6:5). This confirms submission as engaging the whole person, not merely the inner life in isolation.
**[CHAR-3]** S — No body-characteristic link is evidenced; direction cannot be analysed. The characteristic operates at spirit and heart level without a named body-part correlate in this corpus.
**[CHAR-4]** S — No body-characteristic link evidenced; direction cannot be analysed.
**[CHAR-5]** S — No body-characteristic link evidenced.
**[CHAR-6]** S — No body-characteristic link evidenced. Prompt closed.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The soul→body direction (M09-A voluntary register) confirms that genuine humility is an inner act that finds outward expression — it cannot be reversed (outer expression generating inner humility) without the self-referential performance problem that Col2:23 identifies. The body→soul direction in M09-B (the creaturely lowliness condition shaping inner experience) reveals that humility in its condition-register is partly constituted by the bodily-creaturely situation — the person who is genuinely low in estate cannot escape the experience through inner assertion alone. This directionality distinction helps clarify why the two sub-groups (M09-A voluntary, M09-B experienced) have different operational profiles: M09-A is primarily inner → outer; M09-B involves a body → inner dimension.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The bidirectional body-soul patterns evidenced for Humility (CHAR-1) and Submission (CHAR-2) reveal different but structurally parallel consequences for understanding each characteristic. For Humility (CHAR-1): the soul→body direction (M09-A voluntary register — inner humbling produces bodily weeping) clarifies why the M09-A and M09-B registers have different operational profiles. The voluntary register flows from inside out; the imposed/condition register involves the body's creaturely state shaping the inner experience. This directional distinction maps precisely onto the volume-split finding (Observation #16) — the two registers are not merely different occasions but different directional profiles of the same characteristic. For Submission (CHAR-2): the bidirectionality confirms the characteristic as engaging the whole embodied person — the soul must maintain genuine will-submission against the competing pull of bodily passions (body→soul — Rom6:12), while genuine inner submission necessarily expresses through bodily service (soul→body — Eph6:5). The characteristic cannot be abstracted from the embodied person. Cluster-level: both characteristics' directionality findings confirm M09's account of the person as constitutively embodied — the characteristics are not purely inner-being states but engage the whole person in both directional modes.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — The inner-to-outer directionality confirms that wilful sinning originates in the inner person (will, heart, conscience-bypassed) and externalises through the body — which is why the prescription for preventing speech-mode sinning (Psa 39:1; Job 31:30) is inner resolve acted out as external restraint. The body is the execution venue, not the origin point. The outer-to-inner feedback (consequence returning, 1Cor 6:18; Ecc 5:6's destroyed work) reveals that sinning creates a loop: the inner act externalises, the external act damages, and the damage returns to the inner person as guilt, consequence, and relational rupture. This loop is what the cultic-atonement system (VCG-04) interrupts — the sin offering breaks the consequence-return cycle by providing substitutionary resolution.

**[CHAR-10]** E — The bidirectional body-link (2Pe 2:14 — eyes as both receptor and projector of desire) reveals that addressing enticement requires both directing what the eyes look toward (the outer-to-inner direction) and transforming what the inner desire seeks (the inner-to-outer direction). The eyes carry the desire's distortion into the world and bring the world's lures into the desire. Governing the eyes without governing the desire is insufficient; governing the desire without governing the gaze is equally incomplete.

**[CHAR-11]** E — The bidirectional body-characteristic link (T2.7.1) reveals why the condition is self-reinforcing: the inner condition drives bodily expression (members deployed for sin), and the bodily expression reinforces the inner condition (passions feeding back into the will's captivity). Rom 6:19 (adjacent to the corpus — the broader Romans 6 argument) notes that presenting members to impurity leads to greater impurity — the feedback loop deepens the condition through each cycle. This explains why Paul prescribes the body's active re-presentation to God (Rom 6:13 — "present yourselves to God") as part of the liberating response: the feedback loop must be broken at both the inner and bodily levels simultaneously.

**[CHAR-12]** S — No body-part link is evidenced. The characteristic operates at the constitutional soul-level (will, identity-allegiance) and structural-universal (Gal 3:22 — everything under sin) without bodily-organic expression in this corpus.

**[CHAR-13]** E — The bidirectional body-record link (body acts generating the record; record weight deteriorating the body) reveals that the body is simultaneously an instrument of sin-record creation and a recipient of the record's consequences. Psa 38:3 — the bones bear the consequence of sin (moral → physical direction) while the hands and mouth that sinned (physical → moral direction) are the instruments. The body is thus a two-way channel: it creates entries in the divine record through sinning acts and then bears the physical weight of what has been recorded.

**[CHAR-14]** E — The bidirectional body-link reveals that forgiveness sought and received cannot be reduced to a purely interior event: the seeking requires bodily expression (hand-laying — 2Ch 29:23; baptism — Act 2:38 — a bodily act) and the receiving is grounded in a bodily historical event (blood poured out — Mat 26:28). The characteristic thus bridges the inner (volitional seeking, faith-reception) and the outer (bodily seeking-acts, historical atonement) — neither pole alone constitutes the complete characteristic.
**[CHAR-15]** S — No body-part link evidenced. The characteristic operates at the corporate-moral, heart, mind, and will levels without bodily-organic expression in this corpus.

**[CHAR-16]** E — The bidirectional body-link (inner character → outer conduct; outer abasement ← inner conscience) reveals that addressing the sinner-identity requires both outer and inner action: Jam 4:8 — "cleanse your hands" (outer) "and purify your hearts" (inner) — neither alone is sufficient. The sinner's hands can be cleansed without the heart being purified (outward compliance without inner change); the heart can be internally troubled without the hands being cleansed (inner guilt without outer repentance). The bidirectional link demands address at both levels simultaneously.

**[CHAR-17]** E — The bidirectional body-guilt link reveals that guilt-as-inner-state has a bodily-expressive and bodily-located dimension: it is not purely interior. Ezr 9:6's face-avoidance makes the guilt visible in the body's posture; Exo 28:38's forehead-bearing makes the guilt-bearing a physical act; Isa 6:7's lip-touching makes the removal a physical event. The body is thus the medium through which guilt is expressed, borne, and resolved — none of these are purely inner-spiritual events.

**[CHAR-18]** E — The bidirectional body-iniquity link reveals that iniquity-as-accumulated-crime is not a purely inner-abstract condition but engages the body at both ends of its trajectory. The iniquity is enacted through the body (Isa 59:3 — fingers), accumulated as inner weight (Psa 38:4 — over the head), and expressed in bodily decay (Psa 31:10 — bones wasting). Addressing iniquity must therefore address both the inner moral-crime reality and its bodily manifestations; the body is the instrument, carrier, and bearer of the iniquity-burden simultaneously.

**[CHAR-19]** E — The bidirectional body-transgression link reveals that transgression-as-deliberate-boundary-crossing operates through the body at both ends: the inner transgression is enacted through the body's speaking members (lips — Pro 12:13) and returns to burden the body's carrying members (neck — Lam 1:14). Addressing transgression thus requires addressing both: the inner heart-transgression (Psa 36:1 — where it speaks from) and the outer bodily expression (Pro 12:13 — lips). The body both mediates transgression outward and bears its returning burden.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The remedy-direction of the body-link (priest's finger/hands applying blood to altar) confirms that in the unintentional-sinning corpus, the *body participates primarily in the remedy rather than in the sinning act*. This is analytically coherent: unintentional sinning operates in the knowledge-gap (the mind did not know; the heart was not engaged), not through specific bodily organs as the vehicles of the sinning. The body then becomes the instrument of the ritual remedy — physically performing the atonement that addresses the mind-gap that produced the violation. The body's role is restorative rather than transgressive.

**[CHAR-20]** E — The bidirectional body-faithlessness link reveals that faithlessness cannot remain purely inner: it expresses through the body (turning backs — 2Ch 29:6) and returns upon the body (womb curse — Num 5:27). The most intimate covenant (marriage) produces the most bodily-specific consequence when broken. This confirms CHAR-20 as a constitutively embodied characteristic: the covenant bonds that faithlessness breaks are not purely spiritual but embodied in relational, social, and physical realities — and their breaking produces embodied consequences.

**[CHAR-21]** E — The bidirectional body-perversion link reveals that CHAR-21 operates through every directional channel simultaneously: inner twisting expresses through the body (mouth, eyes), external influences corrupt the inner (bribery, bad company), and inner corruption deteriorates the body (Psa 38:6; 2Cor 4:16). This multi-directional body-engagement is unique among M10 characteristics — no other characteristic studied engages the body through as many distinct directional channels as CHAR-21.

**[CHAR-22]** E — The inner-to-outer directionality confirms that CHAR-22's body-engagement is expressive rather than generative: the hand and tongue *express* the inner injustice; they do not *create* it. The heart devises (inner); the hands enact (outer). This means addressing CHAR-22 requires addressing the inner origin (the heart — Psa 58:2) rather than merely restraining the hand's expression (though Eze 18:8's hand-withholding is the immediate conduct-level remedy). The inner-to-outer direction makes CHAR-22's remedy fundamentally a heart-transformation rather than a conduct-correction.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The inner-to-outer direction confirms that the speech of confession is not primary but derivative: the conscience-and-will movement precedes and produces the speech. This means that genuine confession cannot be manufactured from the outside in — external pressure can produce the words (Pharaoh — Exo 9:27/10:16; Saul — 1Sa 15:30) but not the inner movement that makes those words true confession. The corpus also reveals that the outer speech, once genuinely spoken, feeds back to the inner: the prodigal's enacted confession (Luk 15:21) is more complete than his planned one (15:18) — the speaking is itself a moral event that deepens the inner reality named.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The bidirectional mouth-link makes the active-denial mode of conscience suppression *self-sealing*: the more the person speaks the denial, the more entrenched the inner suppression becomes. God's judgment (Jer 2:35 — "I will bring you to judgment for *saying*") falls on this speech-act precisely because it is not merely symptom but cause of the deepening suppression. The spoken denial is held accountable because it is an active contribution to the person's moral self-deception, not merely its passive expression.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The bidirectional link means that the physical habituation of refusal (the gestural patterns of stiff neck and stubborn shoulder) is not merely expressive but formative: consistently embodying resistance shapes the inner person in the direction of resistance. Neh 9:29's "stiffened their neck" — the perfect aspect suggests a completed, formed posture. The consequence: refusal to repent becomes more embodied and therefore more entrenched with each iteration of the refusal-gesture. Breaking the refusal to repent requires not only a change of will-direction but a reversal of the formed bodily-metaphor posture of resistance.

**[CHAR-6]** S — No body-part link is evidenced. The characteristic operates from inner constitution outward to institutional structures (altars — Hos 8:11) rather than through named body-part links. The institutional-structural externalisation (Hos 8:11) is the closest external expression evidenced, but this is social-institutional rather than bodily-organic.
**[CHAR-7]** S — No body-part link is evidenced. The characteristic operates from inner will through authority relationships and institutional structures rather than through bodily-organic channels.
**[CHAR-8]** S — No body-part link is evidenced. The characteristic operates at the political-social and volitional level without bodily-organic channel expression.

**[CHAR-9]** E — The inner-to-outer directionality reveals that the mouth is not the cause but the symptom: addressing the mouth without addressing the heart is insufficient. But the directionality also confirms that the mouth is the point of intervention: Eph 4:31 / Col 3:8 command that slander be "put away from you" — the command is at the level of the expressed speech, not only at the level of the inner heart condition. Both must be addressed: the heart's corruption (the source) and the mouth's expression (the externalisation). The mouth is thus both diagnostic (revealing the heart's condition) and the point of practical renunciation.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The soul-to-body directionality means that the characteristic cannot be addressed at the body level alone — the body's expressions (speech, action, eyes) are symptoms rather than causes. This is analytically confirmed by the Ezekiel corpus (VCG-07): the call to turn is addressed to the inner person's "way" and "will" (Eze 18:21 — "turns away from all his sins and does what is just and right"), not primarily to bodily behaviour as the point of address. Behavioural change is the evidence of inner turning (Eze 33:15 — "restores the pledge, gives back what he has taken by robbery") but the inner turn is the cause. The directionality also means that the body becomes a measure of the inner character's state — examining the wicked person's speech (VCG-08) reveals the inner orientation (Pro 12:6: "the words of the wicked lie in wait for blood").

**[CHAR-2]** E — The consistently inner-to-outer directionality means that addressing the body's expressions (stopping the mouth, controlling the eye) without addressing the constitutional inner condition is insufficient. Mat 12:34 (vc=14419 — VCG-03) makes this explicit: you cannot speak good "when you are evil" — the mouth's output is determined by the heart's state, not by behavioural self-control. Luk 11:39 (vc=14407 — VCG-05) exposes the same issue: the Pharisees clean the outside but the inside remains full of greed and wickedness — external cleansing does not address the constitutional inner condition. The directionality establishes that transformation must begin at the constitutional inner level (heart, conscience, mind) for the body's expressions to genuinely change.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The primarily inner-to-outer direction means that addressing the body's expressions (controlling the lips, physically opening the ear) without addressing the inner constitutional condition is insufficient. Luk 16:15 (vc=21 — VCG-02) makes this explicit in the NT register: "God knows your hearts" — the divine verdict on abomination bypasses all outward expression and goes directly to the inner constitutional condition. The Pharisees who exalt themselves before men (outward social performance) are still abominable in God's sight because the heart-level pride remains. The directionality establishes that abomination's address requires transformation at the heart/conscience level, not merely behavioural or speech-level correction. The secondary ear-to-inner feedback (Pro 28:9) suggests that deliberate bodily acts of reception (opening the ear to God's law) do have inner consequences, but the primary causation remains inner-to-outer.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The bidirectional character of the body-characteristic link means that the physical environment of idolatrous objects (the installed idols, the visible detestable things) actively reinforces and deepens the inner attachment. This is confirmed by the Deuteronomic reform strategy (VCG-02): Deu 7:25 (vc=1682 — VCG-02): "you shall burn with fire" — the physical destruction of the idol-objects removes the visual-desire feedback loop. 2Ch 34:33 (vc=65946 — VCG-03): Josiah's removal of all abominations from the territory enabled the people to "not turn away from following the Lord" — removing the physical objects removed their reinforcing influence on the inner attachment. The bidirectionality establishes that addressing idolatrous abomination requires both inner transformation (the heart turning) and physical removal of the outer idol-objects (the feedback mechanism).

**[CHAR-5]** E — The primarily inner-to-outer direction means that external behavioural control without inner address is insufficient — the scheming continues internally even if constrained externally. Jer 4:14 (vc=38205 — VCG-02): "wash your heart from evil" — the required address is inner (wash the heart), not merely behavioural. The secondary outer-to-inner feedback (mouth devouring iniquity — Pro 19:28 — VCG-03) reveals that speech habits reinforce the inner appetite, making the characteristic self-perpetuating through its own expressive channels. The directionality establishes that addressing iniquity requires inner transformation at the heart/thought level and management of the expressive channels that feed back into it.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The primarily inner-to-outer direction means that addressing the speech output without transforming the inner will is insufficient — the characteristic's source is the will's hardened defiance (Rev 16:9/11/21 — VCG-01), and only transformation at the will level (repentance) would address it. Rev 16:9 (VCG-01): "they did not repent" — the non-addressed inner will continues generating blasphemous speech regardless of external judgment. The secondary feedback (speaking blasphemy deepens the will's hardening) means that the act of expressing evil through speech is not merely symptomatic but formative: the characteristic reinforces itself through its own expression. Addressing evil speech requires inner will-transformation (repentance), not merely speech-management.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's unanimous inner-to-outer primary directionality establishes a shared therapeutic principle across all six characteristics: addressing the body's expressions without transforming the inner source is insufficient. Each characteristic makes this explicit in its own way — Char 1 (the Ezekiel inner-turning corpus VCG-07), Char 2 (Luk 11:39 — cleaning the outside while inside remains evil), Char 3 (Luk 16:15 — God knows the heart beyond social performance), Char 4 (both inner transformation and physical removal of idol-objects required), Char 5 (Jer 4:14 — "wash your heart from evil"), Char 6 (repentance required, not speech-management — Rev 16:9). The cluster-level consequence: genuine transformation of any M10b characteristic requires inner-constitutional address, not surface-behavioural management. The cluster also reveals that Chars 4 and 5's secondary feedback loops create an additional therapeutic requirement: managing the outer expressive channels (removing idol-objects, avoiding evil speech habits) to prevent the feedback reinforcement of the inner evil.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The predominantly body-to-soul direction reveals the characteristic as one in which the creaturely body's vulnerability is the primary generating reality. The inner person does not produce the ritual defilement-state through sin of the soul (that is Characteristics 2-3); rather, the body's contact with death, disease, and discharge creates a condition that then imposes itself on the whole person — conscience, will, social standing. This reveals the characteristic as a condition of creaturely finitude and mortality, not primarily a condition of inner moral failure. The soul's response — whether the will seeks remedy or refuses it — is the morally significant act within the condition; but the condition itself arrives through the body.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The primarily soul-to-body direction confirms the characteristic as originating in the inner person's willingness and desire rather than in bodily contact (distinguishing it from Characteristic 1). The defilement flows from the soul's disordered desire outward to the body — the body becomes the site of the condition's expression and consequence (Rom 1:24). The bidirectional element at 2Cor 7:1 reveals that once the condition is established, it inhabits the whole constitutional person — not only in the soul but also in the body — making the call to cleansing a call for the whole person's engagement.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The soul-to-body direction at Num 5:27 (VCG-01) reveals the characteristic as one in which covenantal volitional betrayal produces bodily consequences — the body bears the judicial consequence of the soul's covenantal defection. This reveals the characteristic as one in which the sacred relational order (covenant) is so constitutive of the person's and community's existence that betrayal of it produces consequences at the physical/bodily level. The covenantal bond is not merely a spiritual or social reality but one with bodily stakes.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The top-down directionality reveals why human restraint is futile (Luk 8:29 — chains and shackles broken): attempting to restrain the body (the lowest level of expression) cannot address the spirit-level cause. Only divine authority (operating at the spirit level — commanding the spirit directly, Mar 5:8) is effective. The consequence: the resolution must match the origin — external spirit-level invasion requires external divine authority at the spirit level to reverse.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The directional differences carry the most significant implications for understanding how each characteristic is resolved. Characteristic 1 (body-to-soul direction): the remedy addresses the body — washing, waiting, priestly examination — because the origin is bodily. Characteristic 2 (soul-to-body direction): the remedy must address the soul — repentance, cleansing of conscience and will (2Cor 7:1 — "let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of body and spirit, bringing holiness to completion in the fear of God") — because the origin is soul-level desire and will. Characteristic 3 (soul-to-body-and-environment direction): the remedy requires corporate moral transformation at the soul level and eventually divine action at the environmental level (Eze 37:23 — "I will save them... and will cleanse them"). Characteristic 4 (spirit-through-soul-to-body direction): only divine authority at the spirit level is effective — human restraint at the body level (Luk 8:29 — chains and shackles) is futile because it addresses the wrong level. The cluster's resolution principle: effective remedy always addresses the origin level. The failure of human remedies in Characteristic 4 (chains fail) is the most dramatic statement of this principle: when defilement originates at the spirit level through external agency, body-level remedies cannot reach it.

findings.finding_value: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level (chesed as covenantal-soul character), heart-level (Hos 11:8 — "my heart recoils"), and somatic-level (re.chem, splanchnon) are all richly evidenced. The constitutional architecture is bottom-up: the womb and entrails are the originating ground; the soul and heart are the engagement points; the act is the constitutional expression. Four body-part functions are identified: constitutive (womb — the generative image of compassion), expressive (gut — the felt movement), indicative (Synoptic pattern — splanchnizō signals the compassion-event), and mediating (heart in Hos 11:8 — the deliberative locus where compassion and judgment contend). The four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) is uniquely evidenced in this registry — consistently inside-out and bottom-up. T2.8 established no body deposit; T5.7 is formally closed. The constitutional portrait confirms the sb_classification (soul-body interface) and extends it: compassion is the most somatically grounded characteristic in the programme, with its originating logic residing in the body's deepest interior.

findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional levels are each carried by specific vocabulary families in T7. The somatic-body level (T2.6 — gut, womb) is carried by the RACHAM/SPLANCHN root families — the body's interior as the etymological ground of both. The soul-character level (T2.2) is carried by the CHASAD family — chesed as the settled covenantal character disposition. The heart-deliberative level (T2.3) is evidenced most richly in Hos 11:8 (T7's primary anchor for divine compassion). questions.question_text: Where does this verse say the characteristic originates — generated within the person, received from another person, bestowed by God, carried generationally, introduced by another spirit (angelic or adversarial), or not stated?

findings.session_b_note:
The data establishes a layered answer:

**Primary origin: Bestowed by God / received from outside.** The spirit-level origin is the divine disposition (God is *forgiving* — sal.lach, Psa 86:5) which is the source from which the human capacity to forgive derives. OBS-064-003: "The spirit-level origin of forgiveness (divine disposition, divine act) is not merely theological framing but is embedded in the lexical restriction of the OT salach vocabulary."

**NT development:** The forgiveness-authority is Spirit-bestowed (Joh 20:22-23) — the disciples receive the capacity to forgive as a gift of the Spirit, not as a natural human capacity.

**Human exercise-level:** At the soul level, the human person exercises forgiveness from within — "from the heart" (Mat 18:35). But this exercise is possible only because of the prior reception: F-003 establishes that vertical reception enables horizontal extension. The human exercise-origin is derivative, not primary.

**Generational:** Not addressed in the data (see T2.8 silence). No generational transmission of forgiveness-capacity is examined.
