findings.finding_value: M01-A has a clearly multiple origin: divine implantation, human formation through hearing, social reinforcement, and responsive awe at God's acts all produce the same reverential fear. This multiplicity is itself a finding: the characteristic can be generated through different pathways converging on the same inner disposition.

The origin is multiple across the cluster. The multiplicity is structured: ordered fear (M01-A) is formed through divine gift and human formation; disordered fear (M01-G) originates in constitutional failure; acute fear (M01-B) is externally triggered; chronic anxiety (M01-F) originates in the mind's forward projection in response to real circumstances.

The origin is multiple. The cluster evidences at least four distinct origins: (1) external moral provocation (perceived wrongdoing from another agent — M02-D-VCG-01); (2) constitutional attribute (divine jealousy as identity-level — M02-E-VCG-01); (3) wounded pride-investment meeting non-compliance (M02-B-VCG-03: Est 1:12; 3:5); (4) Spirit-empowerment transforming news of injustice into fierce anger (1Sa 11:6; Judg 14:19 — M02-B-VCG-02). The origin is multiple and varies by the register of anger evidenced.

The origin is clearly multiple. The corpus evidences four distinct origins: external loss/adversity (predominant), divine bestowal, internal moral perception, and self-infliction. This multiplicity reveals that grief is not a simple reactive state but a complex inner-being characteristic that can arise through multiple constitutional pathways. The divine-bestowal origin is theologically distinctive — it shows that God himself initiates grief in the inner person as part of redemptive or disciplinary purpose, making grief not merely a creaturely response but a divinely governed inner state.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Multiple origins: both external-responsive (God's acts received by the soul) and internal-volitional (the will choosing to exult). The two origins are not contradictory — the volitional exultation of Hab 3:18 is grounded in theological knowledge of who God is, making the will's act a response to an already-known divine reality rather than an arbitrary emotion.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Multiple. The evidence across the 15 VCGs of Characteristic 2 shows Joy originating through five distinct pathways (divine production, encounter, will, community, practice). No single origin is exclusive. The different sub-groups evidence different primary origins: M04-B-VCG-01 (feast-commandment joy) is practice-originated; M04-B-VCG-05 (God-directed psalmist joy) is encounter-originated; M04-C-VCG-04 (Spirit-fruit joy) is divinely-produced; M04-D (sunchairo) is community-originated.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Multiple — Spirit, faith, eschatological orientation, and volitional reframing each play a distinct originating role. The Spirit is primary; the others are enabling conditions or means through which the Spirit's origin reaches the person.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Multiple. The four origin pathways (divine character, divine acts, speech, evaluative faculty) each produce Gladness through a different route. This multiplicity is distinctive: Joy has a similar multiplicity but with the Spirit and commanded-will as prominent origins; Gladness's origins cluster around character-recognition, circumstance-response, and evaluative discernment.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Multiple — more so than any other M04 characteristic, reflecting the characteristic's five-sub-group breadth. The origin varies by mode: inner-being constitution (affective Delight), divine sovereign will (God's cha.phets), covenantal relationship (God's pleasure in persons), received word (sha.a cheered by consolation), corrupt formation (M04-P's habituated misdirection).

**[CHAR-5]** E — Multiple — the most varied origin-set in M04, consistent with Pleasure's role as the broadly receptive characteristic: it receives from persons, speech, creation, God's character, and worship-acts.
**[CHAR-6]** E — Multiple — divine acts, cognitive-limit encounters, direct perceptive encounter, and deliberate memory all originate Wonder through different pathways.

**[CLUSTER]** E — All seven have multiple origins, but the multiplicity varies: (1) Suffering-Joy (Char 7) is the least multiple (Spirit, faith, eschatological orientation, volitional reframing — four pathways, with Spirit as primary); (2) Joy (Char 2) has the most complex origin-matrix: divine production, encounter with God's acts, volitional choice, community, and prescribed practice — five distinct pathways; (3) Pleasure (Char 5) has the widest phenomenological origin spread. The breadth of Joy's origin-matrix confirms it as the cluster's most multi-access characteristic — it can be produced, encountered, chosen, shared, and practiced.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Definitively multiple. CHAR-1 cannot be reduced to a single originating source. The volume-split into three sub-groups (unjust wound, moral consequence, divine encounter) was designed precisely because the evidence shows three distinct originating dynamics — all producing the same fundamental inner experience of shame. This multiplicity of origin is one of CHAR-1's analytically significant features: the same felt inner state can be produced by unjust external wounding, by one's own moral failure, by divine judgment, or by the encounter with the holy.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Multiple origins matching the four VCGs: (1) Social community acting (VCG-01 — Ammonites shaving David's envoys). (2) Military conquest (VCG-02 — Assyria, Babylon). (3) Divine judicial action (VCG-03 — God bringing down the proud). (4) Past moral failure accumulating as carried burden (VCG-04). The origin in all cases is external to the recipient. Multiple rather than singular.

---

**[CHAR-3]** E — CHAR-3 originates in two ways: (1) From the inner disposition of the dishonorer (VCG-01): absent-regard, willful refusal to acknowledge worth, self-righteous contempt — generated from within the dishonorer's own inner-being condition. (2) From sovereign assignment (VCG-02): the potter's right, created order, received social treatment — external sources that assign dishonour-standings without the agency of either party being the primary origin.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — CHAR-4 originates from within the conscience's evaluative operation: it is the conscience assessing conduct and desires against God's standard. In the functioning mode (VCG-01), the origin is the conscience's proper operation with God's standard as the reference. In the disordered-desire mode (VCG-02), the origin is within the appetitive faculty. In the inverted mode (VCG-03), the origin of the inversion is the choice of an earthly standard as the evaluative reference replacing God's standard.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — CHAR-5 originates from outside the recipient: the contempt of others is the source (VCG-01 — the inner dismissive attitude of others; VCG-02 — the violent rejection by others; VCG-03 — the verbal assault by others). The origin is consistently external. Multiple rather than singular origins (dismissal, violence, speech) all producing the same received condition of contempt-shame.

---

**[CHAR-6]** E — CHAR-6 originates from within the person through the exercise of the moral will: the person who chooses not to engage in deliberate wrongdoing maintains the inner moral condition that CHAR-6 names. In Gen 20:5, Abimelech's innocence originated from his genuine not-knowing (he took Sarah believing she was Abraham's sister, not his wife) — it is innocence grounded in both ignorance and moral intention. In Psa 26:6, innocence is maintained through active moral choice. In Hos 8:5, the incapacity for innocence results from the accumulated moral choices of sustained idolatry — the origin of the loss is internal to the moral choices the people have been making.

---

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's origins span four types, making M07 one of the most origin-diverse clusters in the programme. (1) External human agency: Chars 2, 3, 5 — humiliation inflicted by armies or community, worth denied by another person, contempt directed by the self-righteous. (2) Divine judicial action: Chars 1-M07B, 2, 3 — God putting enemies to shame, bringing down the proud, assigning dishonour-standings. (3) Internal moral failure: Chars 1-M07B, 1-M07C, 4, 6 — shame arising from one's own sin, shamefulness as the quality of one's conduct, loss of innocence through idolatry. (4) Relational encounter with holiness: Char 1-M07C — the shame of Ezr 9:6 that cannot lift its face to God; Char 6 — approach to God requiring the innocence that Char 6 names and its absence blocks. These four origin-types confirm that the shame-field is not a single-cause phenomenon but a domain reached from multiple directions in the fallen world.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — The evidence reveals a multiple-but-unified origin. Single generative root: 2Ti 3:2 (vc=1899, M08-A4-VCG-01) — filautos as the dispositional ground from which pride and arrogance flow; Mar 7:22 (vc=33928, M08-A4-VCG-01) — CHAR-1 constitutionally within the fallen inner person. Multiple occasion-triggers that activate from this root: prosperity (Deu 8:14, vc=34223, M08-A1-VCG-01), power (2Ch 26:16, vc=34044, M08-A1-VCG-01), beauty (Eze 28:17, vc=34047, M08-A1-VCG-02), military victory (Dan 11:12, vc=34234, M08-A1-VCG-02), and the general condition of simply being human in a fallen state (Rom 1:30, vc=33932, M08-A4-VCG-01: haughtiness among vices of the morally disordered mind generally). The origin is singular at the root (self-love, the fallen inner person) and multiple in the occasions that release it.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The origin is multiple in trigger but unified in constitutional source. The unified source is the will's self-authorising impulse (zid root) arising from the heart. Multiple trigger-points: contempt for God's law (Psa 119:21, vc=34098 — wandering from commandments), absence of God-fear (Psa 86:14, vc=34097 — "they do not set God before them"), self-deceptive overconfidence (Obd 3, vc=34108 — "the arrogance of your heart has deceived you"), and distorted claim to privilege (Luk 3:8, vc=55578 — "we have Abraham as our father"). All these trigger the same core: the will asserting beyond its authorised limits.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Multiple but unified: the alazoneia disposition (inner substrate, unified), the soul's desires (Psa 10:3, vc=33354), the heart's prideful orientation (CHAR-1 substrate), and the cognitive self-comparison process (2Cor 10:12 context) all contribute to CHAR-3's generation. The unifying source is the inner self's orientation toward its own elevation (CHAR-1), from which the specific boasting act emerges. The occasion triggers vary: wealth (Psa 49:6, vc=33355), religious identity (Rom 2:17, vc=33882), apostolic credentials (2Cor 11:18), creaturely achievements (Jer 9:23).

**[CHAR-4]** E — Multiple but unified: various occasions activate the same underlying cognitive self-inflation. The unified source is the mind's fleshly orientation (Col 2:18: "nous tēs sarkos") that generates inflation when stimulated by knowledge, partisan loyalty, or spiritual experience. Multiple trigger-occasions (knowledge, partisan attachment, leadership elevation, spiritual experience) activate the same cognitive-inflation dynamic from within.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Multiple-but-unified: the heart is the single constitutional origin-site; multiple structural goods (military power, wealth, fortification, ease) are the multiple occasion-triggers. Lev 26:19 (vc=33982): power; Eze 28:5 (vc=34046): wealth; Jer 49:16 (vc=34167): fortified height; Eze 16:49 (vc=33979): material ease — all activate the same inner heart-pride from different structural occasions.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster comparison reveals a consistent pattern: unified constitutional source with multiple occasion-triggers. Each characteristic has a single constitutional source-faculty (heart or mind) but multiple external occasions that activate that source. CHAR-1 can be triggered by prosperity, power, beauty, or military success. CHAR-4 by knowledge, partisan attachment, leadership elevation, or spiritual experience. CHAR-5 by military might, wealth, fortification, or ease. The cluster-synthesis: M08 is a triggered cluster — the internal constitutional sources are present but require activation by external received goods. This explains why M08 is particularly dangerous in conditions of genuine blessing and achievement.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The origin is clearly multiple, as T2.9.1 demonstrates. The most significant tension within the multiple origins is between the Spirit-directed (1Pe1:2 — Spirit produces it) and the person-generated (Phili2:12 — "work out your own salvation with fear and trembling") registers. Phili2:13 (outside this corpus but structurally implied by Phili2:12's context — "for it is God who works in you both to will and to work") would resolve this tension as a both-and: God works; the person works. The corpus evidence alone (Phili2:12 — the human command; 1Pe1:2 — the Spirit's direction) presents both origins without contradiction, implying the characteristic's origin is jointly human-volitional and Spirit-enabled.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The two-verse corpus suggests the origin is constituted by at least two factors: (1) the person's own moral condition (the failure or limitation that occasions the breaking); and (2) the encounter with divine holiness or truth (Isa57:15 — the high-and-holy One's self-disclosure as the frame within which the contrite spirit is named). Both factors together constitute the origin: the characteristic arises when the person's moral reality is confronted in the light of God's holiness, and neither factor alone is sufficient.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Heb5:2 evidences a multiple origin: the characteristic requires both the self-knowledge of one's own weakness AND the encounter with the erring other's condition. Neither alone is sufficient: self-awareness without the erring other produces nothing; encounter with the erring without self-awareness produces severity rather than gentleness. The origin is the relational conjunction of the two.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The evidence suggests multiple contributing origins: genuine godliness (1Ti2:2 — paired with eusebeia), integrity (Tit2:7 — listed alongside integrity), and characterological formation that produces the gravity appropriate to leadership roles (1Ti3:4). The characteristic arises from the convergence of these forming influences rather than a single constitutional source.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The origin is multiple, as T2.9.1 demonstrates: the characteristic originates both from within (the freely-moving heart of VCG-01) and from God (the divinely-upheld willing spirit of VCG-02). The most significant insight is that these two origins are not contradictory but complementary: the self-generated willing-heartedness of VCG-01 is the natural expression of the genuine inner orientation; the divinely-given willing spirit of VCG-02 is the same characteristic requiring divine restoration and sustaining after the inner orientation has been disrupted by moral failure.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The origin is multiple, as T2.9.1 demonstrates. The structural distinction between M09-A and M09-B maps precisely onto this plurality: M09-A (voluntary) is primarily person-generated and divinely-occasioned; M09-B (imposed) is primarily divinely-imposed or circumstantially-generated. Within M09-A, the Colossian material (Col2:18; Col2:23) adds a fourth origin-variant: humility can be *performed* — generated from a false origin (self-referential asceticism) rather than from genuine inner transformation. The genuine characteristic must originate from the heart's actual response to God and to others, not from a self-constructed discipline that keeps the self at the centre.

**[CLUSTER]** E — All six characteristics evidence multiple origins, but the nature and degree of multiplicity varies systematically. Humility (CHAR-1) has the most explicit multiple-origin profile: volitional self-application (M09-A), divine-occasioning through word-reception, divine imposition (M09-B), and — negatively — performed self-referential asceticism (Col2:23 as a fourth, false origin). Submission (CHAR-2) similarly evidences multiple origins: volitional reorientation, faith-enabled, Spirit-directed (1Pe1:2), and formed through suffering (Heb5:8). Willing-heartedness (CHAR-6) is the most theoretically significant: its two VCG-level origins (inner-generated VCG-01; divinely-restored VCG-02) confirm the same characteristic can have genuinely different origins depending on the person's moral-spiritual state — not contradictory but complementary. Contrition (CHAR-3), Meekness (CHAR-4), and Dignity (CHAR-5) evidence multiple contributing factors without the same explicit plurality of named origin-types. Cluster-level: no M09 characteristic has a singular, context-independent origin. The cluster's most analytically significant multiple-origin finding is CHAR-6's VCG split: the same inner quality can be self-generated (person in good standing with God) or divinely-restored (person after moral failure) — confirming that the question of origin is always context-dependent.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — The origin is clearly multiple in the corpus. No single origin-source is evidenced as exhaustive. The corpus presents internal origins (will, heart, conscience-bypassed) and external origins (social pressure, temptation, exposure) operating alongside each other. Neh 6:13 (external trap) and 1Sa 15:24 (external pressure) show sinning arising from a combination of external pressure and internal capitulation of the will. Gen 39:9 shows sinning arising purely from internal temptation (Potiphar's wife's offer) met by internal resistance — external trigger, internal response. The multiplicity of origins supports reading wilful sinning as a relational phenomenon (always involving a setting, a pressure, and a will) rather than a purely internal generation.

**[CHAR-10]** E — Multiple — with distinct origins for each mechanism. The composite nature of the characteristic (three mechanisms) produces necessarily multiple constitutional origins: desire-faculty (enticement), social-conformity pressure (hypocrisy), will's departure (apostasy). No single constitutional origin covers all three.

**[CHAR-11]** E — The origin is singular at its source (one man — Rom 5:12) but universal in its reach ("death spread to all men" — Rom 5:12; "all have sinned" — Rom 3:23). The singular origin (Adam) generates the universal condition. Rom 5:16 — "the judgment following one trespass brought condemnation" — one act at the origin produced a universal judicial standing (condemnation) for all. The singularity of the origin is what makes the condition's universality intelligible: it is not that each person originates their own sin-condition from scratch but that all share in the one origin's consequence.

**[CHAR-12]** E — Multiple. Individual practice (Joh 8:34 — the person's own sinning practice) and the devil's originary sinning (1Jo 3:8 — primordial spiritual source) are distinct constitutional origins. The individual practice is the proximate origin of each person's enslavement; the devil's originary sinning is the ultimate origin of the enslaving power that the individual's practice aligns with. The two origins work together: the individual's practice is what aligns them with and comes under the devil's originary sin-power.

**[CHAR-13]** E — Multiple — and constitutively so. The 205-verse corpus explicitly demonstrates at least four distinct constitutional origins (heart's thought, will's act, birth-condition, corporate transmission — T2.9.1). No single origin covers all 205 verses: chet (VCG-01) emphasises personal-liability origin; Psa 51:5 emphasises birth-condition origin; VCG-04 emphasises corporate-representational origin; VCG-05's broad chat.tat corpus emphasises the act-origin. The characteristic's scope is precisely its multi-originary nature.

**[CHAR-14]** E — Multiple — and structurally so. The seeking dimension originates in conscience recognition (Lev 4:14) and volitional turning (Act 2:38 — repent). The receiving dimension originates in God's provision of the atonement-mechanism (Exo 29:36 — God's daily sin-offering institution; Mat 26:28 — Christ's blood). These multiple origins reflect the characteristic's bi-directional structure: the seeking originates in the person; the receiving originates in God.

**[CHAR-15]** E — Both — a singular founding origin with multiple subsequent reinforcing origins. Isa 43:27 — "your first father sinned" — singular founding origin; "and your mediators transgressed against me" — multiple subsequent institutional transgressors who deepened and extended the condition. The origin is thus singular in its founding moment (first father) but multiplied through subsequent generations of leaders and communities who continued the pattern.

**[CHAR-16]** E — Multiple — and the multiplicity is analytically significant. The federal imputation origin (Rom 5:19 — Adam's one act) is singular in its initiating moment; the habitual-formation origin (Gen 13:13 — sustained extreme sinning) requires multiple acts over time. The characteristic thus has both a singular federal origin (applying to all through Adam) and a multiple individual origin (applying to the extreme sinner-type through accumulated formation). These are not competing origins but different levels of the same constitutional reality.

**[CHAR-17]** E — Multiple — and the multiplicity across five VCGs is the corpus's richest inter-origin complexity. Individual unintentional acts (VCG-01 — Lev 4/5 sequences), communal accumulation across generations (VCG-02 — Ezr 9:7), guilt loaded onto a representative bearer (VCG-03 — Exo 28:38), punitive inheritance from ancestors (VCG-04 — Gen 19:15), and indelibility before divine memory (VCG-05 — Jer 2:22; Eze 21:23/24) are all distinct guilt-origins operating simultaneously in the 97-verse corpus.

**[CHAR-18]** E — Multiple — and the multiplicity across eight VCGs represents the greatest origin-complexity in M10. Individual willful acts (VCG-04 — Eze 18:20 — personal crime), heart-originated allegiance (VCG-08 — Eze 14:3), inherited pre-personal condition (Psa 51:5), generational transmission (VCG-02 — Exo 20:5), cultic failure (VCG-01 — Lev 5:1/17), and communal accumulation (VCG-05 — Ezr 9:6) are all distinct iniquity-origins operating simultaneously across the 162-verse corpus.

**[CHAR-19]** E — Multiple — nine VCG registers name different originating contexts. Individual volitional choice (VCG-01 — Isa 1:2 — "they have rebelled"), Adamic inheritance (VCG-05 — Rom 5:15/16), heart-level inner voice (VCG-09 — Psa 36:1), inherited national identity (VCG-03 — Amos — nations whose transgression is counted), deceptive persuasion (VCG-04 — 1Ti 2:14 — Eve deceived), and revolt-speech (VCG-02 — Jer 28:16 — false prophecy as revolt). The characteristic has the most diverse origin-set of any M10 characteristic studied, covering individual, communal, inherited, coerced, and heart-generated origins.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The origin is multiple. No single cause is evidenced as exhaustive. The corpus presents: epistemic limitation as an inner origin (not knowing the prohibition, Lev 4:2), perceptual limitation as an inner origin (not seeing the morally relevant fact, Num 22:34), and situational pressure as an external-contextual origin (urgency of battle, 1Sa 14:33/34). The multiplicity reflects the variety of ways in which the gap between available knowledge and moral requirement can arise — through ignorance, through limited perception, and through situational distraction.

**[CHAR-20]** E — Multiple — the three VCGs name distinct originating contexts. Spirit-level disposition (Mal 2:15 — VCG-03); pride-generated (2Ch 26:16 — VCG-01 Uzziah); allegiance-transfer (1Ch 5:25 — transferring loyalty to false gods — VCG-01); lust-captivity (Pro 11:6 — lust capturing the will — VCG-02); unguarded spirit (Mal 2:15 — VCG-02 marital). The characteristic has multiple originating pathways: all share the spirit-level as the constitutional location but reach that location through different triggering conditions (pride, misplaced desire, unguarded spirit).

**[CHAR-21]** E — Multiple — across five VCG registers. Heart-origin (VCG-01/03 — Pro 6:14); desire-origin (VCG-05 — Eph 4:22; 2Pe 1:4); instinct-origin (VCG-05 — Jude 10); bribery-triggered cognitive corruption (VCG-02 — Exo 23:8); created-order violation (VCG-04 — Lev 18:23 — te.vel). CHAR-21 has the most diverse origin-set of any M10 characteristic studied in terms of the different inner faculties named as origin-points (heart, desire, instinct) plus external triggering conditions (bribery, bad company — 1Cor 15:33).

**[CHAR-22]** E — Multiple across the three VCG registers. Heart-devising (VCG-02 — Psa 58:2/64:6); God-denial (VCG-01/03 — Psa 53:1; Job 18:21); self-trust (VCG-02 — Hos 10:13); material inducement (VCG-01 — 2Ch 19:7 — bribery); emergence from within a blameless being (Eze 28:15 — the cherub's internal emergence). CHAR-22 has diverse origins but all share the will-level as the constitutional location of the departure from right conduct.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The origin is multiple. Conscience (2Sa 24:10), knowledge (2Sa 19:20), external judgment-pressure (Exo 9:27), intercessory solidarity (Neh 1:6), and communal recognition (VCG-02 corporate confessions — Judg 10:10; 1Sa 7:6) all appear as originating conditions. The multiplicity confirms that confession is not generated by a single faculty but by a convergence of inner conscience, situational pressure, relational orientation, and communal solidarity. What distinguishes genuine from hollow confession is which of these origins dominates: when inner conscience dominates (2Sa 24:10; Luk 15:18), the confession is genuine; when external pressure alone drives it (Exo 9:27/10:16 — Pharaoh) without inner conscience-origin, the hollow form results.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The origin is clearly multiple. Active denial (Jer 2:35) originates from the will's self-interested claim. Perceptual blindness (Jer 16:10) originates from communal-formational degeneration. Habituated absence (Ecc 8:12) originates from repeated sinning over time. Epistemic suppression (1Cor 15:34) originates from ignorance of God. The three modes of the characteristic (active denial, perceptual blindness, habituated absence) each have a distinct origin, sharing only the common outcome: conscience not performing its moral-witness function.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The origin is multiple. Inherited moral legacy (Jeroboam-pattern), divided heart (2Ki 10:31), cognitive minimisation (1Ki 16:31), and deliberate post-knowledge choice (Heb 10:26) all contribute to the origin in different instances. The Kings corpus shows inherited legacy as the dominant origin; Neh 9:29 shows communal formation; Heb 10:26 shows individual deliberate choice. The characteristic's diverse origins reflect its wide evidential base.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The origin is clearly multiple. Individual psychological cycling (Exo 9:34), communal inheritance (Hos 10:9; 2Ki 17:7), institutional misdirection (Hos 8:11), and dispositional absence (Ecc 7:26) all appear as distinct originating conditions. The multiplicity confirms that habitual defection can arise from several different starting points, all of which converge in the same outcome: the will's settled direction toward sin.

**[CHAR-7]** E — The origin is effectively dual: (1) the leader's personal inner sinful commitment (constitutional source), and (2) the authority position that makes the transmission possible (structural enabler). Neither alone constitutes contagious sin: personal sinning without authority produces CHAR-1/5/6; authority without sinful inner commitment does not transmit sin. The two must combine. The Kings corpus shows a third contributing origin: the received sinning pattern from prior leaders (1Ki 22:52 — following father, mother, and Jeroboam) — the leader's own sinful commitment is often itself a received pattern.

**[CHAR-8]** E — The origin is multiple. Opportunity-based origin (2Ki 1:1; 3:5), spiritually-grounded authority vacuum (2Ch 21:10), and unexplained decisive break (1Ki 12:19 — Israel's revolt from Davidic house in the Rehoboam context) represent distinct originating conditions. What is common across all: the presence of an established governing relationship that is broken by a decisive volitional act.

**[CHAR-9]** E — Multiple. Heart-corruption (Mat 15:19), conceit/craving (1Ti 6:4), unbelief (1Ti 1:13), and constitutive anti-God orientation (VCG-03) are distinct originating conditions across the corpus. The common element: all originate from an inner moral condition rather than from external triggers. The characteristic is generated from within; external provocations may occasion sinful speech but do not constitute its origin.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The evidence presents multiple contributing origins rather than a single point. Pride appears as a root: Pro 21:4 (VCG-03) names "haughty eyes and a proud heart" as the lamp of the wicked — pride is an originating inner attitude. The exclusion of God (VCG-02) is another originating event. Social alignment with the wicked (Psa 1:1 — "walks in the counsel of the wicked") contributes as an external-becoming-internal origin. Job 34:8 (re.sha, VCG-11) notes that "walking in company with evildoers" reflects a chosen inner alignment — social context becomes a contributory origin. The evidence thus presents a multiple-origin picture: pride, God-exclusion, chosen volitional direction, and social-moral alignment all contribute to the settling of this characteristic.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The evidence presents the origin as the singular constitutional condition of human inner nature (the "you who are evil" baseline of Mat 7:11 and Luk 11:13 — VCG-02). However, the VCG-05 saturation cluster (Rom 1:29 — VCG-05: "filled with all manner of unrighteousness, evil, covetousness, malice") shows the constitutional condition producing multiple specific vices — the singular constitutional evil generates a multiplicity of specific expressions. The relationship is one origin (the constitutional condition) producing multiple expressions (the vice catalogue). Additionally, VCG-01's cosmic-evil dimension (the evil one's domain — 1Jo 5:19: "the whole world lies in the power of the evil one") introduces a supra-personal source that is external to the individual but operative in the environment that shapes the constitutionally evil person.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The evidence presents multiple originating inner conditions. The VCG structure itself maps multiple: pride/arrogance in heart (VCG-02), dishonest practice revealing a character of fraud (VCG-01), the corrupt inner person's religious approach (VCG-03), conscience silencing (VCG-04), and the identity constituted by abomination (VCG-05). Pro 26:25 (vc=1694 — VCG-02): "seven abominations in his heart" — the very plurality (seven) suggests multiple concurrent originating conditions within the same person. Pro 6:16 (vc=65952 — VCG-05): "six things that the Lord hates, seven that are an abomination" — the listing implies multiple distinct origins for the abominable category, not a single root. The origin is thus multiple: various specific inner conditions each qualify as originating sources of abomination.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The evidence presents multiple originating pathways: (1) pride perverting gifts into idols (Eze 7:20 — vc=65909/65975 — VCG-05: pride as the internal mechanism); (2) coveting what is on the idols (Deu 7:25 — VCG-02: desire/covetousness as the entry mechanism); (3) marital-relational entanglement with idolaters (Ezr 9:1; 9:14 — VCG-03: relational influence); (4) royal institutionalization (VCG-03 — kings who install abominations, leading communities into them by authority); (5) inherited patterns from ancestors (Eze 20:4 — VCG-05: "abominations of their fathers"). The origin is thus multiple: pride, covetousness, relational entanglement, royal authority, and generational inheritance all appear as originating pathways.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The evidence presents multiple originating inner faculties working together: the heart (Isa 32:6 — VCG-02 — busy), the thought-life (Isa 59:7 — VCG-02 — thoughts of iniquity), and the will (Job 36:21 — VCG-04 — chosen rather than affliction). These are not three separate origins but three facets of the same inner generative process. Additionally, relational-social influence appears as a secondary originating channel: Job 34:8 (vc=38214 — VCG-04): "travels in company with evildoers" — chosen association with evildoers shapes the inner person toward iniquity. The origin is primarily internal and multiple (heart + mind + will in conjunction) with a secondary social-relational influence pathway.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The evidence presents multiple originating conditions, varying by VCG. VCG-01: the origin is the hardened will combined with authority-rejection and cognitive incomprehension (Jude 8: authority-rejection + sensory indulgence; Jude 10: incomprehension + contempt). VCG-02: the origin is moral failure (Rom 2:24), false attribution (Rom 3:8), misuse of freedom (Rom 14:16; 1Cor 10:30), or received slander's social consequence (1Cor 4:13). VCG-03: the origin is malicious hostile evaluation (Joh 18:30) or civil-legal process wrongdoing (Act 25:5; 1Pe 2:14). The origin is thus multiple and varies by register — from the hardened-will's authority-rejection (VCG-01) to hostile social judgment (VCG-03) to moral failure enabling defamation (VCG-02).

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster unanimously presents multiple originating conditions — no characteristic in the cluster has a singular, isolated origin. Chars 1 and 5 both show volitional choice + relational formation (chosen association) as dual originating conditions. Char 4 shows pride (Eze 7:20) + covetousness (Deu 7:25) + relational entanglement (1Ki 11:5) as multiple originating pathways. Char 3 shows multiple originating inner conditions (crooked heart, arrogant heart, lying lips, dishonest practice). Char 2 shows the fallen constitutional background as the universal enabling condition within which more specific evil expressions arise. Char 6 shows the authority-rejection + self-indulgence precondition (Jude 8) as the composite origin. The cluster's unanimous multiple-origin pattern confirms that M10b inner evil is not a simple causal phenomenon — it arises from the conjunction of constitutional susceptibility, volitional choice, and relational influence.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The origin is clearly multiple. The 133-verse corpus encompasses at least five distinct origin pathways (external contact, internal bodily process, authoritative verdict, spatial proximity, ingestion). The diversity of origins reflects the characteristic's function as a comprehensive system for managing the person's sacral status across the full range of bodily and relational interactions with the material world. No single origin dominates; the system is designed to catch the full range of creaturely vulnerability.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The origin is clearly multiple. The constitutional origin (Job 14:4) is prior to and deeper than the habitual-desire origin (Rom 1:24); the formative-context origin (1Cor 8:7) is different again. The characteristic does not have a single point of origin but arises through the intersection of inherited constitutional vulnerability, unchecked desire, formative context, and progressive conscience-suppression.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The origin is clearly multiple. The characteristic does not arise from a single type of act or disposition but from the intersection of sexual betrayal, idolatrous attachment, deliberate desecration, and habitual moral conduct — all of which produce corporate/covenantal defilement through different mechanisms applied to different sacred objects (person, sanctuary, land, name).

**[CHAR-4]** E — The origin is singular in kind (always an unclean spirit as the external agent) but may involve multiple individual spirits. Mar 5:13 (VCG-02): "the unclean spirits came out and entered the pigs" — plural spirits inhabiting one person. Mar 9:25 (VCG-01): one specific spirit addressed as "mute and deaf" — singular. The origin is consistently external-spiritual-agent, whether singular or multiple in number.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Characteristics 1, 2, and 3 all have multiple origins; Characteristic 4 has a singular-kind origin. The multiple-origin characteristics (1, 2, 3) reflect their comprehensive scope: Characteristic 1 covers the full range of bodily-material vulnerability; Characteristic 2 covers the range of inner-moral-constitutional pathways; Characteristic 3 covers the range of covenantal-volitional betrayals. Characteristic 4's singular-kind origin (always an unclean spirit as the external agent) reflects its structural simplicity: one type of agent, one type of mechanism, consistent across all 21 verses. The cluster-level pattern: the defilement conditions that arise from the person's own constitution (Chars 1-3) have multiple origins because the creaturely inner life and its sacral environment are complex and multi-vulnerable. The defilement condition that arrives from outside (Char 4) has a singular origin because it is imposed by one type of agent through one type of mechanism.

findings.session_b_note:
The origin is consistent (divine) but the **mechanism of origination changes** across contexts:

- **OT cultic context:** The origin mechanism is sacrifice and priestly mediation — external and ritual (Lev 4:20; group 5379-001). The divine act of forgiving is triggered by correct external performance.
- **OT intercessory context:** The origin mechanism is the divine character itself — the appeal to God's name and hesed (Dan 9:19; group 5379-002). Forgiveness originates in what God is.
- **New covenant:** The origin mechanism is Christ's atoning blood (Eph 1:7) — a singular historical act that grounds all subsequent forgiveness.
- **NT access-postures:** The inner-being postures (repentance, faith, confession) are not origins but access-points — the origin remains divine; the access mechanism changes.

The origin (divine character and act) is consistent; the mechanism through which it reaches the human person varies across covenant contexts. This is partially addressed in OBS-064-014 and F-005 but not assembled as an origin-framework.

findings.session_b_note:
Yes — the contextual variation in origin is one of the structurally significant features of the compassion vocabulary:

**In prophetic/covenantal contexts:** Origin is predominantly divine — God's inner movement (Hos 11:8), God's sovereign freedom (Rom 9:15), God's everlasting chesed (Isa 54:8). The human person's compassion is derivative and responsive.

**In Synoptic Gospel contexts:** Origin is primarily Christological — Jesus's gut-movement (splanchnizō) as the incarnate embodiment of divine compassion enacted in human form. This is neither purely divine-origin nor purely human-origin — it is the point where the two meet in the Incarnation.

**In Epistle and community contexts:** Origin is located in the character formed within the community of faith — sumpathēs and eusplanchnos (1 Pet 3:8) as qualities cultivated within the new humanity. In this context, compassion originates from within the person's formed character, shaped by community and by the gospel.

**In parable contexts:** Origin is presented as arising naturally within the human person in response to need — the father running to the prodigal (Luke 15:20), the Samaritan stopping for the wounded man (Luke 10:33). In these contexts, no divine causation is explicitly named — compassion arises as the human inner response to human need.

findings.session_b_note: The ultimate origin (God's goodness) does not change. What changes is the delivery mechanism and the register of goodness received. In the Hebrew experiential register (884-003), the origin reaches the person through encounter and nearness. In the covenantal register (884-005), through God's word and promise-keeping. In the NT pneumatological register (885-001, 886-002), through the Spirit's production. These represent a progressive clarification and concentration of how goodness is delivered — from encounter and word in the OT to Spirit-production in the NT — but the source is constant. What shifts is not the origin but the mechanism of delivery and the specificity of naming. The NT's pneumatological precision is a clarification, not a change of origin. (OBS-067-OBS-016, OBS-067-OBS-099)

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-002: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level …
findings.finding_value: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level (chesed as covenantal-soul character), heart-level (Hos 11:8 — "my heart recoils"), and somatic-level (re.chem, splanchnon) are all richly evidenced. The constitutional architecture is bottom-up: the womb and entrails are the originating ground; the soul and heart are the engagement points; the act is the constitutional expression. Four body-part functions are identified: constitutive (womb — the generative image of compassion), expressive (gut — the felt movement), indicative (Synoptic pattern — splanchnizō signals the compassion-event), and mediating (heart in Hos 11:8 — the deliberative locus where compassion and judgment contend). The four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) is uniquely evidenced in this registry — consistently inside-out and bottom-up. T2.8 established no body deposit; T5.7 is formally closed. The constitutional portrait confirms the sb_classification (soul-body interface) and extends it: compassion is the most somatically grounded characteristic in the programme, with its originating logic residing in the body's deepest interior.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-015: T2's constitutional origin analysis (somatic-relational-covenantal triple ground) and T4's relational direction analysis are structurally aligned. The somatic origin (womb, gut) grounds the cross-boun…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional origin analysis (somatic-relational-covenantal triple ground) and T4's relational direction analysis are structurally aligned. The somatic origin (womb, gut) grounds the cross-boundary relational direction in T4: splanchnizō's somatic immediacy is precisely what enables it to cross covenantal boundaries — the gut-movement toward the suffering other precedes any covenantal assessment of the relationship. The covenantal origin (chesed) grounds the within-bond sustaining direction in T4. The constitutional origin therefore predicts the relational direction: somatic = cross-boundary; covenantal = within-bond. T2's soul-body interface classification explains T4's scope-by-need finding: because compassion originates at the soul-body interface (before covenantal-rational assessment), its scope is determined by the pre-rational recognition of need rather than the post-rational assessment of covenantal standing.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-017: T2's somatic-constitutional location explains several T6 structural connections. The shared anchor at Isa 53:5 (with R030 contrition) confirms that the somatic wound vocabulary intersects both compass…
findings.finding_value: T2's somatic-constitutional location explains several T6 structural connections. The shared anchor at Isa 53:5 (with R030 contrition) confirms that the somatic wound vocabulary intersects both compassion and contrition at the constitutional-somatic level — both characteristics have somatic-body language as part of their evidential ground. The CHASAD root's crossing of compassion and shame clusters (T6.4 — most unexpected structural finding) is partly explainable from T2: if CHASAD names a covenantal-soul disposition, it can operate in both the positive register (chesed — steadfast love/compassion) and the negative register (bōsheth — shame as the opposite soul-condition of exposed vulnerability). T2's constitutional portrait (soul-body interface) is the constitutional ground for the root-level cluster-crossing that T6 identifies.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-002: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary…
findings.finding_value: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary point of reception (Zec 12:10 — spirit of grace poured out), not the point of generation (grace originates with God — T2.9). The soul level is the site of standing (Rom 5:2 — "this grace in which we stand") and identity (1Cor 15:10 — "by the grace of God I am what I am"). The constitutional movement follows the SD021 four-faces model: divine disposition received at spirit level → relational standing established at soul level → specific capacity gifted → character expressed outward. Heart-location is partially evidenced via eusplanchnos (Eph 4:32 — the tenderheartedness that grace produces, reaching the affective-somatic interface). T2.7 produces a new finding: grace operates bidirectionally through the body-soul interface — soul-to-body (inner posture enacted somatically in prostration, fasting, sackcloth) and body-to-soul (somatic enactment deepening and confirming the inner posture). T2.8 remains open (body deposit question unresolved); T5.7 is left open accordingly. The constitutional origin analysis (T2.9) is the most analytically significant T2 finding: grace does not originate in the human constitutional system at any level — it arrives from outside. The cluster shows context-dependent origin emphasis across all six characteristics: the Psalmic context (Chars 1, 3, 5) emphasises the volitional inner-life as origin; the Proverbs context emphasises the moral character and its formed habits as origin; the prophetic context emphasises communal and national trajectories as the origin-context; the NT epistolary context (Chars 2, 6) emphasises the structural fallen condition as origin. Char 4's Deuteronomic context emphasises relational-proximity and covenant exposure as origin. These context-dependent variations are consistent with the observations of each characteristic's own T2.9.3 findings, and at cluster scope confirm that the M10b characteristics' origins are socially and contextually embedded rather than purely individual-constitutional.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes. The Levitical context (the dominant origin context in the 133 verses) is comprehensively bodily and material. The NT akathartos categorical context (M10c-B-VCG-05) shows a shift: the origin of the "unclean" category at Act 10:14/28 is the conscience-level conviction formed by the categorical system — the origin of the functional unclean status is no longer bodily contact but categorical learned judgment. God's word then overturns that inner categorical origin: "what God has made clean, do not call unclean" (Act 10:28). The 1Cor 7:14 use shows yet another origin: covenantal-relational status (sanctifying influence of the believing spouse) as the origin of the clean/unclean status for children and spouses. The origin thus moves across the Testaments from primarily bodily/material to including categorical-conscience and relational-covenantal origins.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes. The Hebrew prophetic register (VCG-01: Job 14:4, Isa 64:6) frames origin as constitutional — the human condition as such is the unclean source. The Pauline epistolary register (VCG-02) frames origin as habitual-desire and God's judicial abandonment. The Corinthian epistolary register (VCG-03: 1Cor 8:7) frames origin as formative context and conscience-vulnerability. The Revelation apocalyptic register (VCG-04: Rev 16:13, 17:4, 18:2) frames origin as cosmic corruption — the characteristic appearing in spiritual beings sourced in darkness. The origin shifts from personal-constitutional (Job), to societal-moral (Isa 64:6), to habitual-volitional (Pauline), to contextual (1Cor), to cosmic (Revelation), reflecting the breadth of the characteristic's domain.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes. The legal-covenantal context (VCG-01: Lev 18, Num 5, Deu 24) frames origin in specific volitional sexual acts. The prophetic context (VCG-02: Ezekiel) frames origin in corporate spiritual whoredom and idolatrous desire across generations. The narratival context (VCG-01: Gen 34) frames origin in violent personal violation. The lament context (VCG-05: Lam 1:17/4:15) frames origin in the accumulated corporate defilement whose consequences have arrived as exile. The origin shifts in mode (individual volitional act vs corporate sustained pattern) and time-frame (single event vs generational accumulation) across the corpus.

**[CHAR-4]** S — The 21-verse corpus does not evidence different mechanisms of origin across contexts. All 21 verses share the same origin pattern: an external unclean spirit inhabiting a person. The mechanism is the same whether in a synagogue (Mar 1:23), among tombs (Mar 5:2), a child (Mar 7:25, Luk 9:42), or many persons (Act 5:16, Act 8:7). The consistency of the origin mechanism across all contexts confirms the characteristic as purely externally-generated.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Characteristics 1, 2, and 3 show significant origin-context variation; Characteristic 4 does not. Characteristic 1: origin shifts across the Testaments from primarily bodily-material (Levitical corpus) to categorical-conscience (Act 10:14/28) and relational-covenantal (1Cor 7:14) — the origin of what constitutes "unclean" is itself revised by new-covenant revelation. Characteristic 2: origin shifts from constitutional-existential (Hebrew prophetic — Job 14:4, Isa 64:6) through habitual-volitional (Pauline — Rom 1:24, Eph 4:19) through contextual-formative (1Cor 8:7) to cosmic (Revelation — Rev 16:13). Characteristic 3: origin shifts from individual-volitional-sexual (legal corpus — Lev 18, Num 5) through corporate-generational-idolatrous (Ezekiel) through violent-personal (Gen 34) to accumulated-exilic (Lamentations). Characteristic 4: origin is consistent across all contexts. The cluster-level pattern: the three person-generated characteristics (1-3) show origin-context variation reflecting the breadth and diversity of the scriptural witness to each domain; the externally-imposed characteristic (4) does not vary because its mechanism is structurally simple and agent-determined rather than context-sensitive.

questions.question_text: Does the characteristic move across constitutional levels (spirit→soul→body), or onto the person from an external source — including another spirit (angelic or adversarial) — or in another direction; and if so in what sequence or pattern? If no movement, record none.

findings.session_b_note:
Yes — the sb_classification (Spirit-soul interface) names the primary constitutional movement, and the data supports a full movement sequence:

**Spirit → Soul:** Divine forgiveness (spirit-level origin, divine act) is received by the human person at the soul level — the inner standing before God is restored (group 879-001), the condition changes. OBS-064-002: "the received divine forgiveness genuinely transforms the soul's relational orientation." Movement: from the divine spirit-level through to the human soul-level.

**Soul → Outward expression:** The soul-level reception generates outward acts — the horizontal extension of forgiveness to others (group 5377-002), the bodily expressions of the woman in Luk 7:47 (weeping, anointing). Movement: from the soul-level inner reception outward.

findings.session_b_note:
Yes — the data reveals a clear constitutional movement pattern, running from the body's interior upward through the soul, and then outward through action. This is the most structurally significant finding of T2.

The movement sequence, assembled from the vocabulary:

**Stage 1 — Somatic arousal (body level):** The gut stirs (splanchnizō), the compassion grows warm (ni.chum — Hos 11:8), the heart recoils (lev — Hos 11:8). These are body-level and heart-level events — involuntary, pre-volitional, arising from the deepest constitutional interior.

**Stage 2 — Soul engagement:** The somatic arousal engages the soul-level disposition — either activating the already-present ra.chum / chesed / sumpathēs quality (if it is formed) or producing a one-time response of mercy. The chesed vocabulary names this soul-level engagement as the constitutive quality that gives the somatic arousal its character direction.

**Stage 3 — Volitional engagement:** The compassion-movement reaches the will. In the judicial-prohibition contexts (chus — "your eye shall not pity"), this is the point at which compassion can be overridden. In the Synoptic Gospel pattern, it is the point at which action is determined: "stretched out his hand and touched him" (Mark 1:41).

**Stage 4 — Outward action:** Eleēmosunē (almsgiving), physical touch (Mark 1:41), raising the dead (Luke 7:15), feeding the crowd (Matt 15:32). Compassion arrives at its constitutional destination in outward action. SD-016 names this as the three-stage model: visceral stirring → mercy orientation → concrete act.

findings.session_b_note:
Yes — the verse evidence supports a constitutional movement sequence that has not been explicitly assembled before:

1. **Spirit level**: The primary site of the contrite condition — spirit is named first and most frequently (Psa 34:18; Isa 57:15; Psa 51:17; Isa 66:2)
2. **Heart level**: Consistently alongside spirit — the heart is the second constitutional level engaged (Psa 51:17 — "broken and contrite heart"; Isa 57:15 — "revive the heart of the contrite"; Psa 38:8 — "tumult of my heart")
3. **Soul level**: Evidenced in the most severe anguish mode (Psa 143:3 — nefesh crushed to the ground) — the crushing penetrates to the innermost existential level
4. **Body level**: Bones broken (Psa 51:8), groaning expressed (Psa 38:8), trembling (Isa 66:2) — the constitutional movement reaches to somatic expression

The sequence is inward-to-outward in one sense (spirit → heart → soul → body) but the verse evidence presents it as simultaneous rather than strictly sequential at every level. What can be said: the deeper the crushing, the more constitutional levels are implicated.

*New finding: the full constitutional scope of contrition — spirit, heart, soul, body — has not been assembled as a movement sequence in prior analysis. The data supports this four-level constitutional picture when all verse evidence is read together.*

findings.session_b_note:
Yes. The evidence supports constitutional movement across all three levels, though not uniformly for every fellowship mode.

**Spirit to soul:** The divine nature participation sequence (2Pe 1:4) — God grants promises → escape from corruption → participation in divine nature — implies a movement from the divine-offered (spirit level) through the inner moral condition (soul level) to ontological transformation. The escape from corruption is a soul-level change enabled by spirit-level access.

**Soul to body:** The disciplinary wounding sequence (Pro 20:30) — blows → wound → cleansing of innermost parts — moves from the somatic event (body) inward to the moral core (soul/heart). This is body-to-soul movement.

**Spirit to soul to body:** The Phili 3:10 trajectory — knowing Christ (spirit-level relational knowledge) → sharing sufferings (somatic engagement) → conformity to his death (somatic-constitutional) → resurrection (return to spirit-level transformation) — traces a full constitutional circuit: spirit orientation → somatic participation → transformational output at spirit level.

**New finding:** Fellowship is one of the few characteristics in the programme for which the verse evidence establishes constitutional movement across all three levels (spirit, soul, body) in a traceable pattern. The full circuit is most visible in the Phili 3:10 trajectory. This has significant implications for Session D synthesis about fellowship's structural role in the inner-being framework.

findings.finding_value: T2 as a whole reveals that goodness has a comprehensive multi-level constitutional presence — from Spirit-level origin through soul-orientation, heart-engagement, and mind-evaluative functions to outward expression — but with a marked asymmetry in evidence quality. Spirit-level (Q&A-037-039), soul-level (Q&A-040-041), and heart-level (Q&A-043-044) are all substantively evidenced. Mind-level is partially evidenced through cognitive dimensions. Body-level is thin — the gladness-of-heart compound (tov-lev) and the taste-and-see perceptual metaphor are the somatic markers, but no constitutional body deposit is evidenced (T2.8 silent). The most structurally significant T2 finding is the six-step constitutional movement (Q&A-064): Spirit-level origin → soul reorientation → heart engagement → volitional alignment → agentive resolve → outward expression. This movement is top-down and outward, with no evidenced reversal from body to inner being. Goodness is constitutionally deep but does not leave a somatic deposit.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-067-008: What T1 named (goodness as primarily a quality — a settled characterological property) is confirmed and located by T2. The constitutional movement identified in T2 (six-step: Spirit → soul → heart → v…
findings.finding_value: What T1 named (goodness as primarily a quality — a settled characterological property) is confirmed and located by T2. The constitutional movement identified in T2 (six-step: Spirit → soul → heart → volition → agency → expression) explains how a characterological quality (T1's finding) is not a static property but a dynamic disposition that moves through the person from its deepest level outward. T1's four constituent poles (ontological, moral-character, experiential, volitional) map directly onto T2's constitutional levels: the ontological pole operates at Spirit-level origin; the moral-character pole at soul and heart; the experiential pole at soul-seeking; the volitional pole at the volitional step. The two tiers read together reveal that goodness is a quality that is simultaneously constitutionally located and constitutionally mobile — it has its deepest root at the Spirit level and its expression at the social-ethical level.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-067-016: T2's constitutional movement (six-step sequence) and T5's transformation sequences (positive arc and moral awareness arc) describe the same developmental reality from two analytical perspectives. T2 d…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional movement (six-step sequence) and T5's transformation sequences (positive arc and moral awareness arc) describe the same developmental reality from two analytical perspectives. T2 describes where goodness moves in the person (constitutional levels); T5 describes how goodness moves the person (mechanisms and sequences). The six-step T2 sequence (Spirit → soul → heart → volition → agency → expression) is the constitutional substrate through which T5's transformation arcs operate. T5's three mechanisms (encounter, Spirit-infusion, recognition-confrontation) are the relational/contextual triggers that activate the T2 constitutional movement. Together: the T2 constitutional architecture provides the vertical structure through which T5's developmental arcs run. Formation is not a disembodied process — it is the progressive deepening of goodness through the constitutional levels identified in T2.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-067-017: T2 confirmed that goodness's origin is singular (God) but its delivery is multiple (encounter, word, Spirit). T6 confirmed that goodness's vocabulary is distributed across multiple registries through …
findings.finding_value: T2 confirmed that goodness's origin is singular (God) but its delivery is multiple (encounter, word, Spirit). T6 confirmed that goodness's vocabulary is distributed across multiple registries through shared root families. These two findings are structurally related: the vocabulary distribution (T6.4 — TOV root to R103, AGATHO root to R65, CHRESTO root to R99) reflects the multiple delivery mechanisms of T2. The TOV root's distribution to love (R103) corresponds to the encounter-relational delivery mechanism; the AGATHO root's distribution to generosity (R65) corresponds to the action-expression level of the constitutional movement; the CHRESTO root's shared presence across R67 and R99 corresponds to the dispositional-kindness register of chrēstotēs. The vocabulary distribution is not arbitrary — it tracks the constitutional and relational architecture of how goodness operates and reaches the person. The single-origin of goodness (T2.9.2) is expressed through a vocabulary distributed across the programme's relational-characteristic cluster, reflecting the multiple pathways of the one goodness.

findings.finding_value: Love is the programme's most constitutionally comprehensive characteristic — it occupies all five constitutional levels simultaneously: spirit-sourced (implied via Spirit-as-agent, Rom 5:5, Gal 5:22), soul-located (Song 5:6 — soul failing at beloved's absence; Mat 22:37 — love with all your soul; Joh 15:13 — laying down the soul), heart-inscribed (Pro 3:3; Rom 5:5 infused into hearts), mind-engaged (Mat 22:37 — love with all your mind; Joh 15:15 — love as knowledge-sharing), and body-expressed (kiss, embrace, tears, womb-movement across multiple groups). The constitutional movement pattern is consistently downward: Spirit origin → heart reception → soul experience → body expression. Love's heart-inscription (Pro 3:3) is the closest evidence to a constitutional deposit — the metaphorical writing of chesed into the heart's deepest register produces a lasting dispositional quality (the chasid person-type). The primary finding: love is not confined to any single constitutional level but operates across all levels in an integrated movement from deepest to most outward. This comprehensive constitutional architecture is consistent with love's function as the programme's organising characteristic.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-103-001: Love's definition and its constitutional location are mutually illuminating. The definition identifies love as disposition + act + condition operating through directed attachment toward an object. The…
findings.finding_value: Love's definition and its constitutional location are mutually illuminating. The definition identifies love as disposition + act + condition operating through directed attachment toward an object. The constitutional mapping shows where this triple operation is located: the disposition is heart-inscribed (Pro 3:3) and spirit-sourced (implied via Rom 5:5), stable across constitutional levels; the act is will-engaged (Mat 22:37 — commanded) and soul-mobilised (Joh 15:13 — soul laid down); the condition of being-loved is received at the heart level (Rom 5:5 — poured in) and experienced at the soul level (Zep 3:17 — quieting). The constitutional movement pattern (Spirit → heart → soul → body) maps directly onto the definition's three registers: the deepest dispositional origin (spirit/heart) grounds the stable orientation; the soul-level is where love is experienced as feeling; the body-level is where act and condition become visible. Together: the constitutional location analysis confirms that love's definition is not a surface account but a constitutional claim — love operates at every depth of the inner person, which is precisely what the 'whole heart, soul, and mind' commandment (Mat 22:37) requires.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-103-008: The constitutional location data and the relational interface data converge on the same structural claim: love's inner depth is its relational reach. The deeper love is constitutionally (heart-inscrib…
findings.finding_value: The constitutional location data and the relational interface data converge on the same structural claim: love's inner depth is its relational reach. The deeper love is constitutionally (heart-inscribed, soul-constitutive, Spirit-sourced), the further its relational reach — from neighbour-love (soul-level reciprocal) to enemy-love (will-level against grain) to divine love (Spirit-level transcendent). The constitutional movement pattern (Spirit → heart → soul → body — Q&A-056) maps onto the relational directional pattern: divine love enters at the deepest constitutional level (Spirit, heart) and produces relational acts at the outermost level (community legibility, bodily expression). The GOD→HUMAN axis operates at the constitutional depth where love is received (heart-infusion — Rom 5:5); the HUMAN→GOD axis requires total constitutional mobilisation (Mat 22:37 — all heart, soul, mind); the HUMAN→HUMAN axis is the outward bodily expression of the internal constitutional reality. Constitutional and relational are thus not two separate dimensions of love but the inside and outside of the same movement.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-103-009: The formation process in T5 works precisely through the constitutional locations identified in T2. Spirit infusion (Rom 5:5) enters at the deepest level (Spirit → heart), establishing love's constitut…
findings.finding_value: The formation process in T5 works precisely through the constitutional locations identified in T2. Spirit infusion (Rom 5:5) enters at the deepest level (Spirit → heart), establishing love's constitutional ground. Obedience-pathway purifies the soul (1Pe 1:22) — the soul-level constitutional location is the target of formation's clearing work. Training in the community (Tit 2:4) operates at the body-habit level — forming love through repeated communal acts that imprint the body's relational patterns. The heart-inscription of chesed (Pro 3:3) is the formation's goal-state: love sufficiently formed that it is constitutionally inscribed, no longer needing to be generated afresh for each act. The eschatological trajectory (perfect love, direct knowledge, pleasures forevermore) describes the perfection of the constitutional architecture: all levels operating without obstruction, permanently, toward the proper object. Constitutional location is thus not a static description but a dynamic formation target: each level can be more or less formed in love, and the formation process addresses each level in sequence.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-111-002: T2 reveals mercy as a whole-person constitutional reality. No single level contains it: mercy originates at the spirit-soul interface, operates on the soul (addressing the nephesh-guilt), engages the …
findings.finding_value: T2 reveals mercy as a whole-person constitutional reality. No single level contains it: mercy originates at the spirit-soul interface, operates on the soul (addressing the nephesh-guilt), engages the heart through the visceral compassion vocabulary (splanchna), engages the mind through the memory-erasure mechanism (Heb 8:12), and operates through the body as both the medium of mercy-seeking (embodied posture) and the mechanism of mercy's effect (blood-atonement). The triadic constitutional movement (Q&A-065): inner disposition → soul-transformation → embodied expression. The key finding reading T2 as a whole is the receiving-before-generating origin structure (Q&A-062): mercy cannot be generated from within the person but must be received from outside and then expressed through the constitutional architecture. Body deposit: none. T5.7: formally closed.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-111-008: T1 defines mercy as a four-element structure (disposition, mechanism, petition-response, spatial locus) and T2 maps mercy's constitutional architecture across all levels. Reading T1 and T2 together: t…
findings.finding_value: T1 defines mercy as a four-element structure (disposition, mechanism, petition-response, spatial locus) and T2 maps mercy's constitutional architecture across all levels. Reading T1 and T2 together: the constitutional location of mercy precisely maps the four definitional elements. The felt disposition (T1) corresponds to the spirit-soul interface location (T2). The institutional mechanism (T1) corresponds to the soul-level atoning operation (T2). The petition-response (T1) corresponds to the embodied seeking and heart-level engagement (T2). The spatial locus (T1) corresponds to the mercy seat as constitutional-institutional anchor (T2). T1's definitional complexity is explained by T2's constitutional complexity — mercy's definition is complex because its constitutional location is complex.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-111-014: T2 maps mercy's constitutional locations (soul, mind, heart, body, spirit-soul interface) and T3 maps its faculty engagements. Reading together: the constitutional locations and the faculty engagement…
findings.finding_value: T2 maps mercy's constitutional locations (soul, mind, heart, body, spirit-soul interface) and T3 maps its faculty engagements. Reading together: the constitutional locations and the faculty engagements are co-extensive. Soul-level location (T2) corresponds to conscience and moral evaluation faculty engagement (T3) — the soul is where guilt resides and where conscience/moral evaluation operate. Mind-level location (T2, memory-erasure) corresponds to memory faculty engagement (T3, asymmetric memory structure). Heart/splanchna location (T2) corresponds to affect faculty (T3). The receiving-before-generating origin (T2) corresponds to relational capacity as foundational enabler (T3.11). T2 and T3 together: constitutional location and faculty engagement are two descriptions of the same inner-being reality — where mercy operates constitutionally (T2) is where it activates faculties (T3).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-111-016: T2's constitutional architecture (spirit-soul interface origin, soul-level operation, embodied expression) maps directly onto T5's formative sequences (the four inner-state sequences in Q&A-128 all sh…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional architecture (spirit-soul interface origin, soul-level operation, embodied expression) maps directly onto T5's formative sequences (the four inner-state sequences in Q&A-128 all show external mercy entering through the soul level and producing inner-state transformation). Reading T2 and T5 together: the constitutional route mercy travels (T2's triadic movement — OBS-111-065) is the same route the formative sequence takes (T5's external-to-internal pattern — Q&A-129). Mercy enters the constitutional architecture from outside (received) and then traverses spirit-soul-body in its transformative work. The receiving-before-generating origin (T2) means the formative developmental arc (T5) always begins with external mercy received, not internal mercy generated.

findings.session_b_note: Yes — the sequence in Psa 51:8 establishes movement across levels: divine action breaks bones (body level) → inner being is crushed (spirit/heart level) → the person is invited to rejoice (body and spirit together in restoration). Isa 57:15 names the reverse movement: God revives spirit and heart (spirit-soul level) → the person becomes receptive (character/relational level). *New finding: contrition moves downward (from divine confrontation through spirit to body) and the resolution moves upward (from spirit/heart through reviving to relational restoration) — two opposing constitutional movements framing the contrition event.* OBS-030-045, OBS-030-046, OBS-030-055.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-030-002: T2 establishes that contrition operates at the deepest constitutional level (spirit as primary locus) with secondary engagement at heart, soul, and body. The constitutional portrait is comprehensive: …
findings.finding_value: T2 establishes that contrition operates at the deepest constitutional level (spirit as primary locus) with secondary engagement at heart, soul, and body. The constitutional portrait is comprehensive: spirit broken at the innermost level, heart broken at the moral-evaluative level, nephesh crushed at the whole-self level, and bones as the somatic expression of the inner breaking. What T2 reveals as a whole is the embodied depth of contrition — it is not a disembodied inner experience but a constitutional event that traverses all levels of the person. The bidirectional constitutional movement (downward through divine confrontation, upward through reviving) is the structural frame within which contrition functions: it reaches the bottom and creates the conditions for movement back upward. The T2.8 finding (no body deposit) means contrition does not leave a permanent somatic trace — it is a passing constitutional event, not a permanent constitutional mark.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-030-008: The definition tier (T1) establishes contrition as a settled inner condition produced by encounter; the constitutional tier (T2) maps where that condition lives and how it moves. Together they reveal …
findings.finding_value: The definition tier (T1) establishes contrition as a settled inner condition produced by encounter; the constitutional tier (T2) maps where that condition lives and how it moves. Together they reveal that contrition's definition is constitutionally grounded: the characteristic cannot be understood apart from its constitutional loci (spirit and heart as primary sites) and its constitutional movement (downward crushing, upward reviving). The three-mode structure (T1) maps precisely onto the constitutional evidence (T2): the penitential mode is primarily spirit-level; the anguish mode is primarily soul-level (nephesh crushed to the ground); the substitutionary mode is primarily somatic (bodily wounds). Definition and constitutional location are structurally co-determining for this characteristic.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-030-015: The constitutional tier (T2) establishes that contrition originates in the encounter between divine holiness and human moral condition (T2.9) and moves constitutionally downward through the person; th…
findings.finding_value: The constitutional tier (T2) establishes that contrition originates in the encounter between divine holiness and human moral condition (T2.9) and moves constitutionally downward through the person; the relational tier (T4) establishes that the primary relational direction is vertical (human before God). The constitutional origin (external, from divine holiness) and the relational direction (vertical, toward God) are structurally aligned: contrition's constitutional ground explains its relational asymmetry. Because contrition originates from divine-human encounter, its primary relational interface is necessarily with God — the one whose holiness generated the encounter. The vertical asymmetry in T4 is not arbitrary but constitutionally determined by T2's origin analysis.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-030-016: The constitutional tier (T2) confirms no body deposit (T2.8); the formative tier (T5) closes T5.7 accordingly. Together T2 and T5 reveal that contrition's formative work is entirely at the spirit-soul…
findings.finding_value: The constitutional tier (T2) confirms no body deposit (T2.8); the formative tier (T5) closes T5.7 accordingly. Together T2 and T5 reveal that contrition's formative work is entirely at the spirit-soul level — it produces characterological change (lowliness, word-permeability) without leaving a somatic residue. The constitutional movement (T2.10 — downward through crushing, upward through reviving) maps precisely onto the formative sequence (T5.2 — crushing → contrite posture → divine reviving). T2's constitutional account and T5's formative account are describing the same event from two perspectives: T2 maps the space; T5 maps the time. The absence of a body deposit (T2.8/T5.7) means contrition's formation is renewable — the person can undergo the crushing-and-reviving cycle repeatedly without constitutional accumulation, which is consistent with T5's account of contrition as a recurring formative event.

findings.session_b_note: Yes — Pro 20:30 establishes a body-to-inner movement: physical strokes → cleansing of innermost parts. 2Pe 1:4 implies outer-to-inner: escape from external corruption → inner participation in divine nature. OBS-062-039, OBS-062-058.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-062-002: T2 reveals fellowship's constitutional location is distributed across levels according to its mode: existential mode (soul/nephesh level — Ecc 9:4), companionship mode (heart level — Psa 119:63, Jer 1…
findings.finding_value: T2 reveals fellowship's constitutional location is distributed across levels according to its mode: existential mode (soul/nephesh level — Ecc 9:4), companionship mode (heart level — Psa 119:63, Jer 13:23), desire-driven mode (desire-faculty — 2Pe 1:4), suffering mode (somatic — Pro 20:30, Isa 53:5). The deepest mode (ontological — 2Pe 1:4) implies spirit-level but this is inferential rather than explicit. T2's most significant finding is the desire-faculty as the constitutional engine directing fellowship: desire determines the fellowship object, and the fellowship object determines the constitutional formation. The body-deposit question (T2.8) remains open — the wound-mark as a persisting joining-trace is the nearest evidence, but its programme-relevance is uncertain.

findings.session_b_note: Yes — Luk 7:47 establishes a constitutive movement: forgiveness received → love produced. The movement is from the state of being forgiven (relational-status change) through the inner being to the emergence of love-orientation. Jer 31:34 establishes: forgiveness → direct knowledge of God. The constitutional movement is from guilt-bearing (blocked relational condition) through forgiveness to freed inner access. OBS-064-017, OBS-064-029.
