findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-064-002: T2 reveals that forgiveness engages multiple constitutional levels but with a distinctive constitutional pattern. The heart is the one explicitly named locus — Mat 18:35 ("from your heart") names the …
findings.finding_value: T2 reveals that forgiveness engages multiple constitutional levels but with a distinctive constitutional pattern. The heart is the one explicitly named locus — Mat 18:35 ("from your heart") names the heart as the required depth of genuine forgiveness-giving. The cognition-faculty (Jer 31:34 — "remember no more"; "they shall know me") is the most clearly evidenced constitutional engagement alongside the heart. The somatic compassion faculty (splagchnizomai — Mat 18:27) is the named somatic-affective origin-point of the forgiving act. Spirit and soul levels are inferred from the guilt-forgiveness structural relationship and the Spirit's mediating role (Mar 3:29, Joh 20:23) rather than explicitly named. The body-deposit question is data-silent (T2.8); T5.7 closes formally. The constitutional movement is explicit (Luk 7:47 — guilt-bearing → forgiveness received → love generated; Jer 31:34 — forgiveness → direct knowledge of God). T2's key finding: the constitutional structure of forgiveness is act-centred, not state-centred — it is a constitutional event (the moment of release) that produces constitutional consequences (love, reverence, direct access).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-008: T1 establishes forgiveness as an act; T2 maps where the act is constitutionally located. The four modes (T1) each engage different constitutional levels (T2): covenantal-objective mode engages no name…
findings.finding_value: T1 establishes forgiveness as an act; T2 maps where the act is constitutionally located. The four modes (T1) each engage different constitutional levels (T2): covenantal-objective mode engages no named inner-being locus (external mechanism); divine relational-personal mode engages the full constitutional range (spirit, heart, cognition — via the access-postures of faith, repentance, confession); human horizontal mode explicitly requires the heart (Mat 18:35); intercessory mode requires the dependence-posture at the constitutional level of the plea. The somatic compassion origin-point (T2.5 — splagchnizomai) is the constitutional expression of the volitional-release act (T1.4.1 — the act must be chosen). Definition and constitutional location are co-determining: the mode of forgiveness determines which constitutional level is engaged.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-014: T2's constitutional locations map onto T3's faculty engagements. The heart-locus (T2.3 — Mat 18:35) corresponds to T3's volition, moral evaluation, and conscience faculties — all heart-level. The cogn…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional locations map onto T3's faculty engagements. The heart-locus (T2.3 — Mat 18:35) corresponds to T3's volition, moral evaluation, and conscience faculties — all heart-level. The cognition-locus (T2.4 — Jer 31:34) corresponds to T3's cognition and memory faculty engagements. The somatic-compassion locus (T2.5 — splagchnizomai) corresponds to T3's affect faculty at its somatic depth. The constitutional movement (T2.10 — guilt-bearing → forgiveness → love) is the sequence in which T3's faculties are engaged: conscience identifies the guilt → volition releases the claim → affect produces the love-response. Constitutional location determines faculty engagement sequence.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-016: T2's constitutional movement (guilt-bearing → forgiveness → love → capacity to extend) is T5's formation sequence described at the constitutional level. T2's finding that the constitutional event prod…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional movement (guilt-bearing → forgiveness → love → capacity to extend) is T5's formation sequence described at the constitutional level. T2's finding that the constitutional event produces further inner states (love, direct access to God) is T5's transitional-formative account. The body-deposit gap (T2.8 — data silent; T5.7 closed) means the formation is entirely inner-constitutional — the formative event leaves no somatic residue, which is consistent with T5's finding that forgiveness is transitional rather than permanently marking. The eschatological telos (T5.6 — Jer 31:34) is the permanent constitutional state that present forgiveness-events anticipate.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-002: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level …
findings.finding_value: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level (chesed as covenantal-soul character), heart-level (Hos 11:8 — "my heart recoils"), and somatic-level (re.chem, splanchnon) are all richly evidenced. The constitutional architecture is bottom-up: the womb and entrails are the originating ground; the soul and heart are the engagement points; the act is the constitutional expression. Four body-part functions are identified: constitutive (womb — the generative image of compassion), expressive (gut — the felt movement), indicative (Synoptic pattern — splanchnizō signals the compassion-event), and mediating (heart in Hos 11:8 — the deliberative locus where compassion and judgment contend). The four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) is uniquely evidenced in this registry — consistently inside-out and bottom-up. T2.8 established no body deposit; T5.7 is formally closed. The constitutional portrait confirms the sb_classification (soul-body interface) and extends it: compassion is the most somatically grounded characteristic in the programme, with its originating logic residing in the body's deepest interior.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-008: T1's four-kind structure (character quality, inner event, condition of object, externalised act) maps precisely onto T2's constitutional levels. The character-quality kind (ra.chum — dispositional com…
findings.finding_value: T1's four-kind structure (character quality, inner event, condition of object, externalised act) maps precisely onto T2's constitutional levels. The character-quality kind (ra.chum — dispositional compassionate character) operates at the soul level (T2.2 — chesed as soul-character). The inner-event kind (splanchnizō — the moment of being-moved) operates at the somatic level (T2.6 — the gut as the site of the stirring). The condition-of-object kind (eleeinos — the pitiable state) is the constitutional trigger that activates the somatic-constitutional movement. The externalised-act kind is the constitutional endpoint of T2.10's four-stage movement sequence. T1's definition and T2's constitutional account are co-determining: the characteristic cannot be adequately defined without specifying the constitutional levels at which its four kinds operate.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-014: T2's four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) maps directly onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The somatic-arousal s…
findings.finding_value: T2's four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) maps directly onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The somatic-arousal stage (T2.6 — gut stirring, splanchnizō) corresponds to T3.1's perceptive-trigger stage (sight activates the somatic response) and T3.4's affect stage (the stirring is the affective movement). The soul-engagement stage (T2.2 — chesed as soul-character) corresponds to T3.8 moral evaluation (the soul assesses the need) and T3.9 conscience (the conscience activates the response). The volitional-engagement stage (T2.3 — heart-locus as deliberative site) corresponds to T3.6 volition (the will directs the action). The outward-action stage corresponds to T3.7 agency. T2 and T3 describe the same movement sequence from two perspectives: T2 maps the constitutional levels; T3 maps the faculties active at each level.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-015: T2's constitutional origin analysis (somatic-relational-covenantal triple ground) and T4's relational direction analysis are structurally aligned. The somatic origin (womb, gut) grounds the cross-boun…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional origin analysis (somatic-relational-covenantal triple ground) and T4's relational direction analysis are structurally aligned. The somatic origin (womb, gut) grounds the cross-boundary relational direction in T4: splanchnizō's somatic immediacy is precisely what enables it to cross covenantal boundaries — the gut-movement toward the suffering other precedes any covenantal assessment of the relationship. The covenantal origin (chesed) grounds the within-bond sustaining direction in T4. The constitutional origin therefore predicts the relational direction: somatic = cross-boundary; covenantal = within-bond. T2's soul-body interface classification explains T4's scope-by-need finding: because compassion originates at the soul-body interface (before covenantal-rational assessment), its scope is determined by the pre-rational recognition of need rather than the post-rational assessment of covenantal standing.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-016: T2's four-stage constitutional movement (somatic arousal → soul → volition → action) and T5's three mechanisms of change (encounter/sudden, covenantal-sustaining/gradual, participatory-ontological) ar…
findings.finding_value: T2's four-stage constitutional movement (somatic arousal → soul → volition → action) and T5's three mechanisms of change (encounter/sudden, covenantal-sustaining/gradual, participatory-ontological) are structurally complementary. T2 describes the movement within a single compassion-event; T5 describes how that event accumulates into character over time. The encounter/sudden mechanism (T5) corresponds to the full four-stage sequence of T2 in a single instance. The covenantal-sustaining mechanism (T5) corresponds to the repeated operation of the somatic-soul pathway (T2.2 — soul-level chesed as the sustaining character) over time. The participatory-ontological mechanism (T5) corresponds to the constitutional direction T2 identifies but leaves at spirit-level gap: if the deepest formation is participatory-ontological, the spirit-level dimension (T2.1 — entirely silent) may be where this operates — a convergent gap from two tiers.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-018: T2's constitutional levels are each carried by specific vocabulary families in T7. The somatic-body level (T2.6 — gut, womb) is carried by the RACHAM/SPLANCHN root families — the body's interior as th…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional levels are each carried by specific vocabulary families in T7. The somatic-body level (T2.6 — gut, womb) is carried by the RACHAM/SPLANCHN root families — the body's interior as the etymological ground of both. The soul-character level (T2.2) is carried by the CHASAD family — chesed as the settled covenantal character disposition. The heart-deliberative level (T2.3) is evidenced most richly in Hos 11:8 (T7's primary anchor for divine compassion). T7's vocabulary arc (womb to almsgiving) traverses exactly the constitutional range T2 maps: from the most interior somatic level (womb) through the character-soul level to the externalised action level. The dual primary anchor (T7) maps onto T2's constitutional depth: Hos 11:8 evidences constitutional depth (heart-level deliberation of compassion over judgment); Luke 10:33 evidences constitutional breadth (the full four-stage movement from sight to action).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-002: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary…
findings.finding_value: T2 produces the clearest constitutional portrait of any characteristic in the current review set. The sb_classification (spirit-soul interface) is confirmed with precision: spirit level is the primary point of reception (Zec 12:10 — spirit of grace poured out), not the point of generation (grace originates with God — T2.9). The soul level is the site of standing (Rom 5:2 — "this grace in which we stand") and identity (1Cor 15:10 — "by the grace of God I am what I am"). The constitutional movement follows the SD021 four-faces model: divine disposition received at spirit level → relational standing established at soul level → specific capacity gifted → character expressed outward. Heart-location is partially evidenced via eusplanchnos (Eph 4:32 — the tenderheartedness that grace produces, reaching the affective-somatic interface). T2.7 produces a new finding: grace operates bidirectionally through the body-soul interface — soul-to-body (inner posture enacted somatically in prostration, fasting, sackcloth) and body-to-soul (somatic enactment deepening and confirming the inner posture). T2.8 remains open (body deposit question unresolved); T5.7 is left open accordingly. The constitutional origin analysis (T2.9) is the most analytically significant T2 finding: grace does not originate in the human constitutional system at any level — it arrives from outside. This is confirmed at T6 as the structural uniqueness of grace: the only characteristic that is not produced by any other inner-being characteristic.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-008: T1's four-kind structure (disposition, standing, capacity, character quality) maps onto T2's constitutional levels. The divine-disposition kind operates at the level of grace's origin (T2.9 — God's ow…
findings.finding_value: T1's four-kind structure (disposition, standing, capacity, character quality) maps onto T2's constitutional levels. The divine-disposition kind operates at the level of grace's origin (T2.9 — God's own disposition; not a human constitutional level). The standing kind operates at the soul level (T2.2 — Rom 5:2 "this grace in which we stand"). The capacity kind operates at the spirit-soul interface — the specific enabling for specific tasks (2Cor 12:9) is received at the deepest level and expressed through specific faculties. The character-quality kind operates at the soul-to-body level (T2.7 — gracious conduct and speech expressing the received inner character outward). T1's constitutional movement finding (SD021 four-faces sequence) is the longitudinal form of T2's spatial map: T2 identifies the constitutional levels; T1 identifies the movement between them.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-014: T2's constitutional movement (spirit reception → soul standing → capacity → character expression) maps onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The spirit-reception stage (T2.1) corresponds to T3.1 (per…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional movement (spirit reception → soul standing → capacity → character expression) maps onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The spirit-reception stage (T2.1) corresponds to T3.1 (perception — grace enabling the inner sight and hearing that receives it). The soul-standing stage (T2.2) corresponds to T3.9 (conscience — grace as the condition within which conscience can operate without destruction) and T3.8 (moral evaluation — the standing produces the clarity of moral self-assessment). The capacity-gifting stage (T2.1 — spirit level) corresponds to T3.7 (agency — capacity given constitutes agency for the task). The character-expression stage (T2.7 — outward through body-soul) corresponds to T3.10 (conscientiousness — the integrated moral-action expression of received grace-character). T2 maps the constitutional space; T3 maps the faculties active at each spatial level; the two tiers describe the same movement from orthogonal perspectives.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-015: T2's origin analysis (grace does not originate in the human constitutional system — it arrives from God) and T4's directional analysis (God-to-human is primary and dominant) are the same finding from …
findings.finding_value: T2's origin analysis (grace does not originate in the human constitutional system — it arrives from God) and T4's directional analysis (God-to-human is primary and dominant) are the same finding from constitutional and relational perspectives respectively. The spirit level as reception point (T2.1) and the God-to-human direction as primary (T4.1) are mutually explanatory: because grace originates with God and is received at the spirit level, the primary relational direction is necessarily God-initiated toward the human spirit. The human-to-God direction (T4.2 — supplication) corresponds to T2.10's constitutional movement in reverse: the soul's recognition of need translates into the somatic enactment of supplication (prostration, fasting, sackcloth), which is T2.7's bidirectional body-soul finding. Constitutional location and relational direction are co-determining.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-016: T2's constitutional movement (SD021 sequence: disposition → standing → capacity → character) and T5's five formation mechanisms describe the same formation arc from spatial and temporal perspectives. …
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional movement (SD021 sequence: disposition → standing → capacity → character) and T5's five formation mechanisms describe the same formation arc from spatial and temporal perspectives. T2 identifies the constitutional levels through which grace moves; T5 identifies the mechanisms by which grace moves through each level in different contexts. The encounter mechanism (T5 — sudden specific relational event) produces the spirit-level reception (T2.1 — the initial point of arrival). The word mechanism (T5 — Act 20:32 — grace through proclaimed word) produces the soul-standing establishment (T2.2 — the word's sustained effect on the person's constitutive condition). The mediated-transformation mechanism (T5 — tenderheartedness → forgiving — Eph 4:32, SD030) corresponds to T2.7's bidirectional body-soul finding: the inner transformation mediates outward through the body-soul interface. T2.8's open question (body deposit) and T5.7's open status are formally aligned — both pending further investigation.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-017: T2's constitutional origin finding (grace does not originate in the human constitutional system) and T6's structural uniqueness finding (grace is not produced by any other inner-being characteristic) …
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional origin finding (grace does not originate in the human constitutional system) and T6's structural uniqueness finding (grace is not produced by any other inner-being characteristic) are the same finding from constitutional and structural perspectives. They confirm each other from different analytical directions: T2 establishes that there is no constitutional source for grace within the human person; T6 establishes that there is no characteristic-level source for grace within the programme's inner-being landscape. The vocabulary's structural completeness (T7 — but relevant here as T6.4) reflects this constitutional uniqueness: because grace originates entirely from outside the human system, its vocabulary must encode the full two-sided circuit (giving and receiving) from within a single root, with no gap left for a generative human-side term.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-018: T2's constitutional levels are carried by specific grammatical forms in T7. The spirit-reception level (T2.1) is carried by the perfect passive form of charitoō (kecharitōmenē — the completed act of b…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional levels are carried by specific grammatical forms in T7. The spirit-reception level (T2.1) is carried by the perfect passive form of charitoō (kecharitōmenē — the completed act of being-made-the-object-of-grace, with continuing state) — the most precise grammatical encoding of a constitutional arrival that has permanently changed the person's standing. The soul-standing level (T2.2) is carried by charis as noun (the inhabited state of favour) and chen as the relational standing-in-favour term. The character-expression level is carried by chen in its conduct/speech register (889-003) and charizō in its human-forgiving mode. T7's NT coinage finding (charitoō invented to carry the standing-in-favour concept) is the lexical evidence that T2's spirit-level reception was conceptually unprecedented — no prior vocabulary could name what happened constitutionally when grace-as-standing arrived.

findings.session_b_note: Yes — covenant shows constitutional movement across multiple levels. (1) Divine Spirit → human inner person: 2 Cor 3:6 (Spirit administers the new covenant — OBS-034-061); Isa 59:21 (God's Spirit placed upon the person, God's words placed in the mouth). The new covenant moves from the divine Spirit into the constitutional core of the human person. (2) Inner → somatic (soul → body): the inner covenantal commitment is expressed and enacted through bodily acts — oath (spoken), cutting ritual (bodily enactment — OBS-034-044), blood-shedding (sacrifice), circumcision (bodily inscription — OBS-034-053). The inner disposition moves outward into somatic expression. findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-034-002: T2 as a whole reveals that covenant operates across the full constitutional range of the inner person with no single exclusive location. The heart is the primary site (Q&A-044), the mind is co-located…
findings.finding_value: T2 as a whole reveals that covenant operates across the full constitutional range of the inner person with no single exclusive location. The heart is the primary site (Q&A-044), the mind is co-located (Q&A-047), the soul gives totality of engagement (Q&A-041), the mouth is the expressive-constitutive organ (Q&A-050), and the body participates through blood and circumcision (Q&A-053). The single most structurally significant T2 finding is the constitutional movement shift from OT to NT covenantal mode: OT covenant moves outer→inner→outer; new covenant moves inner→inner→outer (Q&A-066). This movement-shift is the constitutional-level expression of the Sinai-to-new-covenant transformation — it places the origin of covenant faithfulness at the level of God's own interior action within the person rather than the person's compliance with external demand. T2 confirms that covenant is constitutively somatic as well as inner — it cannot be reduced to a purely invisible spiritual reality because it is enacted, sealed, and transmitted through bodily acts and substances.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-034-014: T2 locates covenant in the constitutional organs (heart, mind, soul, mouth, body). T3 reveals which inner faculties operate within and through those locations. The T2 × T3 synthesis: the constitutiona…
findings.finding_value: T2 locates covenant in the constitutional organs (heart, mind, soul, mouth, body). T3 reveals which inner faculties operate within and through those locations. The T2 × T3 synthesis: the constitutional location (T2) and the faculty operation (T3) are not separate realities but different analytical views of the same inner-being reality. The heart (T2) is where the integrating functions of willing, knowing, moral evaluation, and affect operate (T3.6 volition, T3.2 cognition, T3.8 moral evaluation, T3.4 affect). The mind (T2) is where cognition (T3.2) and memory (T3.3) operate. The soul-totality (T2) corresponds to the conscientiousness and relational capacity (T3.10, T3.11) that engage the whole person. The constitutional location and the faculty operation are two descriptions of the same inner reality: location is where the faculty is housed; faculty is what the location does. The new covenant writes on the heart/mind (T2) and thereby transforms cognition toward knowing God (T3.2) — the constitutional location is the mechanism for the faculty transformation.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-099-002: T2 reveals a clear and important constitutional asymmetry for kindness: the heart is its named constitutional site (Pro 3:3 — explicitly inscribed there), while the soul, mind, and body are not named …
findings.finding_value: T2 reveals a clear and important constitutional asymmetry for kindness: the heart is its named constitutional site (Pro 3:3 — explicitly inscribed there), while the soul, mind, and body are not named locations — the soul appears as beneficiary, the mind as instrument, the body as the direction of outward expression. This asymmetry is not a gap in the evidence but a structural feature: kindness is a heart-level characteristic. Its constitutional movement is a coherent downward-outward trajectory — Spirit-formation produces the heart-level disposition, which in turn generates deliberate relational acts. The origin of kindness is triple: divinely initiated (in God's own character), Spirit-mediated (Gal 5:22), and humanly formed (the chasid's character accumulated through covenantal faithfulness). These three are not competing explanations but sequential layers of the same formation process. T2's most significant intra-tier finding: the body-deposit question (T2.8) closes formally — no deposit evidence exists — which confirms that kindness does not transmit generationally through biological means but through covenantal-formative means (Exo 20:6 — "to a thousand generations" = covenantal, not biological).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-008: What kindness is (T1) and where it resides constitutionally (T2) are tightly integrated. T1's working definition — stable inner disposition of loyal goodwill, constituted by faithfulness/compassion/fo…
findings.finding_value: What kindness is (T1) and where it resides constitutionally (T2) are tightly integrated. T1's working definition — stable inner disposition of loyal goodwill, constituted by faithfulness/compassion/forgiveness — is realised at the heart level (T2). The heart is not merely the storage location of kindness but the site where its constituent elements are inscribed as character (Pro 3:3 — "write them on the tablet of your heart"). The T2 constitutional movement pattern (Spirit-formation → heart-inscription → relational disposition → deliberate acts) maps directly onto T1's three modes (Spirit formation / deliberate act / dispositional orientation) — the movement pattern is the mechanism by which the T1 disposition comes into being. The T1 finding that kindness is composite (faithfulness + justice + compassion + forgiveness) is structurally consistent with T2's finding that it is a heart-level characteristic: the heart in Scripture is precisely the site where complex moral orientation is integrated — not a single emotion but the whole-person covenantal direction.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-014: T2's finding that kindness is located in the heart and moves outward through a constitutional trajectory (Spirit → heart → disposition → acts) connects structurally with T3's finding that kindness eng…
findings.finding_value: T2's finding that kindness is located in the heart and moves outward through a constitutional trajectory (Spirit → heart → disposition → acts) connects structurally with T3's finding that kindness engages the heart's integrating faculties — volition, agency, conscientiousness, moral evaluation, relational capacity, and conscience. The heart in T2 is not merely a location label but the integrating site where all these faculties converge (T2.3.2 — Q&A-045). The constitutional movement pattern in T2 (downward-outward from Spirit to acts) is powered by the multi-faculty engagement that T3 documents: the Spirit-formation produces the heart-level disposition, but the heart exercises volition (choosing to be kind), agency (enacting kindness), and conscientiousness (sustaining kindness reliably over time) to move the disposition into action. The T3 finding that kindness engages taste as the primary perceptive faculty (1Pet 2:3 — "tasted that the Lord is good") is the perceptive entry point for the T2 constitutional movement: the person first tastes divine kindness, then the Spirit forms it in the heart, then the heart's faculties exercise it outward. The two tiers together describe a complete inner-to-outer movement with both location (T2) and mechanism (T3) identified.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-015: T2's constitutional location findings (heart as primary site; Spirit as origin) directly enable and ground T4's relational interface findings. The T4 circuit (divine → human → giving → communal) is no…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional location findings (heart as primary site; Spirit as origin) directly enable and ground T4's relational interface findings. The T4 circuit (divine → human → giving → communal) is not possible without a constitutional base that can receive, hold, and transmit kindness — which is exactly what T2's heart-level location provides. The T2 finding that kindness originates in God's own character (Exo 34:6), is Spirit-mediated into the believer (Gal 5:22), and is inscribed on the heart (Pro 3:3) describes the constitutional preparation of the relational equipment T4 maps. The T2 finding that kindness moves outward (soul → body expression) is the constitutional basis for T4's "giving" direction: the inner character disposition (T2) is what makes outward relational giving (T4) possible. Conversely, T4's relational circuit — and specifically the giving direction grounded in received divine kindness (Eph 4:32) — explains why the T2 constitutional movement runs in the direction it does: the constitutional movement is outward because the characteristic is constitutively relational.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-016: T2 and T5 together reveal the complete formation story for kindness. T2 identifies the target — heart-level character formation as the constitutional site where kindness is deposited and inscribed. T5…
findings.finding_value: T2 and T5 together reveal the complete formation story for kindness. T2 identifies the target — heart-level character formation as the constitutional site where kindness is deposited and inscribed. T5 identifies the mechanisms — Spirit-formation, inscription, and encounter — and the trajectory — from initial reception through formation to chasid identity and eschatological preservation. The T2 finding that no body-deposit exists (T2.8) is structurally consistent with T5's finding that the three formation mechanisms are non-biological: Spirit-formation, inscription, and encounter are all constitutional (spirit/heart level) or relational (encounter), not somatic. The T2 origin finding (triple origin: divine character → Spirit-mediated → humanly formed) maps onto T5's mechanism finding (encounter → inscription → organic Spirit-production) as the same formation process described from different angles — T2 asks where it comes from; T5 asks how it gets there. The eschatological dimension in T5 (the chasid is preserved beyond death) connects with the constitutional permanence finding of T2: a Spirit-formed heart-inscribed character does not dissolve with the body because it was never primarily a body-level deposit.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-017: T2's heart-location finding and T6's structural relationship findings together reveal something about kindness that neither tier alone states: the heart is not only the constitutional site of kindness…
findings.finding_value: T2's heart-location finding and T6's structural relationship findings together reveal something about kindness that neither tier alone states: the heart is not only the constitutional site of kindness but the site where kindness's constituent adjacent characteristics (faithfulness, justice, compassion, forgiveness) are also inscribed. Pro 3:3 — "write them on the tablet of your heart" — names the heart as the inscription site for chesed and emet (faithfulness/truth) together, suggesting that the T6 co-occurrence pattern (kindness + faithfulness as the most persistent pair) has a constitutional basis: they are co-inscribed. This means T6's network of adjacent characteristics is not merely relational or contextual co-occurrence but a constitutional clustering: they share the same constitutional site. The T2 constitutional movement outward (heart → acts) and T6's causal network (kindness → reproduced kindness → sustained covenant relationships) trace the same movement from two angles — T2 names the direction, T6 names the mechanism of propagation.

findings.session_b_note: Yes — and this is the most analytically significant T2 finding for the peace registry. (3) Body → inner (the redemptive reversal): Isa 53:5 — the Servant's wounded body → peace received in others' inner being; the movement against the normal direction, accomplished through the cross.

The human receives peace (T4.4) through the same constitutional locations — the receptive soul (Psa 131:2, T2.2) and the directed mind (Isa 26:3, T2.4) are the reception points. findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-060-002: T2 as a whole reveals that this characteristic has no single constitutional home — it operates across the full spirit-soul-body register through different modes. Spirit is the location in two modes: a…
findings.finding_value: T2 as a whole reveals that this characteristic has no single constitutional home — it operates across the full spirit-soul-body register through different modes. Spirit is the location in two modes: as the object of endowing giving (Neh 9:20) and as the faculty transformed eschatologically (Isa 61:3). Soul (nephesh/nafshi) appears in divine self-reference in the giving-over context (Jer 12:7). Heart (leb) is the faculty where the giving decision is made (Hos 11:8). Hidden inner parts (tukhoth) are the target of wisdom-giving (Job 38:36). Rahamim (visceral compassion) is the inner-being quality that determines giving direction. Body appears as the expressive medium of self-giving (Isa 50:6) and as constituted by breath-giving (Isa 42:5). No constitutional body deposit is confirmed. Three movement patterns — constitutive (spirit→mind), expressive (inner→body), transformative (outside-in→inside renewed→inside-out) — show the characteristic is constitutionally dynamic. What T2 reveals as a whole: this characteristic operates at every constitutional level not because it is superficially distributed but because giving as an inner-being act can reach the spirit (endowing), the heart (deciding), the soul (attaching), the hidden inner parts (forming), and the body (expressing and constituting). It is constitutionally pervasive.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-001: The definition of faithfulness-as-giving (T1 — disposition-in-action, triadic architecture) aligns precisely with the constitutional movement patterns (T2 — constitutive, expressive, transformative). …

The disposition-in-action structure is not abstractly defined: it is enacted through specific constitutional pathways. The constitutive mode (Spirit→mind) corresponds to the endowing operational mode (T1.4). The expressive mode (inner→body) corresponds to the self-giving mode (T1.4). The transformative mode (outside-in→inside renewed→inside-out) corresponds to the eschatological operational mode (T1.4). What neither T1 nor T2 states alone: the definition of this characteristic is constitutionally embedded — each definitional mode maps onto a distinct constitutional movement pattern. The characteristic is not defined independently of its constitutional location; it is what it is through how it moves across the spirit-soul-body structure.

T2 asks where; T3 asks which faculty. Reading them together reveals: the heart (leb, T2.3) is the location of affect-volition integration (T3.4, T3.6) — where compassion (affect) determines giving (volitional act). The hidden inner parts (tukhoth, T2.5) are the constitutional home of the cognitive-formative faculty (T3.2 — the wisdom that is given there). The body (T2.6-7) is the somatic site of agentive expression (T3.7 — agency expresses through the body). The spirit (ruach, T2.1) is both the object of constitutive giving and the faculty whose depletion the eschatological giving addresses — connecting to the agency and relational capacity faculties that cannot operate from a faint spirit. What this pair reveals: constitutional location and faculty engagement are two descriptions of the same inner-being event. The characteristic is located constitutionally precisely where the relevant faculties operate.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-009: The constitutional movement patterns (T2.10 — constitutive spirit→mind, expressive inner→body, transformative outside-in→inside renewed→inside-out) directly correspond to the formation mechanisms (T5.…
findings.finding_value: The constitutional movement patterns (T2.10 — constitutive spirit→mind, expressive inner→body, transformative outside-in→inside renewed→inside-out) directly correspond to the formation mechanisms (T5.3 — gradual formation, encounter/event, sovereign reversal). The constitutive movement (spirit→mind) corresponds to the gradual-formation mechanism: Spirit given to instruct forms inner capacity over time through repeated constitutional deepening. The expressive movement (inner→body) corresponds to the encounter/event mechanism: the covenantal giving event produces an immediate inner-to-outer response (altar-building). The transformative movement (outside-in→inside renewed→inside-out) corresponds to sovereign reversal: the eschatological giving reaches in and renews, then the renewed inner life expresses outward (praise). What this pair reveals: constitutional movement and formative mechanism are two descriptions of the same transformative process. The characteristic forms the person through the constitutional pathways by which it moves — formation is constitutional movement over time.

The hatred at heart level activated a contempt at the evaluation faculty level. The movement is not across body-soul-spirit levels but within the soul from disposition to evaluation and then to volitional intention (Gen 27:41: settled hatred → murderous intention).

The movement from inner cognitive verdict (mind) to heart-level evaluative posture to volitional action (will) to speech expression (mouth) to social contagion (biz.za.von — Est 1:18). Within the soul, contempt moves from cognitive assessment through evaluative heart to expressed behaviour.

From conscience-level response → moral evaluation faculty (confirming the recoil) → maintained distance → bodily expression (spitting, keeping aloof). The movement is from the deepest inner-being response upward through cognitive confirmation and outward through bodily expression.

From the absence of the inner governing framework (God-consciousness removed from the person's operative centre) → absence of restraining character qualities → exercise of unrestrained destructive power → self-harm (Pro 11:17) and eventual divine judgment. The movement is from inner constitutional condition through to external destructive expression and ultimately to the person's own undoing.

From external social designation (others designate the person as shameful) → social delivery (taunts, insults, physical contempt) → inner reception at the heart (Psa 69:20) → restructuring of self-perception (Psa 22:6) → sustained condition of fear and diminishment. The adversary relationship generates a sequence of inner responses: the relational-structural positioning of an adversary → urgency and appeal in the person facing it → vigilance → relief at the adversary's defeat or removal.

From soul-level pleasure in another's destruction → bodily expression (clapping, stamping) → purposive destructive action. The movement is from the soul's inner state outward through the body into active harm.

**[A1 — God Righteousness]** Yes — God's righteousness moves from the divine level to the human level through proclamation (A1-005: declared and witnessed to), through the Messiah (A1-007: divine righteousness incarnated), and through the Spirit's conviction (Joh 16:8: the Spirit convicts the world concerning righteousness). The movement is top-down: divine → creaturely, through multiple mediating channels.

**[A2 — Human Righteousness]** Yes — righteousness received from God moves through the inner person from heart (inscribed law, A2-005) to will (hunger, A2-006) to conduct (outward flowing, A2-012) to speech (A2-011) to community impact (A2-015). The movement is from the heart outward: heart → will → action → community. This is the characteristic's internal constitutional movement.

**[B — Moral Uprightness]** Yes — the inner disposition of uprightness in the heart expresses itself through speech (lips) and conduct (walking in uprightness). The movement is from the inner orientation (heart) to external expression (speech, action).

**[C — Justification]** The judicial declaration of justification moves from God's tribunal (external) into the person's standing (relational-judicial). The resulting standing then connects to the reckoning faculty (F): the person who is justified is instructed to count themselves as righteous (Rom 6:11). The movement: divine declaration → new standing → inner reckoning → action.

**[D — Avenging Justice]** The cry for justice moves from the inner being (the petition of the wronged person, 944-001) outward to God, and then the response moves back from God to the situation (God acts to give justice). The movement is bidirectional: inner petition → God → divine action → restored order.

**[E — Condemnation]** Condemnation moves from external (the verdict of God or court) to internal (the inner weight of being under verdict). Self-condemnation (autokatakritos) moves from the inner conscience outward as a verdict against the self. The movement in E is bidirectional: external verdict → inner weight; inner conscience → self-verdict.

**[F — Moral Reckoning]** The reckoning faculty moves from mind (the deliberative act of counting) to will (the decision to act from the conclusion) to action (the behavioral expression of what has been reckoned). The movement is mind → will → action — cognitively initiated and behaviorally completed.

**[G — Structural Opposites]** Wickedness moves from the heart (the hard and impenitent heart, Rom 2:5) outward to systemic corruption (wickedness in the place of justice, Ecc 3:16). The movement is from inner hardness to outer systemic disorder — a parallel but inverted movement to righteousness's heart → community impact (A2).

**[CLUSTER — T2.10]** E. Constitutional movement in M26 follows three main patterns:
1. Top-down: God's righteousness → human person (A1-007, A2, C)
2. Inside-out: Heart → will → action → community impact (A2, B, G)
3. Outside-in: External verdict → inner standing → reckoning → action (C, E, F)
The cluster reveals that righteousness is not static at one constitutional level — it moves through the person (inside-out) and is received from outside (top-down or outside-in). The inside-out and outside-in patterns converge in the justified person: they receive the declaration (outside-in) and then live from it through the reckoning faculty (inside-out through F).

findings.session_b_note:
The full movement sequence implied by the data:

1. **Divine disposition (spirit level, God)** → God's character as sal.lach (Psa 86:5) — the eternal origin
2. **Divine act** → the specific forgiving act (sacrifice, declaration, Christ's atonement) — the event in history or covenant
3. **Spirit mediation** → the Spirit creates the inner openness (Mar 3:29 logic) — the mediating movement
4. **Soul reception** → the human person receives the forgiveness — inner condition changes (guilt → release; afesis state)
5. **Soul transformation** → love-orientation produced (Luk 7:47), reverence (Psa 130:4), hope (Psa 130:5-7) — the downstream inner states
6. **Soul exercise** → horizontal forgiveness extended from the heart (Mat 18:35; Luk 17:3-4) — the derivative human act
7. **Bodily expression** → visible acts (Luk 7:47 woman; bodily healing as indicator) — the outer surface

The sequence is **downward and outward** in its primary movement: from the divine spirit level, through Spirit mediation, into the human soul, generating inner states, and expressing outward through acts and bodily evidence. This sequence is implicit in the data but not assembled as a constitutional movement map in the existing observations.

*Adds structure:* The sequential map above is the clearest organisation of the constitutional movement data that the programme has produced. It draws from multiple observations (OBS-064-002, OBS-064-029, OBS-064-014, F-003) but has not been assembled in this form.

7. **Bodily expression** → visible acts (Luk 7:47 woman; bodily healing as indicator) — the outer surface

The sequence is **downward and outward** in its primary movement: from the divine spirit level, through Spirit mediation, into the human soul, generating inner states, and expressing outward through acts and bodily evidence. This sequence is implicit in the data but not assembled as a constitutional movement map in the existing observations.

*Adds structure:* The sequential map above is the clearest organisation of the constitutional movement data that the programme has produced. It draws from multiple observations (OBS-064-002, OBS-064-029, OBS-064-014, F-003) but has not been assembled in this form.

findings.session_b_note:
The sequence is consistently bottom-up and inside-out in the data:

- It begins in the deepest body interior (womb/gut/heart)
- It moves through the soul-level disposition
- It engages the will
- It arrives at the other through action

This is not a top-down cognitive process (deciding to be compassionate, then feeling it, then acting). The vocabulary insists on the pre-volitional somatic origin: compassion arises before it is chosen. The volitional engagement is real — the will can suppress or direct it — but it does not initiate it.

The Hos 11:8 pattern makes this sequence explicit in divine terms: the heart recoils (somatic) → the compassion grows warm (affective/soul) → the judgment is overridden (volitional) → the promised restoration follows (action-oriented). The four stages of T2.10 Prompt 1 are all visible in a single verse.

The one significant complication: the chesed/channum vocabulary (soul-level constitutive disposition) may precede the somatic event in terms of formation — the person who is ra.chum (constitutively compassionate) has a formed soul-level quality that enables the somatic response to arise more readily. This suggests a circular or reciprocal pattern over time: somatic events form the soul-level disposition; the soul-level disposition enables and channels future somatic events.

findings.session_b_note:
The sequence is partially evidenced. In the penitential-relational mode, spirit and heart are engaged simultaneously (they appear together in anchor verses as a pair). Soul appears only in the experiential-anguish mode, where the crushing is more severe. The body appears in somatic expression (groaning, trembling) and as the image of the deepest structural breaking (bones).

The pattern appears to be: **the severity of the crushing determines how many constitutional levels are reached**. The penitential-relational mode engages spirit and heart. The experiential-anguish mode (more externally imposed and severe) reaches soul and body. The substitutionary mode (externally imposed on the Servant) uses physical/somatic language most prominently (pierced, crushed, wounded, healed) while the inner-being outcomes (peace) are at the relational level.

*Partial: the severity-to-depth pattern is a reasonable inference from the verse distribution; the data does not state it explicitly.*

findings.session_b_note:
Two patterns are discernible:

**Pattern 1 — Inward/downward:** External or divine action → physical engagement → inner constitutional transformation. This is the wound-fellowship pattern: external wounding reaches inward to the constitutional core. The movement runs from outside-somatic to inside-constitutional.

**Pattern 2 — Upward/transformational:** Inner-constitutional orientation → somatic participation → eschatological transformation. This is the Phili 3:10 pattern: inner knowing of Christ → somatic sharing of sufferings → constitutional conformity to death → resurrection. The movement runs from inside outward through the somatic and then beyond.

Both patterns operate simultaneously in different fellowship modes. The characteristic is not constitutionally fixed at one level — it moves, and the direction of movement depends on which mode of operation is active.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-067-002: T2 as a whole reveals that goodness has a comprehensive multi-level constitutional presence — from Spirit-level origin through soul-orientation, heart-engagement, and mind-evaluative functions to outw…
findings.finding_value: T2 as a whole reveals that goodness has a comprehensive multi-level constitutional presence — from Spirit-level origin through soul-orientation, heart-engagement, and mind-evaluative functions to outward expression — but with a marked asymmetry in evidence quality. Spirit-level (Q&A-037-039), soul-level (Q&A-040-041), and heart-level (Q&A-043-044) are all substantively evidenced. Mind-level is partially evidenced through cognitive dimensions. Body-level is thin — the gladness-of-heart compound (tov-lev) and the taste-and-see perceptual metaphor are the somatic markers, but no constitutional body deposit is evidenced (T2.8 silent). The most structurally significant T2 finding is the six-step constitutional movement (Q&A-064): Spirit-level origin → soul reorientation → heart engagement → volitional alignment → agentive resolve → outward expression. This movement is top-down and outward, with no evidenced reversal from body to inner being. Goodness is constitutionally deep but does not leave a somatic deposit.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-067-008: What T1 named (goodness as primarily a quality — a settled characterological property) is confirmed and located by T2. The constitutional movement identified in T2 (six-step: Spirit → soul → heart → v…
findings.finding_value: What T1 named (goodness as primarily a quality — a settled characterological property) is confirmed and located by T2. The constitutional movement identified in T2 (six-step: Spirit → soul → heart → volition → agency → expression) explains how a characterological quality (T1's finding) is not a static property but a dynamic disposition that moves through the person from its deepest level outward. T1's four constituent poles (ontological, moral-character, experiential, volitional) map directly onto T2's constitutional levels: the ontological pole operates at Spirit-level origin; the moral-character pole at soul and heart; the experiential pole at soul-seeking; the volitional pole at the volitional step. The two tiers read together reveal that goodness is a quality that is simultaneously constitutionally located and constitutionally mobile — it has its deepest root at the Spirit level and its expression at the social-ethical level.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-067-014: T2 identified the constitutional movement of goodness from Spirit-level through soul and heart to outward expression (six-step sequence, Q&A-064). T3 names the faculty operations at each level: Spirit…
findings.finding_value: T2 identified the constitutional movement of goodness from Spirit-level through soul and heart to outward expression (six-step sequence, Q&A-064). T3 names the faculty operations at each level: Spirit-level corresponds to Spirit-production (T2.1) → T3.6 volitional reconstitution (the Spirit enables the resolve for good); soul-level seeking (T2.2) → T3.1 perceptual encounter (tasting and seeing); heart-level knowing and gladness (T2.3) → T3.3 memory and T3.4 affect; evaluative-cognitive function (T2.4) → T3.2 cognition and T3.8 moral evaluation; outward expression (T2.10) → T3.7 agency and T3.11 relational capacity. The two tiers together reveal that the constitutional movement is not an abstract structural description but a faculty-by-faculty account of how goodness moves through the person. Each constitutional level corresponds to specific faculty engagements. The T3 faculty map gives content to the T2 constitutional architecture.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-067-015: T2 confirmed that goodness originates externally to the person — the origin is God's character, Spirit, and word; the person is the site of reception, not generation (Q&A-060-061). T4 maps the relatio…
findings.finding_value: T2 confirmed that goodness originates externally to the person — the origin is God's character, Spirit, and word; the person is the site of reception, not generation (Q&A-060-061). T4 maps the relational architecture of this origin: the God-to-human direction (T4.1) is the relational channel through which the external origin reaches the person; the human-to-God direction (T4.2) is the responsive movement that the received goodness enables; the human-to-human direction (T4.3) is the overflow once received. T2's single-origin/multiple-mechanism finding (Q&A-061) maps onto T4's three relational directions: the encounter mechanism corresponds to the human-to-God direction (seeking and tasting); the covenantal-word mechanism corresponds to the God-to-human covenantal direction; the Spirit-infusion mechanism is the Spirit's work in the human constitutional levels (T2.1-2.2). The constitutional and relational architectures are co-extensive — they describe the same reality from inside (constitutional) and outside (relational).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-067-016: T2's constitutional movement (six-step sequence) and T5's transformation sequences (positive arc and moral awareness arc) describe the same developmental reality from two analytical perspectives. T2 d…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional movement (six-step sequence) and T5's transformation sequences (positive arc and moral awareness arc) describe the same developmental reality from two analytical perspectives. T2 describes where goodness moves in the person (constitutional levels); T5 describes how goodness moves the person (mechanisms and sequences). The six-step T2 sequence (Spirit → soul → heart → volition → agency → expression) is the constitutional substrate through which T5's transformation arcs operate. T5's three mechanisms (encounter, Spirit-infusion, recognition-confrontation) are the relational/contextual triggers that activate the T2 constitutional movement. Together: the T2 constitutional architecture provides the vertical structure through which T5's developmental arcs run. Formation is not a disembodied process — it is the progressive deepening of goodness through the constitutional levels identified in T2.

findings.session_b_note: The pattern from the data: divine love (Spirit-sourced) → enters heart (Rom 5:5) → produces soul-response (rest, joy, grief) → expresses bodily (kiss, embrace, tears, running). The intermediate soul-level is confirmed by OBS-103-041 and OBS-103-062 (Song) — love is experienced at the soul level before it expresses bodily. The body-level expression follows the soul-level experience: grief in the soul produces tears in the body; compassion-movement in the inner organs produces running and embrace. Pattern summary: Spirit origin → heart reception → soul experience → body expression.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-103-002: Love is the programme's most constitutionally comprehensive characteristic — it occupies all five constitutional levels simultaneously: spirit-sourced (implied via Spirit-as-agent, Rom 5:5, Gal 5:22),…
findings.finding_value: Love is the programme's most constitutionally comprehensive characteristic — it occupies all five constitutional levels simultaneously: spirit-sourced (implied via Spirit-as-agent, Rom 5:5, Gal 5:22), soul-located (Song 5:6 — soul failing at beloved's absence; Mat 22:37 — love with all your soul; Joh 15:13 — laying down the soul), heart-inscribed (Pro 3:3; Rom 5:5 infused into hearts), mind-engaged (Mat 22:37 — love with all your mind; Joh 15:15 — love as knowledge-sharing), and body-expressed (kiss, embrace, tears, womb-movement across multiple groups). The constitutional movement pattern is consistently downward: Spirit origin → heart reception → soul experience → body expression. Love's heart-inscription (Pro 3:3) is the closest evidence to a constitutional deposit — the metaphorical writing of chesed into the heart's deepest register produces a lasting dispositional quality (the chasid person-type). The primary finding: love is not confined to any single constitutional level but operates across all levels in an integrated movement from deepest to most outward. This comprehensive constitutional architecture is consistent with love's function as the programme's organising characteristic.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-103-001: Love's definition and its constitutional location are mutually illuminating. The definition identifies love as disposition + act + condition operating through directed attachment toward an object. The…
findings.finding_value: Love's definition and its constitutional location are mutually illuminating. The definition identifies love as disposition + act + condition operating through directed attachment toward an object. The constitutional mapping shows where this triple operation is located: the disposition is heart-inscribed (Pro 3:3) and spirit-sourced (implied via Rom 5:5), stable across constitutional levels; the act is will-engaged (Mat 22:37 — commanded) and soul-mobilised (Joh 15:13 — soul laid down); the condition of being-loved is received at the heart level (Rom 5:5 — poured in) and experienced at the soul level (Zep 3:17 — quieting). The constitutional movement pattern (Spirit → heart → soul → body) maps directly onto the definition's three registers: the deepest dispositional origin (spirit/heart) grounds the stable orientation; the soul-level is where love is experienced as feeling; the body-level is where act and condition become visible. Together: the constitutional location analysis confirms that love's definition is not a surface account but a constitutional claim — love operates at every depth of the inner person, which is precisely what the 'whole heart, soul, and mind' commandment (Mat 22:37) requires.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-103-007: Love's constitutional architecture and its faculty engagement are structurally aligned. The heart's engagement with love (Q&A-044, Q&A-045) corresponds to the heart's known integrating function across…
findings.finding_value: Love's constitutional architecture and its faculty engagement are structurally aligned. The heart's engagement with love (Q&A-044, Q&A-045) corresponds to the heart's known integrating function across the programme: the heart is the location of knowing (Joh 15:15 — knowledge-disclosure as love's act), willing (Mat 22:37 — love commanded), feeling (Song 5:2 — heart awake in love-awareness), and moral awareness (Pro 3:3 — chesed inscribed). Each of the heart's functions corresponds to a faculty: knowing → reason and memory; willing → will; feeling → emotion; moral awareness → moral sensitivity. The soul-level constitutional location (Song 5:6 — soul failing at beloved's absence) corresponds to the identity and relational capacity faculties: the soul whose vitality is partly constituted by the love-object is the soul whose identity (T3.10) and relational capacity (T3.11) are most deeply invested in love. The Spirit-sourced origin of love (implied) corresponds to the deep pre-reflective faculty level (L-005 — love below conscious attention): the Spirit's infusion produces love at a depth below ordinary faculty-awareness. Constitutional depth and faculty depth are directly correlated.

findings.finding_value: T2 reveals mercy as a whole-person constitutional reality. No single level contains it: mercy originates at the spirit-soul interface, operates on the soul (addressing the nephesh-guilt), engages the heart through the visceral compassion vocabulary (splanchna), engages the mind through the memory-erasure mechanism (Heb 8:12), and operates through the body as both the medium of mercy-seeking (embodied posture) and the mechanism of mercy's effect (blood-atonement). The triadic constitutional movement (Q&A-065): inner disposition → soul-transformation → embodied expression. The key finding reading T2 as a whole is the receiving-before-generating origin structure (Q&A-062): mercy cannot be generated from within the person but must be received from outside and then expressed through the constitutional architecture. Body deposit: none. T5.7: formally closed.

The constitutional portrait is comprehensive: spirit broken at the innermost level, heart broken at the moral-evaluative level, nephesh crushed at the whole-self level, and bones as the somatic expression of the inner breaking. What T2 reveals as a whole is the embodied depth of contrition — it is not a disembodied inner experience but a constitutional event that traverses all levels of the person. The T2.8 finding (no body deposit) means contrition does not leave a permanent somatic trace — it is a passing constitutional event, not a permanent constitutional mark.

findings.finding_value: T2 produces the most distinctive constitutional portrait in the current review set. Spirit-level location is entirely absent — three consecutive S ratings — forming a new gap. By contrast, soul-level (chesed as covenantal-soul character), heart-level (Hos 11:8 — "my heart recoils"), and somatic-level (re.chem, splanchnon) are all richly evidenced. The constitutional architecture is bottom-up: the womb and entrails are the originating ground; the soul and heart are the engagement points; the act is the constitutional expression. Four body-part functions are identified: constitutive (womb — the generative image of compassion), expressive (gut — the felt movement), indicative (Synoptic pattern — splanchnizō signals the compassion-event), and mediating (heart in Hos 11:8 — the deliberative locus where compassion and judgment contend). The four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) is uniquely evidenced in this registry — consistently inside-out and bottom-up. T2.8 established no body deposit; T5.7 is formally closed. The constitutional portrait confirms the sb_classification (soul-body interface) and extends it: compassion is the most somatically grounded characteristic in the programme, with its originating logic residing in the body's deepest interior.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-008: T1's four-kind structure (character quality, inner event, condition of object, externalised act) maps precisely onto T2's constitutional levels. The character-quality kind (ra.chum — dispositional com…
findings.finding_value: T1's four-kind structure (character quality, inner event, condition of object, externalised act) maps precisely onto T2's constitutional levels. The character-quality kind (ra.chum — dispositional compassionate character) operates at the soul level (T2.2 — chesed as soul-character). The inner-event kind (splanchnizō — the moment of being-moved) operates at the somatic level (T2.6 — the gut as the site of the stirring). The condition-of-object kind (eleeinos — the pitiable state) is the constitutional trigger that activates the somatic-constitutional movement. The externalised-act kind is the constitutional endpoint of T2.10's four-stage movement sequence. T1's definition and T2's constitutional account are co-determining: the characteristic cannot be adequately defined without specifying the constitutional levels at which its four kinds operate.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-014: T2's four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) maps directly onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The somatic-arousal s…
findings.finding_value: T2's four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) maps directly onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The somatic-arousal stage (T2.6 — gut stirring, splanchnizō) corresponds to T3.1's perceptive-trigger stage (sight activates the somatic response) and T3.4's affect stage (the stirring is the affective movement). The soul-engagement stage (T2.2 — chesed as soul-character) corresponds to T3.8 moral evaluation (the soul assesses the need) and T3.9 conscience (the conscience activates the response). The volitional-engagement stage (T2.3 — heart-locus as deliberative site) corresponds to T3.6 volition (the will directs the action). The outward-action stage corresponds to T3.7 agency. T2 and T3 describe the same movement sequence from two perspectives: T2 maps the constitutional levels; T3 maps the faculties active at each level.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-015: T2's constitutional origin analysis (somatic-relational-covenantal triple ground) and T4's relational direction analysis are structurally aligned. The somatic origin (womb, gut) grounds the cross-boun…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional origin analysis (somatic-relational-covenantal triple ground) and T4's relational direction analysis are structurally aligned. The somatic origin (womb, gut) grounds the cross-boundary relational direction in T4: splanchnizō's somatic immediacy is precisely what enables it to cross covenantal boundaries — the gut-movement toward the suffering other precedes any covenantal assessment of the relationship. The covenantal origin (chesed) grounds the within-bond sustaining direction in T4. The constitutional origin therefore predicts the relational direction: somatic = cross-boundary; covenantal = within-bond. T2's soul-body interface classification explains T4's scope-by-need finding: because compassion originates at the soul-body interface (before covenantal-rational assessment), its scope is determined by the pre-rational recognition of need rather than the post-rational assessment of covenantal standing.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-016: T2's four-stage constitutional movement (somatic arousal → soul → volition → action) and T5's three mechanisms of change (encounter/sudden, covenantal-sustaining/gradual, participatory-ontological) ar…
findings.finding_value: T2's four-stage constitutional movement (somatic arousal → soul → volition → action) and T5's three mechanisms of change (encounter/sudden, covenantal-sustaining/gradual, participatory-ontological) are structurally complementary. T2 describes the movement within a single compassion-event; T5 describes how that event accumulates into character over time. The encounter/sudden mechanism (T5) corresponds to the full four-stage sequence of T2 in a single instance. The covenantal-sustaining mechanism (T5) corresponds to the repeated operation of the somatic-soul pathway (T2.2 — soul-level chesed as the sustaining character) over time. The participatory-ontological mechanism (T5) corresponds to the constitutional direction T2 identifies but leaves at spirit-level gap: if the deepest formation is participatory-ontological, the spirit-level dimension (T2.1 — entirely silent) may be where this operates — a convergent gap from two tiers.

findings.session_b_note: A discernible pattern emerges across the evidence. For OT covenant: the movement runs outer → inner → outer: God declares the covenant externally (word, law on stone) → calls for inner reception and commitment (heart and soul) → inner commitment is enacted outwardly (oath, sacrifice, bodily circumcision). The inner person is the receptive and responsive site between God's external word and the body's covenant-expression. For new covenant: the movement runs inner → inner → outer: God acts internally (Spirit on the person, law written on heart — Heb 8:10) → the inner person is constituted anew in their knowing and willing → this inner renewal expresses outwardly through faithfulness and speech (Isa 59:21). The shift from OT to NT covenantal movement is structurally significant: from outer-to-inner (law imposed on the person from outside) to inner-to-inner-to-outer (Spirit working from within outward). This is the constitutional-level mechanism of the transformation trajectory — DIM-34-001 confirmed at the movement level.

findings.finding_value: T2 as a whole reveals that covenant operates across the full constitutional range of the inner person with no single exclusive location. The heart is the primary site (Q&A-044), the mind is co-located (Q&A-047), the soul gives totality of engagement (Q&A-041), the mouth is the expressive-constitutive organ (Q&A-050), and the body participates through blood and circumcision (Q&A-053). The single most structurally significant T2 finding is the constitutional movement shift from OT to NT covenantal mode: OT covenant moves outer→inner→outer; new covenant moves inner→inner→outer (Q&A-066). This movement-shift is the constitutional-level expression of the Sinai-to-new-covenant transformation — it places the origin of covenant faithfulness at the level of God's own interior action within the person rather than the person's compliance with external demand. T2 confirms that covenant is constitutively somatic as well as inner — it cannot be reduced to a purely invisible spiritual reality because it is enacted, sealed, and transmitted through bodily acts and substances.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-034-008: T1 defines covenant as constitutively composite — operating in four modes (disposition, act, quality, condition). T2 reveals that each mode has a distinct constitutional location: the disposition-mode…
findings.finding_value: T1 defines covenant as constitutively composite — operating in four modes (disposition, act, quality, condition). T2 reveals that each mode has a distinct constitutional location: the disposition-mode (God's relational commitment) operates at the deepest constitutional level (spirit/relational), the act-mode (human entry) is enacted through somatic performance (oath = mouth, cutting = body, blood), the quality-mode (moral faithfulness) resides in heart and character, and the condition-mode (new covenant transformation) is inscribed on heart and mind by divine action. The T1 × T2 synthesis: covenant's four modes correspond to four distinct constitutional locations and operations, and the new covenant's primary contribution is shifting the constitutional origin from external to internal — the condition-mode is not entered by human act but produced by God's inner writing. The composite mode structure (T1) is constitutionally grounded across the full inner person (T2).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-034-016: T2 identifies a shift in constitutional origin across the covenant trajectory: from external bestowal (Noahic) to bilateral reception (Sinai) to generational transmission (Davidic) to internal Spirit-…
findings.finding_value: T2 identifies a shift in constitutional origin across the covenant trajectory: from external bestowal (Noahic) to bilateral reception (Sinai) to generational transmission (Davidic) to internal Spirit-generation (new covenant — Q&A-064). T5 identifies a corresponding shift in the mechanism of change: from external-demand (old covenant letter) to internal-inscription (new covenant Spirit — Q&A-131, Q&A-132). The T2 × T5 synthesis: the constitutional origin shift (T2) and the mechanism shift (T5) are the same development described at two different levels. The new covenant's internal Spirit-generation (T2) is the constitutional reality that underlies the internal-inscription mechanism (T5). These are not two separate developments but one single inner-being transformation described at the constitutional-location level (T2) and at the developmental-mechanism level (T5). The new covenant produces a change in where covenant comes from (T2: now from within through the Spirit) and a change in how it produces change (T5: now through inscription rather than instruction).

findings.session_b_note: Three patterns are identifiable: (1) Cascading loss pattern: inner peace → somatic peace is the normal condition; inner dis-peace → somatic deterioration follows the causal chain inner-to-body (Psa 32:3, 38:3, Deu 28:65). The sequence is consistent: first the inner person is disordered (by sin, by judgment, by absent trust), then the body registers the disorder. The body is the last to fail and the indicator of deep inner trouble. (2) Cascading gift pattern: God gives peace (Num 6:26, Joh 14:27) → heart and mind receive it (Phili 4:7, Isa 26:3) → body enacts it (Psa 4:8 — lying down in sleep). The sequence moves from divine source through inner-being faculties into somatic expression. The body's rest is the downstream expression of the inner peace received. (3) Redemptive reversal pattern: suffering body of the Servant (Isa 53:5) → inner peace produced in others; this reversal moves counter to the normal direction and is unique in the corpus. The three patterns together establish peace as a constitutionally mobile characteristic — it does not reside statically in one location but flows through the whole person, and flows in different directions under different conditions.

findings.session_b_note: Two distinct movement patterns are evidenced. (1) The endowing pattern: divine giving moves from spirit level downward and outward — Spirit given → understanding formed in the hidden inner parts → person equipped to instruct/act. The sequence is constitutive: each level is enabled by the gift at the deeper level. (2) The expressive pattern: inner orientation (trust, covenantal commitment) moves from inner to outer — inner disposition → bodily act (Isa 50:6) or visible response (altar-building, Gen 12:7) or praise (Job 1:21). The sequence is expressive: the inner is prior, the outer is derivative. (3) The eschatological pattern: external divine act transforms internal state — God gives eschatologically → faint spirit becomes praising spirit → outer garment of praise expresses transformed inner state. The sequence is transformative: outside-in → inside renewed → inside-out again. These three patterns (constitutive, expressive, transformative) represent the full movement architecture of the characteristic.

What T2 reveals as a whole: this characteristic operates at every constitutional level not because it is superficially distributed but because giving as an inner-being act can reach the spirit (endowing), the heart (deciding), the soul (attaching), the hidden inner parts (forming), and the body (expressing and constituting).
